# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides an overview of the project, the purpose of the Solution Design Document, and identifies its intended audience. ## 2.1 Project Overview Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has initiated a project to modernize its data workflow and analytics capabilities by leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The scope encompasses designing a comprehensive data workflow from ingestion through transformation to visualization, tailored to UMS's business requirements. Key objectives include the establishment of a Fabric workspace, development of an end-to-end ETL pipeline, implementation of machine learning processes, and integration of Power BI for actionable business analytics. The solution aligns UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s suite of services, specifically Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science for machine learning applications. ## 2.2 Document Purpose The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to formally outline the technical architecture, design decisions, and implementation plan for the UMS Power BI & Fabric project. It serves as the definitive reference for design review, stakeholder sign-off, and provides detailed guidance for implementation and operational handover. ## 2.3 Document Audience This document is intended for UMS IT administrators, business stakeholders, project sponsors, and technical teams, as well as Enfrasys Solutions architects and consultants. It is designed to facilitate informed review, approval, and collaborative execution throughout the project lifecycle. # 3.0 Microsoft Power BI & Fabric Overview This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, emphasizing their roles in supporting Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data workflow, analytics, and security requirements. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is a comprehensive analytics platform designed to unify data integration, engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Fabric consolidates multiple Microsoft services into a cohesive ecosystem, enabling organizations to streamline their data workflows from ingestion to visualization. Fabric comprises several core components: - **Data Factory:** Provides robust data integration and orchestration capabilities, allowing UMS to ingest, transform, and move data across various sources. - **Synapse:** Offers advanced analytics and big data processing, supporting UMS in complex data modeling, warehousing, and scalable analytics workloads. - **Data Science:** Enables machine learning applications, facilitating predictive analytics and AI-driven insights for UMS’s business use cases. - **OneLake:** Acts as a unified data lake storage layer, centralizing all data assets and simplifying access and governance. For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing Microsoft Fabric to establish a dedicated workspace, develop end-to-end ETL pipelines, conduct machine learning processes, and ensure seamless integration with visualization tools. ## 3.2 Power BI Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and analytics tool that empowers users to create interactive reports and dashboards. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, leveraging data stored in OneLake and processed through Data Factory and Synapse for real-time analytics and visualization. Power BI’s integration within Fabric enables UMS to: - Visualize transformed and modeled data directly from Fabric workspaces. - Facilitate business-aligned analytics and reporting. - Provide secure, scalable access to insights for stakeholders across Universiti Malaysia Sabah. Enfrasys Solutions recommends leveraging Power BI within the Fabric environment to deliver actionable insights, support data-driven decision-making, and enhance UMS’s analytics capabilities. ## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. Entra ID is responsible for authenticating users, managing access permissions, and securing resources across Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. Entra ID supports UMS’s requirements by: - Enabling single sign-on (SSO) for seamless access to Fabric and Power BI resources. - Providing centralized identity management for administrators and users. - Enforcing security policies and role-based access controls to protect sensitive data and analytics assets. Enfrasys Solutions recommends Universiti Malaysia Sabah implement Microsoft Entra ID as the authoritative identity provider to secure authentication and access throughout the solution, ensuring compliance and robust security posture. # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the network connectivity and security design for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in relation to Microsoft Fabric integration, focusing on secure data flow and gateway deployment. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Microsoft Fabric is a cloud-based analytics platform from Microsoft that unifies data integration, engineering, and analytics in a single SaaS environment. It enables organizations to securely connect to on-premises data sources, such as SQL Server, via a Data Gateway, ensuring seamless and secure data transfer. The UMS network architecture is designed to enable secure, outbound-only connectivity between the on-premises SQL Server, Data Gateway VM, and Microsoft Fabric. The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM acts as a bridge, facilitating secure data transfer without exposing internal resources to inbound traffic from external networks. ![](images\slide_011_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data flow between UMS SQL Server, OPDG, and Microsoft Fabric. The outbound-only design ensures that all connections initiated from the OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric and related services occur over secure, encrypted channels, minimizing exposure to external threats and aligning with Azure networking best practices. ## 4.2 Fabric Data Gateway The Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure agent that enables cloud services, such as Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, to access data stored within UMS’s on-premises environment. The gateway is installed on a dedicated VM, which initiates outbound connections to Microsoft cloud endpoints, ensuring that no inbound ports are opened on UMS’s internal network. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the deployment, configuration, and validation of the OPDG VM and agent. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall ensure that the on-premises network is prepared, including firewall configuration and network readiness, to support outbound-only connectivity. The Fabric Administrator (also referred to as Data Engineer) is responsible for overseeing workspace configuration, user provisioning, security enforcement, and operational management within Microsoft Fabric. Role assignment and access reviews must be documented and revisited quarterly to maintain compliance and operational integrity. # 6.0 Microsoft Fabric Design and Decision This section outlines the recommended Microsoft Fabric architecture and design decisions for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), including data workflow, access, VM sizing, resource organization, and governance. ## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that combines data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence in a single SaaS environment. It integrates components such as Lakehouse, Dataflow Gen2, AutoML, and Power BI, enabling seamless data ingestion, transformation, analytics, and visualization. The following table summarizes key workflow considerations for UMS’s data ingestion, transformation, and analytics workloads: | ID | Description | Workload Type | |------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------| | DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server. | Data Factory | | DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server. | Data Engineering | | DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse. | Data Engineering | | DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse. | Data Engineering | | DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook, and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering | | DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory | | DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science | | DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse. | Power BI | | DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization. | Power BI | ## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following workflow architecture for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric deployment: ![](images\slide_009_img_003.png) Figure 1: End-to-end data workflow architecture. - **Data Ingestion**: Azure Data Factory pipelines ingest data from the UMS Staging Area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) into the Bronze Lakehouse. - **Bronze Layer**: Stores raw, untransformed data for traceability and auditing. - **Silver Layer**: Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query are used for cleansing and transformation, producing enriched datasets. - **Gold Layer**: Final, transformed data is stored for reporting and analytics; includes outputs from AutoML and manual ML processes. - **Data Science**: Both AutoML and manual ML (via Notebooks) are applied to Silver Lakehouse data, with scored results stored in Gold Lakehouse. - **Semantic Model**: Connected to Gold Lakehouse via OneLake Direct Lake mode, enabling robust data modeling. - **Power BI Integration**: Power BI Desktop connects to the Semantic Model for visualization and reporting. ![](images\slide_021_img_005.png) Figure 2: AutoML and manual ML workflow integration. | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |-----|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Data ingestion via Azure Data Factory | Implemented; pipelines configured for SQL Server data warehouse ingestion | | 2 | Layered Lakehouse architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) | Adopted; ensures data traceability, quality, and optimized analytics | | 3 | Data transformation using Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, Visual Query | Adopted; enables flexible, scalable data engineering | | 4 | Machine learning via AutoML and manual ML in Fabric Notebooks | Adopted; supports both automated and custom ML workflows | | 5 | Model registry and scoring notebook outputs stored in Gold Lakehouse | Adopted; ensures standardized repository for ML results | | 6 | Semantic Model integration with Gold Lakehouse via OneLake | Implemented; enables direct, performant data modeling | | 7 | Power BI Desktop connection to Semantic Model for visualization | Implemented; provides business intelligence and reporting | ## 6.3 Access Design Considerations and Decisions ### Conditional Access Conditional Access in Microsoft Entra ID enables organizations to enforce access controls based on user, location, device, and risk conditions. It is essential for securing data and analytics workloads in Fabric and Power BI. | No. | Policy | Decision | |-----|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Require MFA for all administrative access | Enforced for all Fabric and Power BI administrators | | 2 | Block access from risky locations | Enabled; only trusted IP ranges allowed | | 3 | Require compliant devices | Enabled; access limited to devices meeting UMS compliance | ### Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is a security mechanism requiring users to provide two or more verification methods to access Microsoft Fabric and Power BI resources. | No. | Policy | Decision | |-----|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Enforce MFA for all users | Enabled for all UMS personnel accessing Fabric workloads | | 2 | Enforce MFA for guest/external users | Enabled for all external collaborators | ### Entra ID Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is the identity and access management platform for Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. It enables single sign-on, role-based access control, and conditional access policies. | No. | Policy | Decision | |-----|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Use Entra ID for authentication | All Fabric and Power BI resources integrated with Entra ID | | 2 | Assign workspace roles via Entra ID | Role-based access enforced for all UMS workspaces | ## 6.4 Virtual Machine (VM) Size The Data Gateway VM specification for UMS is as follows: | Component | Specification | |-------------------|---------------------------------------| | Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) | | .NET Framework | Version 4.8 | | vCPU | 8 cores | | RAM | Minimum 8 GB | Enfrasys Solutions shall provision and configure the VM. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ongoing maintenance and monitoring. ## 6.5 Resource Organization Design ### Management Groups Enfrasys recommends structuring Azure management groups to reflect UMS’s organizational hierarchy, separating production, development, and test environments. This enables consistent policy enforcement, cost tracking, and resource governance. - Root Management Group: UMS - Production - Development - Test Enfrasys Solutions will configure the management group structure. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall maintain and update group memberships as organizational needs evolve. ### Naming and Tagging #### Azure Naming Convention | Resource | Abbreviation | Example | |------------------|-------------|--------------------------| | Resource Group | rg | ums-prod-rg | | Storage Account | st | umsprodst01 | | Virtual Machine | vm | ums-prod-datagateway01 | | Network | vnet | ums-prod-vnet | #### Fabric Naming Convention | No. | Item in Fabric | Naming Convention | |-----|-------------------|-----------------------------------------| | 1 | Fabric Capacity | stagingareadevcapacity01 | | 2 | Workspace | StudentAffairs_dev_WS | | 3 | Lakehouse | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK

Etc. | | 7 | Report | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_Report| #### Acronyms | Resource | Abbreviation | |------------------|-------------| | Lakehouse | LK | | Dataflow | DF | | Semantic Model | SM | | Pipeline | PL | | Workspace | WS | Enfrasys Solutions shall implement naming and tagging standards. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ensuring compliance and updating tags as resources evolve. ## 6.6 Governance Consideration ### Governance Disciplines Enfrasys recommends the following governance disciplines for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric environment: - **Cost Management**: Track and optimize resource usage, set budgets, and monitor spending. - **Resource Compliance**: Enforce policies for resource configuration, security, and lifecycle management. - **Monitoring**: Implement real-time monitoring and alerting for performance, security, and operational health. | Azure Tool | Description | Cost Management Discipline | |-----------------------|---------------------------------------------|-------------------------------| | Azure Cost Management | Budget tracking, alerts, usage analytics | Cost Management | | Azure Policy | Enforces resource compliance | Resource Compliance | | Azure Monitor | Performance and operational monitoring | Monitoring | Ownership Assignment: - Enfrasys Solutions: Initial configuration, policy setup, dashboard creation. - Universiti Malaysia Sabah: Ongoing monitoring, budget review, compliance remediation. ### Violation Triggers and Actions | Trigger | Action | Owner | |-----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------| | Budget threshold exceeded | Notify UMS finance team, review usage | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | | Resource non-compliance detected | Remediate configuration, escalate if unresolved | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | | Security alert (e.g., unauthorized access) | Investigate, apply corrective measures | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | | Monitoring alert (performance degradation) | Analyze and optimize workloads | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | Enfrasys Solutions shall provide initial governance templates and support. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall own ongoing governance operations and incident response. --- Appendix references for Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Entra ID, and governance are provided in the Appendix section of this document. # 7.0 Security Design and Decision This section outlines the security architecture and controls for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Azure workloads. ## 7.1 Azure Network Security Groups (NSG) Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a core security feature within Microsoft Azure. NSGs allow administrators to control inbound and outbound network traffic to Azure resources by defining rules based on source, destination, port, and protocol. NSGs are commonly used to enforce least-privilege access, segment workloads, and ensure compliance with organizational security policies. Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the configuration and maintenance of NSG rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall monitor compliance and report any deviations or incidents. ### Outbound NSG Rules | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |--------------------------|----------|-----------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services| 130 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Authentication| 140 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow | No inbound rules are defined for the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM in this phase; all inbound access is managed via Azure services and conditional access policies. ## 7.2 Encryption Design Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure cloud services enforce encryption both at rest and in transit, in accordance with Microsoft’s security best practices. ### Encryption at Rest Data stored within Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure Storage, and related services is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys with AES-256 or higher standards. This includes storage in OneLake, Data Warehouse, and all managed disks. Enfrasys recommends that UMS periodically review Microsoft’s encryption compliance documentation to ensure ongoing alignment with regulatory requirements. ### Encryption in Transit All data exchanged between UMS’s on-premises environment, the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), and Microsoft Fabric is encrypted in transit using SSL/TLS protocols. Outbound NSG rules are strictly limited to HTTPS (TCP port 443) and HTTP (TCP port 80 for connectivity testing), ensuring secure transmission of authentication, data, and service communications. Enfrasys Solutions shall configure all gateway endpoints to enforce SSL/TLS. UMS shall monitor for any exceptions and report them for remediation. ### Microsoft Best Practices References Enfrasys Solutions will adhere to Microsoft’s published best practices for encryption and network security: - Azure Network Security Groups: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-groups-overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-groups-overview) - Encryption at Rest: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/encryption-atrest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/encryption-atrest) - Encryption in Transit: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/encryption-intransit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/encryption-intransit) ## 7.3 Security Task Assignment and Compliance | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|--------------| | NSG Configuration | Implement outbound NSG rules as per design | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | | Encryption Enforcement | Configure SSL/TLS for all gateway endpoints | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | | Compliance Monitoring | Review NSG and encryption compliance, report deviations | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | Ongoing | | Policy Review | Periodically review Microsoft security best practices and update configuration as required | Enfrasys Solutions | Scheduled | ## 7.4 Conditional Access and MFA Enforcement Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID feature that enables organizations to enforce access controls based on user, device, location, and risk signals. Due to licensing constraints, Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s tenant is not eligible for advanced Conditional Access policies. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enforced at the tenant level to mitigate risk and ensure secure access to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. | No. | Policy | Decision | |-----|------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Configure Conditional Access for Power BI, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, Azure Storage | Deferred (pending license upgrade) | | 2 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy | Deferred (pending license upgrade) | | 3 | Enforce MFA for UMS users | Implemented | | 4 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric environment | Enabled via MFA | ![](images\slide_006_img_001.png) Figure 1: Conditional Access and user access flow. ![](images\slide_006_img_002.png) Figure 2: Authentication process with Entra Conditional Access policies. --- Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah strictly adhere to these security controls and conduct regular reviews for compliance and improvement. # 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach This section outlines the phased approach for deployment and migration of the solution for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), detailing preparatory, pilot, production, and post-migration activities. ## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) and Enfrasys Solutions shall execute all preparatory tasks to ensure readiness for the migration and deployment. slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the project context, objectives, and responsibilities for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Power BI & Microsoft Fabric implementation. ## 2.1 Project Overview Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has initiated a strategic project to modernize its data analytics capabilities, focusing on the implementation of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The project scope encompasses designing a comprehensive data workflow—from ingestion, transformation, and orchestration within Microsoft Fabric, to advanced analytics and visualization through Power BI. Key objectives include: - Establishing a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace for UMS. - Developing end-to-end ETL pipelines utilizing Fabric Data Factory. - Conducting machine learning processes leveraging Fabric Data Science and Synapse components. - Integrating Power BI for business-aligned analytics and reporting. This initiative aligns UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s suite of services, enabling scalable data integration, advanced analytics, and actionable insights for business stakeholders. ## 2.2 Document Purpose This Solution Design Document serves as the formal blueprint for UMS’s data analytics modernization using Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. It details the technical architecture, design decisions, implementation workflows, and security considerations required for successful deployment. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for solution design, technical implementation, and deployment activities. UMS is responsible for reviewing the design, providing sign-off, and maintaining data ownership throughout the project lifecycle. ## 2.3 Document Audience The intended audience for this document includes: - UMS IT management and technical teams - UMS business stakeholders and data owners - Enfrasys Solutions architects and implementation specialists Enfrasys Solutions shall lead the solution design, deployment, and technical support. UMS shall review deliverables, provide feedback, approve the design, and retain data ownership. This document is structured to facilitate clear communication and alignment between all parties involved. # 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview This section outlines the foundational Microsoft technologies leveraged in Universiti Malaysia Sabah's (UMS) data platform solution, including Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform designed to unify data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Fabric consolidates multiple core services, including Data Factory, Synapse, Data Science, and OneLake, to streamline the end-to-end data workflow from ingestion to transformation and visualization. - **Data Factory**: Provides robust data integration and orchestration capabilities, enabling seamless movement and transformation of data across diverse sources. - **Synapse**: Offers advanced analytics and big data processing, supporting complex data warehousing and real-time analytics workloads. - **Data Science**: Facilitates machine learning and AI processes, including AutoML and manual modeling, to drive predictive analytics. - **OneLake**: Acts as a unified data lake, centralizing storage and enabling secure, scalable access to data across Fabric services. In the UMS solution, Microsoft Fabric serves as the backbone for the data pipeline, orchestrating ingestion from the UMS SQL Data Warehouse, transformation through ETL processes, and integration with downstream analytics and reporting tools. ### Microsoft Fabric Core Features | Capability | Description | |--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Data Factory | Data ingestion, transformation, and orchestration across multiple sources | | Synapse | Advanced analytics, big data processing, and data warehousing | | Data Science | Machine learning, AutoML, and custom modeling workflows | | OneLake | Unified, secure data lake for centralized storage and access | ### Fabric Configuration & Management Responsibilities - **Enfrasys Solutions**: Responsible for initial setup, configuration, and integration of Microsoft Fabric components, including workspace creation and ETL pipeline design. - **UMS**: Responsible for ongoing management, monitoring, and operational maintenance of Fabric workspaces and associated data workflows. ![](images\slide_009_img_003.png) Figure 1: UMS Fabric Data Workflow Architecture. ## 3.2 Power BI Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and analytics platform, designed to enable interactive data visualization, reporting, and insights sharing across organizations. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, allowing seamless access to curated datasets and facilitating real-time analytics. - **Integration with Fabric**: Power BI connects directly to OneLake within Fabric, enabling users to visualize and analyze refined datasets (e.g., XX_Gold_LK Tables) generated from ETL and machine learning processes. - **Analytics & Reporting**: Power BI empowers UMS stakeholders to create dashboards, reports, and visualizations tailored to business requirements, supporting data-driven decision-making. ### Power BI Core Features | Capability | Description | |--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Data Visualization | Interactive dashboards, charts, and reports | | Data Integration | Direct connectivity to Fabric OneLake, SQL, and other sources | | Sharing & Collaboration | Secure sharing of insights and reports across the organization | | Real-time Analytics| Live data monitoring and alerting | ### Power BI Configuration & Management Responsibilities - **Enfrasys Solutions**: Responsible for initial Power BI workspace integration, dataset configuration, and security setup. - **UMS**: Responsible for ongoing report creation, dashboard management, and user access administration. ![](images\slide_021_img_005.png) Figure 2: UMS AutoML and Power BI Integration Workflow. ## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management solution. Entra ID provides authentication, authorization, and user management services for applications and resources within the Microsoft ecosystem, including Fabric and Power BI. - **Identity Management**: Centralizes user identities, enabling secure sign-in and access control for UMS personnel. - **Access Governance**: Enforces role-based access policies, ensuring only authorized users can interact with sensitive data and analytics resources. - **Integration**: Seamlessly integrates with Fabric and Power BI, supporting Single Sign-On (SSO) and conditional access. ### Entra ID Core Features | Capability | Description | |--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Authentication | Secure user sign-in and credential management | | Authorization | Role-based access control and policy enforcement | | SSO Integration | Single Sign-On across Microsoft Fabric and Power BI | | Conditional Access | Adaptive access policies based on user, device, and location | ### Entra ID Configuration & Management Responsibilities - **Enfrasys Solutions**: Responsible for initial Entra ID configuration, role mapping, and integration with Fabric and Power BI. - **UMS**: Responsible for ongoing user management, access reviews, and policy adjustments. --- # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the network topology, connectivity, and gateway deployment required for secure integration between Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) operates a hybrid network topology that connects its on-premises SQL Server data warehouse with Microsoft Fabric via a secure On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). The topology ensures seamless and secure data transfer, leveraging outbound connections to Microsoft cloud services. ### Design Considerations | ID | Description | Workload Type | |----|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------| | 1 | Secure connectivity between on-premises SQL Server and Microsoft Fabric via Data Gateway | Data Integration | | 2 | Outbound-only network traffic from OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints | Security/Compliance | | 3 | Authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID | Access Management | | 4 | Connectivity testing for OPDG service | Operations | ### Network Topology Diagram ![](images\slide_011_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data flow architecture between UMS SQL Server, On-Premises Data Gateway, and Microsoft Fabric. ## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway ### Microsoft Fabric Definition Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single SaaS offering. It enables organizations to connect, transform, and analyze data across multiple sources, including on-premises and cloud environments. ### On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) Definition The On-Premises Data Gateway is a Microsoft component that facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services, such as Fabric and Power BI. The gateway establishes outbound connections, eliminating the need for inbound ports and minimizing attack surfaces. ### Gateway Deployment and Role Enfrasys Solutions shall deploy the OPDG agent on a dedicated virtual machine within the UMS on-premises network. The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, enabling data flows from UMS’s SQL Server data warehouse to Microsoft Fabric, while adhering to security and compliance requirements. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall respond to notifications and remediate issues. # 7.0 Security Design and Decision This section outlines the security architecture, controls, and responsibilities for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in the deployment of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and supporting Azure components. ## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are fundamental security constructs within Microsoft Azure, used to filter network traffic to and from Azure resources in a virtual network. The diagram illustrates a technical architecture involving Azure components and user access management. 

1. **Fabric-RG**: This represents a Resource Group in Azure, which is a container that holds related resources for an Azure solution. It is depicted with an icon suggesting a fabric or mesh network, indicating a structured environment for managing resources.

2. **UMS Fabric**: This component likely refers to a User Management System within the Azure environment, possibly utilizing Azure Fabric for scalable and reliable service management. It is part of the Fabric-RG, suggesting it is a resource managed within this group.

3. **Conditional Access**: This is a security feature in Azure Active Directory that controls access to resources based on specific conditions. It is represented by a shield with a lock, indicating its role in securing access.

4. **External User**: This component represents users outside the organization who need access to resources within the Azure environment. The diagram shows a connection from the UMS Fabric to the External User, indicating that user access is managed through the UMS Fabric, with Conditional Access policies applied to ensure secure and compliant access.

The data flow suggests that external users interact with the UMS Fabric, which is governed by Conditional Access policies to ensure secure access to resources within the Fabric-RG.

The diagram illustrates the authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric using Entra conditional access policies.

1. **User Authentication Attempt**: The process begins with a user attempting to authenticate to Microsoft Fabric.

2. **Entra Conditional Access Policies**: The authentication request is evaluated against Entra conditional access policies.

3. **Signal Collection**: Signals are gathered, including examples such as users and groups, and network location. These signals provide context for the access request.

4. **Decision Making**: Based on the collected signals, a decision is made regarding the access request. This involves evaluating the conditions set in the policies.

5. **Enforcement**: The decision leads to enforcement actions, which determine whether access is granted or denied based on the policy evaluation.

6. **Microsoft Fabric Access**: If access is granted, the user can interact with Microsoft Fabric, which includes various components such as data analytics, storage, and processing tools. OneLake is highlighted as a part of the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.

The diagram effectively outlines the flow from user authentication to access enforcement, emphasizing the role of conditional access policies in securing Microsoft Fabric.

The diagram represents a data processing and analytics architecture within the UMS Fabric environment. It begins with data ingestion from a Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, labeled as the UMS Staging Area. The data is ingested using Azure Data Factory, which orchestrates the movement into the XX_Bronze_LK Tables, serving as the initial landing zone for raw data.

The data then progresses to the XX_Silver_LK Tables, where it is likely transformed and cleansed. This stage is crucial for preparing data for further analysis and processing. Azure Data Factory continues to facilitate the data movement between these stages.

Next, the data enters the Data Science phase, where advanced analytics and machine learning processes are applied. This phase is supported by Azure Data Factory and involves the use of data science tools to derive insights and predictions.

The processed data is stored in the XX_Gold_LK Tables, representing the final, refined dataset ready for consumption. Identity_SM is involved at this stage, possibly for managing data access and security.

Finally, the data is connected via OneLake to Power BI, enabling visualization and reporting. OneLake acts as a unified data lake, providing seamless integration and access to the data for business intelligence purposes.

The diagram illustrates a data flow architecture involving three main components:

1. **UMS Staging Area - Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse**: This component represents the on-premise data storage system where data is initially staged. It is likely used for storing and processing large volumes of data before it is transferred or utilized by other systems.

2. **On-Premise Data Gateway (OPDG)**: This gateway serves as a bridge between the on-premise data warehouse and external systems. It facilitates secure data transfer without requiring inbound ports, ensuring that data can be sent out securely while minimizing security risks associated with open ports. The gateway handles outbound connections, allowing data to flow from the on-premise environment to external services.

3. **UMS Fabric**: This component represents an external system or service that interacts with the on-premise data warehouse through the OPDG. The UMS Fabric likely provides additional processing, analytics, or integration capabilities, leveraging the data received from the on-premise environment.

The data flow begins at the UMS Staging Area, where data is stored and processed. It is then securely transmitted through the On-Premise Data Gateway, which manages the outbound connection to the UMS Fabric. This setup ensures secure and efficient data transfer between the on-premise environment and external systems, enhancing data utilization and integration capabilities.

The diagram illustrates a data processing and machine learning workflow within an Azure environment, leveraging UMS Fabric and OneLake for data management and integration.

1. **Data Source**: 
   - **XX_Silver_LK Tables**: These tables serve as the initial data source, containing pre-processed data ready for machine learning experiments.

2. **Machine Learning Processes**:
   - **AutoML**: 
     - **AutoML Experiment**: Data from XX_Silver_LK Tables is fed into an AutoML experiment, which automates the selection of algorithms and hyperparameters.
     - **Result Scoring (Using Notebook)**: The results from the AutoML experiment are scored using a notebook, providing insights and metrics on model performance.
   - **Manual Machine Learning**:
     - **Modelling (Using Notebook)**: Alternatively, data can be processed through manual machine learning modeling using notebooks, allowing for custom algorithm selection and parameter tuning.

3. **Data Integration and Storage**:
   - **XX_Gold_LK Tables**: The output from both AutoML and manual machine learning processes is stored in XX_Gold_LK Tables, representing refined and validated data.
   - **Identity_SM**: This component likely handles identity management or metadata associated with the data in XX_Gold_LK Tables.

4. **Data Visualization and Reporting**:
   - **Power BI**: The XX_Gold_LK Tables are connected to Power BI via OneLake, enabling visualization and reporting of the processed data for business intelligence purposes.

5. **Infrastructure**:
   - **UMS Fabric**: Provides the overarching framework for managing and orchestrating the data and machine learning workflows.
   - **OneLake**: Facilitates seamless data integration and connectivity between the storage tables and Power BI.

The diagram effectively outlines the flow of data from initial processing to advanced machine learning and final visualization, emphasizing the integration of automated and manual machine learning techniques within a robust Azure-based infrastructure.

# SIRIM Analytics Deployment # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the SIRIM Analytics Deployment project, the purpose of this solution design document, and its intended audience. ## 2.1 Project Overview A project overview formally defines the scope, objectives, and alignment of the initiative with strategic technology platforms. The objective of the SIRIM Analytics Deployment is to design a robust data workflow for SIRIM’s Human Resource (HR) use-case. The workflow encompasses data ingestion, transformation, and visualization, leveraging Microsoft Fabric capabilities. Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence in a single environment. The solution will utilize Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, and Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing. This design aligns SIRIM’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s modern analytics services. Enfrasys Solutions is assigned to draft the technical design and workflow, while SIRIM shall review and validate the alignment with HR requirements. ## 2.2 Document Purpose A document purpose statement clarifies the intent, scope, and expected outcomes of the formal solution design. The intent of this document is to serve as a comprehensive solution design for SIRIM’s analytics deployment, specifically targeting the HR data workflow. It details architectural decisions, technology selection, access controls, and implementation guidance to ensure a secure, scalable, and efficient analytics environment. This document is intended to guide both technical implementation and business stakeholder alignment. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting this document; SIRIM is tasked with reviewing and providing feedback to ensure completeness and relevance. ## 2.3 Document Audience A document audience definition identifies all stakeholders who are expected to read, review, or act upon the solution design. The intended audience for this solution design document includes: - SIRIM IT personnel (responsible for technical implementation and operations) - SIRIM HR stakeholders (business owners and data consumers) - Enfrasys Solutions architects (design, deployment, and advisory roles) - Project sponsors (executive oversight and approval) Enfrasys Solutions will draft the document for these stakeholders; SIRIM shall review and ensure it meets organizational and project objectives. # 3.0 Microsoft Fabric Analytics Overview This section outlines the foundational analytics technologies to be implemented for SIRIM’s Human Resource data workflow. Enfrasys Solutions provides authoritative definitions and integration guidance for core Microsoft services. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric: Definition and Core Services Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform designed to streamline data integration, engineering, and visualization across the enterprise. Fabric consolidates multiple data workloads under a single SaaS umbrella, enabling seamless collaboration and governance. Its core services include: - **Fabric Data Factory**: Provides robust data integration and orchestration capabilities. It enables ingestion, transformation, and movement of data from diverse sources into centralized storage. - **Fabric Synapse**: Delivers advanced analytics and big data processing. Synapse supports scalable data engineering, SQL analytics, and machine learning workloads. - **Power BI**: Offers business intelligence and visualization tools. Power BI enables interactive reporting, dashboards, and data-driven insights, connecting directly to Fabric’s data stores. Microsoft Fabric is highly relevant to SIRIM’s analytics strategy, as it supports end-to-end data workflows—from ingestion and transformation to visualization—within a secure, governed environment. ## 3.2 Microsoft Entra ID & M365 Integration Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. Entra ID provides authentication, authorization, and user management for cloud and on-premises applications. It ensures secure access to resources and enables granular control over user permissions. Microsoft 365 (M365) is a suite of productivity applications and cloud services, including Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, and Office applications. Integration between Fabric and M365 allows for seamless collaboration, data sharing, and secure access to analytics resources. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that SIRIM leverage Entra ID for identity management across all Fabric workloads and integrate with M365 to enable secure, collaborative analytics environments. ## 3.3 Core Technology Summary Table | Technology | Purpose | Usage in Project | |--------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------| | Fabric Data Factory| Data integration and orchestration | Ingest and move data from PostgreSQL to Lakehouse layers | | Fabric Synapse | Advanced analytics and big data processing | Data cleansing, transformation, and engineering in Lakehouse layers | | Power BI | Business intelligence and visualization | Data visualization and reporting from Gold Lakehouse via OneLake | | Entra ID | Identity and access management | Authentication and authorization for all analytics workloads | | Microsoft 365 | Productivity and collaboration | Secure access, sharing, and collaboration on analytics outputs | Enfrasys Solutions shall provide the detailed content and configuration guidance for these technologies. SIRIM shall validate the requirements and confirm alignment with organizational policies. ![](images\slide_016_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data workflow architecture utilizing Fabric Data Factory, Synapse, and Power BI. # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the Azure network architecture, connectivity flows, and Data Gateway configuration for SIRIM’s Microsoft Fabric deployment. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Microsoft Azure is a cloud computing platform and infrastructure provided by Microsoft, offering a wide range of services including compute, storage, networking, and analytics. Azure subscriptions are the fundamental containers for billing and resource management, enabling organizations to provision and manage cloud resources securely. Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following network design for SIRIM: - **Azure Subscription**: All resources are provisioned within a dedicated Azure subscription for SIRIM. - **Virtual Networks (VNETs)**: Two primary VNETs are established: - One for core SIRIM Fabric workloads (Fabric-VNET). - One for Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD) services (WVD-VNET). - **VNET Peering**: Direct peering between Fabric-VNET and WVD-VNET enables seamless communication while maintaining isolation. - **Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN**: A Virtual Network Gateway in Fabric-VNET establishes secure S2S VPN connectivity between SIRIM’s on-premises network and Azure. - **Network Flow**: - Internal SIRIM users access Fabric resources directly via conditional access policies. - External users connect to WVD, which mediates access to Fabric resources through NSG rules and indirect network paths. - **Private Endpoint**: Fabric workspace is exposed via a private endpoint within Fabric-VNET, ensuring only internal network users can access sensitive resources. ![](images\slide_012_img_003.png) Figure 1: Azure VNET, Peering, and S2S VPN Network Architecture. SIRIM shall confirm all network requirements, including IP ranges, VPN parameters, and user access scenarios. ## 4.2 Fabric Data Gateway Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway is a secure bridge that enables cloud services such as Power BI, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps to access on-premises data sources. The gateway is typically deployed as an agent on a dedicated virtual machine within the Azure environment or on-premises network. For SIRIM, the Data Gateway VM is deployed within the SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG resource group, acting as an intermediary between the TOPAZ PostgreSQL database and SIRIM Fabric. This VM ensures secure, reliable data flow for analytics and integration workloads. ![](images\slide_018_img_005.png) Figure 2: Data Gateway VM bridging TOPAZ and SIRIM Fabric. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the Data Gateway VM architecture. SIRIM shall confirm the VM location, network connectivity, and operational requirements. ### Data Gateway VM Specification | VM Name | OS | vCPU | RAM | Disk | Purpose | |-------------------|------------|------|------|------|-------------------------------------------| | GASPRA | Windows | 4 | 16GB | 128GB| Host Data Gateway agent for Fabric access | ## 4.3 NSG Rules for WVD Network Security Groups (NSGs) are used to control inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources. The following NSG rules are applied to the WVD subnet to secure access to Fabric resources: | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |---------------------|----------|---------------------|--------------|-----------------------|------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_Fabric_Inbound| 110 | Service Tag | 443 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | TCP | Allow | | Allow_Fabric_Outbound| 110 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | Service Tag | 443 | TCP | Allow | ## 4.4 Task/Migration Rollout | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------| | Azure Subscription Setup | Provision dedicated subscription and resource groups | Enfrasys Solutions| Pending | | VNET & Peering Design | Establish Fabric-VNET, WVD-VNET, and configure peering | Enfrasys Solutions| Pending | | S2S VPN Configuration | Set up Virtual Network Gateway and establish VPN to SIRIM HQ | Enfrasys Solutions| Pending | | Network Requirements Review| Confirm IP ranges, VPN parameters, user access scenarios | SIRIM | Pending | | Data Gateway VM Deployment| Install Data Gateway agent on GASPRA VM | Enfrasys Solutions| Pending | | Data Gateway VM Confirmation| Confirm VM location and operational requirements | SIRIM | Pending | | NSG Rule Implementation | Apply NSG rules for secure WVD-Fabric access | Enfrasys Solutions| Pending | ## 4.5 Design Decisions | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |-----|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | VNET Peering between Fabric and WVD environments | Enabled for seamless internal communication | | 2 | S2S VPN for on-premises connectivity | Configured via Azure Virtual Network Gateway | | 3 | Private Endpoint for Fabric workspace | Enabled to restrict access to internal users only | | 4 | Data Gateway VM location and specification | Deployed in SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG, confirmed by SIRIM | | 5 | NSG rules for WVD | Allow inbound/outbound Fabric access as per security table | ## 4.6 Design Considerations | ID | Description | Workload Type | |-----|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------| | 1 | Secure connectivity between on-premises and Azure | Hybrid Cloud | | 2 | Segregation of workloads via VNETs and peering | Analytics, VDI | | 3 | Data Gateway VM for bridging on-premises and Fabric | Data Integration| | 4 | NSG rules for controlled access to Fabric | Security | | 5 | Private Endpoint for internal-only Fabric access | Data Analytics | # 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and access scopes for SIRIM personnel within Microsoft Fabric, including recommended mappings and assignment procedures. ## 5.1 Fabric Administrator Role Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. It leverages OneLake for unified data storage and provides robust workspace management and security controls. The Fabric Administrator role is responsible for the overall governance, configuration, and management of Fabric environments. Administrators have full access to manage workspace settings, assign roles, publish and delete content, and enforce security policies. ### Administrator capabilities | Capability | Description | |----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Manage Workspaces | Create, configure, and delete workspaces. | | Assign Roles | Add/remove users, assign workspace roles and permissions. | | Content Management | Publish, edit, and delete datasets, reports, pipelines, and dashboards. | | Security Enforcement | Configure row-level security, semantic models, and access controls. | | Audit & Monitoring | Review activity logs and monitor workspace usage. | Enfrasys Solutions recommends SIRIM assign dedicated Fabric Administrators to ensure proper governance and operational continuity. ## 5.2 Fabric-native Roles Microsoft Fabric provides several built-in workspace roles, each with distinct permissions and access scopes: ### Workspace-level role capabilities | Permission | Admin | Contributor | Member | Viewer | |-------------------------|-------|-------------|--------|--------| | View Content | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | | Modify Content | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | | Share Content | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | | Manage Roles/Permissions| ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | | Publish/Delete Content | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | | Edit Workspace Settings | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | - **Admin**: Full control, including role management and workspace configuration. - **Contributor**: Can create, edit, and delete own content but cannot manage roles or settings. - **Member**: Can create, edit, delete, and share content but cannot manage roles or workspace settings. - **Viewer**: Can view all content but cannot modify, publish, or share. Enfrasys Solutions recommends SIRIM leverage these roles to enforce least-privilege access and operational separation. ## 5.3 SIRIM Workspace Role and Access Enfrasys Solutions proposes the following workspace role mapping for SIRIM personnel. SIRIM shall review, assign, and approve the final role allocations. ### Client workspace role mapping | No. | Workspace Role | Suggested Role | SIRIM Personnel | |-----|---------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------| | 1 | Workspace Admin | Fabric Admin/Data Engineer | En Wazir

SIRIM shall assign and approve personnel for each workspace role. ## 5.4 Row-Level Security and Data Modeling Row-level security (RLS) in Microsoft Fabric restricts data visibility within reports and dashboards, ensuring that users only access data relevant to their roles. The Semantic Model defines table structures, relationships, and RLS policies. Enfrasys Solutions recommends SIRIM configure RLS for sensitive workloads, such as HR data, leveraging existing Microsoft 365 groups (e.g., sirimmgmt@sirim.my) for access control. --- # 6.0 Microsoft Fabric Design and Decision This section outlines the recommended Microsoft Fabric architecture, data workflow, access design, VM sizing, resource organization, and governance for SIRIM’s analytics deployment. ## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. Fabric leverages Data Factory for ingestion, Lakehouse for storage and transformation, Synapse for analytics, and Power BI for visualization. The table below summarizes the key data workflow considerations for SIRIM’s solution: | ID | Description | Workload Type | |------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------| | DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from PostgreSQL. | Data Factory | | DC02 | The bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from PostgreSQL. | Data Engineering | | DC03 | The silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse. | Data Engineering | | DC04 | The gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse. | Data Engineering | | DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the bronze and silver Lakehouse will be performed using Visual Query in SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering | | DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory | | DC07 | Data modeling and row-level security (RLS) configurations will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the gold Lakehouse. | Power BI | | DC08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization. | Power BI | ![](images\slide_016_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data workflow architecture for SIRIM using Data Factory, Lakehouse, Synapse, and Power BI. ## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following architecture for SIRIM’s analytics platform: | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Data ingestion layer | Azure Data Factory pipelines will ingest data from PostgreSQL into the bronze Lakehouse. | | 2 | Storage and transformation | Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers will be used for raw, cleansed, and transformed data respectively. | | 3 | Data movement and transformation | Dataflow Gen2 will orchestrate data movement between Lakehouse layers. | | 4 | Analytics and processing | Synapse Engineering will process data in Silver and Gold layers for advanced analytics. | | 5 | Semantic modeling and security | Power BI Semantic Models will be built on Gold Lakehouse with row-level security (RLS). | | 6 | Visualization | Power BI Desktop will connect to Semantic Model via OneLake for reporting. | | 7 | Data Gateway | Data Gateway agent will be installed on GASPRA VM to bridge on-premises sources and Fabric.| | 8 | Access control | Conditional Access and Private Endpoint will be configured as per SIRIM security requirements.| ![](images\slide_018_img_005.png) Figure 2: Data Gateway architecture bridging TOPAZ PostgreSQL and SIRIM Fabric. ## 6.3 Access Design Considerations and Decisions ### Conditional Access Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID feature that enables organizations to enforce access policies based on user, location, device, and application conditions. | ID | Method | Decision | Rationale | |------|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | AC01 | Conditional Access | Policy will include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, Azure Storage | Ensures only authorized SIRIM users can access analytics workloads | | AC02 | Conditional Access | NSG configured in SIRIM's WVD for Fabric inbound/outbound | Restricts network traffic to Fabric resources | | AC03 | Conditional Access | SIRIM users included in Conditional Access policy | Limits access to only designated SIRIM personnel | ### Private Endpoint Private Endpoint is an Azure networking feature that enables private connectivity to Azure services, ensuring traffic remains within the internal network. | ID | Method | Decision | Rationale | |------|-----------------|----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | PE01 | Private Endpoint| Enable Private Link in Fabric | Restricts Fabric access to internal SIRIM network | | PE02 | Private Endpoint| Create Private Endpoint via Azure portal | Ensures secure, private connectivity to Fabric workspace | | PE03 | Private Endpoint| Disable Public Access from Fabric | Prevents external access to Fabric resources | | PE04 | Private Endpoint| Power BI access remains via Public Endpoint | Power BI does not currently support Private Link for Fabric datasets | | PE05 | Private Endpoint| Copilot not supported on Private Endpoint | Current limitation; Copilot features unavailable for private endpoint scenarios | ## 6.4 Virtual Machine (VM) Size Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following VM specification for the Data Gateway agent. SIRIM shall validate and provide any missing information. | VM Name | OS | .NET Version | vCPU | RAM | Disk | Purpose | |-----------|------------|--------------|------|------|------|------------------------| | GASPRA | Windows | .NET 4.8 | 4 | 16GB | 256GB| Data Gateway agent host| ## 6.5 Resource Organization Design ### Management Groups SIRIM’s Azure resources shall be organized under a management group structure to ensure consistent governance, policy enforcement, and billing separation. Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following hierarchy: - Root Management Group: SIRIM - Sub-management Groups: BIGDATA, EDWH, FABRIC ### Naming and Tagging #### Azure Naming Convention | Resource | Abbreviation | Example | |--------------------|-------------|-----------------------------| | Resource Group | RG | SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG | | Virtual Machine | VM | GASPRA-VM | | Data Factory | DF | SIRIM-EDWH-DF | | Lakehouse | LK | HR_Bronze_LK | | Synapse Workspace | SW | SIRIM-FABRIC-SW | | Power BI Workspace | WS | HR_dev_WS | #### Fabric Naming Convention | Item | Convention | Example | |----------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------| | Fabric Capacity| --capacity | hrdevcapacity01 | | Workspace | --WS | HR_dev_WS | | Lakehouse | --LK | HR_Bronze_LK | | Dataflow | --DF | HR_Bronze_to_Silver_DF | | Semantic Model | --SM | HR_HeadcountWorkforce_SM | | Pipeline | --PL | HR_Ingest_Data_PL | | Report | --Report | HR_HeadCountWorkForce_Report | #### Acronyms | Acronym | Description | |---------|----------------------------| | RG | Resource Group | | VM | Virtual Machine | | DF | Data Factory | | LK | Lakehouse | | SW | Synapse Workspace | | WS | Workspace | | SM | Semantic Model | | PL | Pipeline | ## 6.6 Governance Consideration ### Governance Disciplines | Discipline | Description | Owner | |-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------| | Cost Management | Monitor and optimize Azure/Fabric resource usage and spending | SIRIM | | Policy | Enforce resource configuration and access policies | Enfrasys | | Compliance | Ensure analytics platform adheres to SIRIM’s regulatory standards | SIRIM | ### Violation Triggers and Actions | Trigger | Action | Owner | |-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-----------------| | Unauthorized access attempt | Alert and block access | Enfrasys | | Resource configuration drift | Automated remediation or alert | Enfrasys | | Cost threshold exceeded | Notify SIRIM, review and optimize usage | SIRIM | --- Enfrasys Solutions will draft all configurations and policies. SIRIM shall validate, provide missing information, and approve final implementation. # 7.0 Security Design and Decision This section outlines the security architecture for SIRIM’s Microsoft Fabric and Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD) environment, focusing on network controls and encryption. ## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a Microsoft Azure feature used to filter network traffic to and from Azure resources in a virtual network. NSGs contain security rules that allow or deny inbound and outbound traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol. Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing NSG rules to secure both WVD and Fabric workloads. SIRIM shall review and approve the rules as defined below. ### NSG Rules for WVD and Fabric #### WVD NSG Rules | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |---------------------|---------|------------------|--------------|---------------------|------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_Fabric_Inbound| 110 | Service Tag | 443 | Vm Private IP Addresses | * | TCP | Allow | | Allow_Fabric_Outbound| 110 | Vm Private IP Addresses | * | Service Tag | 443 | TCP | Allow | #### Fabric NSG Rules | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |---------------------|---------|------------------|--------------|---------------------|------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_Fabric_Inbound| 110 | Service Tag | 443 | Vm Private IP Addresses | * | TCP | Allow | | Allow_Fabric_Outbound| 110 | Vm Private IP Addresses | * | Service Tag | 443 | TCP | Allow | ## 7.2 Encryption Design ### Microsoft Fabric Encryption Overview Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, and business intelligence. Security is a core principle, and Microsoft Fabric leverages Azure’s encryption mechanisms for both data at rest and in transit. ### Encryption at Rest Data stored in Microsoft Fabric, Azure SQL Database, Azure Data Explorer, Azure Storage, and Power BI Service is encrypted at rest using Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) and Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) for databases. This ensures that all data is protected from unauthorized access, even if the underlying storage is compromised. - Azure Storage: Uses SSE with AES-256. - Azure SQL Database: Uses TDE, encrypting the entire database, logs, and backups. - Power BI Service: Data is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys. ### Encryption in Transit Data in transit between users, applications, and Microsoft Fabric services is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. This includes all connections to Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage. - All HTTP/S endpoints enforce TLS encryption. - Internal Azure traffic between services is protected by Azure’s backbone network. Enfrasys Solutions shall define and implement encryption mechanisms based on Microsoft best practices. SIRIM shall review and validate the encryption configuration. ## 7.3 Access Design (Conditional Access) ### Conditional Access Overview Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) feature that enables organizations to enforce access controls based on user identity, device state, location, and application sensitivity. Policies can require secure login, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and restrict access to specific resources. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that SIRIM implement Conditional Access policies covering Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage. SIRIM users will have direct access to Fabric, managed by Conditional Access. External users will access Fabric indirectly via WVD, with access managed by NSG rules. ### Access Decisions | No. | Policy | Decision | |-----|--------|----------| | 1 | SIRIM user direct access to Fabric | Allowed with Conditional Access | | 2 | External user indirect access via WVD | Allowed via NSG rules | | 3 | Secure login, MFA enforced | Required for all users | | 4 | Conditional Access for Power BI, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, Azure Storage | Enforced | ## 7.4 Security Task Assignment | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |------|------------|-----------|--------| | Define NSG rules for WVD and Fabric | Draft and implement NSG rules | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | | Review NSG rules | Validate and approve rules | SIRIM | Pending | | Define encryption at rest and in transit | Configure encryption settings | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | | Review encryption configuration | Validate encryption setup | SIRIM | Pending | | Create Conditional Access policies | Configure policies in Entra ID | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | | Review Conditional Access policies | Approve and test policies | SIRIM | Pending | ## 7.5 Security Architecture Diagram ![](security_architecture_diagram.png) Figure 1: Security architecture for SIRIM Fabric and WVD environment. # 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach This section outlines the structured methodology for deploying and migrating the Data Gateway solution for SIRIM, including preparatory actions, pilot testing, production rollout, and post-migration support. ## 8.1 Pre-Migration / Setup Enfrasys Solutions recommends that SIRIM undertake a series of preparatory steps prior to migration to ensure readiness and minimize risk. Responsibilities are explicitly assigned to Enfrasys Solutions (lead) and SIRIM (support/confirmation). ### Preparatory Steps | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |------|------------|-----------|--------| | 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by SIRIM | Enfrasys, SIRIM | Not-Started | | 2 | Confirm on the table to be ingested | SIRIM | Not-Started | | 3 | Create an Azure VM to establish Data Gateway | Enfrasys | Not-Started | ### Pre-Migration Timeline (D-7) | Task | Date | Owner | Status | |------|------|-------|--------| | Confirm data tables for ingestion | 11-June-25 | SIRIM | Not-Started | | Review and approve design document | 13-June-25 | SIRIM | Not-Started | | Provision Data Gateway VM credentials | 13-June-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | ## 8.2 Pilot Deployment The pilot phase involves deploying the Data Gateway agent within a dedicated VM (GASPRA) and validating data connectivity between TOPAZ (PostgreSQL) and SIRIM FABRIC. ### Pilot Deployment Description - Enfrasys Solutions will install and configure the Data Gateway agent on the designated VM. - SIRIM will provide access credentials and confirm the VM environment. - Initial test queries will be executed to validate end-to-end data flow. ### Pilot Test Plan - Validate connectivity between Data Gateway VM and TOPAZ PostgreSQL database. - Confirm successful data ingestion into SIRIM FABRIC. - Execute sample queries as provided by SIRIM. ### Acceptance Criteria - Data Gateway agent operational and connected to source and destination. - Successful ingestion of test data tables. - SIRIM confirms data integrity and accessibility. ### Pilot Timeline (D0) | Task | Date | Owner | Status | |------|------|-------|--------| | Install Data Gateway agent | 17-June-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | Execute pilot ingestion queries | 18-June-25 | SIRIM | Not-Started | | Validate data flow and acceptance | 18-June-25 | SIRIM, Enfrasys | Not-Started | ![](images\slide_018_img_005.png) Figure 1: Data Gateway architecture for pilot and production. ## 8.3 Production Rollout Upon successful pilot completion, Enfrasys Solutions will execute the production rollout, including cutover planning and risk mitigation. ### Production Rollout Plan - Enfrasys Solutions will transition the Data Gateway VM from pilot to production mode. - SIRIM will confirm production data tables and monitor ingestion. - Risk mitigation steps include backup of source data and rollback procedures. ### Cutover Plan - Schedule cutover window to minimize impact on business operations. - Final confirmation of production environment readiness. - Execute production ingestion and monitor for anomalies. ### Production Timeline (D+1) | Task | Date | Owner | Status | |------|------|-------|--------| | Transition Data Gateway to production | 19-June-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | Monitor production ingestion | 19-June-25 | SIRIM | Not-Started | | Execute rollback if necessary | 19-June-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | ## 8.4 Post-Migration / Support Post-migration, Enfrasys Solutions will provide operational support, facilitate handover, and conduct knowledge transfer sessions for SIRIM. ### Support Model - Enfrasys Solutions will provide Tier-2 support for Data Gateway operations for 2 weeks post-migration. - SIRIM will monitor daily ingestion and escalate issues as required. ### Handover and Knowledge Transfer - Enfrasys Solutions will deliver operational documentation and conduct a knowledge transfer session for SIRIM administrators. - SIRIM will acknowledge receipt and understanding of documentation. ### Post-Migration Timeline (D+14) | Task | Date | Owner | Status | |------|------|-------|--------| | Provide operational documentation | 3-July-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | Conduct knowledge transfer session | 3-July-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | Confirm handover and support closure | 3-July-25 | SIRIM | Not-Started | # 9.0 Appendix This section provides reference links and project-specific constraints for SIRIM’s analytic deployment across computing, network, identity & security, logging & monitoring, cloud governance, and Microsoft Fabric. slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.
