# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the UMS Power BI & Microsoft Fabric implementation project, outlining the business context, objectives, document purpose, and intended audience. ## 2.1 Project Overview UMS has initiated a strategic project to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence capabilities through the adoption of Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric. The scope of this engagement includes designing and implementing a comprehensive data workflow that spans ingestion, transformation, and visualization, tailored to UMS’s business requirements. Key objectives are as follows: - Establishment of a Microsoft Fabric workspace to serve as the central hub for data operations. - Development of end-to-end ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines leveraging Fabric Data Factory for robust data integration and orchestration. - Implementation of advanced analytics using Fabric Synapse for big data processing and Fabric Data Science for machine learning applications. - Integration of Power BI to deliver business-aligned analytics and interactive reporting. This initiative aligns UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with the latest capabilities of Microsoft Fabric, enabling scalable, secure, and efficient data-driven decision-making. ## 2.2 Document Purpose The Solution Design Document is intended to serve as the authoritative reference for the design, implementation, and ongoing management of the UMS Power BI & Fabric solution. Its purposes are: - To provide a detailed, formal record of all architectural decisions, design considerations, and implementation plans. - To facilitate structured design review and approval between UMS stakeholders and Enfrasys Solutions. - To guide the technical execution of the project, ensuring alignment with business objectives and compliance with Microsoft best practices. - To serve as a future reference for maintenance, troubleshooting, and expansion of the solution. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting, updating, and maintaining the Solution Design Document. UMS is responsible for reviewing, providing feedback, and formally signing off on the document prior to implementation. ## 2.3 Document Audience The Solution Design Document is intended for the following stakeholders: - UMS IT department (technical leads, data engineers, administrators) - UMS business stakeholders (project sponsors, analytics users) - Enfrasys Solutions project team (enterprise architects, implementation consultants, support personnel) Enfrasys Solutions shall coordinate document review sessions and incorporate feedback from all parties. UMS shall ensure relevant personnel participate in reviews and provide formal approval for each design milestone. # 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, establishing their relevance and integration within the UMS data analytics solution. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform designed to streamline data integration, engineering, science, and visualization across an organization. It consolidates multiple data services into a single SaaS offering, simplifying data workflows and governance. The key components of Microsoft Fabric include: - **Data Factory**: Enables scalable data integration and orchestration, allowing organizations to ingest, transform, and move data across sources. - **Synapse**: Provides advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, supporting real-time and batch analytics on large datasets. - **Data Science**: Facilitates machine learning and advanced analytics, offering tools for AutoML, notebooks, and custom modeling. - **OneLake**: Acts as a unified data lake, storing and managing data from multiple sources, and providing seamless access for analytics and visualization. UMS shall leverage Microsoft Fabric to establish a centralized workspace for end-to-end data workflows, including ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization. ## 3.2 Power BI Power BI is a business intelligence and data visualization tool that enables organizations to analyze and share insights from their data. It offers interactive dashboards, reports, and data modeling capabilities, empowering users to make informed decisions. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, allowing direct connectivity to OneLake and semantic models for real-time analytics. UMS shall utilize Power BI to visualize processed data from Fabric’s Gold Lakehouse, connecting via OneLake to deliver business-aligned analytics and reporting. ## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides authentication, authorization, and user management for applications and services within the Microsoft ecosystem. Entra ID ensures secure access to resources, supports single sign-on, and enables role-based access control across Fabric and Power BI. UMS shall implement Microsoft Entra ID to manage user authentication and access control, ensuring secure and compliant operations within the data analytics environment. ![](images\slide_009_img_003.png) Figure 1: End-to-end data workflow architecture in UMS Fabric environment. ![](images\slide_021_img_005.png) Figure 2: Machine learning and AutoML workflow integration with Power BI in UMS Fabric. # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the network architecture and connectivity decisions for UMS, focusing on secure integration between on-premises SQL Server, Data Gateway VM, and Microsoft Fabric. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single SaaS solution. It enables organizations to connect disparate data sources, perform analytics, and deliver insights securely at scale. UMS’s network architecture is designed to ensure secure, outbound-only connectivity between the on-premises SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, the Data Gateway VM (hosting the On-Premises Data Gateway agent), and Microsoft Fabric. The Data Gateway VM acts as a bridge, facilitating secure communication without exposing on-premises resources to inbound traffic. All connections initiated from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft cloud services are outbound, leveraging HTTPS and HTTP protocols for secure data transfer and authentication. ![](images\slide_011_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data flow from SQL Server through On-Premises Data Gateway to Microsoft Fabric. ## 4.2 Fabric Data Gateway Design The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft component that enables secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services (such as Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, and Azure Data Factory). The gateway operates by relaying queries and data over encrypted outbound connections, eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules. ### 4.2.1 Gateway Placement and Role UMS shall deploy the OPDG agent on a dedicated Virtual Machine within the on-premises environment. This VM will connect to the SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse and securely relay data to Microsoft Fabric. The gateway VM requires outbound network access to Microsoft endpoints for data transfer, authentication, and connectivity testing. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for providing the deployment architecture, configuration guidance, and validation of the gateway setup. UMS shall provision the VM, configure the required network rules, and install the OPDG agent as per Enfrasys’s recommendations. ### 4.2.2 Gateway VM Specification The following table defines the minimum specifications for the Data Gateway VM: | Component | Specification | |------------------|---------------------------------------------| | Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) | | .NET Framework | Version 4.8 | | vCPU | 8 cores | | RAM | Minimum 8 GB | ## 4.3 Network Security and Outbound Rules To ensure secure connectivity, the Data Gateway VM shall be configured with outbound-only Network Security Group (NSG) rules. NSGs use rules to allow or deny traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol, thereby protecting virtual machines and services from unauthorized access. UMS shall implement NSG rules for the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM to ensure secure connectivity to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and provisioning the NSG configuration, while UMS is responsible for ongoing monitoring and management. ### NSG Rules for Data Gateway VM | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |---------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow | ![](diagram/security_gateway_nsg.png) Figure 1: Data Gateway VM NSG configuration. ## 7.2 Encryption Design ### Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, and business intelligence. It provides end-to-end encryption for all data flows, both at rest and in transit, using industry-standard protocols. ### Power BI Power BI is a cloud-based business intelligence service that enables users to visualize and analyze data. Power BI ensures data encryption at rest using Azure Storage encryption and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. ### Data Gateway The On-Premises Data Gateway facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services. All communications from the gateway to Azure services are encrypted in transit using HTTPS (TLS). ### SQL Server SQL Server supports Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) for data at rest and SSL/TLS encryption for data in transit. #### Encryption Design Decisions - Data at rest in Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure SQL Database shall be encrypted using Azure-managed keys. - Data in transit between the Data Gateway, SQL Server, and Microsoft cloud services shall be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. - Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring encryption settings during deployment. UMS shall maintain and periodically review encryption compliance. | No. | Policy | Decision | |-----|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Encryption at Rest | Enabled for all workloads using Azure-managed keys | | 2 | Encryption in Transit | Enforced via TLS 1.2+ for all connections (Gateway, SQL, Fabric, Power BI) | | 3 | NSG Rule Ownership | Enfrasys Solutions to provision; UMS to monitor and maintain | | 4 | Encryption Configuration Ownership | Enfrasys Solutions to configure; UMS to review and audit | ![](diagram/security_encryption_flow.png) Figure 2: Encryption flow across workloads. ## 7.3 Security Responsibilities - Enfrasys Solutions: Design, provision, and initial configuration of NSG and encryption policies. - UMS: Ongoing monitoring, periodic review, and compliance auditing for NSG and encryption settings. # 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach This section outlines the structured deployment and migration methodology for UMS, including preparatory actions, pilot execution, production rollout, and post-migration support. ## 8.1 Pre-Migration / Setup Enfrasys Solutions recommends a comprehensive pre-migration phase to ensure readiness and minimize risks. The diagram illustrates a technical architecture involving Azure components and user access management. 

1. **Fabric-RG**: This represents a Resource Group in Azure, which is a container that holds related resources for an Azure solution. It is depicted with an icon suggesting a fabric or mesh, indicating integration or connectivity.

2. **UMS Fabric**: This component likely refers to a User Management System or a similar service within the Azure environment. It is part of the Fabric-RG, suggesting it is a resource managed within this group.

3. **Conditional Access**: This is a security feature in Azure Active Directory that controls access to resources based on specific conditions. It is represented by a shield with a lock, indicating security and protection.

4. **External User**: This component represents users outside the organization who need access to resources within the Azure environment. The icon suggests a generic user profile.

**Data Flow and Connections**:
- The diagram shows a unidirectional arrow from the UMS Fabric to the External User, passing through Conditional Access. This indicates that external users are granted access to resources managed within the UMS Fabric, but only after meeting the conditions set by Conditional Access policies.
- Conditional Access acts as a gatekeeper, ensuring that only users who meet specific security requirements can access the resources in the Fabric-RG.

This architecture emphasizes secure access management for external users interacting with Azure resources, leveraging Conditional Access to enforce security policies.

The diagram illustrates the authentication and access control process for Microsoft Fabric using Entra conditional access policies.

1. **User Authentication Attempt**: The process begins with a user attempting to authenticate to Microsoft Fabric.

2. **Entra Conditional Access Policies**: The authentication request is evaluated against Entra conditional access policies.

3. **Signal Collection**: Signals are gathered, including examples such as users and groups, and network location. These signals provide context for the access request.

4. **Decision Making**: Based on the collected signals, a decision is made regarding the access request. This involves evaluating the conditions set in the access policies.

5. **Enforcement**: The decision leads to enforcement actions, which determine whether access is granted or denied based on the policy evaluation.

6. **Microsoft Fabric Access**: If access is granted, the user can interact with Microsoft Fabric, which includes various components such as data analytics, storage, and processing tools. OneLake is highlighted as a component within Microsoft Fabric, indicating its role in data storage or management.

The diagram effectively outlines the flow from user authentication to access enforcement, emphasizing the role of conditional access policies in securing access to Microsoft Fabric.

The diagram represents a data processing and analytics architecture within the UMS Fabric environment. It illustrates the flow of data from ingestion to visualization using various Azure components.

1. **Data Ingestion**:
   - **Source**: Data originates from the UMS Staging Area, specifically a Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse.
   - **Data Factory**: Azure Data Factory is used to ingest data from the SQL Server into the UMS Fabric.

2. **Data Processing Layers**:
   - **XX_Bronze_LK Tables**: The initial layer where raw data is stored after ingestion.
   - **XX_Silver_LK Tables**: Data is transformed and cleaned, moving from the Bronze to the Silver layer.
   - **XX_Gold_LK Tables**: Final transformation and enrichment occur here, preparing data for analysis.

3. **Data Science and Transformation**:
   - **Data Factory**: Used again for further data transformation and orchestration.
   - **Data Science**: Advanced analytics and machine learning processes are applied to the data.

4. **Identity Management**:
   - **Identity_SM**: This component likely handles security and identity management, ensuring data access is controlled.

5. **Data Storage and Access**:
   - **OneLake**: Acts as a unified data lake for storing processed data, facilitating easy access and integration.

6. **Data Visualization**:
   - **Power BI**: The processed data is connected via OneLake to Power BI for visualization and reporting.

The architecture efficiently manages data flow from ingestion to visualization, leveraging Azure services for transformation, storage, and analytics.

The diagram illustrates a data flow architecture involving three main components:

1. **UMS Staging Area - Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse**: This component represents the on-premises data warehouse where data is stored and managed. It serves as the initial data source in the architecture.

2. **On-Premise Data Gateway (OPDG)**: This gateway facilitates secure communication between the on-premises data warehouse and external services. It enables data transfer without requiring inbound ports, ensuring security through outbound connections.

3. **UMS Fabric**: This component likely represents a cloud-based service or platform that interacts with the on-premises data warehouse via the OPDG. The connection is secure and outbound, indicating data is sent from the on-premises environment to the UMS Fabric without exposing internal systems to inbound traffic.

The data flow begins at the SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, moves through the On-Premise Data Gateway, and reaches the UMS Fabric, ensuring secure and efficient data transfer.

The diagram illustrates a data processing and machine learning workflow within an Azure environment, leveraging UMS Fabric and OneLake for data management and integration.

1. **Data Source**: 
   - **XX_Silver_LK Tables**: These tables serve as the initial data source, stored within OneLake. They provide the raw or pre-processed data necessary for machine learning tasks.

2. **Machine Learning Processes**:
   - **AutoML**: 
     - **AutoML Experiment**: Data from XX_Silver_LK Tables is fed into an AutoML experiment, which automates the process of model selection and hyperparameter tuning.
     - **Result Scoring (Using Notebook)**: The results from the AutoML experiment are scored using a notebook, which likely involves evaluating model performance metrics.
   - **Manual Machine Learning**:
     - **Modelling (Using Notebook)**: Alternatively, data can be processed through manual machine learning, where custom models are developed and trained using notebooks.

3. **Data Integration and Storage**:
   - **XX_Gold_LK Tables**: The output from both AutoML and manual machine learning processes is stored in XX_Gold_LK Tables, representing refined and processed data ready for further analysis or reporting.
   - **Identity_SM**: This component likely handles identity management or security aspects related to data access and integration.

4. **Data Visualization and Reporting**:
   - **Power BI**: The XX_Gold_LK Tables are connected to Power BI via OneLake, enabling visualization and reporting of the processed data for business intelligence purposes.

The workflow demonstrates a comprehensive approach to data processing, machine learning, and visualization within an Azure-based architecture, emphasizing automation, flexibility, and integration.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI solution design, including project objectives, scope, document purpose, and intended audience. ## 2.1 Project Overview The primary objective of this project is to design and implement a modern data workflow for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The project scope encompasses the establishment of a Fabric workspace, the development of an end-to-end ETL pipeline, the execution of machine learning processes, and the integration of Power BI for advanced analytics and business intelligence. The solution will utilize Microsoft Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Fabric Data Science for machine learning applications. This initiative aims to align UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s unified analytics capabilities, supporting UMS’s business and academic objectives. ## 2.2 Document Purpose The purpose of this document is to serve as the formal solution design for the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI implementation at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). It details the architectural approach, technology selections, workflow designs, and security considerations to ensure a robust, scalable, and secure analytics platform. This document will guide both implementation and governance, providing a definitive reference for all stakeholders. ## 2.3 Document Audience This solution design document is intended for the following audiences: - UMS IT team - UMS analytics and data science teams - Enfrasys Solutions architects and implementation specialists - UMS project sponsors and executive stakeholders Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for preparing, maintaining, and reviewing the technical content of this document. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) stakeholders are responsible for reviewing and providing feedback on requirements, business alignment, and operational readiness. # 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview This section provides a formal overview of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, including their core services and integration, as applied to Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data and analytics solution. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for delivering these technology overviews. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, engineering, science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It provides a suite of services that enable organizations to ingest, transform, analyze, and visualize data within a single, secure environment. The primary components of Microsoft Fabric relevant to the UMS solution are as follows: | ID | Description | Workload Type | |----|------------------------------------------------|----------------------| | 1 | Data Factory: Data integration and orchestration, enabling ingestion from diverse sources and transformation workflows. | Data Integration | | 2 | Synapse: Advanced analytics and big data processing, supporting large-scale data exploration and transformation. | Data Analytics | | 3 | Data Science: Machine learning and AI capabilities, supporting both automated (AutoML) and manual modeling processes. | Machine Learning | | 4 | OneLake: Unified, scalable data lake storage for seamless data access and management across all Fabric workloads. | Data Storage | Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall utilize Microsoft Fabric to design and operate the end-to-end data workflow, from ingestion through transformation to advanced analytics and machine learning. ## 3.2 Power BI Power BI is Microsoft’s business analytics service that enables users to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decisions. Power BI seamlessly integrates with Microsoft Fabric, allowing direct connectivity to data stored in OneLake and processed through Fabric’s data pipelines. This integration ensures that business users can access up-to-date, curated data for reporting and dashboarding without manual data movement. | ID | Description | Workload Type | |----|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------| | 1 | Power BI: Interactive data visualization and reporting, natively integrated with Fabric and OneLake. | Business Intelligence | Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall implement Power BI for business-aligned analytics, leveraging the unified data foundation established within Microsoft Fabric. ## 3.3 Application to UMS Solution The UMS solution leverages Microsoft Fabric and Power BI to deliver a comprehensive data and analytics workflow: - Data is ingested from the UMS Staging Area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) via Fabric Data Factory. - Data is processed through multiple layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold) for refinement and transformation using Fabric Synapse and Data Factory. - Machine learning processes, including AutoML and manual modeling, are executed within the Data Science component, with results stored in Gold tables. - OneLake provides unified storage and seamless data access across all stages. - Power BI connects directly to the Gold tables in OneLake to deliver interactive dashboards and reports for UMS stakeholders. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for architecting and documenting the end-to-end solution, ensuring alignment with Microsoft best practices. ![](images\slide_009_img_003.png) Figure 1: UMS Data Workflow Architecture in Microsoft Fabric. ![](images\slide_021_img_005.png) Figure 2: UMS AutoML and Machine Learning Workflow in Microsoft Fabric. # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the network architecture and technical decisions for secure data connectivity between Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It enables organizations to connect, process, and analyze data from various sources, both on-premises and in the cloud, within a single, secure environment. Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data flow architecture is designed to securely transfer data from the on-premises SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse (UMS Staging Area) to Microsoft Fabric using the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, facilitating outbound connectivity from the internal network to Microsoft Fabric without requiring inbound firewall ports, thereby minimizing security risks. Data flows from the UMS Staging Area through the OPDG, which then securely relays the data to Microsoft Fabric for further analytics and processing. ![](images\slide_011_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data flow from UMS on-premises SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via On-Premises Data Gateway. ## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft component that enables secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services, such as Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Power Apps, and Azure Logic Apps. The gateway is installed on a dedicated virtual machine within the client’s secure network perimeter, ensuring that data remains protected during transit and that no inbound firewall ports are required. Enfrasys Solutions recommends deploying the OPDG on a dedicated VM that meets or exceeds the following specifications to ensure reliability and performance: ### VM Specification Table | Component | Specification | |------------------|------------------------------------------------| | Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) | | .NET Framework | Version 4.8 | | vCPU | 8 cores | | RAM | Minimum 8 GB | ### Deployment Responsibilities Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for: - Providing deployment guidance and best practices for the OPDG. - Assisting with initial configuration and integration with Microsoft Fabric. - Validating network connectivity and performing gateway health checks. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall be responsible for: - Provisioning the required VM according to the specifications above. - Coordinating with internal IT to ensure outbound connectivity to Microsoft Fabric endpoints. - Installing the OPDG software and managing the VM lifecycle, including patching and monitoring. ### Task/Migration Rollout Table | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|--------| | VM Provisioning | Allocate and prepare VM according to specification | Universiti Malaysia Sabah| | | Network Configuration | Ensure outbound connectivity to Microsoft Fabric | Universiti Malaysia Sabah| | | OPDG Software Installation | Install and configure On-Premises Data Gateway | Universiti Malaysia Sabah| | | Deployment Guidance | Provide deployment and configuration guidance | Enfrasys Solutions | | | Integration & Validation | Test connectivity and validate data flow | Enfrasys Solutions | | ## 4.3 Design Considerations | ID | Description | Workload Type | |----|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------| | 1 | Secure, outbound-only connectivity from on-premises to Microsoft Fabric | Data Integration | | 2 | Dedicated VM for OPDG to ensure performance and isolation | Infrastructure | | 3 | Compliance with Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s security and IT governance | Security | ## 4.4 Design Decisions | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |-----|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------| | 1 | Use On-Premises Data Gateway for secure data transfer | Approved | | 2 | Deploy OPDG on dedicated VM with specified resources | Approved | | 3 | Outbound-only network configuration to minimize security exposure | Approved | # 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric & Power BI This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and recommended role mappings for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. ## 5.1 Microsoft Fabric Administrator Role Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data integration, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence on a single SaaS foundation. The Microsoft Fabric Administrator role is a privileged role with full control over the Fabric environment, responsible for governance, configuration, and oversight of all Fabric resources. Administrators have the following capabilities: | Capability | Description | |------------|-------------| | Environment Management | Configure and manage Fabric capacities, settings, and integrations. | | Security Oversight | Assign roles, manage access, and enforce security policies. | | Resource Provisioning | Provision, monitor, and decommission Fabric workspaces and artifacts. | | Audit & Compliance | Review logs, monitor usage, and ensure compliance with organizational policies. | Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the Fabric administrator role structure. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall assign and approve personnel to the administrator role based on organizational requirements. ## 5.2 Microsoft Fabric-native Roles Microsoft Fabric and Power BI provide several native roles to support data lifecycle and analytics operations. These roles are defined as follows: | Permission | Admin | Contributor | Member | Viewer | |------------|-------|-------------|--------|--------| | Manage workspace | ✔️ | | | | | Add/remove users | ✔️ | | | | | Publish content | ✔️ | ✔️ | | | | Edit content | ✔️ | ✔️ | | | | View content | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | | Share content | ✔️ | ✔️ | ✔️ | | | Schedule refresh | ✔️ | ✔️ | | | | Delete workspace | ✔️ | | | | Key native roles in Microsoft Fabric include: - **Fabric Admin**: Full control over all aspects of the workspace and its resources. - **Data Engineer**: Responsible for data integration, transformation, and pipeline management. - **Business User Admin**: Manages business user access and workspace-level permissions. - **Data Analyst**: Consumes, analyzes, and visualizes data within workspaces. - **Stakeholder/Project Director**: Views reports and dashboards, provides strategic guidance. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) assign these roles according to personnel responsibilities and operational needs. ## 5.3 UMS Workspace Role and Access Mapping The following table presents the recommended mapping of workspace roles to UMS personnel. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the design of this mapping. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is responsible for the assignment and approval of all workspace roles to ensure alignment with internal policies and operational requirements. # 6.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Design and Decision This section outlines the architecture, workflow, access, and governance design for Microsoft Fabric and Power BI in the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) environment. ## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence on a single SaaS foundation. Power BI is a business analytics solution that enables interactive visualizations and business intelligence capabilities with an interface simple enough for end users to create their own reports and dashboards. The following table summarizes the design considerations for the data workflow, from ingestion to visualization: | ID | Description | Workload Type | |------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------| | DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server. | Data Factory | | DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server. | Data Engineering | | DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse. | Data Engineering | | DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse. | Data Engineering | | DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering | | DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory | | DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science | | DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse. | Power BI | | DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization. | Power BI | ![](images\slide_009_img_003.png) Figure 1: Data workflow architecture from ingestion to visualization. ## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following design decisions for each stage of the data workflow for Universiti Malaysia Sabah: | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | DD01 | Data ingestion will be performed using Azure Data Factory pipelines. | Adopt Data Factory for scheduled and orchestrated data ingestion. | | DD02 | Lakehouse architecture will be implemented using Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers for data refinement and governance.| Structure Lakehouse into three layers for traceability and data quality. | | DD03 | Data cleansing/transformation will utilize Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query. | Use Dataflow Gen2 and Notebooks for robust ETL and transformation processes. | | DD04 | Machine learning workflows will leverage both AutoML and manual ML in Fabric Notebooks. | Enable both AutoML for rapid prototyping and Notebooks for advanced modeling. | | DD05 | Model outputs and scoring results will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Centralize all ML results in Gold Lakehouse for consistency and reporting. | | DD06 | The Semantic Model will be built on top of the Gold Lakehouse. | Ensure all business logic and data models are standardized in the Semantic Model. | | DD07 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for visualization. | Use OneLake Direct Lake connectivity for seamless Power BI reporting. | ![](images\slide_021_img_005.png) Figure 2: AutoML and manual ML workflow integration with data layers. ## 6.3 Access Design Considerations and Decisions ### 6.3.1 Conditional Access Microsoft Entra Conditional Access is a policy-based approach to enforce access controls for applications based on user, location, device, and risk signals. | ID | Description | Status/Decision | |------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------| | CA01 | UMS account is not eligible for Conditional Access (CA) due to licensing limitations. | Not implemented (future consideration) | | CA02 | Conditional Access policies for Power BI, Azure Data Explorer, SQL DB, and Storage (future). | Deferred—pending license upgrade | | CA03 | MFA enforced at the tenant level for all UMS users. | Enforced | | CA04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric environment under current MFA policy. | Enabled | ![](images\slide_006_img_002.png) Figure 3: Conditional Access and authentication flow for Microsoft Fabric. ### 6.3.2 Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) | ID | Description | Status/Decision | |------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------| | MFA1 | Enforce MFA for all UMS users accessing Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. | Implemented at tenant level | | MFA2 | Review MFA prompts to minimize user disruption. | Ongoing | ### 6.3.3 Workspace Permissions | ID | Description | Status/Decision | |------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------| | WP01 | Assign workspace roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer) based on least privilege. | To be operationalized by UMS | | WP02 | Enfrasys to provide initial role mapping and guidance. | Completed | ## This structure supports governance, policy enforcement, and cost management. The top-level group represents the UMS tenant, with child management groups for environments (e.g., Production, Development, Staging) and further subgroups for workloads such as Fabric, Power BI, and Data Science. ### 6.5.2 Naming and Tagging Consistent naming conventions facilitate resource management, automation, and cost tracking. The following tables define the naming standards for Azure and Fabric resources. #### Azure Naming Convention | Resource | Abbreviation | Example | |-------------------|--------------|-----------------------| | Resource Group | rg | ums-prod-fabric-rg | | Storage Account | st | umsprodst01 | | Virtual Machine | vm | ums-dev-opdg-vm01 | | Data Factory | df | ums-stg-df01 | #### Fabric Naming Convention | No. | Item in Fabric | Naming -- | |-----|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Fabric Capacity | stagingareadevcapacity01 | | 2 | Workspace | StudentAffairs_dev_WS | | 3 | Lakehouse | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK

6.A Microsoft Fabric and Power BI Reference ### Introduction/Prerequisites Microsoft Fabric overview: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/) Power BI documentation: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/) ### Limits and Boundaries Microsoft Fabric limits: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/data-limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/data-limits) Power BI service limits: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/enterprise/service-limits-quotas-capacity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/enterprise/service-limits-quotas-capacity) ### Others Microsoft Fabric best practices: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/get-started/fabric-best-practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/get-started/fabric-best-practices) Power BI security: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/enterprise/service-security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/enterprise/service-security) Azure Data Factory documentation: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/introduction](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/introduction) # 7.0 Security Design and Decision This section outlines the security architecture and operational controls for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) deployment. ## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a core Azure security feature that enables the filtering of network traffic to and from Azure resources in an Azure virtual network. NSGs contain security rules that allow or deny inbound and outbound traffic, based on source or destination IP address, port, and protocol. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah implement the following NSG outbound rules for the OPDG VM to ensure secure, compliant connectivity to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft cloud services. ### OPDG VM Outbound NSG Rules | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow | Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the design and implementation of the above NSG rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall monitor ongoing compliance with the defined security policies. ## 7.2 Encryption Design ### Microsoft Fabric Encryption Microsoft Fabric is a unified, end-to-end analytics platform that brings together data integration, engineering, and business intelligence. All data at rest in Microsoft Fabric is encrypted using Microsoft-managed keys, leveraging Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) with AES-256. Data in transit is protected using TLS 1.2 or higher. ### Power BI Encryption Power BI is a business analytics service that enables interactive visualizations and business intelligence capabilities. Power BI encrypts data at rest using Microsoft-managed keys and supports customer-managed keys (CMK) for Premium capacities. Data in transit between clients and the Power BI service is secured using TLS encryption. ### On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) Encryption The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services. OPDG encrypts all data in transit using HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or higher). No data is stored at rest on the gateway unless explicitly configured for diagnostics or logging, which should also leverage disk encryption. Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the security architecture, including the selection and configuration of encryption mechanisms for all components. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall be responsible for monitoring compliance with encryption policies and for maintaining any required audit documentation. ## 7.3 Security Task Assignment | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|--------| | NSG Rule Implementation | Design and apply outbound NSG rules to OPDG VM according to specifications | Enfrasys Solutions | | | Encryption Policy Review | Review and confirm encryption at rest and in transit for Fabric, Power BI, and OPDG | Enfrasys Solutions | | | Compliance Monitoring | Ongoing monitoring of security controls and compliance with UMS policies | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | | | Security Documentation | Maintain evidence of encryption and network security compliance | Universiti Malaysia Sabah | | ## 7.4 Security Architecture Diagram ![](diagrams/security-nsg-opdg.png) Figure 7.1: OPDG NSG and security data flow. # 7.5 Security Design Decisions | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |-----|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Outbound NSG rules for OPDG VM | Allow HTTPS and authentication endpoints as per Microsoft requirements | | 2 | Encryption at rest and in transit | Enforce Microsoft-managed encryption for all data at rest and TLS for all data in transit| | 3 | Responsibility assignment | Enfrasys Solutions: Security design; The diagram illustrates a technical architecture involving Azure components and user access management. 

1. **Fabric-RG**: This represents a Resource Group in Azure, which is a container that holds related resources for an Azure solution. It is depicted with an icon suggesting a fabric or mesh, indicating a structured environment for resource management.

2. **UMS Fabric**: This component likely refers to a User Management System within the Azure Fabric, responsible for handling user identities, roles, and permissions. It is part of the Fabric-RG, suggesting it is a resource managed within this group.

3. **Conditional Access**: This is a security feature in Azure Active Directory that controls access to resources based on specific conditions. It is represented by a shield with a lock, indicating its role in securing access.

4. **External User**: This component represents users outside the organization who need access to resources within the Azure environment. The diagram shows a connection from the UMS Fabric to the External User, indicating that user access is managed through the UMS Fabric and governed by Conditional Access policies.

The data flow suggests that external users request access to resources managed within the Fabric-RG. Their access is controlled by Conditional Access policies, ensuring that only authorized users can interact with the UMS Fabric resources. This setup enhances security by applying specific access conditions and managing user identities effectively.

The diagram illustrates the authentication and access control process for Microsoft Fabric using Entra conditional access policies.

1. **User Authentication Attempt**: The process begins with a user attempting to authenticate to Microsoft Fabric.

2. **Entra Conditional Access Policies**: The authentication request is evaluated against Entra conditional access policies.

3. **Signal Collection**: Signals are gathered, including examples such as users and groups, and network location. These signals provide context for the access request.

4. **Decision Making**: Based on the collected signals, a decision is made regarding the access request. This involves evaluating the conditions set in the access policies.

5. **Enforcement**: The decision leads to enforcement actions, which determine whether access is granted or denied based on the policy evaluation.

6. **Microsoft Fabric Access**: If access is granted, the user can interact with Microsoft Fabric, which includes various components such as data analytics, storage, and processing tools. OneLake is highlighted as part of the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.

The diagram effectively outlines the flow from user authentication attempts to policy evaluation and enforcement, ensuring secure access to Microsoft Fabric resources.

The diagram represents a data processing and analytics architecture within the UMS Fabric environment. It illustrates the flow of data from ingestion to visualization using various Azure components.

2. **On-Premise Data Gateway (OPDG)**: This gateway facilitates secure data transfer between the on-premise data warehouse and external systems. It acts as a bridge, allowing data to flow out securely without requiring inbound ports, enhancing security by minimizing exposure to external threats.

3. **UMS Fabric**: This component is likely a cloud-based service or platform that receives data from the on-premise data warehouse via the OPDG. The UMS Fabric could be used for further data processing, analytics, or integration with other cloud services.

4. **Data Visualization and Reporting**:

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.

# 3.0 Microsoft Power BI & Fabric Overview

This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, detailing their roles and integration within the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data analytics solution.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. It unifies data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single, seamless environment. Microsoft Fabric includes core components such as Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, Data Science for machine learning, and OneLake as a unified data lake for storage and management. Fabric’s architecture is designed to accelerate data-driven decision-making by enabling organizations to ingest, transform, analyze, and visualize data at scale.

In the context of Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Microsoft Fabric serves as the foundation for the end-to-end data workflow. Data is ingested from the UMS Staging Area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) using Fabric Data Factory, processed through bronze, silver, and gold lakehouse layers, and analyzed using Data Science and Synapse components. OneLake provides unified storage, ensuring seamless integration between data sources, transformation processes, and analytics outputs.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for enabling and configuring Microsoft Fabric services, establishing the Fabric workspace, and ensuring the platform components are operational. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for user adoption, including data stewardship, business process alignment, and ongoing usage of the Fabric environment.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s business analytics service that enables users to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decisions through interactive reports and dashboards. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, allowing users to connect directly to data stored in OneLake, build semantic models, and leverage advanced analytics capabilities. Power BI supports both self-service and enterprise BI scenarios, providing robust data modeling, visualization, and collaboration features.

Within the UMS solution, Power BI is used to connect to the Semantic Model built on top of the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake. This integration enables analysts and stakeholders at Universiti Malaysia Sabah to visualize refined data, perform ad-hoc analysis, and publish business-aligned reports. The seamless connection between Power BI and Fabric ensures data consistency, security, and real-time access to analytics outputs.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for enabling Power BI integration within the Fabric workspace, configuring data connectivity, and supporting semantic model development. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for user adoption, report creation, and embedding Power BI into business processes.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture and connectivity decisions supporting Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment, with a focus on secure integration between on-premises resources and cloud services.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Microsoft Fabric solution requires secure, reliable connectivity between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric cloud services. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid network topology utilizing the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) to bridge internal SQL data warehouses with Microsoft Fabric, ensuring compliance with Azure networking best practices and minimizing exposure to external threats.

The OPDG is deployed within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) on UMS’s internal network. All outbound connections to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services are secured via HTTPS, with no inbound ports required. This approach leverages Azure outbound security rules to enforce controlled, auditable access.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

This section details the security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment, focusing on network security groups (NSGs) and encryption.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a core Azure security feature that enables administrators to control inbound and outbound network traffic to Azure resources. NSGs use rules to allow or deny traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol, ensuring granular network segmentation and protection.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the configuration and deployment of all NSG rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall be responsible for ongoing compliance monitoring and audit of network security controls.

### Inbound NSG Rules

No inbound rules are required for the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM in this scenario, as all communication is initiated outbound to Microsoft services. The default Azure NSG configuration, which denies unsolicited inbound traffic, shall be maintained.

### Outbound NSG Rules

The following outbound NSG rules are required to ensure secure connectivity for the OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services:

| Allow_OPDG_Authentication  | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                                                                                                              | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160    | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

UMS shall ensure that no additional outbound traffic is permitted except as defined above, in alignment with Azure security best practices.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a fundamental security requirement for protecting data at rest and in transit within Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and all associated data flows.

### Encryption at Rest

All data stored within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys by default, leveraging Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) with AES-256. This ensures that all datasets, reports, and intermediate storage are protected against unauthorized access at the storage layer.

### Encryption in Transit

All communications between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID are encrypted in transit using SSL/TLS (HTTPS). This includes:

- Outbound data transfers from the OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
- Authentication and token exchanges with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory).
- Connectivity checks and service status communications with Microsoft endpoints.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS enforce the use of HTTPS for all client-to-service and service-to-service communications and regularly review SSL/TLS cipher suites to ensure compliance with current security standards.

## 7.3 Security Best Practices

Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following security best practices for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment:

- Implement least privilege access for all administrative and user roles.
- Regularly review and update NSG rules to minimize the attack surface.
- Enable Azure Security Center and configure security alerts for anomalous activities.
- Perform periodic compliance audits and penetration testing.
- Ensure all VMs and services are patched and updated according to Microsoft’s security advisories.
- Maintain a comprehensive incident response plan.

1. **User Authentication Attempt**: The process begins with a user attempting to authenticate to Microsoft Fabric.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI & Microsoft Fabric solution design, including project context, document intent, and target audience. ## 2.1 Project Overview The Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI & Fabric project is initiated to modernize and streamline UMS’s data workflow, spanning data ingestion, transformation, advanced analytics, and visualization. The project scope encompasses the design and implementation of an end-to-end data pipeline leveraging Microsoft Fabric’s integrated services. Key objectives include: - Establishing a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace for UMS. - Designing and deploying an end-to-end ETL pipeline for data integration and orchestration using Fabric Data Factory. - Enabling advanced analytics and big data processing through Fabric Synapse. - Implementing machine learning processes within the Fabric Data Science environment. - Integrating Power BI for business-aligned analytics and visualization to support UMS’s strategic decision-making. This initiative aligns UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s latest capabilities, ensuring scalable, secure, and future-ready data infrastructure. ## 2.2 Document Purpose The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to formalize the architecture, design decisions, and implementation approach for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Power BI and Microsoft Fabric deployment. This document serves as the authoritative reference for all stakeholders, ensuring clarity, alignment, and traceability throughout the project lifecycle. It details the technical and operational blueprint for the proposed solution, and will be used to guide implementation, validate requirements, and facilitate review and sign-off by both Enfrasys Solutions and UMS. ## 2.3 Document Audience This document is intended for the following audiences: - UMS IT Department: Responsible for technical review, implementation support, and ongoing operations. - UMS Data Analytics Team: Key stakeholders for data workflow, analytics requirements, and validation of business outcomes. - Enfrasys Solutions Project Team: Accountable for solution design, implementation, and project delivery. - UMS Project Stakeholders: Senior management and decision-makers overseeing project objectives and outcomes. Both Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah are responsible for jointly reviewing and formally signing off on this Solution Design Document to ensure mutual understanding and agreement on the proposed approach. # 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, detailing their roles and integration within the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data analytics solution. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. Fabric consolidates multiple data services into a single SaaS platform, enabling organizations to manage their entire analytics workflow with a unified experience and security model. Core services of Microsoft Fabric include: - **Data Factory**: Provides data integration and orchestration capabilities, allowing organizations to ingest, prepare, and transform data from various sources at scale. - **Synapse**: Delivers advanced data analytics and big data processing, supporting complex data transformations, warehousing, and real-time analytics workloads. - **Data Science**: Facilitates machine learning and advanced analytics, supporting both automated (AutoML) and manual model development workflows. - **OneLake**: Acts as a unified data lake, enabling seamless data access, storage, and management across all Fabric services. In the UMS solution, Microsoft Fabric orchestrates the end-to-end data workflow—from ingestion in the UMS Staging Area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse), through transformation and enrichment in Bronze, Silver, and Gold tables, to advanced analytics and machine learning, culminating in business intelligence reporting. ![](images\slide_009_img_003.png) Figure 1: End-to-end data workflow architecture in Microsoft Fabric for UMS. ## 3.2 Power BI Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization platform. It enables users to connect to a wide range of data sources, build interactive reports and dashboards, and share insights securely across the organization. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, leveraging OneLake as its unified data foundation. This integration allows UMS to seamlessly visualize and analyze refined data from the Gold layer, ensuring that business users and decision-makers have access to timely, accurate, and actionable analytics. Within the UMS solution, Power BI serves as the primary interface for business-aligned analytics and reporting, enabling data-driven decision-making across departments. ![](images\slide_021_img_005.png) Figure 2: Machine learning workflow integration with Power BI for data visualization. ## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and access control for users, applications, and resources within the Microsoft ecosystem. In the UMS solution, Microsoft Entra ID governs identity and access management for all Fabric and Power BI resources. This ensures that only authorized UMS personnel can access sensitive data, manage analytics assets, and administer the environment, in line with organizational security and compliance requirements. ## 3.4 Responsibility Assignment The following table outlines the responsibility assignment for drafting and reviewing this section: | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |---------------------|----------------------------------------------|----------------------|----------| | Content Drafting | Develop content for Fabric, Power BI, Entra ID overview | Enfrasys Solutions | Complete | | Content Review | Review and validate section content | UMS | Pending | # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the network connectivity, gateway architecture, and security controls for integrating Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) on-premises data sources with Microsoft Fabric. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that enables organizations to manage, analyze, and visualize data across hybrid environments. It integrates with on-premises data sources via secure gateways, ensuring seamless and secure data transfer between local infrastructure and cloud services. For UMS, the network design establishes secure connectivity between the on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (Data Warehouse), the Data Gateway Virtual Machine (VM), and Microsoft Fabric. The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) acts as the bridge, facilitating outbound-only, encrypted communication to Microsoft Fabric without exposing the internal network to inbound connections. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and documenting the network architecture. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall provide comprehensive on-premises network details, including firewall configurations, IP address ranges, and existing connectivity constraints. ![](images\slide_011_img_004.png) Figure 1: Data flow from UMS SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via On-Premises Data Gateway. ## 4.2 Fabric Data Gateway (On-Premises Data Gateway) The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft component that enables secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Fabric, Power BI, and Azure Data Explorer. The gateway is installed on a dedicated VM within UMS’s network, providing a secure outbound channel for data synchronization and refresh operations. ### 4.2.1 OPDG Architecture - The OPDG VM is deployed within the UMS data center, connected to the local SQL Server instance. - All communication from the OPDG to Microsoft Fabric and related services is outbound over HTTPS (TCP 443), eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules. - The gateway handles authentication with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), ensuring secure identity validation and token management. - The architecture supports high availability and scalability by allowing multiple gateways to be clustered if required. ### 4.2.2 OPDG VM Specification | Component | Specification | |------------------|------------------------------------------------| | Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) | | .NET Framework | Version 4.8 | | vCPU | 8 cores | | RAM | Minimum 8 GB | ### 4.2.3 Network Security Group (NSG) Rules The following NSG rules are required to ensure the OPDG VM can securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID NSGs allow administrators to define security rules that permit or deny traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol, thereby safeguarding critical workloads from unauthorized access. Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing the following NSG rules for the Data Gateway VM to ensure secure connectivity to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for defining these controls, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall operationally enforce and monitor them. ### Data Gateway VM NSG Rules #### Outbound Rules | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |-----------------------------|----------|-----------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow | No inbound rules are defined for public access; all inbound access must be strictly controlled and monitored according to the operational policies set by UMS. ## 7.2 Encryption Design Encryption is essential to protect sensitive data both at rest and in transit across all data flows between SQL Server, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI. ### Encryption at Rest Microsoft Fabric and Power BI utilize Azure Storage infrastructure, which enforces encryption at rest using Azure-managed keys (default) or customer-managed keys (CMK) for advanced scenarios. Data stored in Azure SQL Database, OneLake, and Power BI datasets is encrypted using AES-256, meeting industry standards for data confidentiality. ### Encryption in Transit All data transmitted between SQL Server (on-premises or Azure-hosted), Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI is secured using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or higher. This ensures that data is protected from interception or tampering during transfer. The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM communicates with Microsoft cloud endpoints exclusively over HTTPS (TCP 443), as enforced by the NSG rules above. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for defining and validating all encryption controls. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall ensure operational enforcement, including certificate management and regular compliance reviews. ## 7.3 Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID feature that enables organizations to enforce access policies based on user, device, location, and risk. While UMS’s current licensing does not permit advanced Conditional Access policies, Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level to mitigate unauthorized access risks. 2. **UMS Fabric**: This component likely refers to a User Management System within the fabric architecture. It is responsible for handling user identities, permissions, and roles within the Azure environment.

3. **Conditional Access**: This is a security feature in Azure Active Directory that controls access to resources based on specific conditions. It ensures that only authenticated and authorized users can access certain resources, enhancing security by enforcing policies.

4. **External User**: Represents users outside the organization who need access to resources within the Azure environment. These users are subject to conditional access policies to ensure secure and compliant access.

**Data Flow and Connections**:

The diagram illustrates the authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric using Entra conditional access policies.

1. **User Authentication Attempt**: The process begins with a user attempting to authenticate to Microsoft Fabric.

2. **Entra Conditional Access Policies**: The authentication request is evaluated against Entra conditional access policies. This involves three key steps:
   - **Signal**: Various signals are gathered, such as user and group information, and network location.
   - **Decision**: Based on the signals, a decision is made regarding access permissions.
   - **Enforcement**: The decision is enforced, determining whether the user can proceed.

3. **Inbound Access to Microsoft Fabric**: Once access is granted, the user can interact with Microsoft Fabric, which includes various components and services such as data analytics, storage, and processing tools.

4. **OneLake Integration**: Microsoft Fabric integrates with OneLake, providing unified data storage and management capabilities.

This architecture ensures secure and conditional access to Microsoft Fabric, leveraging Entra policies to evaluate and enforce authentication requests.

The diagram represents a data processing and analytics architecture within the UMS Fabric environment, utilizing Azure services.
