6.C Microsoft Entra ID ### Introduction/Prerequisites Microsoft Entra ID Overview: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/active-directory-whatis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/fundamentals/active-directory-whatis) ### Limits and Boundaries Entra ID Licensing: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/licensing/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/licensing/) ### Others Conditional Access Documentation: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/conditional-access/overview) ## 6.D On-Premises Data Gateway ### Introduction/Prerequisites On-premises Data Gateway Documentation: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-install](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-install) ### Limits and Boundaries Gateway System Requirements: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-system-requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-system-requirements) ### Others Gateway Security and Architecture: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-security) # 7.0 Security Design and Decision This section defines the security architecture for the UMS Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment, focusing on network security groups (NSG) and encryption standards. ## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are security rules applied to Azure resources to control inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet or network interface level. NSGs enable granular control over network communication, allowing only authorized traffic to and from resources such as virtual machines. ### 7.1.1 Outbound NSG Rules for On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) The following outbound NSG rules are required to ensure secure communication between the OPDG VM and Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules comply with Azure networking best practices and ensure secure data transfer and authentication. | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow | Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the initial configuration and validation of these NSG rules. UMS shall be responsible for ongoing monitoring and periodic review to ensure compliance with organizational security policies. ## 7.2 Encryption Design Microsoft recommends that all data at rest and data in transit be protected using industry-standard encryption mechanisms to safeguard confidentiality and integrity. ### 7.2.1 Data at Rest Encryption Data stored within Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and associated Azure services is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys by default. This includes databases, storage accounts, and service data. UMS shall ensure that all resources leverage Azure’s built-in encryption features, and, where required, configure customer-managed keys for enhanced security. ### 7.2.2 Data in Transit Encryption All data transmitted between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services must use secure protocols such as HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or higher). The outbound NSG rules defined above enforce secure communication over TCP port 443, ensuring encryption in transit. Enfrasys Solutions shall perform the initial security configuration for data encryption. UMS shall be responsible for ongoing monitoring, key management (if customer-managed keys are adopted), and periodic compliance validation. # 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach This section outlines the phased deployment and migration strategy for UMS, assigning clear responsibilities to Enfrasys Solutions and UMS for each stage. ## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup Enfrasys Solutions recommends a structured pre-migration phase to ensure all foundational elements are in place before pilot and production activities commence. The following table details preparatory tasks, responsible parties, and current status. | No | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks | |----|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------|---------| | 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys / UMS | Not-Started | | | 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started | | | 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | | 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys / UMS | Not-Started | | UMS shall ensure timely review and sign-off of the design document. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the technical setup of the Fabric environment and the On-Premises Data Gateway, with UMS providing necessary access and server confirmations. ## 8.2 Pilot The pilot phase is designed to validate the migration approach, environment configuration, and data integration processes in a controlled setting before full-scale production rollout. - Enfrasys Solutions shall: - Provision and configure the pilot Fabric environment. - Coordinate with UMS to ingest a subset of data from the staging area database. - Install and test the On-Premises Data Gateway in collaboration with UMS. - Conduct initial data load and validate connectivity, data integrity, and security controls. - UMS shall: - Provide access to the staging area database and necessary infrastructure. - Participate in pilot validation and provide feedback on data accuracy and system behavior. Upon successful pilot completion, both parties shall review outcomes and sign off before proceeding to production rollout. ## 8.3 Production The production rollout will follow a formalized migration timeline to minimize risk and ensure business continuity. The timeline is structured as follows: - **D-7 (Pre-Cutover):** - Finalize production environment setup (Enfrasys Solutions). - Confirm data readiness and access (UMS). - Conduct user acceptance testing (UMS with Enfrasys support). - **D0 (Cutover):** - Execute production data migration (Enfrasys Solutions). - Switch over business processes to the new environment (UMS). - **D+1 (Post-Cutover):** - Monitor system health and data flows (Enfrasys Solutions). - Address initial issues and stabilize operations (Enfrasys Solutions). - Validate business process continuity (UMS). | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------| | 1 | Finalize production environment setup | Enfrasys | Pending | | 2 | Confirm data readiness and access | UMS | Pending | | 3 | User acceptance testing | UMS / Enfrasys | Pending | | 4 | Execute production data migration | Enfrasys | Pending | | 5 | Switch over business processes | UMS | Pending | | 6 | Monitor and stabilize post-migration | Enfrasys | Pending | | 7 | Validate business process continuity | UMS | Pending | All production activities shall be tracked and reported to both Enfrasys Solutions and UMS project stakeholders. ## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support Following migration, Enfrasys Solutions shall provide post-migration support, including system monitoring, issue resolution, and knowledge transfer to UMS administrators. - Enfrasys Solutions shall: - Monitor environment health and data flows for at least 7 days post-migration. - Provide incident response and troubleshooting for migration-related issues. - Conduct knowledge transfer and handover sessions for UMS IT personnel. - UMS shall: - Participate in handover sessions. - Assume responsibility for day-to-day operations and ongoing monitoring after the post-migration support window. This phased approach ensures a controlled, transparent migration with clear accountability and minimal disruption to UMS business operations. # 9.0 Appendix This appendix provides reference resources and section mapping for each major solution area. Responsibilities for implementation, configuration, and operational management are clarified between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS. ## 9.1 Appendix 1 Computing ### Introduction/Prerequisites Azure Compute Overview: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/) ### Limits and Boundaries Azure VM Size Limits: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes) ### Others Azure Compute SLA: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sla](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sla) ## The diagram represents a technical architecture focused on user access management within an Azure environment. 

**Components:**

1. **Fabric-RG (Resource Group):**
   - Represents a logical container in Azure that holds related resources for an Azure solution. It is used to manage and organize resources like UMS Fabric.

2. **UMS Fabric:**
   - Likely a service or application within the Fabric-RG, possibly related to user management or a specific application fabric that handles user interactions and data processing.

3. **Conditional Access:**
   - A security feature that controls access to resources based on specific conditions. It ensures that only authenticated and authorized users can access the UMS Fabric.

4. **External User:**
   - Represents users outside the organization who need access to the UMS Fabric. These users are subject to conditional access policies.

**Data Flow and Connections:**

- The diagram shows a direct connection from the UMS Fabric to the External User, indicating that external users interact with the UMS Fabric.
- Conditional Access acts as a gatekeeper, ensuring that external users meet specific security requirements before accessing the UMS Fabric.
- The flow suggests that once conditional access requirements are satisfied, external users can interact with the resources within the Fabric-RG, specifically the UMS Fabric.

This setup is designed to secure access to Azure resources, ensuring that only verified external users can interact with the system, thereby protecting sensitive data and applications.

The image is a technical architecture diagram.

1. **User Authentication Attempt**: The process begins with a user attempting authentication to Microsoft Fabric.

2. **Entra Conditional Access Policies**: This component evaluates the authentication attempt using conditional access policies. It consists of three sub-components:
   - **Signal**: Collects signals such as user and group information, and network location.
   - **Decision**: Based on the signals, a decision is made regarding access.
   - **Enforcement**: Implements the decision, allowing or denying access based on the policy evaluation.

3. **Inbound to Microsoft Fabric**: If access is granted, the user is allowed inbound access to Microsoft Fabric.

4. **Microsoft Fabric**: This component represents the suite of services and tools within Microsoft Fabric, including various icons that likely represent different functionalities or applications within the platform.

5. **OneLake**: This is a specific component or service within Microsoft Fabric, possibly related to data storage or management.

The diagram illustrates the flow of authentication and access control, emphasizing the role of conditional access policies in securing access to Microsoft Fabric services.

The diagram represents a data processing and analytics workflow within the UMS Fabric environment, utilizing Azure services.

1. **UMS Staging Area**: Data originates from a Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, serving as the staging area for initial data collection.

2. **Data Factory**: The data is ingested into the system using Azure Data Factory, which orchestrates the movement and transformation of data.

3. **XX_Bronze_LK Tables**: The ingested data is first stored in Bronze tables, which typically contain raw, unprocessed data.

4. **XX_Silver_LK Tables**: Data is then transformed and refined into Silver tables, where it is cleaned and enriched for further analysis.

5. **Data Science**: Advanced analytics and machine learning processes are applied to the Silver data using Azure Data Science tools, enhancing data insights.

6. **XX_Gold_LK Tables**: The processed data is stored in Gold tables, representing the final, highly curated dataset ready for business intelligence applications.

7. **Identity_SM**: This component likely handles identity management and security, ensuring data access is controlled and secure.

8. **OneLake**: The data is integrated with OneLake, facilitating seamless data storage and access across the Azure ecosystem.

9. **Power BI**: The final data is connected to Power BI via OneLake, enabling visualization and reporting for end-users.

The workflow demonstrates a structured approach to data management, from ingestion to analytics, leveraging Azure's capabilities for efficient data processing and business intelligence.

The diagram illustrates a data flow architecture involving three main components:

1. **UMS Staging Area - Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse**: This component represents the on-premises data storage system where data is initially staged. It is likely used for storing and processing large volumes of data before it is transferred to other systems.

2. **On-Premise Data Gateway (OPDG)**: This gateway facilitates secure data transfer between the on-premises data warehouse and external systems. It enables outbound connections without requiring inbound ports, ensuring security and compliance. The gateway acts as a bridge, allowing data to flow securely from the SQL Server to external services.

3. **UMS Fabric**: This component represents the external system or service that receives data from the on-premises data warehouse via the OPDG. The UMS Fabric likely provides additional processing, analytics, or integration capabilities, leveraging the data received from the warehouse.

The data flow begins at the UMS Staging Area, where data is stored and processed. It is then securely transmitted through the On-Premise Data Gateway, which ensures that the connection is outbound and secure, eliminating the need for inbound ports. Finally, the data reaches the UMS Fabric, where it can be further utilized for various purposes such as analytics, reporting, or integration with other systems.

The diagram represents a data processing and machine learning workflow within an Azure environment, specifically utilizing UMS Fabric and OneLake for data management and integration.

1. **Data Source**: 
   - **XX_Silver_LK Tables**: These tables serve as the initial data source, likely containing pre-processed or intermediate data ready for machine learning experiments.

2. **Machine Learning Processes**:
   - **AutoML**: 
     - **AutoML Experiment**: Data from XX_Silver_LK Tables is fed into an automated machine learning experiment. This process involves using Azure's AutoML capabilities to automatically select the best model and hyperparameters for the given dataset.
     - **Result Scoring (Using Notebook)**: The results from the AutoML experiment are scored using a notebook, which likely involves evaluating the model's performance metrics and validating its predictions.
   - **Manual Machine Learning**:
     - **Modelling (Using Notebook)**: Alternatively, data from XX_Silver_LK Tables can be used for manual machine learning modeling. This involves custom model development and training using notebooks, allowing for more control over the machine learning process.

3. **Data Storage and Integration**:
   - **XX_Gold_LK Tables**: The output from both AutoML and manual machine learning processes is stored in XX_Gold_LK Tables. These tables represent a refined and finalized dataset, ready for further analysis or reporting.
   - **Identity_SM**: This component likely represents a service or module responsible for managing identities or metadata associated with the data in XX_Gold_LK Tables.

4. **Data Visualization and Reporting**:
   - **Power BI**: The data stored in XX_Gold_LK Tables is connected to Power BI via OneLake, enabling visualization and reporting. This connection allows stakeholders to create dashboards and reports to gain insights from the processed data.

Overall, the diagram illustrates a comprehensive workflow for data processing, machine learning, and reporting within an Azure environment, leveraging automated and manual machine learning techniques, data storage solutions, and visualization tools.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides an overview of the project, the intent of this Solution Design Document, and identifies the key audience and responsibilities for review and sign-off.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) seeks to modernize its data platform by adopting Microsoft Fabric. The project is scoped to design and implement an end-to-end data workflow, encompassing data ingestion, transformation, and visualization. Key objectives include establishing a Microsoft Fabric workspace, developing a robust ETL pipeline, enabling machine learning processes, and integrating Power BI for advanced business analytics. The solution will leverage Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science capabilities for machine learning applications.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

This Solution Design Document serves as the authoritative reference for the technical and architectural decisions underpinning the Microsoft Fabric implementation at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The document is intended to ensure alignment with UMS’s business requirements, support effective adoption of Microsoft Fabric services, and provide a clear framework for implementation, governance, and ongoing operations. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for preparing the Solution Design Document, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for reviewing and providing formal sign-off to confirm alignment with business objectives.

## 2.3 Document Audience

The primary audience for this document includes:
- Universiti Malaysia Sabah IT department (technical leads, system administrators)
- UMS business stakeholders (data owners, analytics leads)
- Enfrasys Solutions technical delivery team

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the preparation and technical accuracy of this document. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for internal review, validation of business requirements, and final approval prior to implementation.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview

This section provides an overview of the core Microsoft technologies forming the foundation of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) modern data and analytics platform. Enfrasys Solutions will provide technical guidance, while UMS shall supply business context and requirements.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data integration, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence on a single SaaS foundation. It brings together services such as Data Factory for data ingestion and orchestration, Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science for machine learning and AI workloads. Fabric centralizes data storage in OneLake, enabling seamless collaboration and data accessibility across the organization.

Within UMS, Microsoft Fabric will serve as the backbone for the end-to-end data workflow, from ingestion (via Data Factory) to transformation (using Synapse and Data Engineering capabilities), machine learning (Data Science), and ultimately, business reporting. This approach ensures that UMS’s data is securely ingested from the Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, processed through standardized bronze, silver, and gold layers, and made available for advanced analytics and reporting.

Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for architecting and configuring the Fabric workspace, data pipelines, and machine learning processes. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall define business requirements, data sources, and use cases to ensure alignment with institutional objectives.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s industry-leading business analytics solution, designed to visualize data, share insights across an organization, and embed them in applications or websites. Power BI seamlessly integrates with Microsoft Fabric, leveraging OneLake as a unified data source and connecting directly to semantic models for real-time analytics.

In the UMS solution, Power BI will be used to connect to the Gold Lakehouse layer via OneLake, enabling the creation of interactive dashboards and reports that reflect the latest, business-ready data. This empowers UMS stakeholders with timely, data-driven insights for decision-making. Power BI Desktop will be the primary tool for report development, while Power BI Service will facilitate sharing and collaboration.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide guidance on Power BI integration, workspace setup, and best practices. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall identify key business metrics, reporting requirements, and stakeholders.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and role-based access control for users, applications, and resources within the Microsoft ecosystem, including Fabric and Power BI.

For UMS, Entra ID will ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive data and analytics assets within the Fabric workspace and Power BI environment. Integration with Entra ID allows for centralized identity management, auditability, and compliance with institutional security policies.

Enfrasys Solutions will design and implement Entra ID integration, including role assignments and access policies. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall provide user lists, role definitions, and access requirements.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture and key design decisions for secure data connectivity between Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single SaaS solution. It enables organizations to connect, analyze, and visualize data from various sources, both on-premises and in the cloud.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid network architecture that securely bridges the on-premises SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse (UMS Staging Area) with Microsoft Fabric using the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). The OPDG will be deployed on a dedicated virtual machine within the UMS data center. This configuration ensures secure, outbound-only connectivity, eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules and reducing the attack surface.

## 4.2 Fabric Data Gateway

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft component that facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Fabric, Power BI, Power Apps, and Azure Logic Apps. The gateway enables organizations to keep their data sources on-premises while securely leveraging cloud-based analytics and integration capabilities.

Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the design, configuration, and deployment of the Data Gateway VM and its connectivity to Microsoft Fabric. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall provide access to the on-premises environment, including network, Active Directory, and SQL Server resources required for installation and ongoing operations.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

This section details the security architecture, network controls, and encryption strategy for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment.

## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a core component of Microsoft Azure’s network security model. NSGs allow administrators to define granular inbound and outbound network traffic rules for resources deployed within Azure Virtual Networks, thereby reducing the attack surface and enforcing least-privilege access.

### 7.1.1 Outbound NSG Rules

The following outbound rules are required to enable secure communication between the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine and Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and associated Microsoft cloud services.

| Name                        | Priority | Source                  | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net                                      | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                                                                             | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

### 7.1.2 Inbound NSG Rules

Inbound rules must be defined to restrict access to the OPDG VM, allowing only authorized management and monitoring connections. Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following default inbound security posture:

| Name             | Priority | Source         | Source Ports | Destination              | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|------------------|----------|----------------|--------------|--------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_RDP_Admin  | 100      | Admin IP Range | *            | VM Private IP Addresses  | 3389              | TCP      | Allow  |
| Deny_All_Inbound | 4000     | Any            | *            | VM Private IP Addresses  | *                 | Any      | Deny   |

Enfrasys Solutions shall define and implement all NSG rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall review and validate these rules for alignment with internal security policies and compliance requirements.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a foundational security control for all data processed and stored within Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and associated Azure resources.

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI employ encryption at rest and in transit by default, adhering to Microsoft’s security best practices:

- **Encryption at Rest:** All data stored in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI is encrypted using Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) with Microsoft-managed keys. For sensitive workloads, customer-managed keys (CMK) can be configured for enhanced control.
- **Encryption in Transit:** Data transmitted between clients, services, and the On-Premises Data Gateway is protected using TLS 1.2 or higher, ensuring confidentiality and integrity during network transfer.

Enfrasys Solutions shall define and configure all encryption controls in accordance with Microsoft’s best practices and Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s internal security requirements. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall validate the encryption configurations to ensure compliance with institutional data protection policies.

![](architecture/powerbi-fabric-secure-gateway.png)

Figure 7-1: Secure data flow and network segmentation for Power BI and Microsoft Fabric.

## 7.3 Security Design Decisions

| No. | Design Decision                                                                 | Decision                                                                                 |
|-----|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Outbound access from OPDG VM restricted to Microsoft service endpoints only      | Allow only required Microsoft domains and ports as per NSG rules                         |
| 2   | Inbound access limited to administrative IPs via RDP                            | Permit only authorized admin ranges; deny all other inbound traffic                      |
| 3   | Encryption enforced for data at rest and in transit                             | Use Azure SSE for data at rest; enforce TLS 1.2+ for all data in transit                 |
| 4   | Responsibility assignment for security controls and validation                  | Enfrasys Solutions to define/implement; UMS to validate and approve                     |

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section details the recommended deployment and migration methodology for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), including preparatory actions, pilot, production rollout, and post-migration support.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI solution design, document intent, and target audience.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is undertaking this project to modernize its data workflow and analytics capabilities by adopting Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The project scope encompasses the design and implementation of a comprehensive data workflow—from ingestion through transformation to visualization—leveraging Microsoft Fabric’s integrated services. Key objectives include establishing a Fabric workspace, developing an end-to-end ETL pipeline, conducting machine learning processes, and integrating Power BI for actionable business analytics. The solution will utilize Microsoft Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Fabric Data Science for machine learning applications. This initiative is aligned with UMS’s broader cloud adoption strategy and aims to deliver scalable, secure, and business-aligned data insights.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The Solution Design Document serves as the authoritative reference for the design, review, and implementation of the UMS Microsoft Fabric and Power BI solution. Its intent is to provide detailed architectural and workflow specifications, facilitate stakeholder review and sign-off, and guide the technical implementation. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for preparing this document, ensuring alignment with best practices and Microsoft recommendations, and supporting UMS throughout the review and implementation process. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is responsible for reviewing, providing feedback, and formally approving the design prior to commencement of deployment activities.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for the following audiences:
- UMS IT administrators and technical teams
- UMS business stakeholders and data owners
- Enfrasys Solutions consultants and project delivery team

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for leading project initiation, design, and technical implementation, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is responsible for stakeholder engagement, business requirements validation, and operational acceptance.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview

This section provides a formal overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID as foundational technologies for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) modern data platform.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) offering. Fabric’s core components include:

- **Data Factory**: Enables data integration and orchestration, supporting ingestion from diverse sources and transformation using pipelines and dataflows.
- **Synapse**: Delivers advanced analytics and big data processing, providing a unified workspace for data engineering, data warehousing, and real-time analytics.
- **Data Science**: Facilitates machine learning workflows, including AutoML and manual model development, supporting the entire model lifecycle from experimentation to deployment.
- **OneLake**: Acts as a unified, enterprise-grade data lake, centralizing storage for all data assets and enabling seamless integration across Fabric workloads.

For UMS, Microsoft Fabric provides the backbone for data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and analytics. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial setup and configuration of Fabric workspaces, pipelines, and security boundaries. UMS shall operate and maintain the day-to-day data workflows, model development, and analytic processes within the Fabric environment.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: End-to-end data pipeline architecture leveraging Microsoft Fabric components.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s business analytics service that empowers users to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decision-making. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, enabling direct connectivity to curated, business-ready data for reporting and dashboarding.

Key features include:

- **Semantic Model Integration**: Power BI connects to the Fabric Semantic Model, which is built upon data processed and stored in OneLake, ensuring a single source of truth for analytics.
- **Direct Lake Connectivity**: Power BI supports Direct Lake mode, allowing high-performance, real-time access to data in OneLake without the need for data duplication.
- **Comprehensive Visualization**: Power BI Desktop and online services provide robust tools for building interactive reports and dashboards.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Enfrasys Solutions will establish the foundational Power BI workspaces, configure secure connectivity to Fabric’s Semantic Model, and implement role-based access. UMS is responsible for ongoing report development, publishing, and consumption within the defined governance framework.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: Machine learning workflow and Power BI integration within the Fabric and OneLake ecosystem.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and conditional access for users, applications, and resources across Microsoft 365, Azure, and Microsoft Fabric.

Entra ID’s role in the UMS solution includes:

- **Centralized Identity Management**: Governs user authentication and authorization for all Fabric and Power BI resources.
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Enables fine-grained assignment of administrative, contributor, and viewer roles within workspaces.
- **Conditional Access and Security**: Supports advanced security policies, ensuring only authorized UMS personnel can access sensitive data and analytics assets.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure Entra ID integration, establish RBAC policies, and ensure secure onboarding of UMS users. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ongoing user lifecycle management and adherence to access governance policies.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture and connectivity design for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to enable secure, high-performance integration between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data movement, data engineering, and business intelligence within the Microsoft cloud ecosystem. It provides seamless integration with both cloud-based and on-premises data sources, supporting secure data transfer and centralized analytics.

UMS maintains an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse as the primary staging area for enterprise data. To enable secure and reliable connectivity between this on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric, Enfrasys Solutions recommends the deployment of an On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, facilitating outbound-only connections from the UMS data center to Microsoft Fabric, thereby minimizing the attack surface and complying with best security practices.

The overall network architecture includes:
- The UMS on-premises SQL Server data warehouse.
- A dedicated virtual machine (VM) hosting the On-Premises Data Gateway.
- Secure outbound connectivity from the OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft cloud services.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are critical for controlling inbound and outbound network traffic to Azure resources. An NSG consists of security rules that allow or deny traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah implement dedicated NSG configurations for all virtual machines hosting the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) to ensure secure and compliant connectivity with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, SQL Server, Data Gateway (OPDG), and OneLake all support industry-standard encryption mechanisms to protect data at rest and in transit. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah enforce encryption for all data flows and storage locations as outlined below.

### Encryption at Rest

- **Microsoft Fabric & OneLake**: Data is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys with Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) leveraging AES-256.
- **Power BI**: All datasets and reports are encrypted at rest in the Power BI service using Microsoft-managed keys; BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) is available for Premium capacities.
- **SQL Server (Azure SQL/Managed Instance)**: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) is enabled by default, using AES encryption.
- **On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)**: Credentials and configuration data are encrypted using Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI) on the gateway VM.

### Encryption in Transit

- **Data Gateway to Microsoft Fabric/Power BI**: All traffic is transmitted over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+) to ensure confidentiality and integrity.
- **User Access to Power BI/Fabric**: All browser and client connections use HTTPS/TLS.
- **SQL Data Flows**: Connections between Power BI/Fabric and SQL Server (on-premises or Azure) must enforce TLS encryption.
- **OneLake Data Access**: All data movement between OneLake and compute resources is secured using HTTPS.

1. Enfrasys Solutions shall configure the Fabric pilot environment based on the agreed design.
2. UMS shall provide access to representative datasets and user accounts for pilot validation.
3. Enfrasys Solutions shall migrate a limited, non-critical dataset to the Fabric environment.
4. UMS shall conduct functional and user acceptance testing (UAT) using the pilot environment.
5. Enfrasys Solutions shall address any issues identified during UAT.

### Pilot Acceptance Criteria

- Successful connectivity between on-premises systems and Microsoft Fabric.
- Data integrity is maintained post-migration.
- UMS users can access and interact with migrated datasets without errors.
- All critical pilot use cases are validated and signed off by UMS.

## 8.3 Production

Upon successful pilot completion and UMS sign-off, Enfrasys Solutions recommends proceeding with the production cutover.

### Production Cutover Steps

1. Enfrasys Solutions shall finalize the Fabric production environment configuration.
2. UMS shall freeze changes to source datasets during the production migration window.
3. Enfrasys Solutions shall execute the migration of all identified production datasets.
4. UMS shall perform post-migration validation and confirm data integrity.
5. Enfrasys Solutions shall resolve any post-migration issues identified by UMS.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the UMS Power BI & Microsoft Fabric implementation, the purpose of this Solution Design Document, and the intended audience.

## 2.1 Project Overview

UMS has initiated a project to modernize its data analytics platform by implementing Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric. The primary business objectives are to streamline data ingestion, transformation, and visualization processes, enabling advanced analytics and business intelligence for UMS stakeholders. The project scope encompasses establishing a Fabric workspace, designing and deploying end-to-end ETL pipelines, integrating machine learning workflows, and embedding Power BI dashboards for actionable business insights. Key outcomes include improved data-driven decision-making, enhanced operational efficiency, and alignment of UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s capabilities, specifically leveraging Fabric Data Factory for data integration, Fabric Synapse for big data analytics, and Data Science for machine learning applications.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The formal purpose of this Solution Design Document is to detail the technical architecture, workflow design, and implementation approach for the UMS Power BI & Fabric solution. It serves as the authoritative reference throughout the project lifecycle, guiding solution development, deployment, and operational management. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting and maintaining this document, while UMS is responsible for reviewing and approving all design decisions to ensure alignment with business requirements and IT governance.

## 2.3 Document Audience

The intended audience for this document includes:

- UMS IT Department: Responsible for technical review, operational readiness, and ongoing platform management.
- UMS Business Stakeholders: Responsible for validating business requirements and ensuring delivered analytics meet organizational objectives.
- Enfrasys Solutions Project Team: Responsible for solution design, implementation, and technical support.
- UMS Executive Sponsors: Responsible for project oversight and final approval of solution design.

Enfrasys Solutions shall lead the drafting, technical validation, and update of this document. UMS stakeholders are responsible for review, feedback, and formal approval at each stage of the project lifecycle.

# 3.0 Microsoft Power BI & Fabric Overview

This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, and their strategic roles in the UMS data platform solution.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data integration, data warehousing, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS experience. Its core components include Data Factory for data ingestion and orchestration, Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, Data Science for machine learning, and OneLake as a unified data lake. 

In the UMS solution, Microsoft Fabric serves as the foundational platform for the end-to-end data workflow—encompassing data ingestion from the UMS Staging Area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse), multi-layered data transformation (Bronze, Silver, Gold layers), advanced analytics, and seamless integration with Power BI for visualization. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the enablement, configuration, and deployment of Microsoft Fabric services. UMS shall be responsible for user adoption, operationalization, and ongoing data stewardship within the Fabric environment.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: UMS Data Workflow leveraging Microsoft Fabric and OneLake.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization service. It enables organizations to connect to diverse data sources, model and transform data, and create interactive dashboards and reports. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, allowing seamless access to curated and transformed data for analytics and business decision-making.

Within the UMS solution, Power BI is the primary tool for business-aligned analytics and reporting. It connects to the Gold layer tables in OneLake, delivering actionable insights to stakeholders. Enfrasys Solutions will provision and integrate Power BI with the Fabric workspace, ensuring data connectivity and security. UMS shall drive user adoption, report development, and business process integration using Power BI.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: AutoML Workflow and Power BI integration in Microsoft Fabric.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, conditional access, and identity governance for users and applications across Microsoft 365, Azure, and other integrated services. Entra ID is the authoritative identity provider for both Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, ensuring secure access, role-based permissions, and compliance with organizational policies.

In the UMS solution, Entra ID governs access to the Fabric workspace, OneLake storage, and Power BI resources. Enfrasys Solutions will configure Entra ID integration, including role assignments and conditional access policies, to enforce least-privilege access and secure data workflows. UMS shall maintain user lifecycle management and compliance monitoring within Entra ID.

---

**Responsibility Assignment Summary**

| Item                  | Activities                                              | Action By            | Status      |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| Microsoft Fabric      | Platform enablement, configuration, deployment         | Enfrasys Solutions   | Planned     |
| Power BI Integration  | Provisioning, workspace integration, data connectivity | Enfrasys Solutions   | Planned     |
| Entra ID Integration  | Access configuration, role assignment                  | Enfrasys Solutions   | Planned     |
| User Adoption         | Report development, operationalization, training       | UMS                  | Planned     |
| Data Stewardship      | Ongoing data management, compliance                    | UMS                  | Planned     |

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section details the network architecture and connectivity design for UMS, including secure integration between on-premises resources and Microsoft Fabric.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that brings together data engineering, data integration, and business intelligence capabilities within the Microsoft cloud ecosystem. It provides secure, scalable, and unified data access and analytics across various Microsoft services.

UMS's network architecture is designed to ensure secure, reliable connectivity between on-premises infrastructure and Microsoft Fabric. The solution leverages outbound-only connectivity via the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) and does not implement Azure Private Link at this stage. All data flows utilize encrypted channels, and outbound traffic is strictly controlled through defined security rules.

Key elements include:
- On-premises data sources (e.g., Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse)
- On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) deployed on a dedicated VM
- Secure outbound flows to Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft services
- Conditional Access policies enforced via Microsoft Entra ID

Limitations:
- Private Link is not implemented; all connectivity is outbound over the public internet using HTTPS.
- Inbound connections to the on-premises network are not permitted.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Data flow from UMS on-premises SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via OPDG.

## 4.2 Fabric Data Gateway

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft component that facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services, including Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The OPDG operates as a bridge, enabling outbound-only, encrypted connections without requiring inbound firewall exceptions.

### 4.2.1 OPDG Virtual Machine Specification

The OPDG will be deployed on a dedicated virtual machine with the following specifications:

| Component         | Specification                                              |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Operating System  | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit)       |
| .NET Framework    | Version 4.8                                               |
| vCPU              | 8 cores                                                   |
| RAM               | Minimum 8 GB                                              |

### 4.2.2 Outbound Security Rule Requirements

To ensure secure and reliable operation of the OPDG, the following outbound security rules must be implemented on the gateway VM. These rules allow only the necessary traffic to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and authentication endpoints.

| Name                      | Priority | Source                 | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                 | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|---------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160   | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                            | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

### 4.2.3 Deployment Responsibilities

| Item                             | Activities                                                                                      | Action By          | Status |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|--------|
| OPDG VM Provisioning             | Deploy and configure the virtual machine according to specifications                            | UMS                | Planned|
| OPDG Installation & Configuration| Install Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway and perform initial configuration                    | Enfrasys Solutions | Planned|
| Network Security Group (NSG)     | Configure outbound security rules as per requirements                                           | Enfrasys Solutions | Planned|
| On-Premises Network Readiness    | Ensure firewall and routing permit outbound HTTPS/HTTP as per rule requirements                 | UMS                | Planned|
| Connectivity Testing             | Validate connectivity from OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints                   | Enfrasys Solutions | Planned|

## 4.3 Design Decisions

| No. | Design Decision                                                                                              | Decision            |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| 1   | Use of On-Premises Data Gateway for secure outbound data integration                                         | Approved            |
| 2   | No implementation of Azure Private Link; all connectivity is outbound via public internet                    | Approved            |
| 3   | Strict outbound security rules enforced on OPDG VM                                                           | Approved            |
| 4   | Dedicated VM with specified resources for OPDG                                                               | Approved            |
| 5   | Enfrasys Solutions responsible for OPDG deployment and NSG configuration; UMS responsible for network readiness | Approved            |

# 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric

This section defines role-based access and responsibilities within Microsoft Fabric for UMS, including administrative and workspace-level roles.

## 5.1 Fabric Administrator Role

Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence in a single SaaS experience. The Fabric Administrator role is a privileged role responsible for managing Fabric tenant settings, controlling workspace creation, enforcing security and compliance, and overseeing integration with Microsoft Entra ID and other services.

### Administrator Capabilities

| Capability                | Description                                                                                   |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Tenant Settings           | Configure global Fabric settings, including security, compliance, and workspace defaults.     |
| Access Management         | Assign and revoke administrative roles and workspace permissions.                             |

# 6.0 Microsoft Fabric Design and Decision

This section details the solution design for UMS’s data workflow, access, resource organization, and governance within Microsoft Fabric. All tables and diagrams referenced are included as per requirements.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data integration, engineering, science, and visualization. It includes Data Factory for orchestration, Synapse for analytics, OneLake for unified storage, and Power BI for business intelligence. The following table summarizes the key workflow design considerations for UMS:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                      | Workload Type    |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                             | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                            | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                                 | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                                | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook, and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).      | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                     | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                          | Power BI         |

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a layered Lakehouse architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) for UMS, leveraging Fabric Data Factory, Synapse, and Power BI. The ETL pipeline utilizes Dataflow Gen2 and Notebooks for transformation, while Machine Learning integration is achieved via AutoML and manual notebooks. 

### ETL and Lakehouse Layering

- **Bronze Layer:** Stores raw ingested data from SQL Server.
- **Silver Layer:** Contains cleansed and enriched data, processed via Dataflow Gen2 and Notebooks.
- **Gold Layer:** Holds transformed and scored data, ready for analytics and reporting.

### Machine Learning Integration

- **AutoML and Manual ML:** Cleaned data from Silver Lakehouse is used for ML experimentation. Models are trained, evaluated, and scored in Notebooks, with results stored in Gold Lakehouse.
- **Model Registry:** Trained models are registered for lifecycle management.
- **Semantic Model:** Power BI connects to Gold Lakehouse via OneLake for visualization.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision
This section outlines the security architecture for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment, focusing on network security, encryption, and operational responsibilities.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a fundamental security feature in Microsoft Azure, providing granular control over inbound and outbound traffic to resources such as virtual machines and subnets. NSGs use rules to permit or deny traffic based on source, destination, protocol, and port, thereby enforcing network segmentation and minimizing attack surfaces.

UMS shall implement NSG rules to secure the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM, ensuring only authorized communication with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related cloud services. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration of these NSG rules, while UMS is responsible for ongoing compliance and monitoring.

### NSG Rules Mapping to Data Gateway and Fabric Components

| Name                      | Priority | Source                | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                               | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|---------------------------|----------|-----------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160   | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                            | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These NSG rules ensure secure outbound connectivity for the OPDG VM, supporting data transfer, authentication, and connectivity diagnostics in accordance with Microsoft’s security best practices.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

### Microsoft Fabric and Power BI Encryption Overview

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI employ industry-standard encryption protocols to protect data at rest and in transit. Encryption at rest uses Azure-managed keys and, where required, customer-managed keys for enhanced control. Encryption in transit leverages SSL/TLS protocols to secure all communications between clients, gateways, and Microsoft cloud endpoints.

UMS shall ensure all data flows between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI are encrypted both at rest and in transit. Enfrasys Solutions will configure encryption settings and validate secure connections during deployment; UMS is responsible for user compliance, periodic reviews, and reporting.

#### Encryption Controls

- **Data at Rest**: All datasets stored in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI are encrypted using Azure Storage encryption with AES-256. Customer-managed keys may be utilized for additional compliance requirements.
- **Data in Transit**: All communications between OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI endpoints are encrypted via SSL/TLS (HTTPS), ensuring confidentiality and integrity during data transfer.
- **Authentication Traffic**: Identity verification and token exchanges with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) are encrypted using HTTPS.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends periodic audits and reviews of encryption configurations. UMS shall maintain compliance with Microsoft security guidelines and report any deviations or incidents.

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the phased deployment and migration approach for the UMS solution, including preparatory activities, pilot execution, production rollout, and post-migration support.

## 8.2 Pilot Deployment Approach

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS first conducts a pilot deployment to validate solution components, data integration, and user access. The pilot will involve:

Pilot completion and sign-off by UMS is required before proceeding to production rollout.

## 8.3 Production Rollout Plan (D0)

The production rollout will commence upon successful pilot completion and UMS approval. The following table outlines the production migration activities and responsibilities.

All production activities are targeted for execution on D0 (cutover day).

## 8.4 Post-Migration Support (D+1)

Following cutover, Enfrasys Solutions will provide post-migration support to ensure solution stability and address any issues. The support and handover activities are as follows:

- Monitoring of data flows and system health for 3 business days post-cutover.

**Handover Responsibilities:**

- **UMS:** Responsible for accepting operational ownership and ongoing administration after handover.

All post-migration support activities are scheduled for D+1 to D+3, with formal handover upon UMS acceptance.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.
