# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI & Microsoft Fabric solution design, outlining the business context, project scope, document intent, and target audience. ## 2.1 Project Overview Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has initiated a strategic project to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence capabilities. The project is scoped to design an end-to-end data workflow, encompassing data ingestion, transformation, and visualization, leveraging Microsoft Fabric. The primary objectives are as follows: - Establish a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace for UMS. - Develop a comprehensive ETL pipeline to support data integration and orchestration using Fabric Data Factory. - Enable advanced analytics and big data processing through Fabric Synapse. - Implement machine learning processes leveraging Fabric Data Science capabilities. - Integrate Power BI for business-aligned analytics and visualization. This initiative aligns with UMS’s cloud adoption strategy, ensuring that data-driven decision-making is supported by a robust, scalable, and secure platform. ## 2.2 Document Purpose The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to formally capture the technical and architectural decisions for the UMS Power BI & Microsoft Fabric implementation. This document serves to: - Articulate the proposed infrastructure and workflow design, as outlined in the project agenda. - Provide a reference for all stakeholders regarding the scope, objectives, and technical approach. - Ensure alignment between UMS’s business requirements and the capabilities of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. - Guide implementation, migration, and operational activities. - Serve as the authoritative baseline for review, sign-off, and future enhancements. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the authorship and maintenance of this document. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is responsible for its review, feedback, and formal sign-off. ## 2.3 Document Audience This Solution Design Document is intended for the following audiences: - Enfrasys Solutions: Project consultants, solution architects, and implementation engineers responsible for design, deployment, and support. - Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS): Project sponsors, IT management, technical leads, data engineers, business analysts, and end-user representatives. - Other stakeholders: Business and technical users involved in analytics, reporting, and data-driven initiatives. The document is designed to be accessible to both technical and business stakeholders, ensuring comprehensive understanding and alignment throughout the project lifecycle. # 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Entra ID, establishing the foundation for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) analytics and data workflow solution. ## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It consolidates multiple data services into a single SaaS offering, enabling organizations to manage the entire data lifecycle from ingestion to visualization within a secure, governed environment. ### Core Features - **Data Factory**: Microsoft Fabric Data Factory provides robust data integration and orchestration capabilities. It enables the ingestion, transformation, and movement of data from various sources into a unified platform. This service supports both code-free and code-based data pipeline development, allowing for scalable ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes tailored to UMS’s business requirements. - **Synapse**: Fabric Synapse delivers advanced analytics and big data processing. It combines data warehousing, big data analytics, and data integration into a single service, supporting high-performance queries and advanced analytics workloads. This functionality is essential for UMS to analyze large datasets and derive actionable insights. - **Data Science**: The Data Science component within Microsoft Fabric empowers organizations to build, train, and operationalize machine learning models at scale. It provides integrated tools for data exploration, feature engineering, and model deployment, supporting UMS’s machine learning and predictive analytics initiatives. - **OneLake**: OneLake is the unified data lake storage layer in Microsoft Fabric. It provides a single, secure, and scalable repository for all data assets, ensuring seamless data access and governance across the analytics lifecycle. Enfrasys Solutions recommends Microsoft Fabric as the foundational platform for UMS’s analytics modernization, ensuring end-to-end data workflow management, scalability, and security. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for technology selection and solution design, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall ensure business alignment and requirements validation. ## 3.2 Power BI Power BI is a leading business intelligence and data visualization platform from Microsoft. It enables organizations to transform raw data into interactive reports and dashboards, facilitating data-driven decision-making at all organizational levels. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, allowing seamless connectivity to data pipelines, data warehouses, and machine learning outputs. This integration ensures that UMS can visualize data processed within Fabric in real time, leveraging advanced analytics and AI-powered insights. Key visualization capabilities include: - Creation of interactive dashboards and reports - Support for natural language queries - Advanced data modeling and custom visualizations - Real-time data monitoring and alerting Enfrasys Solutions will architect the integration of Power BI with Microsoft Fabric, ensuring secure and efficient data flow for analytics. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall define business-aligned KPIs and reporting requirements to maximize the value of Power BI visualizations. ### 3.2.1 Entra ID Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides centralized authentication, authorization, and conditional access controls for users and applications across Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and other Microsoft services. Entra ID ensures secure access to analytics resources by: - Enforcing multi-factor authentication and conditional access policies - Managing user identities, groups, and roles - Providing audit trails and compliance reporting Enfrasys Solutions will configure Entra ID to enforce security best practices and role-based access control for the analytics environment. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall manage user assignments and ensure alignment with organizational security policies. # 4.0 Network Design and Decision This section outlines the network architecture and connectivity decisions for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), focusing on secure Azure connectivity and the deployment of the Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) requires a secure and robust network architecture to enable seamless integration between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric services in Azure. The design leverages Azure’s connectivity features and emphasizes an outbound-only connection model for maximum security. The architecture utilizes the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) deployed within the UMS environment to bridge on-premises data sources, such as the UMS Staging Area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse), with the cloud-based UMS Fabric. All connectivity from the OPDG to Microsoft Fabric is strictly outbound, eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules and minimizing the attack surface. ![](images\slide_011_img_004.png) Figure 1: Secure data flow from UMS on-premises SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via OPDG. This outbound-only connectivity ensures that data transfers are initiated from the UMS network, passing securely through the gateway to the Microsoft Fabric environment in Azure. No inbound ports are exposed, aligning with best security practices and compliance requirements. ## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway ### Definition The Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure, lightweight agent that acts as a bridge, enabling cloud services such as Microsoft Fabric to access on-premises data sources. The gateway securely transmits data from on-premises environments to cloud services using outbound HTTPS connections, ensuring that no inbound firewall ports are required. ### OPDG Deployment Model Enfrasys Solutions recommends deploying the OPDG on a dedicated virtual machine within the UMS network. This VM will host the gateway agent, providing a secure conduit for data movement between the UMS Staging Area (SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) and Microsoft Fabric. The OPDG leverages a secure outbound connection model, where all data transfers to Microsoft Fabric are initiated from within the UMS network. This model significantly reduces exposure to external threats and simplifies firewall management. ### VM Specifications for OPDG The following table details the recommended specifications for the OPDG virtual machine: | Component | Specification | |-------------------|------------------------------------------------| | Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) | | .NET Framework | Version 4.8 | | vCPU | 8 cores | | RAM | Minimum 8 GB | ### Roles and Responsibilities | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |---------------------------------------- |-------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|----------| | OPDG VM Provisioning | Provision VM with required OS and hardware specifications | UMS | Pending | | OPDG Agent Installation & Configuration | Install and configure OPDG agent on provisioned VM | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | | On-Premises Data Source Readiness | Ensure SQL Server and network connectivity are prepared | UMS | Pending | | Gateway Registration with Fabric | Register OPDG with Microsoft Fabric | Enfrasys Solutions | Pending | Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the deployment, configuration, and registration of the OPDG. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall ensure the readiness of the on-premises data sources and provision the required virtual machine infrastructure. This design ensures a secure, scalable, and compliant data integration pathway between UMS’s on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric in Azure. # 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric & Power BI This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and access mapping for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. ## 5.1 Fabric Administrator Role Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It provides a centralized environment for managing data workflows, security, and governance. The Fabric Administrator role is responsible for the overall governance and management of the Fabric environment. This includes configuring security, managing workspaces, assigning roles, and ensuring compliance with Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data policies. Fabric Administrators have full access to all workspace settings and can delegate permissions to Workspace Admins, who manage day-to-day operations at the workspace level. Key responsibilities of the Fabric Administrator include: - Overseeing the creation and management of Fabric workspaces. - Assigning and auditing workspace roles. - Ensuring data security and compliance. - Coordinating with Workspace Admins for operational management. Enfrasys Solutions shall configure the Fabric Administrator role, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall assign designated personnel to this role. ## 5.2 Fabric-native Roles Microsoft Fabric and Power BI provide a suite of native roles to support a range of data, analytics, and governance functions. The following roles are recommended for UMS: | Role | Description | |------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Contributor | Can create, edit, and delete content within assigned workspaces, including datasets and reports. | | Viewer | Has read-only access to view reports, dashboards, and datasets within the workspace. | | Data Engineer | Responsible for data ingestion, transformation, and pipeline management within Fabric. | | Business User Admin | Manages business user access, ensuring correct permissions and onboarding for non-technical users. | | Data Analyst | Develops analytical models, creates reports, and interprets data for business decision-making. | | Stakeholder | Reviews reports and dashboards, provides feedback, and participates in strategic decisions. | | Project Director | Oversees project delivery, ensures alignment with organizational goals, and manages stakeholders. | Enfrasys Solutions shall configure these roles within the Fabric environment. UMS shall ensure all users complete MFA enrollment and adhere to tenant-wide MFA policies. ### External User Access External user access to Microsoft Fabric resources shall be governed by the same Conditional Access and MFA enforcement as internal users. UMS shall review and approve all external user invitations, and Enfrasys Solutions will configure access policies accordingly. ![](images\slide_006_img_001.png) Figure 4: External user access and Conditional Access enforcement. ## 6.4 Virtual Machine (VM) Size The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component for secure data transfer between UMS’s on-premises SQL Server and Microsoft Fabric. UMS shall respond to alerts, remediate non-compliance, and participate in periodic governance reviews. --- # Appendix ### Introduction/Prerequisites Microsoft Fabric Overview: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/) Power BI Documentation: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/) Azure Management Groups: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview) ### Limits and Boundaries Microsoft Fabric Capacity and Limits: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/service-limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/service-limits) Power BI Service Limits: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/service-service-limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/service-service-limits) Azure Naming Rules and Restrictions: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/resource-name-rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/resource-name-rules) ### Others Conditional Access in Entra ID: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/overview) Azure Cost Management: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/) On-premises Data Gateway Documentation: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-install](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-install) # 7.0 Security Design and Decision This section outlines the security controls and encryption standards for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment. ## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are fundamental security constructs within Microsoft Azure, providing granular control over inbound and outbound network traffic to Azure resources. NSGs operate by enforcing security rules that allow or deny network traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol. NSGs are essential for safeguarding cloud workloads and ensuring only authorized communications occur between UMS’s on-premises and cloud resources. Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the configuration, implementation, and validation of the NSG outbound rules as detailed below. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall be responsible for ongoing compliance monitoring and periodic review of NSG effectiveness. | Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | |-----------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------| | Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow | | Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160 | VM Private IP Addresses| * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow | ## 7.2 Encryption Design ### SSL/TLS Encryption Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) and Transport Layer Security (TLS) are cryptographic protocols designed to provide secure communication over a computer network. All communications between the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI endpoints shall be protected using TLS 1.2 or higher, ensuring confidentiality and integrity of data in transit. Enfrasys Solutions shall configure all required endpoints and services to enforce TLS encryption. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall ensure compliance by verifying that all client applications and integrations support and utilize TLS 1.2 or above. ### Data-at-Rest Encryption Data-at-rest encryption ensures that data stored on disk within Azure resources is protected using strong encryption algorithms. Azure Storage, SQL Database, and related services employ Azure-managed keys by default, with an option for customer-managed keys for enhanced control. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) utilize Azure’s built-in encryption for all storage accounts, databases, and virtual machines associated with the Fabric and Power BI deployment. UMS shall be responsible for monitoring encryption compliance and key management practices. ### Fabric and Power BI Encryption Standards Microsoft Fabric and Power BI are cloud-based analytics platforms that adhere to Microsoft’s enterprise-grade security and compliance standards. Both services implement encryption for data in transit and at rest using industry-standard algorithms (such as AES-256). Enfrasys Solutions shall ensure that all data flows between UMS’s on-premises infrastructure and Microsoft Fabric/Power BI are encrypted by default, leveraging the secure channels established by the On-Premises Data Gateway and Azure NSG rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall regularly review Microsoft’s compliance documentation to ensure continued alignment with institutional security policies. # 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach This section outlines the structured approach and responsibilities for the deployment and migration activities for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). ## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup The following table details the preparatory activities required before migration, with clear assignment of responsibilities to Enfrasys Solutions and UMS. | No | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks | |----|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|------------------|--------------|---------| | 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started | | | 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started | | | 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | | 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started | | Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the technical deployment and configuration, while UMS shall ensure environment readiness and provide necessary confirmations. ## 8.2 Pilot The pilot phase will commence seven days prior to production cutover (D-7), focusing on validating processes and minimizing risk. **Pilot Timeline (D-7):** - UMS shall confirm environment readiness and provide final sign-off. ## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support Post-migration support will commence immediately after production cutover (D+1), ensuring stability and knowledge transfer. **Post-Migration Timeline (D+1):** - D+1: Initiate post-migration support and monitoring. - D+2: Conduct knowledge transfer and documentation handover. - D+3: Review incident logs and resolve outstanding issues. | Item | Activities | Action By | Status | |------|----------------------------------------------------|------------------|--------------| | 1 | Initiate post-migration support and monitoring | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | 2 | Conduct knowledge transfer to UMS IT team | Enfrasys | Not-Started | | 3 | Review and resolve post-migration incidents | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started | | 4 | Final support sign-off | UMS | Not-Started | Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for post-migration support and knowledge transfer. slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the design initiative for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data analytics modernization leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI.

## 2.1 Project Overview

The primary objective of this project is to design and implement a comprehensive data workflow solution for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), encompassing data ingestion, transformation, and visualization. The scope includes the establishment of a Microsoft Fabric workspace, development of an end-to-end ETL pipeline, execution of machine learning processes, and seamless integration with Power BI for advanced business analytics. The design leverages key Microsoft Fabric services, including Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science for machine learning applications. This initiative is intended to align UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with the latest capabilities of Microsoft Fabric, enabling data-driven decision-making and operational efficiency.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to formally define the technical architecture, design decisions, and implementation approach for UMS’s Power BI and Microsoft Fabric deployment. The document outlines the proposed infrastructure, workflow design, security models, and migration strategy. It serves as the authoritative reference for all stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring alignment, traceability, and clarity of requirements and deliverables. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting this document, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is responsible for review and formal sign-off.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for the following primary stakeholders:
- UMS IT Department
- UMS Data Analytics Team
- Enfrasys Solutions Project Team

Stakeholders are expected to review, provide feedback, and approve the design to ensure successful implementation and alignment with UMS’s business objectives.

# 3.0 Microsoft Power BI & Fabric Overview

This section provides an overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, with a focus on their definitions, core features, and business value for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS).

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

### Definition

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform delivered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. It unifies data engineering, data integration, data warehousing, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single platform. Fabric is designed to simplify the process of ingesting, transforming, analyzing, and visualizing data at scale.

### Core Features

- **Data Factory**: Provides data integration and orchestration capabilities for ingesting data from diverse sources, supporting ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) and ELT (Extract, Load, Transform) pipelines.
- **Synapse**: Offers advanced analytics, big data processing, and data warehousing, enabling organizations to analyze large datasets efficiently.
- **Data Science**: Integrates machine learning tools and AutoML capabilities, supporting end-to-end data science workflows within the platform.
- **Unified Workspace**: Centralizes data assets, pipelines, and analytics artifacts, streamlining collaboration and governance.
- **Security and Compliance**: Incorporates enterprise-grade security, role-based access control, and compliance with regulatory standards.

### Business Value for UMS

- **Accelerated Time-to-Insight**: Enables Universiti Malaysia Sabah to rapidly develop and deploy data workflows from ingestion to visualization.
- **Simplified Data Management**: Reduces complexity by consolidating multiple analytics workloads into a single platform.
- **Scalability**: Supports UMS’s growth by handling increasing data volumes and advanced analytics requirements.
- **Collaboration**: Facilitates cross-functional collaboration among data engineers, data scientists, and business analysts.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the Fabric environment and workflow. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall validate the proposed design and requirements.

## 3.2 Power BI

### Definition

Microsoft Power BI is a business analytics service that enables users to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decision-making. Power BI provides interactive reports and dashboards, connecting to a wide range of data sources both on-premises and in the cloud.

### Integration with Microsoft Fabric

Power BI is natively integrated with Microsoft Fabric, allowing seamless access to data processed and stored within Fabric workspaces. This integration ensures that data pipelines, machine learning outputs, and analytics results developed in Fabric are directly available for visualization and business intelligence reporting in Power BI.

### Business Value for UMS

- **Enhanced Decision-Making**: Empowers UMS stakeholders with real-time, actionable insights through interactive dashboards and reports.
- **Unified Analytics Experience**: Streamlines the transition from data preparation to visualization, reducing manual effort and errors.
- **Accessibility**: Enables users across UMS to access insights securely from any location or device.
- **Alignment with Business Objectives**: Supports analytics initiatives aligned with UMS’s strategic goals, including research, administration, and operational excellence.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring Power BI integration and developing initial dashboards. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall review and validate the analytics outputs.

## 3.3 Entra ID

### Definition

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and role-based access control for users, applications, and resources across Microsoft cloud services.

### Role in Access and Identity Management

Within the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment, Entra ID serves as the backbone for authentication and authorization. It manages user identities, enforces access policies, and ensures that only authorized personnel can access sensitive data and analytics resources.

- **Single Sign-On (SSO)**: Allows UMS users to access Fabric, Power BI, and other Microsoft services with a unified identity.
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Assigns permissions based on user roles, ensuring appropriate access to data and analytics assets.
- **Security and Compliance**: Supports multi-factor authentication, conditional access policies, and auditing to meet regulatory requirements.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring Entra ID integration and defining access roles. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall validate the assigned roles and user mappings.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture, data gateway deployment, and security considerations for integrating Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) on-premises environment with Microsoft Fabric.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

The network design ensures secure, efficient connectivity between UMS’s on-premises data warehouse, the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine, and Microsoft Fabric. The architecture leverages outbound-only connections to minimize exposure and maintain compliance with security best practices.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Network connectivity between UMS on-premises, OPDG VM, and Microsoft Fabric.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the network architecture and OPDG deployment. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall provide detailed information regarding on-premises network topology, firewall configurations, and data source accessibility.

## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway

Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence on a single SaaS foundation. It enables organizations to connect, analyze, and visualize data from various sources, both on-premises and in the cloud.

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) serves as a secure bridge between UMS’s on-premises Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse and Microsoft Fabric. The OPDG is deployed on a dedicated virtual machine within the UMS environment, facilitating secure, outbound data transfer without requiring inbound firewall rules.

Enfrasys Solutions shall oversee the installation and configuration of the OPDG agent. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for provisioning the VM according to the following specifications:

| Component        | Specification                                 |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework   | Version 4.8                                  |
| vCPU             | 8 cores                                      |
| RAM              | Minimum 8 GB                                 |

## 4.3 Connectivity Security

The network architecture for OPDG follows an outbound-only connectivity model, ensuring that all communications from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and related services are initiated from within the UMS environment. This approach eliminates the need for inbound firewall exceptions, thereby reducing the attack surface and enhancing overall security posture.

The following Azure Network Security Group (NSG) rules are required to support secure connectivity for the OPDG VM:

| Name                        | Priority | Source                   | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                   | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|--------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                               | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

Enfrasys Solutions shall configure the required NSG rules and validate outbound connectivity. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ensuring that the on-premises firewall permits outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) and HTTP (TCP 80) traffic to the specified Microsoft endpoints.

# 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric

This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and personnel assignments for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) within Microsoft Fabric.

## 5.1 Fabric Administrator Role

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single SaaS experience. The Fabric Administrator role is a privileged position responsible for managing and securing the Fabric environment at the tenant level.

### Definition

The Fabric Administrator is a designated individual or team with elevated permissions to oversee the configuration, governance, and operational health of Microsoft Fabric across the organization.

### Responsibilities

- Tenant-level configuration and policy management
- Assignment and governance of workspace roles
- Monitoring and auditing Fabric activities
- Managing integration with Microsoft Entra ID and other Microsoft 365 services
- Ensuring compliance with Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) security and data governance policies

Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for defining the Fabric Administrator role and mapping initial responsibilities. Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shall confirm the personnel designated for this role.

## 5.2 Fabric-native Roles

Microsoft Fabric provides a set of native workspace roles to facilitate secure and efficient collaboration. These roles include Workspace Admin, Workspace Contributor, and Workspace Viewer.

### Workspace Admin

Workspace Admins have full control over workspace settings, permissions, and content management. They can add or remove users, configure access, and manage all resources within the workspace.

### Workspace Contributor

Workspace Contributors can create, edit, and publish content within the workspace but cannot manage workspace-level permissions or settings.

### Workspace Viewer

Workspace Viewers have read-only access to content within the workspace. They can view reports, dashboards, and datasets but cannot modify or publish content.

# 6.0 Microsoft Fabric Design and Decision

This section details the design and decisions for Microsoft Fabric implementation for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), covering data workflow, access, VM sizing, resource organization, and governance.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single SaaS experience. It integrates with OneLake, Power BI, and Azure Data services to provide a comprehensive analytics solution.

The following table summarizes the key data workflow design considerations for UMS:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                                        | Workload Type    |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                                               | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                                              | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                                                   | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                                                  | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook, and Visual Query.      | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).                        | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                                       | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                                            | Power BI         |

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a modern, layered data architecture for UMS, leveraging Microsoft Fabric’s Lakehouse paradigm and integrating with Power BI for analytics and reporting. The workflow is designed to ensure data quality, traceability, and scalability.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 6.1: End-to-end Data Workflow in Microsoft Fabric

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 6.2: Machine Learning (AutoML) Workflow in Microsoft Fabric

Key workflow design decisions:

| No. | Design Decision                                                                                                          | Decision                                                                                       |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Data is ingested from Microsoft SQL Server via Azure Data Factory into the Bronze Lakehouse.                             | Adopted                                                                                        |
| 2   | Data is cleansed and transformed in the Silver Lakehouse using Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query.               | Adopted                                                                                        |
| 3   | Gold Lakehouse stores curated, business-ready data and ML outputs for reporting and analytics.                           | Adopted                                                                                        |
| 4   | Machine Learning is performed using both AutoML and manual notebooks, with outputs registered and stored in Gold layer.  | Adopted                                                                                        |
| 5   | Power BI connects to the Semantic Model via OneLake for real-time data visualization and reporting.                      | Adopted                                                                                        |

## 6.3 Access Design Considerations and Decisions

Access to Microsoft Fabric must be secured using Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) features. Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) are critical to safeguarding UMS data assets.

### Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a policy-based approach in Microsoft Entra ID that evaluates signals (user, device, location, risk) to enforce access controls. UMS currently does not meet the licensing requirements for advanced Conditional Access policies. As such, Enfrasys recommends enforcing MFA at the tenant level and revisiting Conditional Access policy implementation when the appropriate Entra ID P1/P2 licenses are available.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 6.3: Conditional Access Architecture

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 6.4: Authentication and Access Control Flow

| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts                                    |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                                      |

### MFA Enforcement

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enforced at the tenant level for all UMS users accessing Microsoft Fabric. This is a mandatory security measure to reduce unauthorized access risks.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

This section outlines the security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah, focusing on Azure NSG implementation and encryption strategies for Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG).

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a core Azure capability that allow administrators to control inbound and outbound network traffic to Azure resources. NSGs use security rules to permit or deny traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol, ensuring that only authorized network communication occurs.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah implement the following outbound NSG rules to secure the OPDG virtual machine and its connectivity with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services.

### Outbound NSG Rules

| Name                        | Priority | Source                   | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                           | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|--------------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                      | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                       | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the design and configuration of these NSG rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall review and approve the security controls to ensure compliance with institutional policies.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a critical component of the security architecture for cloud-based analytics and integration platforms. Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and OPDG employ industry-standard encryption mechanisms to protect data at rest and in transit.

### 7.2.1 Encryption at Rest

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI encrypt all customer data at rest using strong encryption algorithms such as AES-256. Data stored within Azure services is protected by Microsoft-managed keys by default, with the option for customer-managed keys in supported SKUs. The OPDG VM should utilize Azure Disk Encryption to secure operating system and data disks, leveraging Azure Key Vault for key management.

### 7.2.2 Encryption in Transit

All data transmitted between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI is encrypted using SSL/TLS protocols. Outbound NSG rules ensure that only HTTPS (port 443) and, for connectivity testing, HTTP (port 80) are permitted. This guarantees that sensitive information, including authentication tokens and analytical data, is protected from interception during network transit.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and validating the encryption configurations across all components. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall review the implemented encryption controls as part of their compliance and governance processes.

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a high-level overview of the UMS Microsoft Fabric and Power BI solution design, including project context, objectives, and document intent. ## 2.1 Project Overview Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that brings together data integration, engineering, science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence capabilities into a single SaaS experience. Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business analytics service that enables users to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decisions across the organization. UMS’s adoption of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI is driven by the need to modernize data workflows, enhance analytics, and support data-driven decision-making. The project scope includes the design and implementation of an end-to-end data workflow, covering data ingestion, transformation, machine learning processes, and business visualization. Key components include establishing a Fabric workspace, developing ETL pipelines using Fabric Data Factory, leveraging Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics, and integrating Power BI for business-aligned reporting. This initiative aligns with UMS’s cloud adoption strategy and aims to deliver scalable, secure, and efficient analytics services. High-level objectives: - Establish a robust Microsoft Fabric workspace for UMS. - Design and implement an end-to-end ETL pipeline. - Enable machine learning and advanced analytics using Fabric Data Science and Synapse. - Integrate Power BI for comprehensive business analytics and visualization. - Align solution design with UMS’s business requirements and Microsoft best practices. ## 2.2 Document Purpose This document serves as the formal solution design for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric and Power BI implementation. It provides a detailed blueprint for the technical architecture, workflow design, security model, and migration approach. slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project scope, document intent, and target audience for the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI solution design at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). The summary establishes the foundational context for subsequent technical and architectural sections.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has initiated a strategic project to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence environment, leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The primary business objective is to enable robust, scalable, and secure data workflows that support advanced analytics, operational reporting, and machine learning-driven insights. Technically, the project encompasses the design and implementation of a comprehensive data workflow—from ingestion through transformation to visualization—within the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.

The solution scope includes:
- Establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored to UMS’s operational and governance requirements.
- Development of end-to-end ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines utilizing Fabric Data Factory for seamless data integration and orchestration.
- Integration of Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics, big data processing, and support for complex business use cases.
- Deployment of machine learning applications using Fabric Data Science, enabling predictive analytics and data-driven decision-making.
- Integration of Power BI to deliver business-aligned dashboards, reports, and actionable insights to stakeholders across UMS.

This holistic approach aligns UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s capabilities, ensuring the university can efficiently harness data assets for both academic and administrative purposes. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the overall solution design, technical implementation, and initial rollout, while UMS will provide business requirements, participate in design reviews, and oversee operational adoption.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this document is to serve as a formal solution design for UMS’s adoption of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. It details the architectural decisions, workflow designs, security considerations, and operational models required for successful deployment and integration. The document provides a comprehensive blueprint for both technical and business stakeholders, ensuring clarity on the project’s objectives, deliverables, and implementation approach.

Enfrasys Solutions has prepared this design document to facilitate structured review, feedback, and sign-off. The document is intended to guide the implementation phase, inform governance decisions, and serve as a reference for ongoing operations and future enhancements. Ownership of technical accuracy and completeness lies with Enfrasys Solutions, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for validating business alignment and operational readiness prior to sign-off.

## 2.3 Document Audience

The solution design document is intended for the following audiences:

- UMS IT Department: Responsible for reviewing technical architecture, security controls, and operational workflows; will oversee solution adoption and ongoing management.
- UMS Business Stakeholders: Includes academic, administrative, and executive users who will leverage Power BI analytics and insights for decision-making; will validate business requirements and use case alignment.
- Enfrasys Solutions Project Team: Accountable for solution design, implementation, and post-deployment support; will coordinate with UMS stakeholders for requirements gathering, reviews, and sign-off.

Enfrasys Solutions shall lead the preparation, review, and revision of this document. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall provide feedback, validate requirements, and formally approve the solution design prior to implementation. This collaborative approach ensures the solution meets both technical standards and business objectives.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview

This section provides a formal overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, establishing their foundational roles in the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data platform solution. Each technology is defined in both business and technical terms, with explicit focus on their integration and relevance to UMS’s analytics and workflow requirements.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric: Definition and Core Services

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform designed to streamline enterprise data workflows, integrating data engineering, data science, and business intelligence capabilities within a single cloud environment. Fabric consolidates multiple analytics services—Data Factory, Synapse, Data Science, and OneLake—under a common workspace, enabling organizations to ingest, transform, analyze, and visualize data efficiently and securely.

From a business perspective, Microsoft Fabric empowers UMS to centralize its data assets, automate complex ETL pipelines, and leverage advanced analytics for actionable insights. Technically, Fabric provides robust orchestration tools (Data Factory), scalable big data processing (Synapse), integrated machine learning (Data Science), and a unified data lake (OneLake) for seamless data access and governance. This holistic approach reduces silos, enhances operational agility, and ensures that UMS can meet both current and future analytics demands.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends UMS establish a dedicated Fabric workspace as the foundation of its data platform. This workspace will serve as the central hub for all data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization activities, ensuring standardized governance and streamlined collaboration across departments.

### Core Services of Microsoft Fabric

- **Data Factory**: Provides data integration and orchestration, enabling UMS to automate ETL processes and ingest data from diverse sources, such as the SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse.
- **Synapse**: Delivers advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, supporting UMS in scalable data transformation and aggregation.
- **Data Science**: Facilitates machine learning experimentation and deployment, allowing UMS to build, train, and operationalize predictive models within the Fabric environment.
- **OneLake**: Acts as the unified data storage layer, ensuring seamless access and integration across all Fabric services and supporting direct connectivity to visualization tools like Power BI.

## 3.2 Power BI: Definition and Integration with Fabric

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence platform, designed to transform raw data into interactive dashboards, reports, and actionable insights. Power BI enables organizations to visualize data, monitor key metrics, and drive data-driven decision-making across all levels of the business.

For UMS, Power BI serves as the visualization endpoint of the Fabric data workflow. By integrating with Fabric’s OneLake and Semantic Model, Power BI allows UMS users to connect directly to curated, transformed datasets, ensuring real-time analytics and consistent reporting. This integration streamlines the journey from data ingestion (via Data Factory) through transformation (via Synapse and Data Science) to business-aligned visualization, supporting UMS’s strategic objectives in academic and operational analytics.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS leverage Power BI Desktop and Power BI Service for both self-service and enterprise reporting. Direct connectivity to Fabric’s Semantic Model via OneLake ensures high-performance, secure access to the latest data, minimizing latency and maximizing insight accuracy.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID: Definition and Role in Authentication & Access

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. Entra ID provides secure authentication, authorization, and user management for cloud and on-premises applications, ensuring that only authorized personnel can access sensitive resources.

In the context of UMS’s Fabric solution, Entra ID is critical for governing access to data, analytics workspaces, and visualization assets. By integrating Entra ID with Fabric and Power BI, UMS can enforce role-based access controls, audit user activity, and ensure compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements. Entra ID also supports single sign-on (SSO), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and conditional access policies, enhancing the security posture of the entire data platform.

Enfrasys Solutions instructs Universiti Malaysia Sabah to configure Entra ID as the central identity provider for all Fabric and Power BI resources. This will enable seamless, secure access for faculty, staff, and analysts, while maintaining strict governance and auditability.

## 3.4 Data Workflow Architecture in UMS Fabric Environment

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data workflow within the UMS Fabric environment, highlighting the integration of Data Factory, Synapse, Data Science, OneLake, and Power BI. Data is ingested from the UMS SQL Server Data Warehouse, processed through multiple lakehouse layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold), and visualized in Power BI. Identity management via Entra ID ensures secure access throughout the workflow.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: UMS Fabric Data Workflow Architecture.

## 3.5 Machine Learning Workflow in UMS Fabric

The diagram below depicts the machine learning workflow within UMS’s Fabric solution. Cleaned data from the Silver Lakehouse is used for both automated (AutoML) and manual machine learning experiments. Results are scored and stored in the Gold Lakehouse, with identity management integrated for secure access. Power BI connects to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake for visualization of model outputs.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: UMS Fabric Machine Learning Workflow.

## 3.6 Key Design Considerations for UMS Fabric Solution

To ensure optimal performance, security, and scalability of the UMS data platform, Enfrasys Solutions has identified the following design considerations. These considerations address data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization workflows, aligning with UMS’s business and technical requirements.

| ID   | Description                                                                                                         | Workload Type    |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                                | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                               | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                                    | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                                   | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).         | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                        | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                             | Power BI         |

## 3.7 Machine Learning Workflow Design Considerations

The following design considerations pertain specifically to the machine learning workflows within Fabric, ensuring that UMS can support both automated and manual ML experimentation, model lifecycle management, and seamless integration with Power BI.

| ID   | Description                                                                                                         | Workloads type   |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering |
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science     |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science     |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science     |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering |
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering |
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI         |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                             | Power BI         |

---

Enfrasys Solutions emphasizes that the integration of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Entra ID forms the backbone of UMS’s data-driven strategy, enabling secure, scalable, and business-aligned analytics across the university’s operations.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture and connectivity decisions for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), focusing on secure integration between on-premises SQL systems, the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), and Microsoft Fabric cloud services.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid network architecture for UMS that enables seamless, secure connectivity between existing on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric in the cloud. ## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway (OPDG) Design

Microsoft Fabric On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component that enables secure connectivity between UMS’s local data sources and Microsoft Fabric cloud services. The OPDG is installed on a dedicated VM, which acts as a proxy for all data transfers, ensuring that no direct inbound connections are required from the internet to UMS’s internal network.

**Definition:**  
Microsoft Fabric On-Premises Data Gateway is a software agent that securely transfers data between on-premises data sources (such as SQL Server) and Microsoft cloud services (including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure Analysis Services). It operates using outbound HTTPS connections, encrypting all data in transit and supporting enterprise authentication protocols.

For UMS, Enfrasys Solutions recommends deploying the OPDG VM in a network segment with restricted access, ensuring outbound-only connectivity to Microsoft endpoints. This minimizes risk and aligns with Azure networking best practices. All outbound traffic is governed by strict Network Security Group (NSG) rules, allowing only necessary ports and destinations.

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial deployment and configuration of the OPDG VM, including installation of required software and NSG rule setup. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall manage ongoing operations, monitoring, and maintenance of the gateway VM post-deployment.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are critical components in Azure’s security framework, providing granular control over inbound and outbound network traffic at the subnet and VM level. NSGs consist of rule-based access controls, enabling organizations to define which traffic is permitted or denied to and from Azure resources. Each rule specifies protocol, port, source, destination, and access action, ensuring only authorized communication is allowed.

For UMS, Enfrasys Solutions has designed outbound NSG rules to facilitate secure connectivity from the OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and essential Microsoft cloud services. These rules are tailored to support authentication, data transfer, and connectivity verification, all while enforcing Azure networking best practices. Outbound rules are prioritized to ensure that only necessary traffic is allowed, minimizing the attack surface and reducing risk.

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial configuration and validation of NSG rules during the deployment phase. UMS shall assume ongoing monitoring and periodic review responsibilities to ensure continued compliance and security posture. This division of responsibility guarantees that NSG rules remain effective and aligned with evolving operational requirements.

The following table presents the outbound NSG rules recommended for UMS:

| Name                       | Priority | Source                 | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                         | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|----------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services  | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication  | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160     | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                      | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules ensure that the OPDG VM can securely communicate with Microsoft services for data transfer, authentication, and connectivity checks. All traffic is encrypted in transit (see Section 7.2), and only essential endpoints are permitted, reducing exposure to external threats.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a foundational element of the security architecture for UMS’s analytics platform. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a dual-layered encryption approach: encryption at rest and encryption in transit, covering all data flows between SQL databases, OPDG, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI.

### Encryption at Rest

Encryption at rest protects data stored in Azure resources from unauthorized access and exposure. Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure SQL Database utilize Azure-managed encryption mechanisms, such as Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) and Transparent Data Encryption (TDE). These technologies ensure that all data stored within the platform, including backups and snapshots, are encrypted using strong AES-256 algorithms.

UMS shall ensure that all storage accounts, SQL databases, and workspace artifacts are configured with encryption at rest enabled. Enfrasys Solutions will validate these configurations during the initial rollout and provide guidance for ongoing compliance.

### Encryption in Transit

Encryption in transit safeguards data as it moves between components, preventing interception and tampering. All communications between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure SQL Database are conducted over HTTPS, leveraging SSL/TLS protocols. This includes:

- OPDG to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI: Outbound traffic is restricted to HTTPS (TCP port 443), ensuring data is encrypted during transfer.
- OPDG to Azure SQL Database: Data connections use encrypted SQL protocols (TLS 1.2+).
- User access to Power BI dashboards: All access occurs over HTTPS, protecting credentials and analytics data.
- Authentication and token exchange with Entra ID (Azure AD): All identity communications are encrypted via HTTPS.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure all endpoints to enforce encrypted connections and validate certificate integrity. UMS shall monitor for certificate expiration, enforce strong cipher suites, and ensure that any user or application access is restricted to secure channels.

### Responsibilities

The division of responsibilities is as follows:

- **Enfrasys Solutions:** Initial NSG rule configuration, encryption settings validation, and deployment of secure endpoints.
- **Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS):** Ongoing security monitoring, periodic review of NSG rules, certificate management, and incident response.

This collaborative approach ensures that UMS’s analytics environment remains secure, resilient, and compliant with institutional and regulatory standards. Enfrasys Solutions will provide operational handover documentation and training to UMS IT personnel to support continuous security management.

## 8.2 Pilot

The pilot phase serves as a controlled environment to validate the migration strategy, identify potential issues, and refine operational procedures before full-scale deployment. Enfrasys Solutions will initiate the pilot by configuring a subset of workloads within the newly established Fabric environment. This includes ingesting sample data from the staging area database, executing test data flows, and validating connectivity through the On-Premises Data Gateway.

UMS will participate by providing access to representative datasets and supporting user acceptance testing (UAT). Enfrasys Solutions will monitor system performance, security, and data integrity throughout the pilot, documenting any anomalies and recommending corrective actions. The pilot concludes with a joint review session, during which both parties assess outcomes and agree on readiness for production rollout.

This approach minimizes disruption and enables UMS to gain familiarity with the new platform, ensuring operational staff are equipped to manage future workloads.

## 8.3 Production

The production rollout is structured into distinct phases, each with defined timelines and responsibilities to ensure a smooth transition. Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following timeline:

- **D-7 (One Week Before Cutover):** Finalize environment configurations, validate data gateway connectivity, and confirm readiness of all migration assets. UMS is responsible for communicating scheduled downtime and migration plans to affected stakeholders.
- **D0 (Cutover Day):** Execute migration of production workloads, including data ingestion from the staging area database to Microsoft Fabric. Enfrasys Solutions will oversee the migration process, ensuring data fidelity and system stability. UMS will provide real-time support for any operational issues and validate post-migration data accuracy.
- **D+1 (Post-Cutover):** Conduct post-migration validation, monitor system performance, and address any residual issues. Enfrasys Solutions will provide immediate support, while UMS will facilitate user access and feedback collection.

This phased approach ensures that UMS’s data assets are transitioned with minimal risk and maximum transparency. The timeline below illustrates the key activities and responsible parties:

| Item         | Activities                                              | Action By         | Status       |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| D-7          | Environment finalization, stakeholder notification      | Enfrasys / UMS    | Pending      |
| D0           | Production workload migration, data validation          | Enfrasys / UMS    | Pending      |
| D+1          | Post-migration review, user access enablement           | Enfrasys / UMS    | Pending      |

## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support

Post-migration support is essential to ensure operational stability and knowledge transfer. Enfrasys Solutions will provide immediate post-migration assistance, monitoring system health, addressing technical issues, and supporting UMS staff during the initial transition period. This includes troubleshooting connectivity, validating data flows, and resolving user access concerns.

UMS will assume responsibility for routine operations once the environment is stabilized. Enfrasys Solutions will conduct a formal handover, including documentation of system configurations, operational procedures, and escalation paths. Training sessions will be provided to UMS’s IT staff to ensure proficiency in managing the new platform.

This structured support and handover process guarantees that UMS is equipped to sustain ongoing operations, maximize the value of the new solution, and maintain compliance with organizational policies.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.
