# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project’s business objectives, the scope of work, and the strategic alignment of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data modernization initiative with Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. It also outlines the purpose and intended audience of this Solution Design Document, and clarifies the respective roles of Enfrasys Solutions and UMS in successful project delivery.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has embarked on a strategic initiative to modernize its data and analytics landscape, aiming to enhance data-driven decision-making across academic and administrative domains. The primary objective of this project is to design and implement a robust data workflow that spans the entire lifecycle—from data ingestion and transformation to advanced analytics and visualization—leveraging Microsoft Fabric’s integrated platform.

The project scope encompasses the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored to UMS’s operational requirements. This includes the development of an end-to-end Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipeline, the execution of machine learning processes for predictive analytics, and the seamless integration of Power BI for interactive business intelligence and reporting. By adopting Microsoft Fabric, UMS will benefit from unified data integration (via Fabric Data Factory), scalable big data analytics (through Fabric Synapse), and advanced machine learning capabilities (enabled by Fabric Data Science). This strategic alignment ensures that UMS’s cloud adoption roadmap is future-proof, secure, and capable of supporting both current and emerging business needs.

Enfrasys Solutions will lead the architectural design, implementation, and knowledge transfer activities, while UMS will provide business requirements, subject matter expertise, and operational support throughout the project lifecycle. This collaborative approach ensures that the solution is both technically sound and aligned with UMS’s institutional objectives.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this Solution Design Document is to provide a comprehensive and formal blueprint for the implementation of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI within Universiti Malaysia Sabah. It details the technical architecture, workflow design, security considerations, and operational processes required to deliver an enterprise-grade analytics platform.

This document serves as the authoritative reference for all stakeholders involved in the project, ensuring clarity on solution components, integration points, and deployment methodologies. It is structured to guide both the implementation team at Enfrasys Solutions and the IT and business teams at UMS through each phase of the project, from initial setup to post-deployment support. By codifying design decisions and best practices, this document mitigates risk, supports compliance, and provides a foundation for future scalability and innovation.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for the following audiences:

- UMS IT Department: Responsible for operationalizing, maintaining, and supporting the deployed Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment.
- UMS Business Stakeholders: Including academic and administrative leaders who will leverage analytics for strategic and operational decision-making.
- Enfrasys Solutions Architects and Consultants: Accountable for solution design, technical implementation, and knowledge transfer.
- Project Sponsors and Governance Committees: Ensuring alignment with UMS’s digital transformation strategy and compliance with institutional policies.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for delivering the technical architecture, conducting implementation activities, and providing training and documentation. UMS is responsible for supplying business requirements, facilitating access to data sources, and providing ongoing operational support. This clear delineation of roles ensures accountability and effective project execution.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview

This section provides an authoritative overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, establishing their roles and integration within Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data analytics and business intelligence architecture.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform designed to unify data engineering, data integration, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single, cohesive environment. Fabric provides a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) experience, enabling organizations to manage their data estate efficiently, from ingestion through transformation to advanced analytics and visualization. Core services within Microsoft Fabric include Data Factory, Synapse, and Data Science, each delivering specialized capabilities that together enable end-to-end data workflows.

Data Factory within Fabric is responsible for data integration and orchestration, allowing seamless ingestion of data from diverse sources into the platform. This ensures that UMS can efficiently extract, load, and transform data from its Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse into the Fabric environment. Synapse, as part of Fabric, provides advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, empowering UMS to perform large-scale data transformations and complex analytical queries with high performance. The Data Science component enables the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence directly within the platform, supporting both automated and custom model development for predictive analytics.

By adopting Microsoft Fabric, Universiti Malaysia Sabah benefits from a unified analytics ecosystem. This approach breaks down silos between data engineering, data science, and business intelligence teams, streamlines governance, and accelerates the delivery of actionable insights. Fabric’s deep integration with Microsoft’s security and compliance frameworks ensures that UMS’s sensitive academic and operational data remains protected throughout the analytics lifecycle.

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data workflow within the UMS Fabric environment, highlighting the movement of data from ingestion through transformation and ultimately to visualization.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: UMS Data Processing and Analytics Architecture in Microsoft Fabric

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business analytics service that enables organizations to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decision-making. Power BI provides interactive dashboards, paginated reports, and self-service analytics capabilities, empowering users at all levels to access and interpret data relevant to their roles. As a cloud-based platform, Power BI integrates seamlessly with Microsoft Fabric, leveraging the same security, compliance, and data governance standards.

Within the UMS solution, Power BI connects directly to the Semantic Model hosted in Fabric via OneLake, Microsoft’s unified data lake storage layer. This integration allows UMS to visualize cleansed and transformed data from the Gold Lakehouse layer, ensuring that reports and dashboards are always based on the most current and accurate data. Power BI Desktop is used for authoring and modeling, while the Power BI service facilitates sharing and collaboration across academic and administrative departments.

The integration of Power BI with Fabric ensures that UMS’s analytics environment is both robust and agile. Data lineage is preserved from ingestion to visualization, supporting auditability and compliance. This architecture enables rapid prototyping, iterative analytics, and the democratization of data-driven decision-making across the university.

The following diagram depicts the machine learning workflow within Fabric, demonstrating how both automated and manual ML processes feed into the analytics pipeline and ultimately surface insights through Power BI.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: AutoML and Manual Machine Learning Workflow Integration with Power BI

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. Entra ID provides secure authentication, authorization, and identity governance for users, applications, and resources across the Microsoft ecosystem. It is a foundational component for enforcing access controls, managing user lifecycles, and integrating with both on-premises and cloud applications.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Entra ID plays a critical role in securing the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. All user access to Fabric workspaces, data assets, and Power BI reports is governed through Entra ID, ensuring that only authorized personnel can view, modify, or administer sensitive information. Entra ID supports multi-factor authentication, conditional access policies, and role-based access control (RBAC), which are essential for meeting the university’s security and compliance requirements.

By leveraging Entra ID, UMS benefits from centralized identity management, streamlined onboarding and offboarding processes, and consistent enforcement of security policies across all data and analytics workloads. This approach minimizes the risk of unauthorized access and ensures that the university’s data governance standards are upheld at every stage of the analytics lifecycle.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section defines the comprehensive network architecture for the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment, with a focus on secure connectivity between on-premises systems and Microsoft Fabric. The design leverages the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) to ensure seamless, secure, and scalable data integration.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid network architecture that securely bridges UMS’s on-premises SQL Server environment with Microsoft Fabric in the cloud. The core of this connectivity is the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), which acts as a secure conduit for data transfers between the UMS SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse and Microsoft Fabric services.

The OPDG is deployed within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) in the UMS on-premises environment. This architecture ensures that sensitive data remains protected within the UMS network perimeter until explicitly transferred to authorized Microsoft Fabric endpoints. The gateway initiates outbound-only connections, which means no inbound ports are opened on the UMS firewall—significantly reducing the attack surface and aligning with best practices for defense-in-depth.

This architecture supports robust data integration scenarios, enabling UMS to leverage the advanced analytics and reporting capabilities of Microsoft Fabric while maintaining strict control over data egress. By centralizing all data movement through the OPDG, UMS gains enhanced visibility and control over data flows, compliance, and auditability.

The following diagram illustrates the secure data flow between the UMS on-premises SQL Server, the On-Premises Data Gateway, and Microsoft Fabric. Data originates in the UMS Staging Area (SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse), is securely transmitted via the OPDG, and reaches UMS Fabric in the cloud. All connectivity is outbound from the UMS network, ensuring that no external entities can initiate connections into the UMS environment.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Secure data flow from UMS SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via On-Premises Data Gateway.

## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway

Microsoft’s On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component for hybrid data integration. The gateway is a lightweight agent installed on a Windows-based VM within the UMS network. It enables secure, encrypted outbound connections to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services, acting as a bridge between on-premises data sources and cloud-based analytics platforms.

The OPDG is designed for enterprise-grade security and reliability. All communications are outbound over HTTPS (port 443), eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules. This outbound-only model ensures that the UMS network remains protected from unsolicited external access, while still enabling seamless data transfer to Microsoft Fabric.

Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the deployment and configuration of the OPDG, including all gateway software installation, registration with Microsoft Fabric, and validation of connectivity to cloud endpoints. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for preparing the on-premises environment, including provisioning the VM according to the specifications below, ensuring network egress to required Microsoft endpoints, and coordinating with internal IT security teams to permit outbound HTTPS traffic.

The following table outlines the recommended VM specifications for hosting the On-Premises Data Gateway. These specifications are based on Microsoft’s latest guidance and are designed to deliver optimal performance, reliability, and scalability for UMS’s anticipated data workloads.

| Component         | Specification                                   |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Operating System  | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework    | Version 4.8                                    |
| vCPU              | 8 cores                                        |
| RAM               | Minimum 8 GB                                   |

The OPDG VM must be granted outbound internet access to specific Microsoft service endpoints. All required network rules are strictly outbound, ensuring that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data securely using SSL/TLS encryption. No inbound ports are permitted, further reducing the risk of unauthorized access.

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI utilize a robust role-based access control (RBAC) model to safeguard data and delegate responsibilities efficiently. - **Viewer**: Read-only access to published reports and dashboards. Assigned to stakeholders, project directors, and other decision-makers requiring insights without edit privileges.

This RBAC model ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah can enforce the principle of least privilege, reduce the risk of accidental data exposure, and streamline operational workflows. ## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

Machine learning workloads are integrated using AutoML and manual notebook-based approaches, with results stored in the Gold layer for downstream analytics. ## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are critical components for controlling network traffic to and from Azure resources. NSGs allow granular control over inbound and outbound network communications by defining rules based on source, destination, port, and protocol. For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing NSGs to enforce a zero-trust network posture, ensuring only explicitly allowed traffic can traverse the environment.

The NSG rules for the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine are designed to facilitate secure communication with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and essential Microsoft cloud endpoints. These rules are strictly limited to necessary services, minimizing the attack surface and ensuring compliance with Azure networking best practices. Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the configuration and ongoing management of these NSG rules, ensuring that all changes are documented and validated against UMS’s security policies.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a foundational element of the security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Microsoft Fabric deployment. Enfrasys Solutions recommends and implements encryption for data at rest and in transit across all relevant services, including Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG).

### Encryption at Rest

All data stored within Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and associated Azure services is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys, leveraging Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) and Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) where applicable. This ensures that any data persisted in storage accounts, databases, or OneLake repositories is protected from unauthorized access, even in the event of physical compromise of the underlying storage infrastructure.

For the OPDG VM, Azure Disk Encryption is enabled, utilizing BitLocker (for Windows) or DM-Crypt (for Linux) to secure the operating system and data disks. This measure guarantees that sensitive data processed or cached by the gateway remains encrypted on the VM.

### Encryption in Transit

Data in transit between UMS’s on-premises environment, the OPDG VM, and Microsoft cloud services is protected using industry-standard Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocols. All communications to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and authentication endpoints occur over HTTPS (TCP port 443), ensuring confidentiality and integrity of the data as it traverses public and private networks.

Conditional Access policies, when available, further enhance in-transit security by enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and restricting access based on user and device context. Although UMS currently does not meet the licensing requirements for advanced Conditional Access policies, MFA is enforced at the tenant level, providing an additional layer of protection against unauthorized access.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project’s business objectives, scope, and the intended use and audience for this Solution Design Document.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has embarked on a strategic initiative to modernize its data analytics capabilities by implementing Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric. The primary business objective is to enable data-driven decision-making across the university through a robust, scalable, and secure analytics platform. This project encompasses the design and implementation of a comprehensive data workflow that spans data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization. The scope includes the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace, the development of end-to-end ETL pipelines using Fabric Data Factory, execution of advanced analytics with Fabric Synapse, and the integration of Power BI for business-aligned reporting and insights.

The high-level goals of this initiative are to:
- Streamline data integration and orchestration processes using Fabric Data Factory.
- Leverage Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, empowering UMS to handle complex data workloads efficiently.
- Facilitate machine learning applications to support predictive analytics and academic research.
- Deliver actionable business intelligence through Power BI, ensuring that stakeholders at all levels have timely access to relevant data.
- Align UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft’s best practices for security, scalability, and operational excellence.

By adopting this architecture, UMS aims to enhance its analytical maturity, improve operational efficiency, and foster a culture of data-driven innovation across the institution.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to provide a comprehensive technical blueprint for the implementation of Microsoft Power BI and Fabric at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. It serves as the authoritative reference for all design decisions, architectural patterns, and security controls adopted throughout the project. This document is intended to facilitate thorough review and formal sign-off by both UMS and Enfrasys Solutions, ensuring that all requirements are met and risks are addressed prior to implementation. Additionally, it will serve as an ongoing technical reference for UMS IT personnel, project sponsors, and support teams throughout the lifecycle of the solution.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This Solution Design Document is intended for the following audiences:
- UMS IT Department: Technical leads, system administrators, and support engineers responsible for managing and maintaining the Power BI and Fabric environment.
- UMS Business Stakeholders: Department heads, data analysts, and decision-makers who will leverage the analytics platform for operational and strategic insights.
- Enfrasys Solutions Architects and Consultants: The design, implementation, and support team responsible for delivering the solution in accordance with best practices.
- Project Sponsors and Executive Leadership: Senior management overseeing the project’s alignment with organizational goals and compliance requirements.

Responsibility for document review and formal sign-off is jointly assigned to Universiti Malaysia Sabah and Enfrasys Solutions, ensuring all technical, operational, and business requirements are validated and approved prior to project execution.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric and Power BI Overview

This section provides Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) with a comprehensive overview of the core Microsoft technologies forming the foundation of the proposed data platform. Enfrasys Solutions recommends this section as essential reading to ensure all stakeholders understand the technology stack, its capabilities, and its alignment with UMS’s business objectives.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Fabric enables organizations to break down data silos by providing a cohesive set of experiences for data professionals, including data engineers, data scientists, and business analysts.

At the heart of Microsoft Fabric are several core services that collectively address the entire data lifecycle:

- **Data Factory**: This service provides robust data integration and orchestration capabilities. It allows for the ingestion of data from diverse sources, both on-premises and in the cloud, and supports the creation of complex ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines. Data Factory ensures that data is efficiently collected, cleansed, and made available for downstream analytics.
- **Synapse**: Fabric Synapse offers advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities. It enables large-scale data transformation, interactive data exploration, and supports both batch and real-time analytics workloads. Synapse empowers UMS to derive actionable insights from vast datasets through a familiar, unified workspace.
- **Data Science**: The Data Science experience in Fabric provides a collaborative environment for building, training, and deploying machine learning models. It supports the entire machine learning lifecycle, from data preparation to model operationalization, enabling UMS to leverage predictive analytics and AutoML workflows for advanced business scenarios.
- **OneLake**: OneLake is the unified data lake storage layer for Microsoft Fabric. It centralizes all organizational data in a single, secure, and scalable repository, facilitating seamless data access and collaboration across Fabric services.

By adopting Microsoft Fabric, UMS benefits from a modern, cloud-native data platform that accelerates time-to-insight, reduces operational complexity, and enhances data governance through integrated security and compliance features.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s industry-leading business intelligence and data visualization platform. It empowers users to connect to a wide range of data sources, transform raw data into interactive dashboards and reports, and share insights across the organization in a secure and governed manner.

A key advantage of Power BI is its deep integration with Microsoft Fabric. Through this integration, Power BI can natively connect to data stored and processed within Fabric’s OneLake, Data Factory, and Synapse environments. This seamless connectivity allows UMS to visualize data in near real-time, ensuring that decision-makers have access to the latest insights derived from the ETL and machine learning processes orchestrated within Fabric.

The combination of Power BI and Microsoft Fabric provides UMS with an end-to-end analytics solution—from data ingestion and transformation, through advanced analytics and machine learning, to intuitive, business-aligned visualizations. This integrated approach eliminates data silos, improves data quality, and streamlines the delivery of actionable intelligence to stakeholders across the university.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on (SSO), and role-based access control (RBAC) for users, applications, and resources within the Microsoft ecosystem.

Within the context of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, Entra ID plays a critical role in safeguarding UMS’s data assets. It ensures that only authorized personnel can access sensitive data, analytics workspaces, and machine learning resources. Entra ID supports granular permission assignment, conditional access policies, and seamless integration with on-premises Active Directory, enabling UMS to enforce organizational security policies and regulatory compliance requirements.

Enfrasys Solutions assigns responsibility for the definition and configuration of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Entra ID to its solution architects, ensuring that UMS’s technology stack is designed according to industry best practices and tailored to the university’s unique operational needs. UMS is responsible for providing directory information, user role definitions, and participating in access control reviews to ensure alignment with institutional policies.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section details the network architecture, connectivity, and gateway deployment for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Microsoft Fabric implementation. The design emphasizes secure, efficient integration between on-premises resources and cloud services.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid network architecture that ensures secure, reliable connectivity between Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s on-premises data infrastructure and Microsoft Azure cloud services. This architecture is designed to protect sensitive university data while enabling seamless data movement and analytics within Microsoft Fabric.

The core principle of the proposed network design is the use of outbound-only connections from the on-premises environment to the cloud. By restricting all traffic to outbound connections, Universiti Malaysia Sabah eliminates the need to open inbound ports on its firewall, significantly reducing the attack surface and mitigating the risk of unauthorized access. This approach aligns with industry best practices for hybrid cloud security, ensuring that data transfers are initiated only from trusted, internal sources.

In this architecture, data originating from the on-premises Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse is securely transmitted to the Azure environment via the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, facilitating communication between the university’s data warehouse and cloud-based Microsoft Fabric components. All data transfers leverage encrypted outbound connections, ensuring data confidentiality and integrity during transit. This design supports compliance with Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s internal security policies and regulatory requirements.

The network also incorporates Azure Conditional Access policies through Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory). These policies enforce granular access control, evaluating user and device context before granting access to Microsoft Fabric resources. By integrating conditional access, the university ensures that only authorized users—whether internal or external—can access sensitive data and analytics tools, further strengthening the overall security posture.

The following diagram illustrates the secure network flow, conditional access enforcement, and the interaction between on-premises infrastructure and Microsoft Fabric services.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 4.1: Conditional access flow for Microsoft Fabric authentication and data access.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 4.2: Data flow from on-premises SQL Server through the On-Premises Data Gateway to Microsoft Fabric.

## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway

Microsoft Fabric On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component for hybrid data integration. The OPDG enables secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric services in the cloud. It acts as a bridge, allowing cloud services such as Power BI, Azure Data Factory, and Microsoft Fabric to access data residing within the university’s internal network without exposing those resources to the public internet.

Enfrasys Solutions will design the OPDG deployment to ensure optimal performance, high availability, and robust security. The gateway will be installed on a dedicated virtual machine within the university’s on-premises infrastructure. This VM will be configured to initiate only outbound connections to Azure, eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules and thereby reducing the risk of external threats.

Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for providing the necessary on-premises infrastructure, including the virtual machine and network configuration details. Enfrasys Solutions will supply deployment guidance, configuration best practices, and ongoing support to ensure a smooth integration process.

The following table outlines the recommended specifications for the virtual machine hosting the On-Premises Data Gateway. These specifications are based on Microsoft’s best practices to ensure reliable operation and support for anticipated data workloads.

| Component         | Specification                                   |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Operating System  | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework    | Version 4.8                                    |
| vCPU              | 8 cores                                        |
| RAM               | Minimum 8 GB                                   |

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the design, deployment guidance, and configuration of the Data Gateway. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall provision the virtual machine according to the specifications above and provide detailed network and infrastructure information to facilitate a secure and efficient deployment.

This approach ensures a robust, scalable, and secure foundation for hybrid data integration, supporting Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s analytics and reporting objectives within Microsoft Fabric.

# 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI

This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and access assignments for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) personnel within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environments. Proper role assignment is critical to ensure secure, efficient, and auditable data operations.

## 5.1 Microsoft Fabric Administrator Role

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence across the Microsoft ecosystem. The Fabric Administrator, often referred to as the Data Engineer in organizational contexts, is responsible for the secure and effective management of Fabric resources, workspace governance, and data pipeline orchestration.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS assign Fabric Administrator privileges only to experienced personnel with a comprehensive understanding of data governance, security, and platform operations. The Fabric Administrator role carries significant responsibilities, including the creation and management of workspaces, assignment of workspace roles, configuration of data pipelines, and enforcement of security and compliance policies. Administrators are also responsible for monitoring platform usage, managing user access, and ensuring that data assets are protected according to UMS’s internal policies and regulatory requirements.

By centralizing these responsibilities, UMS ensures that data assets remain secure, operational risks are minimized, and platform changes are properly authorized and documented. Enfrasys Solutions will provide guidance and best practices for the ongoing management and review of administrator assignments.

## 5.2 Microsoft Fabric-native Roles

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI provide a set of native workspace roles to facilitate granular access control and operational separation. These roles are designed to align with common organizational responsibilities and data access needs. The primary native roles include Workspace Admin, Contributor, and Viewer.

Workspace Admins have full control over workspace settings, user assignments, and data assets within the workspace. Contributors are empowered to create, modify, and manage datasets, reports, and pipelines but do not have authority over workspace-level security or administrative settings. Viewers are granted read-only access, enabling them to consume published reports and dashboards without the ability to alter underlying data or resources.

This role-based access model enhances security by enforcing the principle of least privilege, ensuring that users are only granted permissions necessary for their job functions. It also streamlines operational workflows and supports clear audit trails for data access and modification. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS periodically review role assignments to maintain alignment with evolving organizational structures and project requirements.

# 6.0 Microsoft Fabric and Power BI Design and Decision

## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

A well-architected data workflow is essential for UMS to ensure data reliability, integrity, and accessibility from ingestion through to advanced analytics and visualization. The workflow must support various workload types, including data engineering, data science, and business intelligence, while maintaining clear separation of raw, cleansed, and transformed data. Enfrasys Solutions has carefully considered the end-to-end data journey, from the initial extraction of data from on-premises SQL Server, through multi-layered Lakehouse storage, to advanced analytics and Power BI visualization.

Key considerations include the use of Azure Data Factory for orchestrating data movement, the implementation of Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers for progressive data refinement, and the integration of both automated and manual machine learning workflows. The design also ensures that all modeled and scored data is centrally stored and made available for semantic modeling and business reporting. These considerations collectively support scalability, maintainability, and future extensibility for UMS’s analytics initiatives.

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions

Microsoft Fabric is a comprehensive analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data integration, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single SaaS experience. Fabric’s Lakehouse architecture, coupled with Power BI, provides UMS with a scalable, high-performance environment for modern analytics workloads.

The selected architecture utilizes a multi-layered Lakehouse pattern (Bronze, Silver, Gold) to ensure data quality and traceability. Data is ingested from the on-premises SQL Server via Azure Data Factory and the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), then processed through the Bronze (raw), Silver (cleansed), and Gold (transformed) layers. Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query tools are employed for transformation and enrichment. For machine learning, both AutoML and manual notebook-driven workflows are supported, with results stored in the Gold layer. Semantic models are built on top of the Gold Lakehouse and exposed via OneLake to Power BI for visualization.

This approach enables UMS to maintain a clear lineage of data, enforce governance standards, and facilitate both self-service and advanced analytics. The architecture supports future expansion, such as deeper integration with Azure ML or advanced governance tools, without disrupting existing workflows.

## 6.3 Access Design Considerations and Decisions

Securing access to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI is critical to protecting UMS’s sensitive data assets. The platform leverages Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) for identity and access management, ensuring that only authenticated and authorized users can interact with data resources. While Conditional Access policies provide granular control over user access based on risk signals and context, current licensing constraints at UMS preclude their immediate implementation. Instead, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enforced at the tenant level to enhance security posture.

### 6.3.1 Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a feature of Microsoft Entra ID that evaluates user sign-in attempts based on signals such as user identity, device compliance, location, and risk. It can enforce policies such as requiring MFA or blocking access under certain conditions. For UMS, Conditional Access is not currently available due to the absence of the necessary Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses. Enfrasys Solutions recommends revisiting this approach in the future as licensing and security needs evolve.

### 6.3.2 Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Given the ineligibility for Conditional Access, MFA is enforced at the tenant level for all UMS users. MFA significantly reduces the risk of unauthorized access by requiring users to provide a second form of verification in addition to their password. This approach ensures that only legitimate users can access sensitive analytics and data assets, even if credentials are compromised. Enfrasys Solutions strongly recommends maintaining tenant-wide MFA enforcement as a baseline security measure.

### 6.3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud-based identity and access management service that underpins authentication for Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and other Azure resources. It centralizes user management, supports MFA, and—when appropriately licensed—enables Conditional Access for advanced security controls. All user provisioning, access assignments, and authentication flows for UMS’s analytics platform are managed through Entra ID, ensuring a unified security perimeter.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

This section defines the security architecture and supporting controls for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment, with a particular focus on network security, encryption, and compliance responsibilities.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

A Network Security Group (NSG) in Microsoft Azure is a fundamental security component that enables organizations to control inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources at the subnet or network interface level. NSGs use rules to permit or deny traffic based on factors such as source/destination IP address, port, and protocol, thereby reducing the attack surface and enforcing least-privilege access.

For the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine, Enfrasys Solutions has designed a set of outbound NSG rules to ensure secure communication with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and essential Microsoft cloud services. These rules are crafted to enable only the minimum necessary connectivity, using secure protocols and restricting destination endpoints to trusted Microsoft domains. This approach not only supports the operational needs of the OPDG but also aligns with Azure networking best practices and the principle of defense-in-depth.

By implementing these NSG rules, UMS benefits from enhanced security posture, reduced risk of unauthorized access, and improved visibility over network flows. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for defining and implementing these security controls, while UMS is tasked with reviewing them to ensure alignment with institutional compliance and governance requirements.

The following table details the specific NSG outbound rules for the OPDG VM:

| Name                         | Priority | Source                  | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                      | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|------------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services    | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication    | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                  | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules collectively ensure that only secure, necessary traffic is permitted outbound from the OPDG VM, thereby supporting both operational requirements and security best practices.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a critical pillar of the overall security architecture for any cloud-based analytics and data platform. Microsoft Fabric and Power BI leverage robust encryption mechanisms to protect data both in transit and at rest, ensuring confidentiality and integrity throughout the data lifecycle.

Encryption in transit is achieved through the use of industry-standard protocols such as HTTPS and SSL/TLS. All communications between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and supporting Microsoft cloud services are secured using HTTPS over TCP port 443. This ensures that sensitive data, authentication credentials, and configuration information are protected from interception or tampering during transmission over public and private networks. The NSG rules defined above further enforce this by allowing only encrypted traffic to the necessary Microsoft endpoints.

Encryption at rest is provided by Microsoft Fabric’s OneLake storage platform, which utilizes Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) with Microsoft-managed keys by default. All data stored within OneLake—including datasets, reports, and dataflows—is automatically encrypted using strong cryptographic algorithms (e.g., AES-256). This ensures that data remains protected even if storage media are compromised. Additionally, Microsoft Fabric supports integration with Azure Key Vault for customer-managed keys, offering UMS the flexibility to enhance control over encryption key management if required by compliance policies.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and implementing the necessary encryption controls, including the configuration of HTTPS/SSL for all data flows and validation of at-rest encryption settings within Microsoft Fabric and OneLake. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for reviewing these controls to ensure they meet the university’s data protection, privacy, and regulatory compliance requirements. This collaborative approach ensures that both operational security and institutional governance objectives are met.

## 8.2 Pilot

Enfrasys Solutions will lead the deployment of a controlled pilot, ingesting a subset of data from the staging area database into the Fabric environment. This pilot will test the connectivity established through the On-Premises Data Gateway, validate data transformation processes, and confirm that security controls are functioning as intended.

During the pilot, UMS is responsible for providing access to the necessary data sources and promptly addressing any data quality or connectivity issues identified. Enfrasys Solutions will monitor system performance, document any issues, and coordinate remediation steps. Upon successful completion of the pilot, both parties will jointly review outcomes and sign off on readiness to proceed to production.

## 8.3 Production

The production rollout is executed in a phased manner to minimize disruption and ensure a smooth transition. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a structured timeline, with key milestones as follows:

- **D-7 (One week before cutover):** Final validation of pilot outcomes, user communication, and scheduling of migration activities. UMS is responsible for notifying all relevant stakeholders and ensuring that no changes are made to source systems during the migration window.
- **D0 (Cutover Day):** Enfrasys Solutions will execute the migration of all agreed data sets into the Microsoft Fabric production environment. System integration, data validation, and initial user acceptance testing are performed in close coordination with UMS.
- **D+1 (Post-migration):** Immediate post-migration support is provided by Enfrasys Solutions to address any issues, finalize user acceptance, and ensure business continuity. UMS validates data integrity and system accessibility.

This phased approach reduces risk, provides clear communication checkpoints, and ensures that both technical and business requirements are met before the solution is fully operational.

## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support

After the production cutover, Enfrasys Solutions provides dedicated post-migration support to address any residual issues and facilitate knowledge transfer to UMS personnel. This includes system monitoring, troubleshooting, and performance tuning to ensure optimal operation of the Microsoft Fabric environment.

A formal handover process is conducted, during which Enfrasys Solutions delivers all relevant documentation, operational runbooks, and conducts training sessions for UMS administrators and users. UMS is responsible for validating that all operational requirements are met and for assuming ownership of day-to-day management tasks upon completion of the support period.

This structured approach ensures a smooth transition, minimizes operational risk, and empowers UMS to maximize the value of their Microsoft Fabric investment.

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a high-level overview of the project, the intent of this Solution Design Document, and its intended audience, with a focus on Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s strategic adoption of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is undertaking a transformative initiative to modernize its data analytics capabilities by adopting Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The primary business objective is to establish a robust, scalable, and secure data platform that enables end-to-end data workflows—from ingestion and transformation to advanced analytics and visualization. This project encompasses the design and implementation of a Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored to UMS’s operational and business requirements.

The project scope includes the development of comprehensive Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipelines, the integration of machine learning processes, and the deployment of business-aligned analytics dashboards using Power BI. By leveraging Microsoft Fabric’s core services—such as Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and integrated Data Science capabilities for machine learning—UMS aims to enhance decision-making, operational efficiency, and academic research outcomes.

The high-level goals of this initiative are to align UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with the latest advancements in Microsoft Fabric, ensure seamless data integration across diverse sources, enable advanced analytics, and provide intuitive, role-based data visualizations for stakeholders across the university.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The Solution Design Document serves as the authoritative reference for the architecture, technical decisions, and implementation approach for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment. Its primary intent is to provide a comprehensive blueprint that guides all stakeholders through the review, approval, and execution phases of the project.

This document details the proposed infrastructure, workflow designs, security considerations, and operational processes. It is structured to facilitate informed decision-making, ensure alignment with UMS’s business objectives, and support compliance with best practices and regulatory requirements. The Solution Design Document is to be used for formal review and sign-off by both Universiti Malaysia Sabah and Enfrasys Solutions, establishing a mutual understanding and agreement on the technical direction prior to implementation.

Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah share joint responsibility for the review and sign-off of this document. Enfrasys Solutions is accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the technical design, while UMS is responsible for validating alignment with institutional requirements and strategic objectives.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This Solution Design Document is intended for a diverse audience comprising both technical and business stakeholders. The primary readers include:

- UMS IT leadership and technical teams responsible for data platform management, integration, and security.
- UMS business stakeholders and academic leaders who will leverage analytics insights for strategic and operational decision-making.
- The Enfrasys Solutions project team, including architects, engineers, and consultants tasked with delivering the solution.

By addressing the needs and perspectives of these groups, the document ensures that all parties are equipped with the necessary information to support successful project delivery, risk mitigation, and ongoing platform governance. Both UMS and Enfrasys Solutions are responsible for reviewing and endorsing the content, thereby ensuring collective ownership of the solution’s design and implementation.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of the core Microsoft technologies forming the foundation of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data platform solution: Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID. Enfrasys Solutions delivers these technology overviews to ensure a clear understanding of each component’s purpose, capabilities, and integration within the overall architecture. UMS is responsible for reviewing and validating these descriptions for alignment with institutional standards and requirements.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, engineering, science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Microsoft Fabric streamlines the process of ingesting, transforming, storing, and analyzing data by providing a suite of tightly integrated services, each tailored for a specific aspect of the data lifecycle. The core services within Microsoft Fabric include:

- **Data Factory**: A robust data integration and orchestration service, Data Factory enables the ingestion of data from diverse sources, including on-premises databases and cloud repositories. It supports the creation of data pipelines for seamless extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) processes, ensuring data is reliably moved and prepared for downstream analytics.
- **Synapse**: Synapse delivers advanced data analytics and big data processing capabilities. It provides a unified analytics workspace where data engineers and analysts can perform large-scale data exploration, transformation, and aggregation using both serverless and provisioned resources.
- **Data Science**: The Data Science component empowers users to develop, train, and operationalize machine learning models directly within the Fabric environment. It supports both automated machine learning (AutoML) and custom notebook-driven experimentation, facilitating advanced analytics and predictive modeling.
- **OneLake**: OneLake is a unified, enterprise-grade data lake that serves as the central storage layer for all data assets within Fabric. It provides a single point of access for structured and unstructured data, supporting efficient data sharing, governance, and management across the organization.

By leveraging Microsoft Fabric, UMS benefits from a cohesive analytics ecosystem that eliminates data silos, simplifies operational complexity, and accelerates time-to-insight. The platform’s native integration between services ensures that data flows seamlessly from ingestion to transformation, machine learning, and visualization, all governed by a consistent security and compliance framework.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise business intelligence and data visualization platform, designed to enable organizations to transform raw data into actionable insights through interactive dashboards and reports. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, allowing users to connect directly to curated datasets, semantic models, and dataflows stored in OneLake or processed through Fabric’s ETL and data science pipelines.

Within the UMS solution, Power BI serves as the primary interface for business users, analysts, and decision-makers to explore, analyze, and present data. The integration with Fabric ensures that Power BI has real-time access to the latest, business-ready data residing in the Gold Lakehouse layer, as well as advanced analytics outputs generated by machine learning models. This direct connectivity streamlines the process of building and sharing insights, ensuring that all stakeholders operate from a single source of truth.

The synergy between Power BI and Fabric delivers several key benefits to UMS:
- **Seamless Data Access**: Power BI can connect to Fabric’s semantic models via Direct Lake (OneLake), eliminating the need for complex data exports or duplications.
- **Advanced Analytics Integration**: Outputs from machine learning experiments and data science workflows are readily available for visualization and operationalization.
- **Enterprise Security**: Power BI leverages the same access controls and governance policies enforced by Fabric and Entra ID, ensuring secure and compliant analytics.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service, providing secure authentication, authorization, and identity governance for users, devices, and applications. Entra ID is foundational to the security architecture of the UMS data platform, underpinning access management for all Fabric and Power BI resources.

In the context of this solution, Entra ID serves several critical roles:
- **Authentication and Single Sign-On (SSO)**: Users authenticate to Fabric and Power BI using their institutional credentials, ensuring a seamless and secure experience.
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Entra ID enables granular assignment of permissions, ensuring that only authorized users can access sensitive data, manage workspaces, or perform administrative tasks.
- **Conditional Access and Compliance**: Entra ID supports advanced security policies, such as multi-factor authentication (MFA) and conditional access, to enforce compliance and protect against unauthorized access.

By standardizing on Entra ID, UMS ensures that all users and administrators interact with the data platform within a secure, governed, and auditable environment. This approach reduces the risk of data breaches, simplifies user lifecycle management, and aligns with best practices for cloud security.

## 3.4 Technology Summary Table

The following table summarizes the core technologies, their primary purposes, and their roles within the UMS solution. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for providing these technology overviews, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is tasked with reviewing and confirming their applicability.

| Technology         | Purpose                                                        | Role in UMS Solution                                         |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Fabric   | Unified analytics platform for data integration, engineering, science, and BI | Foundation for end-to-end data workflows, ETL, ML, and analytics |
| Data Factory       | Data ingestion and orchestration                               | Ingests and prepares data from SQL Server to Fabric Lakehouses |
| Synapse            | Advanced analytics and big data processing                     | Enables large-scale data transformation and aggregation        |
| Data Science       | Machine learning development and operationalization            | Facilitates AutoML and custom ML workflows                    |
| OneLake            | Centralized enterprise data lake                              | Stores all raw, refined, and business-ready data              |
| Power BI           | Business intelligence and data visualization                   | Delivers dashboards, reports, and insights to business users  |
| Microsoft Entra ID | Identity and access management                                | Secures access to Fabric and Power BI resources               |

Enfrasys Solutions will continue to provide guidance and best practices for the adoption and integration of these technologies. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall review the technology stack to ensure alignment with institutional requirements and strategic objectives.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section details the network architecture and connectivity decisions for the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment, focusing on secure, reliable integration between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric in the cloud.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

A robust network topology is essential to ensure seamless data flow and secure communication between UMS’s on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric in Azure. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid architecture that leverages outbound-only connectivity for all cloud integrations, thereby reducing the attack surface and aligning with best practices for cloud security.

The overall topology consists of UMS’s on-premises data center, where critical data assets such as the SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse reside, and the Azure cloud environment, where Microsoft Fabric services are provisioned. Connectivity between these environments is facilitated by the Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), which acts as a secure bridge for data transfer. The OPDG is deployed within a dedicated virtual machine in the UMS data center, ensuring that all communication with Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft cloud services is initiated outbound from the trusted internal network. This design eliminates the need for inbound firewall exceptions, thereby minimizing exposure to external threats.

Outbound-only connections are a critical security measure, as they ensure that all traffic from the OPDG to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services is encrypted via HTTPS. This approach also simplifies firewall configuration and supports compliance with UMS’s internal IT security policies. Enfrasys Solutions will document the network design and required firewall rules, while UMS is responsible for providing detailed on-premises network topology information to ensure compatibility and optimal performance.

## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway

The Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a core component of the hybrid data integration strategy. The OPDG enables secure, high-throughput communication between UMS’s on-premises SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse and Microsoft Fabric services in Azure. By deploying the gateway within a dedicated virtual machine, UMS ensures that sensitive data is transmitted securely without the need for inbound network access.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends the OPDG be installed on a Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) or Windows 10 (64-bit) virtual machine, provisioned with sufficient CPU and memory resources to handle anticipated data loads. The gateway leverages the .NET Framework 4.8 runtime and is optimized for environments where data privacy and regulatory compliance are paramount. The VM must be configured to allow only outbound HTTPS (TCP port 443) and HTTP (TCP port 80, for connectivity checks) traffic to specific Microsoft endpoints, as detailed in the network security group (NSG) rules.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing, documenting, and validating the OPDG deployment and associated network rules. UMS must provide detailed on-premises network information, including IP addressing, firewall configuration, and routing details, to facilitate seamless integration and support troubleshooting.

The following table summarizes the recommended VM specifications for hosting the OPDG:

| Component         | Specification                                  |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Operating System  | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework    | Version 4.8                                    |
| vCPU              | 8 cores                                        |
| RAM               | Minimum 8 GB                                   |

The architecture diagram below illustrates the data flow from the UMS SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, through the On-Premises Data Gateway, to Microsoft Fabric in Azure. The diagram highlights the outbound-only connection model, ensuring secure, controlled data transfer.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Data flow from UMS SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse to Microsoft Fabric via On-Premises Data Gateway.

## 4.3 Outbound Security Rules for Data Gateway

Securing the outbound connectivity of the OPDG virtual machine is critical to maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data as it traverses from UMS’s on-premises environment to Microsoft Fabric. Enfrasys Solutions has defined a set of Azure Network Security Group (NSG) rules that must be applied to the OPDG VM’s network interface or subnet. These rules are designed to allow only the minimum necessary outbound traffic required for the OPDG to function, in accordance with Microsoft’s security best practices.

The following table details the required NSG rules:

| Name                        | Priority | Source                 | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                       | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443              | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443              | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                    | 80               | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules collectively ensure that the OPDG VM can authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), communicate securely with Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints, and perform network connectivity status checks. All other outbound traffic should be denied by default to maintain a strong security posture.

Enfrasys Solutions will oversee the design and implementation of these network security controls, while UMS is responsible for ensuring that the on-premises firewall and network infrastructure permit the required outbound connections from the OPDG VM.

## 4.4 Conditional Access and User Authentication

To further secure access to Microsoft Fabric resources, Enfrasys Solutions recommends the implementation of Entra Conditional Access policies. These policies evaluate user and device signals, such as user identity, group membership, and network location, before granting access to Microsoft Fabric services. This approach ensures that only authorized users, whether internal or external to UMS, can access sensitive data and analytics resources.

The authentication flow begins with a user attempting to connect to Microsoft Fabric. The request is evaluated against Entra Conditional Access policies, which aggregate contextual signals and enforce access decisions in real time. If the policy requirements are met, access is granted; otherwise, the user is denied entry. This layered security model protects UMS’s data assets against unauthorized access and aligns with modern zero-trust principles.

The following diagram illustrates the conditional access flow for Microsoft Fabric:

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 2: Conditional access flow for Microsoft Fabric authentication.

Enfrasys Solutions will design and document the required conditional access policies, while UMS is responsible for reviewing and approving policy configurations to align with institutional security requirements.

# 5.0 Roles in Microsoft Fabric & Power BI

This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and access assignments within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). It details the administrative and workspace roles, their permissions, and the recommended personnel mapping to ensure secure, efficient, and auditable platform operations.

## 5.1 Microsoft Fabric Administrator Role

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single SaaS environment. The Fabric Administrator role is a pivotal position within this ecosystem, responsible for overseeing platform governance, security, and operational health.

The Fabric Administrator is entrusted with configuring tenant-level settings, enforcing security and compliance policies, managing user provisioning, and monitoring resource usage. This role is also responsible for delegating workspace-level permissions, integrating with Microsoft Entra ID for identity management, and ensuring that all activities within the Fabric environment adhere to Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data governance requirements. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that only highly trusted personnel with a strong understanding of both technical and organizational policies be assigned to this role, as administrators have extensive permissions that can impact the entire analytics platform.

The responsibilities of the Fabric Administrator include, but are not limited to:

- Managing and assigning workspace roles across the organization.
- Configuring and enforcing data access policies.
- Monitoring platform usage and auditing activities for compliance.
- Overseeing integration with external data sources and security controls.
- Coordinating with Enfrasys Solutions for escalated support and platform updates.

The following table summarizes the key capabilities of the Fabric Administrator role:

| Capability | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Tenant Settings Management | Configure global settings, enable/disable features, and set compliance policies. |
| User and Role Provisioning | Assign users to workspaces and roles, manage group memberships. |
| Security Enforcement | Apply data protection, access controls, and monitor audit logs. |
| Resource Monitoring | Track usage, quotas, and optimize resource allocation. |
| Integration Oversight | Manage connections to external data sources and third-party applications. |

## 5.2 Fabric-native Roles

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI provide a comprehensive role-based access control (RBAC) model to enable granular permissions management. Native roles are designed to align with common analytics and data governance personas, ensuring that each user has the appropriate level of access for their responsibilities.

The primary native roles include:

- **Admin:** Full control over workspace and its content, including role assignments and deletion.
- **Contributor:** Can create, edit, and publish content within the workspace, but cannot manage workspace settings.
- **Member:** Can view and interact with content, and contribute to collaborative analytics tasks.
- **Viewer:** Read-only access to published reports and dashboards, suitable for stakeholders and decision-makers.

These roles are mapped to typical analytics functions such as Data Engineer, Data Scientist, Business Analyst, and Stakeholder. Assigning the correct role ensures that sensitive data is protected, operational workflows are streamlined, and audit requirements are met. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a least-privilege approach, granting users only the permissions necessary for their job functions.

The following table details the permissions associated with each workspace-level role:

| Permission | Admin | Contributor | Member | Viewer |
|------------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Add/Remove Users | Yes | No | No | No |
| Publish Content | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Edit Content | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| View Content | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Delete Workspace | Yes | No | No | No |
| Manage Data Sources | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Share Reports | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Audit Logs Access | Yes | No | No | No |

This role structure ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah can maintain robust data security while enabling productive collaboration across analytics teams and stakeholders.

## 5.3 UMS Workspace Role and Access

Effective assignment of workspace roles is essential for operational clarity and platform security. Enfrasys Solutions has mapped the recommended workspace roles to Universiti Malaysia Sabah personnel based on their functional responsibilities and departmental alignment. This mapping is designed to facilitate streamlined analytics workflows, clear accountability, and compliance with organizational policies.

Enfrasys Solutions proposes the following role assignments. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall review and confirm the personnel designated for each role to ensure alignment with internal governance and operational requirements.

Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for validating the personnel assignments and communicating any changes to Enfrasys Solutions to maintain accurate access control.

By implementing this structured role and access model, Universiti Malaysia Sabah will benefit from enhanced security, operational efficiency, and clear auditability within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environments.

# 6.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Design and Decision

This section details the solution design for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data workflow, analytics, and governance using Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The design aligns with UMS’s business requirements for secure, scalable, and governed data analytics.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

A robust and scalable data workflow is essential for UMS to achieve seamless data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and analytics. Microsoft Fabric provides a unified platform to orchestrate these processes, leveraging services such as Data Factory for integration, Synapse for analytics, and Data Science for machine learning. The workflow ensures that data flows securely from on-premises sources to cloud-based analytics, supporting both operational efficiency and data-driven decision-making.

The design leverages a multi-layered Lakehouse architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) to ensure data quality, traceability, and reusability. Each layer serves a distinct purpose: raw data landing (Bronze), cleansing and transformation (Silver), and business-ready analytics (Gold). Dataflows and notebooks facilitate movement and transformation between layers, while AutoML and manual ML processes enable advanced analytics. The integration with Power BI via OneLake ensures that insights are delivered efficiently to stakeholders.

| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                          | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the Bronze Lakehouse.                               | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the Silver Lakehouse.                              | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).    | Data Factory     |

| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                        | Power BI         |

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a modern data platform architecture utilizing Microsoft Fabric’s Lakehouse paradigm, Data Factory, and Power BI for UMS. This approach ensures data is efficiently ingested from on-premises sources, processed through scalable transformation layers, and made available for advanced analytics and visualization.

The data ingestion begins with the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), securely bridging the Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse and Fabric’s Data Factory. Data flows into the Bronze Lakehouse as raw records, ensuring data lineage and auditability. Dataflow Gen2 and Notebooks are then used to cleanse and transform data into the Silver Lakehouse, preparing it for machine learning and analytics workloads. The Gold Lakehouse stores highly refined, business-ready data, supporting both manual and AutoML machine learning processes. Outputs from these processes are registered in the Fabric Model Registry for lifecycle management, and scored results are stored in Gold for downstream analytics.

Power BI connects directly to the Semantic Model, which is built atop the Gold Lakehouse, providing UMS with real-time, governed analytics. This architecture enables UMS to scale analytics, ensure data quality, and support advanced use cases such as predictive modeling.
