## 6.6 Governance Consideration

Strong governance ensures that analytics resources are used efficiently, securely, and in alignment with UMS’s strategic objectives. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the technical design and implementation of governance controls, while UMS provides operational input and ongoing oversight.

### 6.6.1 Governance Disciplines

Cost management, resource ownership, and policy enforcement are key governance pillars. The following table outlines the assignment of resources, cost centers, and owners to ensure accountability and transparency.

| Resource           | Cost Center     | Owner                    |
|--------------------|----------------|--------------------------|
| Fabric Capacity    | Analytics      | UMS IT                   |
| Workspace          | Departmental   | UMS Department Leads     |
| Data Gateway       | Infrastructure | UMS IT                   |
| Lakehouse          | Analytics      | UMS Data Engineering     |
| Power BI Reports   | Departmental   | UMS Department Leads     |

### 6.6.2 Violation Triggers and Actions

To maintain compliance and operational integrity, specific triggers and actions are defined for policy violations. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for technical remediation, while UMS ensures operational adherence.

| Trigger                                   | Action                                  | Owner            |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|------------------|
| Unauthorized access attempt                | Block access, alert security team       | Enfrasys, UMS IT |
| Resource naming convention violation       | Notify resource owner, enforce correction | Enfrasys         |
| Exceeding allocated resource quotas        | Alert cost center owner, review usage   | UMS IT           |
| Data refresh failures                      | Log incident, initiate troubleshooting  | Enfrasys         |
| Non-compliant data sharing                 | Revoke sharing, report to governance    | UMS IT           |

This governance framework ensures that UMS’s analytics environment remains secure, cost-effective, and aligned with institutional policies. Enfrasys Solutions will continue to provide guidance and support for ongoing governance enhancements as UMS’s analytics maturity evolves.

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

This section outlines the security architecture, network segmentation, and encryption strategies recommended for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in the deployment of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and supporting Azure services. The design ensures robust protection of sensitive data, compliance with industry standards, and adherence to Microsoft and Azure security best practices.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

Network Security Groups (NSGs) in Azure provide a critical layer of defense by controlling inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources at the subnet and network interface level. For the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine, NSGs are configured to allow only the minimum required connectivity, thus reducing the attack surface and ensuring that only legitimate traffic is permitted.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a least-privilege approach for NSG rules, permitting only essential services and endpoints. This configuration specifically enables secure communication between the OPDG VM, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure core services, and Microsoft Entra ID for authentication, while blocking all other unsolicited traffic. Such a strategy is fundamental to protecting the UMS environment from external threats and unauthorized access.

The following tables detail the inbound and outbound NSG rules for the Data Gateway VM. The outbound rules are designed to facilitate secure data transfer, authentication, and connectivity verification, while the inbound rules restrict access to only those sources and ports necessary for operational integrity.

### Outbound NSG Rules for Data Gateway VM

| Name                        | Priority | Source                  | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net                | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                                                      | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                                                                                              | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

### Inbound NSG Rules for Data Gateway VM

For enhanced security, inbound access to the Data Gateway VM should be tightly controlled. Enfrasys Solutions recommends permitting only trusted administrative sources (such as specific UMS jump hosts or management subnets) and essential service ports. All other inbound traffic should be denied by default.

| Name                       | Priority | Source                | Source Ports | Destination         | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|----------------------------|----------|-----------------------|--------------|---------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_Admin_Management     | 100      | UMS Admin Subnet      | *            | Data Gateway VM     | 3389              | TCP      | Allow  |
| Deny_All_Other_Inbound     | 4096     | Any                   | *            | Any                 | *                 | Any      | Deny   |

The above configuration ensures that only authorized administrators from UMS can access the VM for management purposes (e.g., via RDP on port 3389), while all other inbound attempts are blocked.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Data protection is paramount in the UMS environment, especially given the sensitivity of institutional and research data handled by Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. Enfrasys Solutions prescribes a comprehensive encryption strategy that encompasses both data at rest and in transit, leveraging Azure-native capabilities and Microsoft security standards.

### Encryption at Rest

All data stored within Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, and Power BI is encrypted at rest using strong encryption algorithms, such as AES-256, managed by Microsoft’s Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE). This ensures that data residing in storage accounts, data warehouses, and analytics workspaces is protected from unauthorized access, even if physical storage media were compromised.

For the Data Gateway VM, Azure Disk Encryption is enabled, utilizing Azure Key Vault-managed keys to further safeguard virtual hard disks. This approach aligns with compliance requirements and institutional data governance policies.

### Encryption in Transit

Data in transit between the Data Gateway VM, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and other Azure services is secured using industry-standard protocols such as TLS 1.2 or higher. All communication over public and private networks—including API calls, data synchronization, and user access—is conducted via HTTPS, ensuring confidentiality and integrity against eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks.

Specifically, the outbound NSG rules permit only HTTPS (TCP port 443) traffic to Microsoft cloud endpoints, enforcing encrypted channels for all operational data flows. Additionally, communication between the Data Gateway and on-premises data sources can be configured to use secure protocols such as IPsec or SSL/TLS, depending on the source system’s capabilities.

### Roles and Responsibilities

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the implementation and validation of the security baseline, including NSG configuration, encryption enablement, and periodic security reviews. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ongoing compliance validation, user access reviews, and ensuring that operational practices adhere to institutional and regulatory requirements.

This clear delineation of responsibilities ensures that security controls are both robustly implemented and continuously maintained, providing UMS with a secure, compliant, and resilient analytics environment.

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration approach for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). The strategy is structured to ensure a seamless transition from the existing environment to the new Microsoft Fabric-based architecture, minimizing operational disruption and ensuring data integrity throughout the process.

## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup

A successful migration is predicated on thorough preparation and coordination between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS. Pre-migration activities ensure that all foundational elements—such as environment readiness, documentation, and stakeholder alignment—are in place before any production data or workloads are moved. This phase includes the review and sign-off of the solution design, confirmation of the staging environment, initial setup of the Fabric environment, and installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG).

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a collaborative approach during this stage, with clear task ownership and defined timelines. This approach mitigates risks and ensures that both technical and business prerequisites are addressed before proceeding to pilot and production phases.

The table below details the preparatory tasks, responsible parties, status, and remarks:

| No | Activities                                                            | Planned Start   | Action By         | Status       | Remarks |
|----|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|-------------------|--------------|---------|
| 1  | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off             | Fri, 7-Nov-25   | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |         |
| 2  | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25  | UMS               | Not-Started  |         |
| 3  | Fabric Environment Setup                                              | Wed, 12-Nov-25  | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |         |
| 4  | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25  | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |         |

## 8.2 Pilot

The pilot phase is critical in validating the migration approach, technical configurations, and operational processes before full-scale production deployment. Enfrasys Solutions will lead the pilot deployment, working closely with UMS IT personnel to ensure that all components function as intended in a controlled environment.

During the pilot, a subset of representative data and workloads will be migrated to the new Fabric environment. This allows both technical and business stakeholders to assess system performance, data integrity, and user experience. The pilot also provides an opportunity to refine migration scripts, test the On-Premises Data Gateway, and validate security and access controls.

Key steps in the pilot phase include:

- Selection of pilot data sets and user groups by UMS.
- Configuration and validation of the Fabric environment by Enfrasys Solutions.
- Execution of initial data ingestion and transformation processes.
- End-to-end testing of data flows, reporting, and user access.
- Collection of feedback and identification of any issues or gaps.

Enfrasys Solutions will document all findings and lessons learned during the pilot, which will inform adjustments to the production migration plan. UMS is responsible for providing access to pilot data and relevant business users for acceptance testing.

## 8.3 Production

Transitioning to production requires meticulous planning and coordination to minimize downtime and ensure business continuity. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a phased approach, structured around a D-7 (seven days before cutover), D0 (cutover day), and D+1 (post-cutover) timeline. Each phase includes specific activities and clear assignment of responsibilities.

### D-7: Pre-Cutover

Seven days prior to the production cutover, all preparatory activities must be finalized. This includes a final review of the environment, confirmation of data sets, user communication, and scheduling.

| Item | Activities                                                                 | Action By         | Status       |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1    | Finalize and freeze migration scripts and runbooks                         | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |
| 2    | Confirm production data sets and user mapping                              | UMS               | Not-Started  |
| 3    | Communicate migration schedule and expected downtime to stakeholders       | UMS               | Not-Started  |
| 4    | Complete backup of all critical data                                       | UMS               | Not-Started  |
| 5    | Validate Fabric environment readiness                                      | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |

### D0: Cutover

The cutover day marks the actual migration of production data and switch-over to the new environment. Enfrasys Solutions will execute the migration in close coordination with UMS to ensure all systems are transitioned smoothly.

| Item | Activities                                                                 | Action By         | Status       |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1    | Initiate migration of production data                                      | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |
| 2    | Monitor data transfer and validate integrity                               | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |
| 3    | Switch user access to the new Fabric environment                           | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |
| 4    | Conduct smoke testing and validate business-critical reports               | UMS               | Not-Started  |

### D+1: Post-Cutover

The first day after cutover is dedicated to post-migration validation, issue resolution, and user support. Enfrasys Solutions will provide hypercare support, while UMS will monitor business operations and escalate any issues.

| Item | Activities                                                                 | Action By         | Status       |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1    | Conduct post-migration validation and reconciliation                       | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |
| 2    | Provide hypercare support for users                                        | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |
| 3    | Document and resolve post-migration issues                                 | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |
| 4    | Finalize handover and sign-off on successful migration                     | UMS               | Not-Started  |

## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support

Following successful migration, a structured post-migration support and handover phase ensures that UMS is fully equipped to operate and maintain the new environment. Enfrasys Solutions will provide ongoing support during an agreed transition period, addressing any residual issues and ensuring knowledge transfer to UMS personnel.

Key post-migration activities include:

- Monitoring system performance and user experience.
- Resolving any outstanding technical issues.
- Conducting knowledge transfer sessions and documentation handover.
- Formal transition of operational ownership to UMS IT teams.

The following table outlines the support and handover activities, with clear assignment of responsibilities:

| Item | Activities                                                        | Action By         | Status       |
|------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1    | Monitor system health and performance                             | Enfrasys, UMS     | Not-Started  |
| 2    | Address and resolve post-migration support tickets                | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |
| 3    | Conduct knowledge transfer and training for UMS IT staff          | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |
| 4    | Handover operational documentation and runbooks                   | Enfrasys          | Not-Started  |
| 5    | Formal sign-off of migration and support completion               | UMS               | Not-Started  |

Through this structured deployment and migration approach, Enfrasys Solutions ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah achieves a smooth, secure, and effective transition to the new Microsoft Fabric platform, with minimized risk and maximized operational readiness.

# UMS Power BI & Microsoft Fabric Solution Design

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project’s business context, the purpose of this Solution Design Document, and identifies the key stakeholders involved in Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) adoption of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is embarking on a transformative initiative to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence capabilities. The primary business drivers for this project are to enhance data-driven decision-making, streamline data integration processes, and leverage advanced analytics to support the university’s strategic objectives. UMS seeks to establish a robust data workflow that encompasses data ingestion, transformation, and visualization, thereby enabling timely and actionable insights for stakeholders across academic and administrative domains.

The project scope covers the design and implementation of an end-to-end data workflow within Microsoft Fabric. This includes the establishment of a dedicated Fabric workspace, development of comprehensive ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, execution of machine learning processes, and seamless integration with Power BI for business-aligned analytics. The adoption of Microsoft Fabric’s suite of services—such as Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science for machine learning applications—will ensure that UMS can efficiently manage and analyze large volumes of diverse data sources.

The high-level objectives of this initiative are to:
- Align UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with Microsoft Fabric’s capabilities.
- Enable secure, scalable, and automated data workflows from ingestion to visualization.
- Empower UMS’s stakeholders with self-service analytics and advanced reporting through Power BI.
- Foster a data-driven culture that supports academic excellence and operational efficiency.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this Solution Design Document is to provide a comprehensive and authoritative blueprint for the design, implementation, and governance of UMS’s Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. This document articulates the architectural decisions, technical specifications, and operational workflows that will guide the successful realization of the project objectives.

Serving as a critical reference throughout the project lifecycle, this document ensures alignment between UMS’s business requirements and the technical solution. It provides clarity on roles and responsibilities, facilitates informed decision-making, and forms the basis for subsequent phases such as implementation, testing, and operational handover. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting and maintaining this document, while UMS is accountable for its review, validation, and formal sign-off.

## 2.3 Document Audience

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, establishing the foundational technologies for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data platform modernization. Enfrasys Solutions ensures the accuracy and completeness of all content in this section.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single SaaS offering. It provides a cohesive environment for organizations to manage the entire data lifecycle, from ingestion to advanced analytics and visualization, using a suite of tightly integrated services. Microsoft Fabric is built to simplify complex data architectures, reduce operational overhead, and accelerate time-to-insight for business users and data professionals.

The core services within Microsoft Fabric include:

- **Data Factory**: This service delivers robust data integration and orchestration capabilities. It enables organizations to ingest data from diverse sources, transform it through ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes, and move it efficiently across the data estate. Data Factory supports both code-free and code-centric data pipeline development, allowing UMS to streamline data ingestion and transformation workflows.
- **Synapse**: Fabric Synapse provides advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, combining data warehousing, big data analytics, and data integration into a single unified experience. It enables UMS to analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured data, build scalable analytics solutions, and derive actionable insights through powerful SQL, Spark, and Data Explorer engines.
- **Data Science**: The Data Science component empowers users to build, train, and operationalize machine learning models at scale. It integrates with AutoML (Automated Machine Learning) to simplify the development of predictive analytics, supporting UMS’s goals for advanced analytics and data-driven decision-making.
- **OneLake**: OneLake serves as the unified data lake for Fabric, providing a single, secure, and scalable repository for all organizational data. It eliminates data silos and enables seamless data sharing and collaboration across teams.

By leveraging Microsoft Fabric, Universiti Malaysia Sabah can establish a modern data platform that supports end-to-end data workflows, from ingestion and transformation to advanced analytics and visualization. This approach aligns with UMS’s cloud adoption strategy and ensures agility, scalability, and governance across the data lifecycle.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization platform. It enables organizations to connect to a wide range of data sources, transform raw data into interactive reports and dashboards, and share insights securely across the organization. Power BI’s intuitive interface, rich visualization options, and integration with Microsoft 365 make it a preferred tool for self-service analytics and executive reporting.

Within the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem, Power BI is natively integrated, allowing seamless access to data stored in OneLake and processed by Fabric services. This integration ensures that data prepared and analyzed through Data Factory, Synapse, and Data Science modules can be directly visualized and shared with stakeholders in real time. For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, this means business users and decision-makers can access up-to-date analytics without complex data movement or manual intervention.

The direct integration between Power BI and Microsoft Fabric offers several key benefits to UMS:

- **Unified Data Governance**: Centralized security, compliance, and access controls across the data platform.
- **Accelerated Insights**: Reduced latency between data ingestion, processing, and visualization, enabling timely decision-making.
- **Self-Service Analytics**: Empowerment of business users to explore and analyze data independently, reducing reliance on IT resources.

By adopting Power BI alongside Microsoft Fabric, UMS can foster a data-driven culture, democratize analytics, and ensure consistent, reliable insights across the institution.

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID, formerly known as Azure Active Directory, is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management (IAM) service. It provides secure authentication, authorization, and identity governance for users, applications, and resources across the Microsoft ecosystem. Entra ID is a foundational component for ensuring security, compliance, and operational efficiency in cloud environments.

Entra ID’s primary capabilities include:

- **Single Sign-On (SSO)**: Enables users to access multiple applications, including Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, with a single set of credentials.
- **Conditional Access**: Enforces security policies based on user, device, location, and risk factors, ensuring only authorized users can access sensitive data and analytics.
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Assigns granular permissions to users and groups, aligning access rights with organizational roles and responsibilities.
- **Identity Protection**: Detects and responds to identity-based threats, supporting compliance with regulatory requirements.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Entra ID serves as the backbone for identity and access management across the data platform. It ensures that only authorized personnel can access, manage, and analyze data within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, supporting both security and operational governance. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for ensuring that all identity and access management configurations are accurate, secure, and aligned with UMS’s organizational policies.

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section details the network architecture and connectivity decisions for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment. It encompasses the overall network topology, secure connectivity between on-premises and cloud environments, and the implementation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) as a secure bridge for data integration.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

A robust and secure network design is fundamental to ensure seamless and compliant integration between UMS’s on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric in the cloud. The proposed topology leverages outbound-only connections, minimizing the attack surface and adhering to industry best practices for cloud connectivity and data protection.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hub-and-spoke network architecture, where the on-premises data center connects to Azure via secure outbound connections, specifically through the OPDG. This design eliminates the need for inbound firewall rules, significantly reducing exposure to external threats. All data transfers from UMS’s on-premises environment to Microsoft Fabric are initiated by the gateway, ensuring that sensitive resources remain protected behind the institutional firewall.

The security posture is further reinforced by leveraging Azure’s built-in network security controls, including strict outbound Network Security Group (NSG) rules. These rules restrict the OPDG VM’s traffic to only the required Microsoft endpoints over HTTPS, ensuring encrypted data transmission and compliance with UMS’s regulatory obligations. Conditional Access policies, enforced through Microsoft Entra ID, govern user authentication and access, ensuring only authorized users can interact with critical data assets.

## 4.2 Microsoft Fabric Data Gateway

Microsoft Fabric’s On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component that enables secure, reliable data integration between UMS’s on-premises SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse and cloud-based Fabric resources. The OPDG is deployed as a dedicated virtual machine within UMS’s data center, configured to initiate outbound-only connections to Microsoft cloud endpoints.

Microsoft’s On-Premises Data Gateway is a hybrid connectivity service that facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services, including Power BI, Power Platform, and Fabric. It acts as a bridge, enabling cloud services to access on-premises data without exposing internal systems to inbound internet traffic.

The OPDG architecture for UMS is designed to maximize security and operational efficiency. The gateway VM is provisioned with enterprise-grade specifications to ensure high availability and performance for data transfer workloads. All connectivity from the gateway to Microsoft Fabric is encrypted using SSL/TLS over HTTPS, and only essential endpoints are permitted through the network security configuration. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the overall design, configuration, and validation of the OPDG deployment, while UMS is accountable for preparing and maintaining the underlying on-premises infrastructure, including network readiness and VM provisioning.

# 6.0 Microsoft Fabric & Power BI Design and Decision

This section details the end-to-end design of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data workflow, analytics, and governance architecture leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. ## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, and business intelligence into a single SaaS environment. It combines services such as Fabric Data Factory for orchestration, Synapse for analytics, and Power BI for visualization, all underpinned by OneLake for data storage. The following paragraphs outline the key workflow design considerations for UMS.

The workflow begins with ingestion from UMS’s Microsoft SQL Server data warehouse using Fabric Data Factory pipelines. Data is staged in a Lakehouse architecture, adopting a multi-layered approach (Bronze, Silver, Gold) to progressively refine and transform data. Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query tools are used for cleansing and transformation, while Data Science workloads—including both AutoML and manual ML—are executed on cleansed data to generate predictive insights. The Gold layer serves as the trusted source for Power BI semantic modeling and reporting, with OneLake providing seamless data connectivity throughout.

This approach ensures clear separation of raw, cleansed, and curated data, supports advanced analytics, and enables secure, governed access for business reporting. The table below summarizes the specific workflow design considerations across ETL and ML workloads.

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Decisions

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a Lakehouse architecture with distinct Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers to ensure data lineage, quality, and reusability. The Bronze layer captures raw data from UMS’s SQL Server, providing an immutable source for audit and reproducibility. Transformation and cleansing occur in the Silver layer using Dataflow Gen2 and Notebooks, which enables both low-code and code-first approaches for data engineers and scientists. The Gold layer aggregates and curates data for business consumption, serving as the single source of truth for analytics and reporting.

For machine learning, Enfrasys Solutions proposes a hybrid approach: leveraging both AutoML for rapid prototyping and manual ML via Notebooks for advanced, custom modeling. All trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, supporting lifecycle management and future reuse. Scoring outputs and predictions are consistently stored in the Gold layer, ensuring that Power BI reports always reference the most up-to-date analytical results.

This design maximizes flexibility, scalability, and governance while supporting UMS’s evolving analytics and data science needs. It also ensures seamless integration with Power BI via OneLake, enabling real-time, secure, and performant data visualization.

| No.  | Design Decision                                                                                      | Decision                                                                                   |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Adopt Lakehouse architecture with Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers                                    | Approved: Ensures data quality, lineage, and separation of concerns                        |
| DD02 | Use Dataflow Gen2 and Notebooks for ETL and transformation                                           | Approved: Supports both low-code and code-first data engineering                           |
| DD03 | Store all ML outputs and predictions in Gold Lakehouse                                               | Approved: Guarantees consistency and traceability for analytics                            |
| DD04 | Register trained models in Fabric Model Registry                                                     | Approved: Enables model lifecycle management and reuse                                      |
| DD05 | Connect Power BI Semantic Model to Gold Lakehouse via OneLake                                        | Approved: Provides performant, secure, and real-time analytics                             |
| DD06 | Prioritize manual ML in Notebooks for custom model tuning, with AutoML for rapid experimentation     | Approved: Balances speed and flexibility for UMS’s data science workloads                  |

# 7.0 Security Design and Decision

This section details the security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment, with a focus on network security, encryption, and access control. Enfrasys Solutions has designed a layered security approach to protect sensitive data and ensure compliance with industry best practices, while UMS is responsible for confirming that these controls align with institutional compliance requirements.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

A Network Security Group (NSG) is an Azure resource that acts as a virtual firewall, controlling inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources at both the subnet and network interface level. NSGs are essential in restricting access to only those endpoints necessary for business operations, thereby reducing the attack surface and enforcing the principle of least privilege.

For the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine, Enfrasys Solutions recommends a tightly controlled set of NSG rules. These rules are designed to allow only the required outbound connectivity to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services, while blocking all unnecessary traffic. This approach minimizes exposure to potential threats and ensures that data transfers occur only over secure, monitored channels.

The following table specifies the outbound NSG rules for the Data Gateway VM. Each rule is crafted to enable secure communication, authentication, and connectivity verification with Microsoft cloud services. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for implementing these NSG configurations, while UMS is responsible for reviewing and confirming that the rules meet their internal security and compliance standards.

| Name                        | Priority | Source                  | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                  | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                              | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules ensure the Data Gateway VM can securely authenticate, communicate, and transfer data with Microsoft cloud services using encrypted channels, while maintaining strict control over network traffic.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a critical component of the security architecture for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric deployment. Enfrasys Solutions has selected encryption mechanisms that protect data both at rest and in transit, ensuring end-to-end confidentiality and integrity for all sensitive information handled by the system.

### Encryption at Rest

All data stored within OneLake, Microsoft Fabric, and Power BI is encrypted at rest using Microsoft-managed keys by default. This leverages Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE), which employs strong AES-256 encryption to safeguard data against unauthorized access. For the Data Gateway VM, all disks are encrypted using Azure Disk Encryption, which utilizes BitLocker technology for Windows-based systems. This ensures that even if physical storage is compromised, the data remains unreadable without the appropriate cryptographic keys.

### Encryption in Transit

Data in transit between UMS’s on-premises environment, the Data Gateway VM, and Microsoft cloud services is protected using industry-standard TLS (Transport Layer Security) protocols. All communications between the Data Gateway VM and Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Entra ID endpoints are enforced over HTTPS (TCP port 443), ensuring that sensitive information such as authentication tokens and data payloads are encrypted during transmission. This approach protects against eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, and data tampering.

The following diagram illustrates the secure data flow and access control mechanisms implemented in the UMS environment. It highlights the application of conditional access policies, multi-factor authentication, and encrypted communication channels between users, the Data Gateway VM, and Microsoft Fabric services.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 7.1: Conditional access and secure data flow architecture for Microsoft Fabric in UMS.

### Access Control and Multi-Factor Authentication

Although UMS currently does not meet the eligibility criteria for advanced Conditional Access (CA) policies due to licensing constraints, Enfrasys Solutions has enforced Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level. This ensures that all UMS users must complete an additional verification step during sign-in, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access due to compromised credentials. Should UMS acquire the necessary Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses in the future, Enfrasys Solutions recommends revisiting the implementation of Conditional Access policies for more granular access control.

The following table summarizes the key access control decisions for the UMS environment:

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                                   |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy                                                   |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts               |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                 |

By combining robust network security rules, comprehensive encryption strategies, and enforced multi-factor authentication, Enfrasys Solutions provides UMS with a secure foundation for its Microsoft Fabric deployment. UMS is responsible for validating that these controls satisfy institutional compliance and regulatory requirements, while Enfrasys Solutions maintains responsibility for the ongoing security architecture and technical implementation.

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration methodology for the Microsoft Fabric solution at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). The approach is structured to ensure a controlled, risk-mitigated transition from the current state to the new platform, with clear delineation of responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS.

## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup

A successful migration begins with meticulous preparation. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a sequenced set of preparatory activities to establish a solid foundation for the deployment. These tasks are designed to ensure all stakeholders are aligned, technical prerequisites are fulfilled, and the environment is ready for subsequent phases. The preparatory phase involves both administrative and technical actions, such as documentation sign-off, environment provisioning, and gateway installation.

Delivering the finalized solution design document for review and sign-off is a critical step to ensure mutual understanding of the architecture and migration plan. UMS is responsible for confirming the availability and readiness of the new server for the data warehouse staging area, which is essential for data ingestion processes. Enfrasys Solutions will then proceed with the setup of the Microsoft Fabric environment, ensuring all configurations align with the approved design. The installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a joint effort, requiring UMS to provide access and support, while Enfrasys Solutions executes the technical installation and validation.

The table below details the preparatory tasks, responsible parties, and current status:

| No. | Activities                                                    | Planned Start   | Action By           | Status       | Remarks |
|-----|---------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------|--------------|---------|
| 1   | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off      | Fri, 7-Nov-25   | Enfrasys, UMS       | Not-Started  |         |
| 2   | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25  | UMS                 | Not-Started  |         |
| 3   | Fabric Environment Setup                                      | Wed, 12-Nov-25  | Enfrasys            | Not-Started  |         |
| 4   | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25  | Enfrasys, UMS       | Not-Started  |         |

## 8.2 Pilot

The pilot phase serves as a controlled test of the migration approach and solution functionality within a limited scope, minimizing operational risk before full-scale deployment. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that the pilot include a representative subset of UMS data and users, focusing on validating data ingestion, transformation, and reporting workflows within the Microsoft Fabric environment.

Success criteria for the pilot include:
- Successful connectivity between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric via the OPDG.
- Accurate and timely data ingestion into the staging area.
- Validation of data transformation, quality, and reporting outputs.
- Positive user acceptance feedback from designated UMS pilot participants.
- No critical defects or operational disruptions.

The pilot timeline is structured as follows:
- **D-7 (One week before cutover):** Complete environment provisioning, gateway installation, and initial data mapping.
- **D0 (Pilot cutover day):** Execute data ingestion and transformation processes; conduct user acceptance testing.
- **D+1 (One day after cutover):** Review pilot outcomes, address issues, and formally document lessons learned.

Enfrasys Solutions will lead the technical execution of the pilot, while UMS will facilitate user participation and environment readiness. Both parties will jointly review pilot results and determine readiness for production rollout.

## 8.3 Production

Following a successful pilot, the production deployment phase will expand the solution to the full user base and data scope. Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for executing the technical migration, including full-scale data ingestion, configuration of production data pipelines, and activation of reporting services within Microsoft Fabric. UMS will ensure that all required infrastructure, user access, and data sources are available and operational.

Key production deployment steps include:
- Final validation of the production environment against the approved design.
- Execution of full data migration from on-premises sources to the Microsoft Fabric platform.
- Configuration and activation of production data pipelines and reports.
- User access provisioning and permissions alignment.
- Coordination of cutover activities to minimize downtime and operational impact.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide continuous communication throughout the production deployment, ensuring UMS stakeholders are informed of progress and any required actions. UMS will be responsible for providing timely approvals, environment access, and post-migration sign-off.

## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support

Post-migration activities are essential to ensure operational stability, knowledge transfer, and long-term sustainability of the solution. Enfrasys Solutions will provide immediate post-migration support to address any technical issues, monitor system performance, and validate data integrity. This includes troubleshooting, fine-tuning configurations, and resolving user-reported incidents.

Knowledge transfer sessions will be conducted to equip UMS IT personnel with the necessary skills to manage and maintain the Microsoft Fabric environment. Enfrasys Solutions will prepare and hand over comprehensive documentation covering architecture, operational procedures, and troubleshooting guidelines.

The formal handover process will conclude with UMS providing sign-off on the migration and support deliverables, confirming that all acceptance criteria have been met and that the environment is stable for ongoing operations. Enfrasys Solutions will remain available for extended support as per the agreed service terms.

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project context, objectives, and the intended purpose and audience for this Solution Design Document. It establishes the foundation for subsequent technical and architectural details.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has initiated a strategic project to modernize and enhance its data analytics capabilities by adopting Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The primary business context driving this initiative is the need for a unified, scalable, and secure data platform that supports the full lifecycle of data ingestion, transformation, advanced analytics, and business intelligence reporting. This project is specifically scoped to design and implement an end-to-end data workflow, beginning with raw data ingestion, progressing through transformation and machine learning processes, and culminating in interactive data visualization through Power BI.

The scope of this engagement includes the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace for UMS, the development of robust ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, and the integration of advanced analytics and machine learning using Fabric Synapse and Data Science components. By leveraging Microsoft Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for big data analytics, and Power BI for business-aligned reporting, UMS aims to align its cloud adoption strategy with industry best practices and Microsoft’s latest data platform capabilities. The solution is designed to deliver operational efficiency, improved data-driven decision-making, and a secure, future-ready analytics environment for UMS.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to formally capture and communicate the architectural blueprint, technical design decisions, and implementation approach for the UMS Microsoft Fabric and Power BI project. This document serves as a comprehensive reference for all stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle, providing a basis for technical review, formal sign-off, and as an authoritative guide during the implementation and operationalization phases.

Enfrasys Solutions has prepared this document to ensure that all design considerations, technology selections, and workflow integrations are clearly defined, justified, and aligned with UMS’s strategic objectives. The document is intended to facilitate informed decision-making, risk mitigation, and to provide a clear path for project execution and governance.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This Solution Design Document is intended for a diverse set of stakeholders involved in the planning, implementation, and oversight of the UMS Microsoft Fabric and Power BI project. The primary audience includes, but is not limited to:

- UMS IT Department: Responsible for technical review, operational support, and ongoing management of the implemented solution.
- UMS Data Analytics Team: Engaged in the development, validation, and utilization of data workflows, machine learning models, and business intelligence reports.
- Enfrasys Solutions Project Team: Accountable for solution architecture, design, and delivery of the project in accordance with agreed requirements.
- UMS Executive Stakeholders: Involved in project governance, strategic alignment, and formal sign-off of design decisions.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting and maintaining this document, ensuring accuracy and completeness. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for reviewing, providing feedback, and formally approving the document prior to implementation. This collaborative approach ensures that the solution design meets both technical and business objectives, and that all parties are aligned throughout the project lifecycle.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Entra ID Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of the core Microsoft technologies forming the foundation of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data and analytics platform. The following subsections define Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, establishing a shared understanding of their roles and capabilities in the proposed solution. All content in this section is generated and validated by Enfrasys Solutions.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Overview

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It brings together several powerful services—including Data Factory, Synapse, and Data Science—within a single SaaS environment, enabling organizations to streamline their data workflows and accelerate insights.

Fabric Data Factory provides robust data integration and orchestration, allowing UMS to ingest data from diverse sources, automate ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes, and manage data pipelines efficiently. Fabric Synapse delivers advanced analytics and big data processing, supporting large-scale data transformation and analytical workloads. The Data Science capabilities within Fabric empower data scientists to experiment, build, and operationalize machine learning models directly within the platform, leveraging both AutoML and custom notebook-driven approaches.

By adopting Microsoft Fabric, UMS benefits from a unified analytics environment that reduces data silos, enhances collaboration across data teams, and accelerates time-to-insight. The platform’s native integration with OneLake ensures that data is accessible and manageable across all Fabric workloads, supporting the university’s need for scalable, secure, and future-proof analytics.

| Technology           | Description                                                                                      | Key Features                                                                                              |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Fabric     | Unified analytics platform integrating data movement, engineering, science, and BI.              | Data Factory (ETL), Synapse (analytics), Data Science (ML/AI), OneLake integration, SaaS delivery         |
| Fabric Data Factory  | Data integration and orchestration service within Fabric.                                         | ETL pipelines, data ingestion, workflow automation, connectivity to diverse sources                       |
| Fabric Synapse       | Advanced analytics and big data processing engine within Fabric.                                 | Distributed data processing, SQL analytics, Spark integration, real-time analytics                        |
| Fabric Data Science  | Machine learning and AI capabilities embedded in Fabric.                                         | AutoML, custom notebooks, model training and deployment, experiment tracking                              |

## 3.2 Power BI Overview

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization platform, designed to transform raw data into actionable insights through interactive dashboards, reports, and analytics. As a fully managed SaaS solution, Power BI enables organizations to connect to a wide array of data sources, model and transform data, and share insights securely across the organization.

For UMS, Power BI serves as the visualization and reporting layer of the analytics architecture. It connects seamlessly to processed datasets stored in OneLake, enabling stakeholders to explore data, monitor key performance indicators, and make data-driven decisions. Power BI’s integration with Microsoft Fabric ensures that data lineage, security, and governance are maintained throughout the analytics lifecycle.

The adoption of Power BI empowers UMS to democratize analytics, enabling users at all levels to build, customize, and consume reports without deep technical expertise. Its support for real-time data, advanced analytics, and AI-driven insights further enhances the value derived from the university’s data assets.

| Technology | Description                                                                                     | Key Features                                                                                   |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

Encryption is fundamental to safeguarding data confidentiality and integrity across all stages of the data lifecycle. Enfrasys Solutions mandates a comprehensive encryption strategy for UMS’s Fabric, Power BI, and Data Gateway deployment, addressing both data at rest and data in transit.

### Encryption at Rest

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI employ Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE) by default, ensuring that all stored data—including datasets, reports, and logs—is encrypted using strong AES-256 algorithms. This encryption is transparent and managed by Microsoft, eliminating the risk of human error in key management. For the On-Premises Data Gateway, any cached credentials or configuration files stored on the VM’s disk are protected using Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI) or, where available, BitLocker encryption. These mechanisms ensure that, even in the event of unauthorized physical or logical access to storage media, sensitive data remains protected.

### Encryption in Transit

All data transmitted between UMS’s users, the On-Premises Data Gateway, and Microsoft cloud services is secured using industry-standard Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocols. Power BI and Fabric enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for all client-server and service-to-service communications, protecting data from interception or tampering during transit. The OPDG VM is configured to only allow outbound HTTPS traffic for service communication and authentication, as enforced by the NSG rules, further ensuring that all data exchanges occur over encrypted channels.

### Operational Responsibilities

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for defining and documenting the encryption requirements and ensuring that all configurations adhere to Microsoft security best practices. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for reviewing these recommendations and implementing encryption controls within their operational environment, including the activation of BitLocker on gateway VMs and verification of TLS enforcement for all endpoints.

This layered encryption approach ensures that UMS’s sensitive research, administrative, and operational data is protected against both external threats and insider risks, supporting regulatory compliance and institutional trust.

## 7.3 Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication

Conditional Access is a powerful security feature within Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) that enables organizations to enforce access controls based on user identity, device state, location, and risk signals. While Conditional Access policies provide granular control, it is noted that UMS’s current account tier does not support advanced Conditional Access features. As such, Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level to strengthen user authentication and mitigate unauthorized access.

MFA ensures that all users accessing Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related services must provide an additional verification factor beyond their password. This significantly reduces the risk of account compromise due to phishing or credential theft. Enfrasys Solutions has designed the access policy to include all UMS users in the MFA enforcement scope, ensuring consistent protection across the environment.

The following diagram illustrates the access flow, highlighting the role of Entra Conditional Access and MFA in securing user authentication to Microsoft Fabric:

The diagram below depicts the authentication and access control workflow for Microsoft Fabric. Users initiate authentication, which is evaluated by Entra Conditional Access policies (where available) or enforced MFA. Signals such as user identity and network location are assessed, a decision is made, and enforcement is applied before granting access to Microsoft Fabric and its components, including OneLake.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 7.1: Authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric using Entra ID and MFA.

The following table summarizes the key access control design decisions:

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                                                      |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy                                                                       |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts                                   |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                                     |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the design and documentation of access policies. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for reviewing the recommendations and ensuring that MFA is enforced for all users in the tenant.

## 7.4 Security Design Summary

The security controls outlined in this section provide a defense-in-depth approach for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment. By implementing tightly scoped NSG rules, enforcing encryption at rest and in transit, and mandating MFA for all users, UMS will achieve a robust security posture that aligns with Microsoft best practices and institutional requirements. Enfrasys Solutions will continue to support UMS in reviewing and optimizing these controls as the environment evolves.

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration approach for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), ensuring a structured, risk-mitigated transition to the new Microsoft Fabric environment. The process is divided into four distinct phases: Pre-Migration/Setup, Pilot, Production, and Post-Migration/Support. Each phase includes detailed activities, assigned responsibilities, and defined timelines to ensure accountability and operational clarity.

## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup

The Pre-Migration/Setup phase establishes the foundational elements required for a successful migration. This phase is critical to minimize risks, ensure readiness, and align all stakeholders on objectives and deliverables. Enfrasys Solutions will lead the technical preparations, while UMS will provide necessary data, environment confirmations, and formal sign-offs.

Key activities in this phase include delivering the finalized Solution Design Document for review and approval, confirming the availability and readiness of the new data warehouse server (staging area database), setting up the Microsoft Fabric environment, and installing the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) to facilitate secure data ingestion from UMS’s on-premises systems to the cloud.

These preparatory steps ensure that all technical prerequisites are met and that UMS’s data landscape is fully mapped and validated before any migration activities commence. Early engagement and sign-off from UMS reduce the risk of misalignment and ensure that the migration proceeds with full organizational support.

### Pre-Migration/Setup Activities Table

### Pre-Migration/Setup Timeline

- **D-7 to D-5:** Confirmation and provisioning of the staging area database.
- **D-5 to D-3:** Microsoft Fabric environment setup.
- **D-3 to D-1:** Installation and configuration of the On-Premises Data Gateway.

## 8.2 Pilot

The Pilot phase is designed to validate the migration approach, processes, and technology stack in a controlled environment. This phase involves migrating a subset of representative data and workloads from UMS to the Microsoft Fabric environment. The pilot allows both Enfrasys Solutions and UMS to identify potential issues, optimize configurations, and refine migration runbooks before full-scale production migration.

During the pilot, Enfrasys Solutions will execute the technical migration steps, monitor system performance, and document any deviations from the expected outcomes. UMS will provide test data, participate in user acceptance testing, and formally approve the pilot results. This collaborative approach ensures that both technical and business requirements are met and that the migration process is robust and repeatable.

A successful pilot mitigates risks, builds stakeholder confidence, and provides a blueprint for the production migration phase.

### Pilot Phase Timeline

- **D-4:** User acceptance testing by UMS.
- **D-3:** Documentation of lessons learned and migration runbook updates.

## 8.3 Production

The Production phase encompasses the full-scale migration of all targeted data and workloads from UMS’s on-premises environment to Microsoft Fabric. This phase is executed according to a rigorously defined timeline to minimize business disruption and ensure data consistency.

The production migration is structured into three core stages: Pre-Migration (D-7), Cutover (D0), and Post-Migration Validation (D+1). During Pre-Migration, final checks, user communications, and backup procedures are completed. The Cutover stage (D0) involves the actual migration of data and switchover of production workloads. Post-Migration (D+1) focuses on system validation, user verification, and resolving any issues that arise during the transition.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the technical execution, while UMS provides data, monitors business continuity, and grants formal acceptance at each stage.

### Production Phase Timeline

- **D0:** Production migration and cutover.
- **D+1:** Post-migration validation and user acceptance.

## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support

The Post-Migration/Support phase ensures a smooth transition to steady-state operations and provides UMS with the necessary support and knowledge transfer to maintain the new environment. This phase includes monitoring system stability, addressing post-migration issues, conducting knowledge transfer sessions, and formally handing over operational responsibilities to UMS.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide post-migration monitoring, incident response, and documentation, while UMS will participate in knowledge transfer sessions and acknowledge the formal handover. This collaborative approach ensures that UMS’s IT team is fully equipped to operate and support the Microsoft Fabric environment independently.

| 5    | Acknowledge handover and commence BAU operations              | UMS               | Not-Started  |

### Post-Migration/Support Timeline

- **D+1 to D+7:** System monitoring and issue resolution.
- **D+2 to D+5:** Knowledge transfer and training sessions.
- **D+7:** Formal handover and commencement of business-as-usual (BAU) operations.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Microsoft Fabric Solution Design

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project’s objectives, the purpose of this Solution Design Document, and the intended audience and responsibilities for review and approval.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has embarked on a strategic initiative to modernize its data analytics capabilities by leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The primary business objective is to design and implement a robust data workflow that supports the university’s evolving analytics and reporting needs. The project scope encompasses the end-to-end data lifecycle, beginning with data ingestion, followed by transformation and advanced analytics, and culminating in business-aligned visualization.

The high-level goals of this project include the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace, the development of comprehensive ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, and the integration of machine learning processes to support predictive analytics. Furthermore, the project aims to seamlessly integrate Power BI to provide actionable insights and facilitate data-driven decision-making across the university. The solution will align with UMS’s broader cloud adoption strategy by utilizing key Microsoft Fabric services, namely Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science capabilities for machine learning applications. By adopting this architecture, UMS will benefit from improved scalability, enhanced data governance, and accelerated time-to-insight.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this Solution Design Document is to serve as the authoritative reference for the architecture, design decisions, and operational workflows that will underpin the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric implementation at UMS. This document details the technical blueprint, including the rationale behind each design choice, to ensure alignment with UMS’s business requirements and Microsoft best practices. It provides clear guidance on the deployment, configuration, and integration of the proposed solution components, and establishes a baseline for future enhancements and operational management.

Within the project lifecycle, this document functions as a critical milestone, ensuring all stakeholders have a shared understanding of the solution approach prior to implementation. It will be used to validate requirements, facilitate informed decision-making, and serve as a benchmark for post-deployment review and continuous improvement.

## 2.3 Document Audience

The Solution Design Document is intended for a diverse audience comprising both technical and business stakeholders. The primary readers include:

- UMS IT Department: Responsible for operational ownership, ongoing support, and integration with existing university systems.
- UMS Business Stakeholders: Senior leadership and departmental representatives who will leverage analytics for strategic and operational decision-making.
- Enfrasys Solutions Implementation Team: Accountable for the design, deployment, and configuration of all solution components.
- Project Sponsors and Governance Committees: Oversight and alignment with university-wide digital transformation initiatives.

Responsibility for the review and formal sign-off of this document is jointly assigned to Universiti Malaysia Sabah and Enfrasys Solutions. Both parties must ensure that the documented solution meets the university’s business objectives, adheres to compliance requirements, and is technically sound prior to commencement of implementation activities.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric and Power BI Overview

This section provides an authoritative overview of Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, with a focus on their relevance and integration within the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data analytics solution.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. Fabric consolidates a suite of core services, including Data Factory, Synapse, Data Science, and OneLake, into a single SaaS environment. This unified approach streamlines the development and management of complex data workflows, enabling organizations to derive actionable insights efficiently and securely.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Microsoft Fabric serves as the foundational platform for orchestrating the entire data lifecycle—from ingestion to transformation, advanced analytics, and visualization. The platform’s modular services enable UMS to address diverse analytical requirements, ensuring scalability, security, and operational agility. The following core services are central to the UMS solution design:

- **Data Factory**: Provides robust data integration and orchestration capabilities, allowing UMS to ingest, transform, and move data across various sources and destinations. This service ensures that data is reliably prepared for downstream analytics and reporting.
- **Synapse**: Delivers advanced analytics and big data processing, enabling UMS to perform large-scale data exploration, transformation, and analysis with high performance. Synapse empowers data engineers and analysts to build complex analytical models and pipelines.
- **Data Science**: Facilitates the development and operationalization of machine learning models. UMS can leverage this service to conduct predictive analytics and automate decision-making processes using advanced algorithms.
- **OneLake**: Acts as a unified data lake, centralizing storage for structured and unstructured data. This ensures data consistency, accessibility, and governance across the UMS analytics ecosystem.

By adopting Microsoft Fabric, UMS benefits from a cohesive platform that reduces integration overhead, enhances data governance, and accelerates time-to-insight for business-aligned analytics initiatives.

## 3.2 Power BI

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture and connectivity requirements for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment. The network design prioritizes secure, reliable outbound data flows from on-premises systems to Microsoft Fabric, leveraging the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) as the critical bridge. ## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

The overall network topology for UMS’s Microsoft Fabric solution is designed to provide secure, managed, and auditable data flows between on-premises data sources and the Microsoft Fabric environment. The architecture leverages the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), which is deployed within the UMS on-premises network, to facilitate outbound connectivity to Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft cloud services. This design ensures that sensitive data remains protected within UMS’s network perimeter while enabling seamless integration with cloud analytics and reporting capabilities.

A key principle of this architecture is the use of outbound-only connectivity from the OPDG virtual machine. No inbound ports are required or permitted, significantly reducing the attack surface and simplifying firewall management. All communications from the OPDG to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and authentication services are encrypted using HTTPS (TCP port 443), adhering to industry-standard security protocols. This approach ensures that UMS’s data flows are both secure and compliant with institutional and regulatory requirements.

To support this connectivity, Enfrasys Solutions recommends the implementation of explicit outbound network security group (NSG) rules. These rules allow only the necessary traffic to Microsoft endpoints for data transfer, authentication, and connectivity verification. UMS is responsible for ensuring that the on-premises network is prepared to support these outbound connections, including any required firewall or proxy adjustments. Enfrasys Solutions will provide design guidance and perform the initial configuration of the OPDG and its network settings.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

The solution is designed to accommodate both traditional ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) and advanced machine learning (ML) workloads, providing a seamless integration between raw data sources, processing layers, and reporting endpoints.

The design incorporates a multi-layered lakehouse architecture—Bronze, Silver, and Gold—each serving a distinct purpose in the data lifecycle. The Bronze layer acts as the raw data landing zone, the Silver layer is dedicated to data cleansing and enrichment, and the Gold layer provides curated, analytics-ready datasets. This structured approach enables UMS to maintain data lineage, quality, and governance across all stages.
