## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview

Network Security Groups (NSGs) are a critical Azure security feature that acts as a virtual firewall, controlling inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources, such as virtual machines (VMs) and subnets. NSGs allow granular control over network traffic based on rules that specify source, destination, protocol, port, and action. For KPJ Healthcare Berhad, NSGs are integral to securing hybrid connectivity and any gateway VMs that facilitate communication between on-premises infrastructure and cloud resources.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends the implementation of tightly scoped NSG rules to minimize the attack surface and enforce the principle of least privilege. All inbound and outbound traffic should be explicitly defined, with unnecessary ports and protocols blocked by default. This approach reduces exposure to threats and ensures that only authorized traffic is permitted, supporting both regulatory compliance and operational security.

The following table outlines the recommended NSG rules for hybrid and gateway VMs in KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s environment:

| Name                   | Priority | Source           | Source Ports | Destination      | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | Purpose                                  |
|------------------------|----------|------------------|--------------|------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|-------------------------------------------|
| Allow-VPN-Inbound      | 100      | On-premises IPs  | *            | Gateway Subnet   | 443, 500, 4500    | TCP/UDP  | Allow  | Enable VPN tunnel establishment           |
| Allow-RDP-Admin        | 200      | IT Admin Subnet  | *            | Gateway VMs      | 3389              | TCP      | Allow  | Secure remote administration              |
| Allow-AD-Sync          | 300      | On-premises AD   | *            | Entra Connect VM | 389, 636, 3268    | TCP      | Allow  | Directory synchronization                 |
| Allow-HTTPS-Outbound   | 400      | Gateway VMs      | *            | Internet         | 443               | TCP      | Allow  | Secure cloud service communication        |
| Deny-All-Inbound       | 4096     | *                | *            | *                | *                 | *        | Deny   | Block all other inbound traffic           |
| Deny-All-Outbound      | 4096     | *                | *            | *                | *                 | *        | Deny   | Block all other outbound traffic          |

These rules ensure that only necessary management, synchronization, and VPN traffic is permitted, while all other traffic is denied by default. Enfrasys Solutions will configure and validate these NSG rules. KPJ Healthcare Berhad is responsible for reviewing and approving the final rule set to ensure alignment with internal compliance policies.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is fundamental to protecting sensitive healthcare and operational data in transit and at rest. Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Microsoft Teams, and Single Sign-On (SSO) applications, utilize industry-standard encryption protocols to safeguard data throughout its lifecycle.

### 7.2.1 Exchange Online

Exchange Online is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade cloud email platform. It provides built-in encryption for data at rest using BitLocker and service encryption with Microsoft-managed keys. Data in transit is protected using TLS (Transport Layer Security) for SMTP and HTTPS for client connections.

For KPJ Healthcare Berhad, Enfrasys Solutions will ensure that all mail flow, including hybrid configurations, enforces TLS 1.2 or higher. Additionally, mailbox-level encryption (such as Office Message Encryption) can be enabled for sensitive communications. KPJ Healthcare Berhad is responsible for reviewing encryption configurations to ensure compliance with healthcare data protection requirements.

### 7.2.2 SharePoint Online

SharePoint Online is a secure, cloud-based collaboration platform. Data at rest is encrypted using BitLocker and per-file encryption with unique keys. Data in transit is secured via HTTPS/TLS.

Enfrasys Solutions will validate that all SharePoint sites enforce HTTPS connections and that sharing policies restrict external access unless explicitly authorized. KPJ Healthcare Berhad must review sharing and encryption policies for compliance with internal governance.

### 7.2.3 OneDrive for Business

OneDrive for Business provides personal cloud storage with robust encryption. Data at rest is protected using BitLocker and per-file encryption keys. Data in transit is secured via HTTPS/TLS.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure OneDrive to enforce modern authentication and restrict sharing to trusted domains. KPJ Healthcare Berhad is responsible for ongoing compliance monitoring and user education regarding secure sharing practices.

### 7.2.4 Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams leverages SharePoint and OneDrive for file storage, inheriting their encryption controls. All Teams chat, meeting, and file data is encrypted at rest and in transit using industry-standard protocols.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the project’s business context, the scope of the engagement, and the purpose and audience of this Solution Design Document. It establishes the foundation for the detailed technical and operational guidance that follows.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) is undertaking a strategic initiative to modernize its data analytics environment by leveraging Microsoft Fabric, a unified SaaS platform designed for comprehensive data integration, advanced analytics, and business intelligence. The primary objective of this project is to design and implement a robust data workflow that seamlessly ingests, transforms, and visualizes institutional data to drive informed decision-making and support UMS’s business objectives.

The project scope encompasses the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace for UMS, the development of an end-to-end Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipeline, and the integration of machine learning processes for predictive analytics. In addition, the solution will incorporate Power BI to deliver business-aligned analytics and actionable insights. The design leverages key Microsoft Fabric services, including Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science for machine learning applications. This initiative aligns with UMS’s broader cloud adoption strategy, ensuring scalability, security, and operational efficiency across the university’s data landscape.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to provide a comprehensive and authoritative blueprint for the design, implementation, and governance of the Microsoft Fabric-based analytics platform at UMS. It serves as the primary reference for design review, technical validation, and alignment among all stakeholders, ensuring that the solution meets both business and technical requirements. The document details architectural decisions, workflow designs, security considerations, and operational processes, facilitating a consistent and controlled implementation approach. This document will be used throughout the project lifecycle to guide solution deployment, support change management, and enable effective knowledge transfer.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This Solution Design Document is intended for a broad audience involved in the planning, execution, and oversight of the Microsoft Fabric implementation at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The primary readers include:

- UMS IT management and technical teams responsible for solution review and operational ownership
- Enfrasys Solutions architects, consultants, and implementation specialists responsible for solution design and deployment
- Project sponsors and executive stakeholders at UMS overseeing strategic alignment and value realization
- Security, governance, and compliance personnel ensuring adherence to institutional policies and regulatory standards

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the authorship, accuracy, and maintenance of this document. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is accountable for document review, validation, and formal sign-off, ensuring that the design aligns with institutional objectives and operational requirements.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric, Power BI & Entra ID Overview

This section provides an authoritative overview of the core Microsoft technologies forming the foundation of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data platform solution. The following sub-sections detail Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft Entra ID, highlighting their roles, integration points, and key features within the overall architecture.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single SaaS solution. Fabric brings together core services such as Data Factory, Synapse, and Data Science, providing a seamless environment for organizations to ingest, transform, analyze, and visualize data at scale.

Within the UMS solution, Microsoft Fabric serves as the backbone for the data workflow. Data Factory enables robust data integration and orchestration, supporting the extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) of data from diverse sources into a centralized data lake. Synapse provides advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, allowing UMS to perform large-scale data transformations and aggregations efficiently. The Data Science service empowers data professionals to develop, train, and operationalize machine learning models directly within the Fabric ecosystem, accelerating the delivery of business insights.

By leveraging Microsoft Fabric, UMS benefits from a unified workspace that simplifies administration, enhances security, and accelerates time-to-value for analytics initiatives. The platform's deep integration with other Microsoft services ensures scalability, governance, and operational efficiency, positioning UMS for advanced analytics and AI-driven decision-making.

### Microsoft Fabric Summary Table

| Technology        | Description                                                                                      | Key Features                                                                                  |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Fabric  | Unified analytics platform integrating data movement, engineering, science, and BI.              | Data Factory (ETL), Synapse (Analytics), Data Science (ML), centralized workspace, governance |

**Action By:**  
- Technical definitions and platform deployment by Enfrasys Solutions  
- Validation and alignment with business requirements by Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS)

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is a leading business intelligence and data visualization service from Microsoft, designed to transform raw data into actionable insights through interactive reports and dashboards. Power BI seamlessly integrates with Microsoft Fabric, enabling users to connect directly to curated datasets, dataflows, and machine learning outputs within the Fabric workspace.

In the context of UMS, Power BI acts as the primary interface for business users to explore, analyze, and present data. By leveraging Fabric’s unified data foundation, Power BI ensures that analytics are always based on the latest, governed data, thus enhancing data accuracy and trust. The platform supports advanced analytics features such as natural language queries, AI-powered visualizations, and real-time data streaming, empowering UMS stakeholders to make informed decisions rapidly.

The integration of Power BI with Microsoft Fabric not only streamlines the analytics workflow but also enforces consistent security and access controls, as all user authentication and authorization are centrally managed. This approach reduces operational overhead and ensures compliance with institutional data governance policies.

### Power BI Summary Table

| Technology | Description                                                                                       | Key Features                                                                                      |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Power BI   | Business intelligence and visualization platform for interactive reporting and analytics.          | Integration with Fabric, data modeling, AI visuals, real-time dashboards, secure sharing           |

**Action By:**  
- Technical definitions, integration architecture, and enablement by Enfrasys Solutions  
- Validation of reporting requirements and user adoption by Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS)

## 3.3 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID, formerly known as Azure Active Directory (Azure AD), is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. Entra ID is designed to provide secure authentication, authorization, and conditional access for users, applications, and resources across the Microsoft ecosystem.

For UMS, Entra ID is the authoritative identity provider for all users accessing Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related services. It enforces strong authentication protocols, supports single sign-on (SSO), and enables Conditional Access policies to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive data and analytics assets. Entra ID’s centralized management capabilities allow UMS to streamline user provisioning, monitor access patterns, and respond rapidly to security incidents.

The integration of Entra ID with Microsoft Fabric and Power BI ensures a consistent security posture across the entire analytics platform, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and supporting compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements.

### Microsoft Entra ID Summary Table

| Technology      | Description                                                                                              | Key Features                                                                                   |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Entra ID | Cloud-based identity and access management service for authentication and authorization.                  | SSO, Conditional Access, MFA, centralized user management, integration with Microsoft services |

**Action By:**  
- Technical definitions, identity integration, and policy configuration by Enfrasys Solutions  
- User validation and access policy approval by Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS)

# 4.0 Network Design and Decision

This section outlines the network architecture and design decisions for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in the context of Microsoft Fabric deployment. It details the secure connectivity between on-premises infrastructure and cloud services, the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) design, and the outbound network security rules required to support seamless and secure data integration.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

A robust and secure network architecture is essential to enable reliable data flows between UMS’s on-premises systems and Microsoft Fabric in the cloud. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a hybrid connectivity model that leverages outbound-only connections to Microsoft cloud services, eliminating the need for inbound firewall exceptions and minimizing the attack surface. This model ensures that all data transfers and authentication requests originate from within UMS’s trusted network, traversing securely over encrypted channels to Microsoft endpoints.

The architecture is designed so that all user and system access to Microsoft Fabric is governed by Azure Conditional Access policies, enforced via Microsoft Entra ID. This approach provides granular control over authentication and authorization, ensuring that only compliant and authenticated users can access sensitive resources. The use of outbound-only connections for the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) further enhances security by preventing unsolicited inbound traffic, aligning with both Microsoft and industry best practices for cloud connectivity.

## 7.1 Azure NSG Overview

A Network Security Group (NSG) in Azure is a critical security component that acts as a virtual firewall, controlling inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources at the subnet or network interface level. NSGs are essential for enforcing least-privilege network access, ensuring that only authorized traffic can reach critical workloads such as the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine, which facilitates secure data movement between on-premises systems and Microsoft Fabric services.

For the UMS Fabric deployment, Enfrasys Solutions has designed outbound-only NSG rules for the Data Gateway VM. This approach aligns with the security principle of minimizing attack surfaces by blocking all unnecessary inbound traffic while allowing only the specific outbound flows required for Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Microsoft cloud service connectivity. Outbound rules are meticulously crafted to enable secure HTTPS communication, authentication, and network connectivity verification, ensuring the Data Gateway VM can perform its functions without exposing the environment to unnecessary risk.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is a foundational security control for all data processed, stored, or transmitted within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environments. Microsoft Fabric and Power BI both leverage industry-standard encryption mechanisms to protect data at rest and in transit, ensuring confidentiality and integrity across the entire data lifecycle.

**Encryption at Rest:**  
Data at rest within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI is encrypted using strong cryptographic algorithms such as AES-256. All storage accounts, databases, and OneLake repositories are protected by default with Microsoft-managed keys, and customers may optionally provide their own keys for enhanced control. This ensures that even if physical storage media are compromised, the data remains unreadable and secure.

**Encryption in Transit:**  
All data transmitted between users, services, and Microsoft cloud endpoints is encrypted using TLS (Transport Layer Security) protocols. This includes communications between the Data Gateway VM, Microsoft Fabric services, Power BI, and all supporting Microsoft cloud services. TLS 1.2 or higher is enforced, preventing eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, and tampering with data as it traverses public or private networks.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for defining and documenting all security controls related to encryption, including key management, protocol enforcement, and monitoring. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ensuring that all users and administrators comply with these controls, including the use of strong authentication, secure endpoints, and adherence to organizational security policies.

By implementing comprehensive encryption at rest and in transit, UMS ensures that sensitive academic, research, and operational data remain protected against unauthorized access, supporting regulatory compliance and institutional trust.

## 8.2 Pilot

The pilot phase is designed to validate the migration approach on a limited scope before full-scale production deployment. Enfrasys Solutions will lead the pilot deployment, selecting a representative subset of data and workloads from UMS's environment. This ensures that all integration points, data flow processes, and security controls are thoroughly tested under real-world conditions.

During the pilot, Enfrasys Solutions will configure the Microsoft Fabric environment, connect the On-Premises Data Gateway, and perform initial data ingestion from the staging area. UMS IT personnel will be engaged to review data accuracy, validate business processes, and provide feedback on user experience. This collaborative approach allows for early identification and resolution of issues, reducing risk for the subsequent production rollout.

Key responsibilities during the pilot phase are as follows:
- Enfrasys Solutions: Environment configuration, gateway setup, pilot data migration, troubleshooting, and documentation of outcomes.
- UMS: Validation of migrated data, functional testing, and feedback provision.

## 8.3 Production

The production rollout is executed in a structured timeline to ensure a smooth transition with minimal disruption to UMS operations. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a phased approach, leveraging the following timeline:

- **D-7 (Pre-Migration Week):** Final validation of pilot outcomes, user communication, and scheduling of migration windows. Enfrasys Solutions will conduct readiness assessments and UMS will notify stakeholders of impending changes.
- **D0 (Cutover Day):** Execution of the production migration, including final data synchronization, activation of the new environment, and decommissioning of legacy connections as appropriate. Enfrasys Solutions will oversee technical execution, while UMS will monitor business continuity.
- **D+1 (Post-Migration Day):** Immediate post-migration support, user acceptance testing, and issue resolution. Both Enfrasys Solutions and UMS will collaborate to address any post-cutover anomalies and ensure system stability.

Post-migration activities are critical to ensure the stability and ongoing success of the new environment. # SIRIM Analytics Deployment

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the SIRIM Analytics Deployment project, the purpose of this Solution Design Document, and identifies the intended audience and responsibilities for document management.

## 2.1 Project Overview

The SIRIM Analytics Deployment project is a strategic initiative designed to modernize and streamline the organization’s Human Resource data management and analytics capabilities. The primary objective is to establish a robust data workflow that encompasses the full lifecycle of HR data—from initial ingestion, through transformation and processing, to advanced visualization for actionable insights.

The solution architecture leverages Microsoft Fabric, a unified analytics platform, to ensure seamless integration, scalability, and security. Microsoft Fabric Data Factory will be utilized for data integration and orchestration, enabling efficient and automated ingestion of HR data from various sources into a centralized environment. Fabric Synapse will provide advanced data analytics and big data processing capabilities, supporting complex data transformations and enabling the development of comprehensive HR analytics models. The final stage of the workflow delivers interactive visualizations, empowering SIRIM’s HR stakeholders to make data-driven decisions with confidence.

This deployment aligns with SIRIM’s broader cloud adoption strategy, ensuring that all data operations benefit from the reliability, compliance, and innovation inherent in Microsoft’s cloud ecosystem. The design also incorporates best practices for network security, workspace permission management, and data governance, ensuring that sensitive HR data remains protected throughout its lifecycle.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this Solution Design Document is to serve as the authoritative reference for the design, validation, and implementation of the SIRIM Analytics Deployment. The document provides a comprehensive blueprint covering infrastructure, data workflow, security, access controls, and operational processes, all tailored to SIRIM’s requirements and aligned with Microsoft Fabric best practices.

This document is intended to facilitate design validation by all project stakeholders and to guide the technical implementation, ensuring that all components are delivered according to agreed standards and that risks are proactively managed. Enfrasys Solutions has prepared this document to ensure clarity, transparency, and alignment across teams, and to support SIRIM in achieving a successful analytics transformation.

## 2.3 Document Audience

The Solution Design Document is intended for the following audiences:

- SIRIM IT Department: For technical validation, operational readiness, and ongoing administration.
- SIRIM Human Resource Department: For alignment with HR analytics requirements and data governance needs.
- Enfrasys Solutions Architects and Consultants: For design, implementation, and support activities.
- SIRIM Project Sponsors and Executive Stakeholders: For oversight, strategic alignment, and project approval.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the preparation, accuracy, and completeness of this document. SIRIM is responsible for reviewing the content, providing feedback, and granting formal approval prior to implementation. This collaborative approach ensures that the solution meets both technical and business objectives, and that all stakeholders are engaged throughout the project lifecycle.

# 3.0 Microsoft Fabric Analytics Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of Microsoft Fabric and its supporting ecosystem, including Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, as they pertain to SIRIM’s analytics modernization initiative. The following subsections detail the core technologies, their architectural roles, and the responsibilities of Enfrasys Solutions and SIRIM in the adoption process.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric: Definition, Architecture, and Service Components

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform designed to unify data movement, engineering, and business intelligence within a single, secure environment. It enables organizations to ingest, transform, and visualize data at scale, leveraging cloud-native services for end-to-end analytics workflows. Microsoft Fabric consolidates multiple data services under a cohesive architecture, streamlining the development and operation of modern data pipelines.

The architecture of Microsoft Fabric is built around several core components:

- **Data Factory**: This service provides powerful data integration and orchestration capabilities. It enables the extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) of data from diverse sources into the analytics environment, automating complex workflows and ensuring data consistency.
- **Synapse**: Microsoft Fabric Synapse delivers advanced analytics and big data processing. It supports data engineering, data warehousing, and real-time analytics, empowering organizations to derive insights from large and complex datasets.
- **OneLake**: Serving as the unified data lake for Microsoft Fabric, OneLake centralizes data storage, offering seamless access and integration across all analytics workloads. It supports structured and unstructured data, ensuring scalability and data governance.
- **Power BI**: Power BI is the business intelligence and visualization layer of Microsoft Fabric. It enables users to create interactive reports, dashboards, and semantic models, democratizing access to insights and supporting data-driven decision-making.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends the adoption of Microsoft Fabric for SIRIM’s Human Resource analytics use-case to ensure a robust, scalable, and secure data workflow. The integration of these components allows SIRIM to efficiently ingest data from operational sources, perform advanced data engineering, and deliver actionable insights through intuitive visualizations.

The following diagram illustrates the proposed data workflow architecture, highlighting the flow of data from ingestion to visualization, and the interaction between Microsoft Fabric components.

The diagram below represents the end-to-end data pipeline for SIRIM’s Human Resource analytics use-case. Data is ingested from the TOPAZ system within the SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG resource group using Data Factory. The pipeline processes data through bronze, silver, and gold Lakehouse layers, with each stage refining and enriching the dataset. Synapse is leveraged for advanced engineering on silver tables, while OneLake provides unified data storage. The final, business-ready data in gold tables is visualized using Power BI, ensuring secure access and governance via integrated identity management.

![](images\slide_014_img_003.png)

Figure 3.1: SIRIM Human Resource Data Workflow Architecture

The adoption of this architecture ensures that SIRIM benefits from centralized data governance, streamlined ETL processes, and rapid delivery of business insights. Enfrasys Solutions shall provide detailed technology explanations, architecture design, and enablement workshops, while SIRIM is responsible for the operational adoption and integration of these services into their business processes.

## 3.2 Microsoft 365 and Entra ID: Identity, Access, and Collaboration

Microsoft 365 is a comprehensive suite of productivity and collaboration tools, encompassing applications such as Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, and OneDrive. It provides the foundational platform for secure communication, document management, and collaborative workflows within modern organizations. Microsoft 365 integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, enabling seamless access to analytics outputs and supporting cross-functional collaboration.

Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides centralized authentication, authorization, and security policy enforcement for users and applications across the Microsoft ecosystem. Entra ID is critical for managing user identities, implementing role-based access control (RBAC), and ensuring compliance with organizational security standards.

In the context of SIRIM’s analytics platform, Microsoft 365 facilitates collaboration on analytical assets, while Entra ID governs access to data and reports. This integration ensures that only authorized personnel can access sensitive HR data, and that all activities are auditable and compliant with regulatory requirements.

## 4.1 Network Connectivity Overview

Private Endpoints are used to further enhance security for Fabric services. By restricting access to Fabric resources through internal Azure networking, exposure to public endpoints is minimized. ## 5.2 Microsoft Fabric-native Roles

Microsoft Fabric provides a robust native role-based access control (RBAC) model at the workspace level. Each role is designed to align with specific job functions, ensuring that users are granted the minimum privileges necessary to perform their duties, thereby enhancing security and operational efficiency.

The primary native roles in Microsoft Fabric are as follows:

- **Admin:** Full control over the workspace, including management of roles, permissions, and all content. This role is typically assigned to data engineers or platform administrators who require broad access for operational oversight.
- **Contributor:** Can create, edit, and delete their own content but cannot alter workspace settings or delete content owned by others. This role is suitable for business user admins or data engineers who are responsible for developing and maintaining analytics assets.
- **Viewer:** Granted read-only access to reports and dashboards, without the ability to edit or publish content. This role is ideal for data analysts and business users who need to consume insights without modifying underlying assets.
- **Member:** Able to create, edit, and delete reports, pipelines, and other assets, and share content with others, but cannot manage workspace roles or permissions. This role is generally assigned to data engineers who are actively involved in content development.

## 7.2 Encryption Design

Encryption is fundamental to protecting sensitive data both at rest and in transit within the SIRIM solution. Microsoft Fabric, Data Gateway, and Power BI each implement robust encryption mechanisms, ensuring that data confidentiality and integrity are maintained across all workflows.

### Encryption at Rest

Data at rest within Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage is protected using Azure-managed encryption keys, leveraging industry-standard AES-256 encryption. This ensures that all stored data—whether in databases, data lakes, or intermediate storage—is encrypted by default, mitigating the risk of unauthorized access in the event of a physical or logical breach.

Power BI datasets and artifacts are similarly encrypted at rest. The use of Azure Storage for Power BI and Fabric ensures a consistent encryption approach across the data estate. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring and validating encryption settings during deployment, while SIRIM is accountable for ongoing compliance monitoring and validation.

### Encryption in Transit

All data transmitted between clients, the WVD environment, and Microsoft Fabric services is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. This includes connections from end-user devices to WVD, from WVD to Fabric, and from Fabric to integrated services such as Power BI, Azure Data Explorer, and Azure SQL Database. The use of service tags in NSG rules ensures that only encrypted traffic is permitted, and public endpoints are disabled wherever possible to reduce exposure.

It is important to note that, as of the current Microsoft platform capabilities, Power BI does not support Private Link for Fabric datasets, and certain features such as Copilot are not yet available for private endpoints. As a result, some data flows may traverse public endpoints but remain protected by strong encryption in transit. Enfrasys Solutions will configure all supported private endpoints and enforce NSG rules to restrict access, while SIRIM is responsible for validating that these controls meet organizational compliance standards.

## 7.3 Access Design (Conditional Access and Private Endpoint)

Conditional Access is a critical component of SIRIM’s security design, providing adaptive access control based on user identity, device health, location, and risk. Enfrasys Solutions will configure Conditional Access policies to enforce secure login, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and access restrictions for both SIRIM users and external collaborators.

SIRIM users are granted direct access to Microsoft Fabric resources, governed by Conditional Access policies that include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage. External users access Fabric resources indirectly via the WVD environment, which is protected by NSG rules and network isolation. This layered approach ensures that only authenticated and authorized users can access sensitive data and services.

Private endpoints are enabled for Fabric where supported, ensuring that traffic remains within the Azure backbone and is not exposed to the public internet. However, due to current platform limitations, some services (such as Power BI datasets in Fabric) may still require public endpoints. Enfrasys Solutions will disable public access wherever possible and document any exceptions for SIRIM’s compliance review.

The following table summarizes the key design considerations for Conditional Access and Private Endpoint implementation:

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                 | Private Endpoint                     |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| DC01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage | Enable Private Link in Fabric        |
| DC02 | Configure NSG in existing SIRIM’s WVD for Fabric inbound and outbound              | Create Private Endpoint in Azure portal |
| DC03 | Include SIRIM user inside Conditional Access policy                                | Disable Public Access from Fabric     |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the technical implementation of Conditional Access policies, NSG rules, and private endpoint configuration. SIRIM is responsible for validating that these controls align with internal compliance requirements and for managing policy exceptions as needed.

## 7.4 Security Design Decisions

The following table documents the key security design decisions made for the SIRIM solution, along with the rationale for each decision.

| No. | Design Decision                                                                                                    | Decision                                                                                                    |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | All inbound and outbound access to Microsoft Fabric from WVD is restricted to TLS-encrypted traffic (port 443)     | Enforced via NSG rules using service tags and private IP addresses                                          |
| 2   | SIRIM users access Fabric directly; external users access via WVD with network isolation                           | Conditional Access and NSG rules applied to segregate user types                                            |
| 3   | Conditional Access policies include all relevant Microsoft services (Power BI, Azure Data Explorer, SQL, Storage)  | Configured by Enfrasys Solutions, validated by SIRIM                                                        |
| 4   | Data at rest is encrypted using platform-managed keys (AES-256)                                                    | Enforced across Fabric, Data Gateway, Power BI, and Azure Storage                                           |
| 5   | Data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher                                                               | Required for all client-to-service and service-to-service communications                                     |
| 6   | Private endpoints enabled for Fabric where supported; public access disabled where possible                        | Configured by Enfrasys Solutions; SIRIM to validate compliance                                              |
| 7   | Exceptions documented for features not supporting private endpoints (e.g., Power BI Fabric datasets, Copilot)      | Enfrasys to document, SIRIM to review and accept risk                                                       |

This comprehensive security design ensures that SIRIM’s data and resources are protected in accordance with best practices, regulatory requirements, and the organization’s risk appetite. Enfrasys Solutions will provide detailed documentation and ongoing support to facilitate SIRIM’s compliance validation and audit processes.

# 8.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration strategy for the SIRIM solution. It details the preparatory steps, pilot execution, production cutover, and post-migration support, ensuring a seamless transition with clear ownership and timeline accountability.

## 8.1 Pre-Migration/Setup

A successful migration is predicated on thorough preparation and clear task delineation. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that all stakeholders complete foundational activities prior to any data movement or cutover. These activities include finalizing the design documentation, confirming the data tables for ingestion, and provisioning the necessary Azure infrastructure components, such as the Data Gateway virtual machine. These steps ensure that SIRIM’s environment is fully validated, dependencies are resolved, and all parties are aligned on migration objectives.

Enfrasys Solutions will lead the technical documentation and infrastructure setup, while SIRIM is responsible for confirming business data requirements and providing timely feedback. This collaborative approach minimizes risk and ensures that technical and business prerequisites are satisfied before proceeding.

The following table details the preparatory tasks, responsible parties, and current status:

| Activity                                              | Planned Start     | Planned End       | Action By      | Status      |
|-------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------|---------------|------------|
| Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by SIRIM       | Fri, 13-June-25   | Tues, 17-June-25  | Enfrasys, SIRIM| Not-Started |
| Confirm on the table to be ingested                   | Wed, 11-June-25   | Fri, 13-June-25   | SIRIM         | Not-Started |
| Create an Azure VM to establish Data Gateway          |                   |                   | Enfrasys      | Not-Started |

Enfrasys Solutions will coordinate with SIRIM to ensure all pre-migration tasks are tracked to completion. Any delays or issues will be escalated promptly to maintain the migration schedule.

## 8.2 Pilot

The pilot phase is critical to validate migration processes, test data flows, and ensure that all technical and business requirements are met in a controlled environment. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a pilot window from D-7 to D0, during which a subset of data and workloads are migrated and validated. The pilot scope should include representative data tables, integration points, and end-user acceptance testing.

During the pilot, Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring the migration tools, executing the pilot migration, and providing technical support. SIRIM is responsible for reviewing pilot results, validating data integrity, and confirming that business processes function as intended. This phase allows for early identification and remediation of issues before full-scale production migration.

The pilot timeline and responsibilities are as follows:

| Activity                                  | Planned Start | Planned End | Action By      | Status      |
|--------------------------------------------|---------------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| Conduct pilot migration session            | D-7           | D-5         | Enfrasys      | Planned    |
| Validate ingested data and integration     | D-5           | D-3         | SIRIM         | Planned    |
| Review pilot results and sign-off          | D-3           | D0          | SIRIM, Enfrasys| Planned   |

This structured pilot ensures that SIRIM’s migration objectives are met with minimal disruption and that the production migration is informed by real-world results.

## 8.3 Production

The production migration is executed following successful pilot completion and sign-off. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a structured cutover plan, with clearly defined go-live steps and a timeline that minimizes business impact. The production migration includes final data ingestion, system validation, and user enablement. Cutover is scheduled for D0, with immediate post-migration support on D+1 to address any issues.

Enfrasys Solutions will execute the technical migration steps, monitor system health, and provide hypercare support during and immediately after cutover. SIRIM is responsible for user communication, business process validation, and issue escalation if required.

The production migration steps and timeline are as follows:

| Activity                                  | Planned Start | Planned End | Action By      | Status      |
|--------------------------------------------|---------------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| Finalize production migration preparation  | D-2           | D-1         | Enfrasys      | Planned    |
| Execute production cutover                 | D0            | D0          | Enfrasys      | Planned    |
| Validate production data and processes     | D0            | D0          | SIRIM         | Planned    |
| Post-migration support and monitoring      | D+1           | D+1         | Enfrasys      | Planned    |

This approach ensures that all technical and business stakeholders are engaged throughout the migration, with clear accountability for each activity.

## 8.4 Post-Migration/Support

A robust post-migration support model is essential to ensure ongoing system stability and user satisfaction. Enfrasys Solutions provides immediate post-migration support (hypercare) for a defined period following cutover, during which any technical or operational issues are addressed promptly. After the hypercare period, Enfrasys Solutions will formally hand over operational responsibilities to SIRIM’s IT team, including documentation, knowledge transfer, and escalation procedures.

The support model includes a clear escalation path for unresolved issues, with Enfrasys Solutions providing tier-2/3 support as needed. SIRIM is responsible for first-line user support and ongoing system monitoring, with the ability to escalate complex issues to Enfrasys Solutions.

The post-migration support process is summarized below:

| Activity                                   | Planned Start | Planned End | Action By      | Status      |
|---------------------------------------------|---------------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| Immediate post-migration (hypercare)        | D+1           | D+7         | Enfrasys      | Planned    |
| Knowledge transfer and documentation        | D+2           | D+7         | Enfrasys      | Planned    |
| Formal handover to SIRIM IT                 | D+7           | D+7         | Enfrasys, SIRIM| Planned   |
| Ongoing support and escalation              | D+8           | Ongoing     | SIRIM, Enfrasys| Planned   |

This support and handover model ensures SIRIM’s operational readiness and provides a safety net for any post-migration challenges, enabling a smooth transition to steady-state operations.

The diagram illustrates a technical architecture involving Azure components and user access flow. 

1. **Subscription**: Represents the Azure subscription under which resources are managed. It is the foundational layer for resource organization and billing.

2. **WVD (Windows Virtual Desktop)**: This component is deployed within the subscription, providing virtual desktop infrastructure to external users. It allows users to access virtualized applications and desktops hosted in Azure.

3. **External User**: Represents users outside the organization accessing resources through WVD. They connect to the virtual desktop environment to utilize applications and services.

4. **Fabric-RG (Resource Group)**: A logical container within the Azure subscription that holds related resources for Azure solutions. It organizes and manages resources like SIRIM FABRIC.

5. **SIRIM FABRIC**: A specific application or service hosted within the Fabric-RG. It is accessed by users through the WVD environment.

6. **Conditional Access**: Security measures applied to ensure that only authorized SIRIM users can access the SIRIM FABRIC. It involves policies that enforce access controls based on user identity and compliance requirements.

7. **SIRIM User**: Represents internal users who access the SIRIM FABRIC through conditional access policies. They are authenticated and authorized to use the service.

The data flow begins with external users connecting to the WVD environment, which is part of the Azure subscription. Through WVD, users access the SIRIM FABRIC hosted within the Fabric-RG. Conditional access policies ensure that only authorized SIRIM users can interact with the SIRIM FABRIC, maintaining security and compliance.

The diagram illustrates a network architecture involving Azure Virtual Networks (VNETs), Virtual Network Gateways, and VNET Peering. 

1. **SIRIM**: Represents an on-premises network connecting to Azure via a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN. This connection is established through a Virtual Network Gateway within Azure.

2. **Subscription**: Indicates the Azure subscription under which the resources are provisioned.

3. **VNET (x.x.x.x/x)**: Two separate VNETs are shown, each with a specific IP address range. These VNETs are part of the Azure infrastructure.

4. **Virtual Network Gateways**: Located within a GatewaySubnet, these gateways facilitate the S2S VPN connection from the on-premises network to Azure.

5. **VNET Peering**: Connects the two VNETs, allowing resources within them to communicate with each other. This peering is essential for seamless data flow and resource access across VNETs.

6. **Fabric-RG and Fabric-VNET**: Represents a resource group and VNET dedicated to a specific service or application, possibly related to Microsoft Fabric.

7. **Fabric Private Endpoint**: Located within a Fabric-SUBNET, this endpoint provides secure access to Azure services, ensuring that traffic remains within the Azure network.

8. **WVD (Windows Virtual Desktop)**: Deployed within one of the VNETs, allowing external users to access virtual desktops hosted in Azure.

9. **External User**: Represents users accessing the Windows Virtual Desktop from outside the Azure network.

The architecture ensures secure connectivity between on-premises and Azure resources, leveraging VPN and VNET peering for efficient data flow and resource management.

The diagram represents a data workflow architecture within Azure, specifically focusing on data ingestion, transformation, and visualization.

1. **Data Source**: The process begins with data ingestion from a source labeled "TOPAZ" within the resource group "SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG". This likely represents a database or data storage system.

2. **Data Factory**: Azure Data Factory is used to ingest data from the source. It serves as the ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) tool, orchestrating the movement and transformation of data.

3. **Bronze Tables**: The ingested data is first stored in "XX_Bronze_LK Tables". Bronze tables typically contain raw, unprocessed data.

4. **Silver Tables**: Data is then transformed and moved to "XX_Silver_LK Tables". Silver tables contain cleaned and enriched data, ready for further processing.

5. **Gold Tables**: The final transformation stage involves moving data to "XX_Gold_LK Tables". Gold tables contain highly processed, business-ready data optimized for analytics.

6. **Synapse Engineering**: Azure Synapse Analytics is used for advanced data processing and analytics. It connects with the Silver tables for further engineering and transformation tasks.

7. **Identity_SM**: This component likely represents a security or identity management system, ensuring secure access and data governance.

8. **OneLake**: Data is connected via OneLake, a unified data lake service, facilitating seamless data access and integration.

9. **Power BI**: The processed data in Gold tables is visualized using Power BI, enabling business intelligence and reporting.

This architecture illustrates a comprehensive data pipeline leveraging Azure services for efficient data management and analytics.

The diagram represents a technical architecture involving data flow and system components. It consists of the following elements:

1. **SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG**: This is a resource group that contains the components involved in the data processing workflow.

2. **TOPAZ**: This component appears to be a server or service within the resource group, likely responsible for data storage or processing. It is associated with a PostgreSQL database, indicating it handles relational data.

3. **Data Gateway VM**: This virtual machine acts as a data gateway, facilitating secure data transfer between the TOPAZ component and external systems. It serves as an intermediary, ensuring data is transmitted efficiently and securely.

4. **SIRIM FABRIC**: This component represents an external system or service that receives data from the Data Gateway VM. It likely serves as a data integration or analytics platform, processing and utilizing the data received.

**Data Flow**:
- Data originates from the TOPAZ component, where it is stored or processed within the PostgreSQL database.
- The Data Gateway VM acts as a conduit, securely transferring data from TOPAZ to the SIRIM FABRIC.
- SIRIM FABRIC receives the data for further processing, integration, or analytics purposes.

The architecture ensures secure and efficient data transfer between internal and external systems, leveraging virtual machines and databases for optimal data management.

# KPJ Healthcare Microsoft 365 Migration Project Design # 2.0 Executive Summary This section provides a concise overview of the Microsoft 365 migration project for KPJ Healthcare Berhad, outlining the project’s business drivers, scope, and objectives. It also clarifies the purpose and audience of this Solution Design Document, establishing roles and responsibilities for both Enfrasys Solutions and KPJ Healthcare Berhad. ## 2.1 Project Overview KPJ Healthcare Berhad is undertaking a strategic migration to Microsoft 365 to modernize its collaboration, productivity, and security platforms. The primary business drivers for this initiative include improving operational efficiency, enhancing data security, and enabling seamless collaboration across the organization’s extensive network of healthcare facilities. The migration scope encompasses a substantial user base, with 6,615 license accounts, 5,886 mailboxes, 1,783 shared mailboxes, 808 distribution lists, 210 mail-enabled security groups, 73 security groups, 1,869 SharePoint sites, 17 resource rooms, and 6 SSO applications. The high-level goals for KPJ Healthcare Berhad are to ensure a secure, scalable, and resilient Microsoft 365 environment, minimize disruption during migration, and establish robust governance for ongoing operations. The migration will be executed in structured phases, including pre-migration assessment, pilot migration, production rollout, and post-migration support, ensuring comprehensive coverage and risk mitigation. ## 2.2 Document Purpose The Solution Design Document (SDD) serves as the authoritative blueprint for KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s Microsoft 365 migration. Its purpose is to articulate the technical architecture, design decisions, migration strategies, and operational procedures required to achieve the project’s objectives. The SDD provides detailed guidance for configuring, deploying, and managing Microsoft 365 workloads, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and associated security and compliance controls. It acts as a reference for all stakeholders throughout the migration lifecycle, supporting alignment, accountability, and informed decision-making. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for drafting the SDD, ensuring it reflects best practices and meets KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s requirements, while KPJ Healthcare Berhad is responsible for reviewing and approving the document prior to implementation. ## 2.3 Document Audience The intended audience for this Solution Design Document includes KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s IT management and technical teams, Enfrasys Solutions’ project and engineering personnel, and key business stakeholders involved in the migration. Specifically, the document is designed for KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s IT administrators, infrastructure specialists, and compliance officers who will oversee and manage the Microsoft 365 environment post-migration. Enfrasys Solutions’ architects and project managers will use the SDD to guide implementation and ensure adherence to the approved design. Additionally, executive sponsors and business leaders may reference the SDD to validate alignment with organizational goals and regulatory requirements. Enfrasys Solutions is tasked with preparing the document, while KPJ Healthcare Berhad is responsible for its review, validation, and approval to ensure it meets all operational and compliance needs. # 3.0 Microsoft 365 Overview This section provides a comprehensive overview of the Microsoft 365 platform, its core workloads, and supporting technologies as implemented for KPJ Healthcare Berhad. The design incorporates industry best practices, ensuring robust identity management, seamless collaboration, and secure migration processes. ## 3.1 Microsoft 365 Platform and Core Workloads Microsoft 365 is a unified cloud productivity suite designed to empower organizations with modern collaboration, communication, security, and compliance capabilities. The platform integrates several core workloads, each serving a distinct purpose within the enterprise environment: - **Exchange Online**: Provides secure, scalable email services with advanced anti-spam and anti-malware protection, supporting calendaring and contacts for all users. - **SharePoint Online**: Enables document management, team sites, and intranet portals, fostering collaboration across departments and locations. - **Microsoft Teams**: Delivers real-time communication, meetings, and collaboration, integrating seamlessly with other Microsoft 365 services. - **OneDrive for Business**: Offers personal cloud storage for users, facilitating secure file sharing and synchronization across devices. - **Microsoft Intune**: Provides mobile device management (MDM) and mobile application management (MAM), ensuring endpoint compliance and security. - **Microsoft Defender**: Delivers advanced threat protection for endpoints, email, and cloud workloads, safeguarding KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s digital assets. - **Microsoft Purview**: Ensures data governance, compliance, and information protection, supporting regulatory requirements in the healthcare sector. The integration of these workloads enables KPJ Healthcare Berhad to streamline operations, enhance productivity, and maintain stringent security and compliance standards. Enfrasys Solutions recommends leveraging the full suite of Microsoft 365 workloads to maximize operational efficiency and ensure a consistent user experience across all branches and departments. Entra ID provides secure user authentication, single sign-on (SSO), and access control for all Microsoft 365 workloads, ensuring that only authorized users can access sensitive information and resources. Design and Decision This section outlines the comprehensive security architecture and design decisions for KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s Microsoft 365 and Azure environments. The approach leverages industry-leading Microsoft security features, ensuring robust protection for KPJ Healthcare’s assets, identities, and data across both cloud and on-premises infrastructures. ## 7.1 Azure Network Security Group (NSG) Overview Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are critical components in securing cloud workloads by controlling inbound and outbound traffic to resources within Azure virtual networks. NSGs use rules to filter network traffic based on source, destination, protocol, port, and action, enabling granular access control and minimizing exposure to threats. Enfrasys Solutions has designed NSG rules to ensure that only authorized traffic is allowed, aligning with KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s requirements for healthcare data protection and compliance. The NSG configuration is tailored to support secure integration between Microsoft 365 workloads, on-premises infrastructure, and external partners. Inbound rules restrict access to essential services, while outbound rules ensure data flows only to approved destinations. This approach mitigates risks such as unauthorized access, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the security design of NSG rules, while KPJ Healthcare Berhad shall implement and continuously monitor these rules within their Azure environment. The following table summarizes the recommended NSG rules for KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s Azure workloads: | Rule Name | Source | Destination | Protocol | Port | Action | Purpose | |----------------------|------------------|--------------------|---------|--------|---------|------------------------------------------------------| | Allow-M365-Admin | Admin IP Range | Azure M365 VMs | TCP | 443 | Allow | Secure admin access to Microsoft 365 services | | Allow-Intune-Device | Intune Service | KPJ Devices | TCP | 443 | Allow | Device enrollment and management via Intune | | Allow-Defender-Alerts| Defender Service | KPJ Devices | TCP | 443 | Allow | Endpoint protection and alert communication | | Allow-Entra-Sync | On-prem AD | Entra ID | TCP | 389 | Allow | Directory synchronization for identity management | | Allow-Mail-Flow | External SMTP | Exchange Online | TCP | 25 | Allow | Email communication with external domains | | Deny-All-Other | Any | Any | Any | Any | Deny | Block unauthorized and non-essential traffic | Enfrasys Solutions will ensure these rules are aligned with Microsoft best practices and healthcare industry standards. KPJ Healthcare Berhad must enforce and regularly review NSG rule configurations to maintain ongoing security posture. ## 7.2 Encryption Design for Microsoft 365 Workloads Encryption is a foundational element of Microsoft 365 security, providing protection for sensitive healthcare data both at rest and in transit. Microsoft 365 leverages advanced cryptographic standards to safeguard information, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements such as HIPAA and Malaysia’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). Encryption at rest ensures that all data stored within Microsoft 365 workloads—including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Teams, and Microsoft Defender—is protected using Microsoft-managed keys and, where required, customer-managed keys via Azure Key Vault. Data is encrypted using AES 256-bit encryption, which is recognized as a robust industry standard. This prevents unauthorized access to stored data, even in the event of physical compromise or insider threat. Encryption in transit protects data as it moves between users, devices, and Microsoft 365 services. Transport Layer Security (TLS) is employed for all communications, ensuring that data exchanged between KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s endpoints and Microsoft cloud services cannot be intercepted or tampered with. This includes email transmission via Exchange Online, document sharing in SharePoint and OneDrive, and real-time collaboration in Teams. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the encryption architecture and validating its alignment with Microsoft’s security best practices. KPJ Healthcare Berhad shall implement, configure, and monitor encryption settings across all Microsoft 365 workloads, ensuring that all compliance requirements are continuously met. ### Encryption Design Decisions | No. | Design Decision | Decision | |-----|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Encryption at Rest | Enabled by default for all M365 workloads using AES 256-bit encryption | | 2 | Encryption in Transit | Enforced via TLS for all communications between endpoints and Microsoft services | | 3 | Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) | Optional for workloads requiring enhanced control; recommend Azure Key Vault for CMK | | 4 | Email Encryption | Enabled via Exchange Online; recommend enabling Office Message Encryption for sensitive mail| | 5 | Compliance Monitoring | KPJ Healthcare Berhad to use Microsoft Purview for ongoing monitoring and reporting | The encryption strategy ensures that KPJ Healthcare Berhad’s healthcare data remains confidential, integral, and available, meeting both internal governance and external regulatory requirements. ## 7.3 Security Policy Migration and Governance During the transition from the JCORP tenant to the KPJ Healthcare Berhad tenant, Enfrasys Solutions will oversee the migration of security and compliance policies. This image is a technical architecture diagram.

The diagram illustrates a cloud-based infrastructure setup for KPJ Healthcare, integrating various Microsoft services. It consists of two main cloud environments connected via Cross Tenant Sync. Each environment includes Microsoft Teams, Exchange Online, Microsoft Intune, Entra ID, OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online, and Microsoft Defender.

1. **Cloud Environment 1**:
   - **Microsoft Services**: Teams, Exchange Online, Intune, Entra ID, OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online, Defender.
   - **Cross Tenant Sync**: Facilitates synchronization between the two cloud environments.

2. **Cloud Environment 2**:
   - **Microsoft Services**: Similar setup as Environment 1.
   - **Email Flow**: Incoming and outgoing email items are managed, indicating integration with external email systems.

3. **On-Premises Infrastructure**:
   - **KPJ Health On-prem**: Includes Microsoft Entra Connect and Active Directory Domain Services.
   - **Server LAN**: Hosts domain-joined endpoints and mobile devices.
   - **User Sync**: All KPJ users are synchronized to Entra ID.

4. **Device Management**:
   - **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**: All KPJ devices are onboarded for security management.
   - **Microsoft Intune Enrollment**: KPJ devices are enrolled for mobile device management.

5. **User Access**:
   - **KPJ User Access**: Managed through Entra ID, ensuring secure authentication and access control.

The diagram effectively showcases the integration of cloud services with on-premises infrastructure, emphasizing security and device management through Microsoft Defender and Intune.

This image is a technical architecture diagram. 

The diagram illustrates a cloud-based architecture for a healthcare company, showcasing the integration of various Microsoft services. The architecture is divided into two main cloud environments, each containing similar components:

1. **Cloud Environment Components**:
   - **SharePoint Online**: Used for document management and collaboration.
   - **Exchange Online**: Provides email services.
   - **OneDrive for Business**: Facilitates file storage and sharing.
   - **Microsoft Teams**: Enables communication and collaboration.
   - **Microsoft Defender**: Offers security and threat protection.
   - **Microsoft Intune**: Manages mobile devices and applications.
   - **Entra ID**: Provides identity and access management.
   - **Microsoft Purview**: Ensures data governance and compliance.

2. **Data Flow and Connectivity**:
   - The diagram shows data flow between the two cloud environments, indicating synchronization and sharing of information across services.
   - Orange dashed lines represent the data flow paths, connecting various components within and between the cloud environments.
   - The central document icons suggest data exchange and collaboration between different services and environments.

3. **Purpose and Functionality**:
   - The architecture supports secure communication, collaboration, and data management for the healthcare company.
   - It ensures compliance with data governance policies and provides robust security measures through Microsoft Defender.
   - The integration of Entra ID facilitates seamless identity management across services.

Overall, the diagram represents a comprehensive cloud solution leveraging Microsoft technologies to enhance productivity, security, and compliance for the healthcare sector.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.
