# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design

## 2.0 Executive Summary

### Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has embarked on a strategic initiative to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence capabilities through the implementation of Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric. This project encompasses the comprehensive design of data workflows, spanning ingestion, transformation, and visualization, tailored specifically to UMS’s business requirements. The solution will leverage Microsoft Fabric’s integrated services, including Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science capabilities for machine learning applications. The integration of Power BI will empower UMS with robust, business-aligned analytics, supporting informed decision-making and operational excellence.

### Purpose

The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to provide a formal, detailed blueprint for the deployment of Power BI and Microsoft Fabric within Universiti Malaysia Sabah. This document outlines the architectural approach, technology components, workflow design, and security considerations essential for a successful implementation. It serves as the foundational reference for all stakeholders, ensuring alignment with UMS’s cloud adoption strategy and Microsoft best practices. The design aims to deliver a scalable, secure, and future-ready analytics platform that supports UMS’s academic and administrative objectives.

### Audience

This document is intended for the following audiences:
- UMS stakeholders, including IT leadership, data governance teams, and business unit representatives, who are responsible for oversight, requirements validation, and operational adoption.
- The Enfrasys Solutions project team, including architects, engineers, and implementation specialists, who are responsible for the technical realization of the solution.

### Review and Sign-Off Responsibility

The review and formal sign-off of this Solution Design Document shall be a joint responsibility of Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah. Enfrasys Solutions will provide technical validation and architectural assurance, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will ensure alignment with institutional objectives, compliance requirements, and operational readiness.

## 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides formal definitions and concise overviews of the core technologies underpinning the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data platform solution. Each technology is described with its primary function, and its specific relevance to the UMS implementation is detailed to ensure clarity for all stakeholders.

### Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an end-to-end, unified analytics platform that brings together data integration, engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It enables organizations to ingest, transform, analyze, and visualize data within a single SaaS environment. For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Microsoft Fabric serves as the central platform orchestrating the entire data workflow, from ingestion to advanced analytics and visualization, ensuring seamless integration and governance across all data workloads.

### Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization tool. It enables users to create interactive reports and dashboards, connect to a wide range of data sources, and derive actionable insights. Within the UMS solution, Power BI is integrated with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, providing faculty and administration with real-time analytics and visualizations based on curated, trusted data.

### Data Factory

Data Factory, as part of Microsoft Fabric, is a cloud-based data integration and orchestration service. It enables the creation, scheduling, and management of data pipelines for ingesting, transforming, and moving data across various sources and destinations. For UMS, Data Factory automates the ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes, ensuring timely and reliable data movement from on-premises SQL Server environments into the Fabric Lakehouse architecture.

### Synapse

Synapse within Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics service that combines big data and data warehousing. It provides advanced capabilities for data exploration, transformation, and analytics using familiar SQL and Spark engines. In the UMS architecture, Synapse enables large-scale data processing, complex transformations, and supports advanced analytics workloads, facilitating deeper insights from university data.

### Data Science (AutoML, Notebooks)

The Data Science capabilities in Microsoft Fabric encompass both automated machine learning (AutoML) and interactive notebooks. AutoML automates the selection and tuning of machine learning models, while notebooks provide a collaborative environment for custom code, data exploration, and advanced analytics using Python or PySpark. UMS leverages these tools to enable faculty and researchers to conduct machine learning experiments, model evaluation, and operationalize predictive analytics directly within the data platform.

### OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified, enterprise-grade data lake storage solution. It provides a single, scalable repository for all organizational data, supporting structured and unstructured formats. OneLake underpins the UMS solution by centralizing data storage for bronze, silver, and gold lakehouse layers, simplifying data management, governance, and enabling seamless data access for analytics and reporting.

### On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway is a secure bridge that facilitates data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services. It ensures that data stored within UMS’s local SQL Server environments can be securely ingested into Microsoft Fabric and Power BI without exposing direct database connectivity to the internet. The gateway is critical for hybrid data integration, supporting UMS’s compliance and security requirements.

### Entra ID (Conditional Access/MFA)

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is the cloud-based identity and access management service that provides authentication, authorization, and security controls for Microsoft cloud resources. Conditional Access policies enforce adaptive access controls based on user, location, device, and risk signals, while Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an additional layer of security. For UMS, Entra ID ensures that only authorized users can access sensitive data and analytics resources in Microsoft Fabric, with robust controls to mitigate unauthorized access and data breaches.

### Technology Role Mapping

The following table summarizes each technology, its description, and its role within the Universiti Malaysia Sabah solution:

| Technology                        | Description                                                                                                      | Role in Solution                                                                                   |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Fabric                   | Unified analytics platform for data integration, engineering, science, and BI.                                   | Orchestrates the end-to-end data workflow for UMS, centralizing all analytics workloads.           |
| Power BI                           | Enterprise business intelligence and data visualization tool.                                                    | Provides interactive dashboards and reports for UMS stakeholders, integrated with OneLake.         |
| Data Factory                       | Cloud-based data integration and orchestration service.                                                          | Automates ETL pipelines, moving data from on-premises SQL Server to Fabric Lakehouse layers.       |
| Synapse                            | Integrated analytics service for big data and data warehousing.                                                  | Enables advanced data processing and analytics for UMS’s large-scale datasets.                     |
| Data Science (AutoML, Notebooks)   | Machine learning tools including automated model selection and collaborative coding environments.                 | Supports machine learning experimentation, model training, and advanced analytics for UMS.          |
| OneLake                            | Unified, scalable enterprise data lake storage.                                                                  | Centralizes all data storage for UMS, supporting bronze, silver, and gold lakehouse architectures. |
| On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)    | Secure bridge for data transfer between on-premises sources and Microsoft cloud.                                 | Enables secure hybrid data integration from UMS’s SQL Server to Fabric and Power BI.               |
| Entra ID (Conditional Access/MFA)  | Cloud-based identity and access management with adaptive policies and multi-factor authentication.                | Secures access to UMS data and analytics resources, enforcing compliance and reducing risk.        |

This technology stack ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah benefits from a secure, scalable, and integrated analytics environment, supporting both operational reporting and advanced data science use cases.

## 4.0 Network & Security Design

A secure and robust network and security architecture is paramount for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) integration between on-premises SQL Server workloads and Microsoft Fabric. This section details the connectivity, security controls, and operational responsibilities for the deployment, with a focus on the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), outbound security rules, conditional access and MFA enforcement, and the supporting virtual machine infrastructure.

### 4.1 Overview of Network Connectivity

Microsoft Fabric is a comprehensive analytics platform that enables organizations to integrate, analyze, and visualize data from diverse sources. For UMS, secure data transfer from the on-premises Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse to Microsoft Fabric is achieved via the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). The OPDG is deployed within a dedicated virtual machine, acting as a secure bridge for data movement without requiring inbound ports, thus minimizing the attack surface.

The OPDG initiates outbound connections to Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft cloud endpoints over encrypted channels (HTTPS/TCP 443). This approach ensures that sensitive data is transmitted securely, and the gateway can authenticate and communicate with Microsoft services in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Enfrasys Solutions shall be responsible for the initial deployment and configuration of the OPDG virtual machine, including the installation and registration of the gateway agent. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall assume responsibility for ongoing monitoring, operational maintenance, and incident response for the gateway VM.

#### Data Flow Architecture

The following diagram illustrates the secure data flow from the on-premises SQL Server environment to Microsoft Fabric via the OPDG virtual machine. Data is staged in the UMS SQL Server Data Warehouse, securely transmitted through the OPDG (which only requires outbound connectivity), and ingested by Microsoft Fabric for further analytics and processing.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Secure data flow from on-premises SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via OPDG.

### 4.2 Outbound Security Rules

To ensure the OPDG virtual machine can securely connect to Microsoft Fabric and related services, Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing explicit outbound network security group (NSG) rules. These rules restrict outbound traffic to only the required Microsoft endpoints and ports, reducing the risk of unauthorized data exfiltration or lateral movement.

The following table summarizes the outbound security rules to be configured for the OPDG VM:

| Name                        | Priority | Source                  | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                     | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access | Purpose                                                                                      |
|-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  | Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related endpoints. |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                | 443               | TCP      | Allow  | Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD).          |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                | 80                | TCP      | Allow  | Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.                              |

These rules ensure that only necessary outbound communications are permitted, aligning with the principle of least privilege and Azure security best practices.

### 4.3 Conditional Access and MFA Enforcement

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) provides conditional access policies to enforce identity-driven security controls for cloud access. Conditional access allows organizations to define granular access policies based on user, location, device, and risk signals.

#### Technology Definition

**Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access:** Conditional Access is a policy-based approach to identity security, enabling organizations to require multi-factor authentication (MFA), restrict access based on location or device, and enforce other controls when users access Microsoft cloud services.

#### UMS Implementation

Based on the current licensing and eligibility assessment, Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s tenant does not support advanced Conditional Access (CA) features due to the absence of Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses. As a result, Enfrasys Solutions has enforced tenant-wide multi-factor authentication (MFA) to enhance account security and reduce the risk of unauthorized access.

- **Current Enforcement:** MFA is enabled for all UMS users accessing Microsoft Fabric and related services.
- **Limitations:** Advanced conditional access policies (e.g., location-based restrictions, session controls, private link integration) are not currently available. These capabilities require additional licensing and can be revisited in the future as UMS’s requirements evolve.
- **Future Considerations:** Should UMS acquire the necessary Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses, Enfrasys Solutions recommends revisiting the conditional access design to implement more granular controls.

The following table summarizes the design decisions regarding conditional access and MFA:

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                                      |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy                                                      |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts                   |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                     |

#### Access Control Flow

The diagram below illustrates the authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric using Entra conditional access policies. User authentication attempts are evaluated against tenant-level MFA enforcement, and access is granted to Microsoft Fabric resources only upon successful verification.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 2: Authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric.

### 4.4 Virtual Machine Sizing for OPDG

The OPDG virtual machine must be provisioned with adequate resources to ensure reliable and performant data gateway operations. The following table details the minimum recommended specifications:

| Component         | Specification                           |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Operating System  | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework    | Version 4.8                             |
| vCPU              | 8 cores                                 |
| RAM               | Minimum 8 GB                            |

Enfrasys Solutions shall provision and configure the OPDG VM according to these specifications during the initial deployment phase. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall be responsible for ongoing monitoring of resource utilization and scaling the VM as needed to accommodate future workload growth.

### 4.5 Roles and Responsibilities

- **Enfrasys Solutions:** Responsible for the initial configuration of the OPDG VM, installation of the gateway agent, network security group rule implementation, and tenant-wide MFA enforcement.
- **Universiti Malaysia Sabah:** Responsible for ongoing monitoring, operational maintenance, incident response, and future evaluation of advanced conditional access policies as licensing and requirements evolve.

This comprehensive network and security design ensures secure, compliant, and reliable connectivity between UMS’s on-premises data warehouse and Microsoft Fabric, with clear operational boundaries and future-proofing for enhanced security controls.

## 5.0 Roles and Access

Effective access management is critical to ensuring the security, compliance, and operational integrity of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a layered access control model that leverages Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) for identity management, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) enforcement, and a structured workspace role assignment to align with UMS’s organizational structure.

### 5.1 Conditional Access and MFA Policy Design

**Microsoft Entra ID** is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service, providing secure access to resources, robust authentication, and advanced access policies. Conditional Access in Entra ID allows organizations to define policies that evaluate user, location, device, and risk signals before granting access to cloud applications.

Based on the current assessment, UMS’s tenant does not have the required Microsoft Entra ID Premium (P1/P2) licensing to enable advanced Conditional Access policies. As a result, Enfrasys Solutions has enforced Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level for all users to ensure baseline security. This approach ensures that all users undergo an additional verification step, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and credential compromise.

Should UMS choose to enhance access controls in the future, Enfrasys Solutions recommends acquiring the necessary Entra ID Premium licenses to enable granular Conditional Access policies targeting specific applications such as Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage.

#### Data Flow and Enforcement

The following diagram illustrates the authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric, highlighting the role of Entra Conditional Access and MFA enforcement. When a user attempts to access Microsoft Fabric resources, their authentication request is evaluated against tenant-level MFA requirements. Upon successful verification, access is granted to the relevant Microsoft Fabric services, including OneLake and associated data components.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Microsoft Fabric Authentication and Access Control Flow

This architecture ensures that all users—internal and external—must satisfy MFA requirements before accessing critical data assets, thereby strengthening UMS’s security posture.

#### Conditional Access Recommendations

The table below summarizes the recommended Conditional Access and MFA-related policies for UMS. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial policy configuration and technical validation, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will manage ongoing user assignments and compliance monitoring.

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                 |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS users inside Conditional Access policy                                 |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                |

- **Enfrasys Solutions**: Responsible for policy design, initial configuration, and technical enablement.
- **Universiti Malaysia Sabah**: Responsible for user onboarding, assignment to policies, and ongoing access reviews.

### 5.2 Workspace Roles and User Assignments

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI utilize workspace-based access control, where users are assigned roles that determine their permissions within each workspace. The recommended model for UMS delineates responsibilities and privileges according to operational needs and data governance requirements.

**Workspace Roles Defined:**
- **Workspace Admin**: Full control over workspace management, including user assignment, data governance, and configuration.
- **Workspace Contributor**: Ability to create, edit, and manage content within the workspace but without administrative privileges.
- **Workspace Viewer**: Read-only access for stakeholders and project directors to review reports and dashboards.

The following table details the recommended workspace roles, suggested mappings to UMS personnel, and the corresponding Person-in-Charge (PIC) assignments. Enfrasys Solutions will facilitate the initial role mapping and technical setup, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing user management and periodic access reviews.

|-----|---------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Workspace Admin     | Fabric Admin / Data Engineer         | Dr Suraya Binti Alias, Sektor Analitik Data DARTIC, PPDM Official, Mohd. Zamrie Bin Musa, Noor Afiza Binti Momen, Ts AG Azihar @ AG KU Azihar Bin AG Tangah |
| 2   | Workspace Contributor | Data Engineer / Business User Admin | Mohd Khairul Nizam Bin Senu (DB), Assie Zaee Petrus (DB), Muhaimin Bin Mad Noor (Infra), Nuraliah Binti Alias (Infra), Chong Tze Chien (Server Security), Abdul Latif Matali (Server Security) |
| 3   | Workspace Viewer    | Data Analyst / Stakeholder / Project Director | Director, Dr Farashazillah Binti Yahya, Stakeholders: Roslee Bin Talip, Dayangku Rozlina BTE PG. Aliuddin, Norhanieyati Binti Norhaizat, Zaidie @ Mohd Zaidie Bin Adilai, Professor Madya TS Dr Mohd Hanafi Bin Ahmad Hijazi |

### 5.3 Responsibilities and Ongoing Management

- **Enfrasys Solutions**: Will design and implement initial Conditional Access/MFA policies, configure workspace roles, and provide technical guidance during the onboarding phase.
- **Universiti Malaysia Sabah**: Will assign users to appropriate workspace roles, maintain up-to-date user lists, perform regular access reviews, and manage user lifecycle events (onboarding, offboarding, role changes).

This collaborative approach ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah maintains strong security controls while retaining flexibility and autonomy in day-to-day user and access management.

## 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

### 6.1 Overview of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI Integration

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that brings together data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a unified SaaS experience. It provides a seamless environment for ingesting, transforming, analyzing, and visualizing data at scale. Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and visualization tool, enabling organizations to create interactive reports and dashboards from diverse data sources.

Enfrasys Solutions has architected an end-to-end data workflow for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) that leverages Microsoft Fabric’s Lakehouse architecture, Data Factory pipelines, Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, AutoML, Model Registry, and Power BI integration via OneLake. This design ensures scalable, secure, and governed data processes, supporting advanced analytics and actionable insights.

### 6.2 End-to-End Data Workflow

The data workflow for UMS is structured to maximize data quality, traceability, and analytical value. The process begins with data ingestion from the Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse (UMS Staging Area) and culminates in business intelligence visualizations within Power BI. The workflow is orchestrated as follows:

1. **Data Ingestion:**  
   Azure Data Factory orchestrates the extraction of raw data from the UMS Staging Area (SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) into the Bronze Lakehouse tables. This ensures robust, scheduled, and monitored data movement.

2. **Bronze Lakehouse:**  
   The Bronze layer stores the original, untransformed data. This raw data serves as the immutable source for downstream cleansing and transformation, supporting audit and traceability requirements.

3. **Silver Lakehouse:**  
   Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint are used to cleanse, standardize, and enrich data. The Silver layer contains high-quality, integrated data, ready for advanced analytics and machine learning.

4. **Gold Lakehouse:**  
   Further transformations, aggregations, and feature engineering are performed, resulting in curated datasets optimized for reporting, analytics, and machine learning output storage.

5. **Data Science & AutoML:**  
   Data from the Silver Lakehouse is used for machine learning experiments. Both AutoML and manual ML (via Notebooks) are supported. Trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, and scoring is performed using Notebooks. Results are stored in the Gold Lakehouse for downstream consumption.

6. **Semantic Model & Power BI:**  
   The Gold Lakehouse feeds the Semantic Model, which structures data for business analysis. Power BI Desktop connects via OneLake (Direct Lake) to the Semantic Model, enabling interactive visualization and reporting.

7. **Security & Identity:**  
   The Identity_SM component ensures secure access and metadata management throughout the workflow.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial design, deployment, and configuration of this workflow. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ongoing data governance, access management, and operational usage.

### 6.3 Data Workflow Architecture Diagram

The following diagram illustrates the full data flow, from raw data ingestion to business intelligence visualization. Data is ingested from the SQL Server Data Warehouse, processed through Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers, enhanced by Data Science and AutoML components, and ultimately visualized in Power BI via OneLake.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: UMS End-to-End Data Workflow Architecture

### 6.4 Data Workflow Design Considerations

The following table summarizes the key design considerations for each workload type within the data workflow. These considerations ensure robust data movement, transformation, and analytics capabilities throughout the platform.

| ID   | Description                                                                                                  | Workload Type    |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                         | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                        | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                             | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                            | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).  | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                 | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                      | Power BI         |

### 6.5 AutoML Workflow and Design

Microsoft Fabric’s AutoML capabilities enable UMS to accelerate machine learning experimentation and deployment. AutoML automates model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation, while also supporting manual model development via Notebooks for advanced use cases.

The AutoML workflow begins with cleansed data from the Silver Lakehouse, proceeds through automated or manual model training, and stores results in the Gold Lakehouse. Registered models are managed in the Fabric Model Registry, ensuring robust lifecycle management and versioning. Scoring Notebooks apply models to new data, with outputs available for Power BI visualization.

The diagram below details the AutoML workflow, highlighting data movement from Silver Lakehouse through machine learning processes to Gold Lakehouse and Power BI integration.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: UMS AutoML Workflow in Microsoft Fabric

#### AutoML Workflow Design Considerations

The following table outlines the design considerations for the AutoML and machine learning workloads within the UMS platform:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                                                        | Workloads type    |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering  |
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science      |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science      |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science      |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering  |
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering  |
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented. | Power BI          |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                                                             | Power BI          |

### 6.6 Naming Conventions

Consistent and descriptive naming conventions are critical for operational clarity, governance, and scalability within the Microsoft Fabric environment. The following table defines the standardized naming formats for key Fabric components in the UMS deployment. Enfrasys Solutions will implement these conventions during initial setup; Universiti Malaysia Sabah will ensure their ongoing use and compliance.

| No. | Item in Fabric   | Naming Format (Identity-Scenario/Activity-FabricItemName)      |
|-----|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity  | stagingareadevcapacity01                                       |
| 2   | Workspace        | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                                          |
| 3   | Lakehouse        | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK<br>StudentAffairs_Silver_LK<br>Etc…   |
| 4   | Dataflow         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF<br>StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF<br>Etc.. |
| 5   | Semantic Model   | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_SM                           |
| 6   | Pipeline         | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL<br>Etc..                         |
| 7   | Report           | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_Report                       |

### 6.7 Roles and Responsibilities

- **Enfrasys Solutions:**  
  Responsible for the initial platform design, deployment of Microsoft Fabric components, configuration of Data Factory pipelines, Lakehouse layers, Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, AutoML, Model Registry, and integration with Power BI. Enfrasys will also implement the defined naming conventions and provide knowledge transfer to Universiti Malaysia Sabah staff.

- **Universiti Malaysia Sabah:**  
  Responsible for data governance, access management, ongoing usage of the platform, and adherence to the established naming conventions. UMS will maintain data quality, security, and operational processes post-deployment.

This comprehensive design ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah benefits from a scalable, secure, and future-ready data analytics platform, empowering advanced insights and data-driven decision-making across the institution.

## 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

Enfrasys Solutions has developed a structured deployment and migration approach to ensure a seamless transition for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to the new data platform. This approach is designed to minimize operational disruption, ensure data integrity, and provide clear accountability for all stakeholders. The deployment process is divided into distinct phases, each with specific activities, responsible parties, and planned start dates. This phased methodology enables effective risk management and facilitates timely communication between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS.

The initial phase focuses on the formal review and approval of the Solution Design Document, a critical step to align expectations and confirm the technical scope. Following this, UMS is responsible for confirming the availability and readiness of the new server that will host the staging area database for data ingestion. Upon confirmation, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the setup of the Microsoft Fabric environment, ensuring that all required cloud resources and configurations are established according to the agreed design.

A key step in the migration is the installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) within a dedicated virtual machine. This gateway is essential for secure, reliable data transfer between UMS’s on-premises systems and the Microsoft Fabric environment. Both Enfrasys Solutions and UMS will collaborate closely to ensure successful deployment and configuration of the gateway, including network and security validation.

Throughout these phases, Enfrasys Solutions will provide comprehensive documentation and conduct review sessions with UMS to ensure all deliverables meet the agreed standards. UMS is expected to provide timely feedback, sign-off on key milestones, and facilitate access to required infrastructure components.

The table below summarizes the deployment and migration activities, responsible parties, and current status:

| No | Activities                                                             | Planned Start   | Action By        | Status       | Remarks |
|----|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|------------------|--------------|---------|
| 1  | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off              | Fri, 7-Nov-25   | Enfrasys, UMS    | Not-Started  |         |
| 2  | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25  | UMS              | Not-Started  |         |
| 3  | Fabric Environment Setup                                               | Wed, 12-Nov-25  | Enfrasys         | Not-Started  |         |
| 4  | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway| Mon, 17-Nov-25  | Enfrasys, UMS    | Not-Started  |         |

**Document Review:**  
Enfrasys Solutions shall deliver the finalized Solution Design Document to UMS for review. UMS is responsible for providing feedback and formal sign-off before proceeding to subsequent phases.

**Environment Setup:**  
Upon document approval, Enfrasys Solutions will initiate the Microsoft Fabric environment setup, ensuring all configurations align with UMS’s requirements and security policies.

**Gateway Installation:**  
Enfrasys Solutions, in collaboration with UMS, will install and configure the On-Premises Data Gateway on the designated virtual machine. This step is critical to establish secure connectivity between UMS’s on-premises data sources and the cloud environment.

This structured approach ensures clarity of roles, accountability, and efficient execution of the deployment and migration activities for Universiti Malaysia Sabah.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design

2.0 Executive Summary

Enfrasys Solutions has been engaged by Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to deliver a comprehensive solution design for the implementation of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. This project aims to modernize and streamline UMS’s data workflow, supporting the university’s strategic objectives for data-driven decision making and advanced analytics.

The scope of this engagement encompasses the end-to-end design of data workflows, starting from data ingestion, through transformation and orchestration, to visualization and analytics. The solution leverages the integrated capabilities of Microsoft Fabric, including Fabric Data Factory for robust data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Data Science modules for machine learning applications. Power BI will be seamlessly integrated to provide business-aligned analytics and intuitive data visualization for stakeholders across Universiti Malaysia Sabah.

The intended outcomes of this project are:
- Establishment of a secure and scalable Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored to UMS’s operational requirements.
- Development of an end-to-end Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipeline to ensure reliable and efficient data processing.
- Implementation of machine learning processes to enable predictive analytics and advanced data insights.
- Integration of Power BI for real-time, self-service analytics and interactive reporting.

This document is intended for UMS’s IT leadership, data engineering teams, business analysts, and decision-makers involved in the university’s digital transformation initiatives. It provides a detailed architectural blueprint, design rationale, and recommended workflows to ensure successful adoption and operationalization of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI within UMS’s environment.

The solution design aligns fully with Microsoft’s best practices for cloud adoption, security, and data governance, ensuring that UMS benefits from a future-ready analytics platform. Enfrasys Solutions assumes responsibility for the design, documentation, and advisory components of this engagement, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for implementation, operationalization, and ongoing management as detailed in subsequent sections of this document.

## 3.0 Technology Overview

### 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

### 3.5 Data Science

**Role in UMS Solution:**

### 3.6 OneLake

**Definition:**  
OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified, multi-cloud data lake storage layer. It provides a single, secure, and scalable repository for all organizational data, supporting direct access from analytics and machine learning workloads.

**Role in UMS Solution:**

## 4.0 Network & Security Design

A robust network and security architecture is essential to ensure secure access, data integrity, and compliance for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric environment. This section details the access control mechanisms, security policies, and supporting infrastructure, including the configuration of Conditional Access with Microsoft Entra ID, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) enforcement, Data Gateway deployment, and associated Azure outbound security rules. Each configuration step is explicitly assigned to either Enfrasys Solutions or UMS to ensure clear responsibility and accountability.

### 4.1 Access and Security Architecture

#### 4.1.1 Microsoft Entra ID and Conditional Access

**Microsoft Entra ID** (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and advanced access controls for cloud resources. Conditional Access is a policy engine within Entra ID that evaluates signals (user, location, device, risk) and enforces access controls to protect resources.

For UMS, Conditional Access policies are not currently eligible due to licensing constraints (Entra ID P1/P2 not in place). However, Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS consider future adoption of Conditional Access for granular control over resource access, including risk-based policies and session controls. At present, MFA is enforced at the tenant level to enhance security posture.

Enfrasys Solutions shall configure baseline security policies and provide guidance on Conditional Access policy setup. UMS shall be responsible for user onboarding and ensuring user compliance with MFA requirements.

#### 4.1.2 Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Enforcement

Given the absence of Conditional Access licensing, Enfrasys Solutions enforces MFA at the tenant level for all UMS users. This approach ensures that all authentication attempts require a second verification factor, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access due to compromised credentials. UMS is responsible for user communication and ongoing support related to MFA adoption.

#### 4.1.3 Private Link Limitation

Private Link, which enables private connectivity from Azure resources to platform services, is not implemented in the current design due to technical and licensing limitations. All data flows traverse secure public endpoints with enforced security controls. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS revisit Private Link implementation in future phases to further minimize exposure to public internet.

## 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

Enfrasys Solutions has architected an end-to-end data platform for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) leveraging Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, and Power BI to enable robust data ingestion, advanced analytics, machine learning, and business intelligence. ### 6.1 End-to-End Data Workflow

The data workflow commences with the ingestion of data from the Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse (UMS – Staging Area) using Azure Data Factory pipelines. The ingested data is systematically organized into Lakehouse layers within Microsoft Fabric, following the industry-standard bronze-silver-gold paradigm:

- **Bronze Layer:** Raw data as ingested from the source is stored in the Bronze Lakehouse, ensuring data lineage and auditability.
- **Silver Layer:** Data cleansing and transformation are performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query within the SQL Analytics Endpoint. The cleansed data is stored in the Silver Lakehouse.
- **Gold Layer:** Further transformation and aggregation are performed, with the resultant, analytics-ready data stored in the Gold Lakehouse.

Data movement between these layers is orchestrated via Dataflow Gen2 and Fabric Pipelines, ensuring traceability and operational consistency. The Gold Lakehouse serves as the single source of truth for downstream analytics and machine learning workloads.

Processed data is then exposed to Power BI through OneLake integration, enabling seamless connectivity for semantic modeling and data visualization. Power BI Desktop connects directly to the Semantic Model for report building and dashboarding, empowering UMS with actionable insights.

- Conditional Access policies are subject to the limitations outlined in Microsoft Entra ID documentation. Certain advanced controls require Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses.
- Private Link is not implemented in this solution, which may affect data exfiltration boundaries and network isolation requirements.
- Microsoft Fabric and Power BI have specific licensing tiers and capacity limits. Universiti Malaysia Sabah must ensure compliance with the required licensing for all users and workloads.
- Data Gateway deployments are subject to throughput and concurrency limits as specified in Microsoft documentation.
- Role-based access and workspace permissions in Power BI and Fabric are governed by the platform’s built-in security models.
- Integration with on-premises data sources via Data Gateway requires appropriate network and firewall configuration.
- Some advanced features (e.g., automated machine learning, large model sizes, or premium datasets) may require additional licensing or dedicated capacities.
- All solution components must adhere to Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s organizational security and compliance policies.
- Changes to Microsoft cloud service boundaries or feature sets may impact solution operation and require periodic review.

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This document presents the formal solution design for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) implementation of Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric. The project scope encompasses the design and deployment of a comprehensive data workflow, spanning data ingestion, transformation, and visualization. The solution leverages Microsoft Fabric’s integrated services to support UMS’s business analytics requirements, ensuring a robust, scalable, and secure platform for advanced data-driven decision-making.

The primary objectives of this engagement are to establish a Fabric workspace tailored to UMS’s operational needs, develop an end-to-end ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipeline, enable machine learning processes, and integrate Power BI for actionable analytics. The design aligns UMS’s cloud adoption strategy with the capabilities of Microsoft Fabric, specifically utilizing Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and Fabric Data Science for machine learning applications. These components collectively empower UMS to modernize its data infrastructure, enhance analytical agility, and support business objectives with real-time insights.

The intended audience for this document includes UMS executive stakeholders, IT management, data engineers, analytics professionals, and operational staff responsible for the implementation and governance of the solution. The document serves as a comprehensive reference for understanding the architectural decisions, technology selection, and operational workflows underpinning the project.

Responsibility for the review and sign-off of this solution design is jointly assigned to Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah. Enfrasys Solutions shall provide expert guidance, technical validation, and ensure alignment with best practices, while UMS is responsible for confirming that the design meets its business requirements and operational expectations. Formal approval from both parties is required prior to project execution and deployment.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides comprehensive definitions and roles for all core technologies forming the foundation of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data workflow solution. The architecture leverages Microsoft Fabric’s integrated suite, Power BI, advanced data science tooling, secure connectivity, and robust identity management to deliver end-to-end data ingestion, transformation, analytics, and visualization. Enfrasys Solutions has carefully selected these technologies to ensure scalability, security, and operational efficiency for UMS’s business use cases.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric Platform

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that consolidates data integration, engineering, science, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. It incorporates Data Factory for orchestration, Synapse for analytics, Lakehouse for unified storage, and OneLake as the central data lake. This platform enables seamless data movement, transformation, and advanced analytics, supporting both structured and unstructured data.

UMS benefits from Microsoft Fabric’s ability to centralize data workflows, reduce operational complexity, and accelerate insights through tight integration between ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization. Enfrasys Solutions manages the initial setup, workspace configuration, and core pipeline development, while UMS is responsible for ongoing data operations and business analytics.

### 3.1.1 Fabric Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory provides cloud-native data integration and orchestration capabilities. It enables UMS to automate ETL pipelines, connecting on-premises and cloud sources, and transforming data for downstream analytics. The orchestration is managed by Enfrasys Solutions during initial deployment, with UMS handling routine pipeline monitoring and maintenance.

### 3.1.2 Fabric Synapse

Fabric Synapse delivers powerful analytics and big data processing, supporting batch and real-time workloads. It allows UMS to run complex transformations and analytics at scale, leveraging Spark and SQL endpoints. Enfrasys Solutions configures Synapse environments, ensuring optimal performance and security, while UMS utilizes Synapse for business-driven analytics tasks.

### 3.1.3 Lakehouse & OneLake

The Lakehouse architecture within Fabric unifies storage for raw, cleansed, and transformed data, supporting bronze, silver, and gold layers. OneLake acts as the single data lake, simplifying access and governance across all Fabric workloads. This structure ensures data consistency, traceability, and efficient sharing between engineering, science, and BI teams. Enfrasys Solutions establishes the Lakehouse structure; UMS manages data lifecycle and governance.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and visualization platform. It enables UMS to build interactive dashboards and reports, connecting directly to Fabric’s Semantic Models via OneLake. Power BI supports real-time analytics, self-service BI, and advanced modeling, empowering UMS stakeholders to make data-driven decisions. Enfrasys Solutions provides initial integration and training; UMS develops and maintains business-specific reports.

## 3.3 Dataflow Gen2

Dataflow Gen2 is Fabric’s next-generation data transformation engine. It allows UMS to build reusable dataflows for cleansing, enrichment, and movement between Lakehouse layers. Dataflow Gen2 supports visual and code-based transformations, integrating seamlessly with Data Factory and Synapse. Enfrasys Solutions designs foundational dataflows; UMS customizes and extends them for evolving business needs.

## 3.4 Notebooks

Fabric Notebooks offer interactive environments for data engineering and science, supporting PySpark and Python. UMS uses notebooks for custom transformations, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation. This flexibility enables tailored analytics and machine learning, enhancing explainability and accuracy. Enfrasys Solutions establishes notebook environments; UMS conducts ongoing experimentation and model development.

## 3.5 AutoML

AutoML within Fabric automates machine learning pipeline creation, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter tuning. It accelerates model development for UMS, allowing rapid experimentation and deployment. Results are scored and stored in the Gold Lakehouse for downstream BI. Enfrasys Solutions demonstrates AutoML workflows; UMS iterates and operationalizes models for business use.

## 3.6 On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure bridge between UMS’s SQL Server data warehouse and Microsoft Fabric. It enables encrypted, outbound connectivity without exposing internal networks. OPDG ensures seamless, secure data ingestion from on-premises to cloud, complying with Azure network security best practices. Enfrasys Solutions handles OPDG installation and configuration; UMS maintains the gateway VM and monitors connectivity.

## 3.7 Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is the identity and access management platform underpinning Fabric’s security. It authenticates users, manages roles, and enforces access controls, integrating with Conditional Access policies. Entra ID ensures that only authorized UMS personnel and external users access sensitive data and services. Enfrasys Solutions configures Entra ID and Conditional Access; UMS administers user lifecycle and access reviews.

## 3.8 Conditional Access

Conditional Access policies provide granular, risk-based access control for Fabric resources. They evaluate user identity, device state, location, and group membership before granting access. This mechanism protects UMS’s data from unauthorized access, ensuring compliance and mitigating threats. Enfrasys Solutions designs and implements Conditional Access policies; UMS manages policy updates and access monitoring.

### 3.8.1 Access Control Architecture

The following diagram illustrates the access management flow, highlighting how external and internal users are authenticated via Entra ID and Conditional Access before accessing Fabric resources. Signals such as user identity, group membership, and network location are evaluated, and access decisions are enforced to protect sensitive data.

## 3.9 Data Processing and Machine Learning Workflow

The solution’s data workflow integrates all core technologies, starting from secure ingestion via OPDG, transformation through Data Factory and Dataflow Gen2, advanced analytics and machine learning in Synapse and Notebooks, and visualization in Power BI. The architecture ensures data consistency, security, and operational agility for UMS.

Figure 3: Data workflow architecture from ingestion to analytics and visualization.

## 3.10 Machine Learning Workflow

UMS’s machine learning processes leverage both AutoML and manual notebook-driven modeling. Cleaned data from the Silver Lakehouse is used for experimentation, with results stored in the Gold Lakehouse and visualized via Power BI. This workflow enables rapid innovation and business-aligned analytics.

## 3.12 Technology Roles and Responsibilities

The table below summarizes each core technology, its description, role in the solution, and management responsibility.

This technology stack ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data workflow is robust, secure, scalable, and aligned with best practices for modern analytics and business intelligence. Enfrasys Solutions will manage initial deployment and configuration, while UMS will assume ongoing operational responsibilities for business analytics and data governance.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the network and security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in the context of Microsoft Fabric integration. The design emphasizes secure connectivity between on-premises data sources and cloud services, leveraging the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) deployed on a virtual machine (VM). Enfrasys Solutions has carefully considered the operational, security, and compliance requirements to ensure that UMS’s environment is robust, efficient, and aligned with Microsoft best practices.

## 4.1 Data Connectivity Architecture

The network architecture is designed to facilitate secure and reliable data transfer between UMS’s on-premises data warehouse and Microsoft Fabric. The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) serves as the critical bridge, enabling seamless communication without exposing the internal network to external threats. The OPDG is installed on a dedicated VM within UMS’s infrastructure, ensuring that all data flows are managed, monitored, and encrypted.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends this architecture for its ability to maintain strict security boundaries while providing high-performance data transfer. By using outbound-only connections, the OPDG avoids the risks associated with inbound network exposure. This approach is particularly beneficial for UMS, as it supports compliance with local data protection regulations and minimizes attack surfaces.

The data workflow begins at the UMS Staging Area, which utilizes Microsoft SQL Server 2017 as the primary data warehouse. Data is securely transmitted via the OPDG to the UMS Fabric environment in Azure. This architecture ensures that UMS can leverage advanced analytics and cloud capabilities without compromising the integrity or confidentiality of its on-premises data.

The following diagram illustrates the data flow and connectivity architecture:

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Secure data flow from UMS Staging Area through OPDG to UMS Fabric.

## 4.2 On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) VM Sizing

Proper sizing of the VM hosting the OPDG is essential to ensure optimal performance and reliability. Enfrasys Solutions has evaluated the requirements based on anticipated workloads, data volume, and Microsoft’s technical recommendations. The VM must be provisioned with sufficient resources to handle concurrent data transfers and gateway operations without bottlenecks.

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for providing guidance on VM sizing and configuration. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for provisioning the VM according to the specifications and for installing the OPDG agent. This clear delineation of responsibilities ensures that the deployment process is efficient and that operational ownership is maintained.

| vCPU             | 8 cores                                      |
| RAM              | Minimum 8 GB                                 |

## 4.3 Outbound Security Rules

To maintain a secure environment, outbound security rules are defined for the OPDG VM. These rules ensure that only necessary traffic is allowed from the gateway to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. All outbound connections utilize encrypted protocols (HTTPS), and access is tightly controlled to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration or exposure.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide the security rule definitions, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for implementing these rules in their Azure environment. This collaborative approach ensures that security controls are consistently applied and monitored.

| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                  | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

## 4.4 Access Design and Conditional Access

Access to Microsoft Fabric and associated services is governed by robust authentication mechanisms. Although UMS’s current licensing does not support Conditional Access policies, Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level. This approach provides an additional layer of security, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and mitigating potential threats from compromised credentials.

The access workflow is as follows: Users attempting to access Microsoft Fabric are required to authenticate using MFA. This process ensures that only verified users can interact with sensitive data and services. Enfrasys Solutions will assist in configuring MFA policies, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for user enrollment and ongoing management.

The following diagram illustrates the authentication and access control flow:

## 4.5 Roles and Responsibilities

Clear assignment of responsibilities is critical for successful implementation and ongoing operations. Enfrasys Solutions will provide architectural guidance, security rule definitions, and support for MFA configuration. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for provisioning the OPDG VM, installing the gateway agent, and implementing outbound security rules.

This structured approach ensures that all network and security components are deployed and managed in accordance with best practices, providing Universiti Malaysia Sabah with a secure, scalable, and compliant data integration platform.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section details the approach to roles, access management, and security enforcement within the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. The design leverages Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to safeguard sensitive data and ensure only authorized personnel can interact with analytics resources.

## 5.1 Conditional Access and MFA Enforcement

Conditional Access is a key security feature within Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory), enabling organizations to enforce access policies based on user identity, device compliance, location, and application sensitivity. Conditional Access policies are essential for modern enterprise environments, providing granular control over who can access resources and under what circumstances. However, eligibility for Conditional Access depends on licensing tiers; Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1 or P2 is required for advanced policy configurations.

For UMS, the assessment determined that the current tenant does not possess the necessary licensing for Conditional Access policies. As a result, Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level as a compensatory security measure. MFA ensures that every login attempt is authenticated through an additional verification step, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access and credential compromise.

This approach provides robust baseline security, even in the absence of Conditional Access. Enfrasys Solutions will configure tenant-wide MFA, while UMS will be responsible for user onboarding and ongoing management. Future considerations include upgrading to Entra ID Premium licenses to enable Conditional Access, which would allow for more granular controls such as restricting access based on device compliance or network location.

The following diagram illustrates the technical architecture of user access management within the UMS Azure environment. External users attempting to access the UMS Fabric resources are routed through security controls, ensuring that only authenticated and authorized users can interact with sensitive data assets.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 1: User access management architecture for UMS Fabric.

The authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric leverages Entra ID signals to evaluate user and group information, network location, and other risk factors before granting access to OneLake and other integrated services.

Figure 2: Authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric.
