The diagram illustrates a hierarchical administrative structure for managing IT operations within a hospital network. At the top level, the KPJ HQ Admin is responsible for overarching administrative tasks, including managing all users, groups, devices, policies, and resetting passwords. This role has global oversight and control over the entire network.

Below the KPJ HQ Admin, the HOS IT Hospital Admins are tasked with more localized management duties specific to individual hospitals. Their responsibilities include managing and updating hospital users, managing hospital groups, managing hospital devices, and resetting passwords for hospital users. This indicates a delegation of administrative tasks from the HQ level to the hospital level, allowing for more focused and efficient management of hospital-specific IT needs.

The diagram further breaks down the hospital-level administration into HOS IT Hospital Admins and Hospital Users, suggesting a tiered approach to user management within each hospital. This structure ensures that hospital admins have the necessary authority and tools to manage their respective environments effectively, while hospital users are the end recipients of these administrative actions.

This architecture supports secure, scalable identity management across multiple tenants, leveraging Azure Entra ID for cloud-based authentication and Microsoft Entra Connect for identity synchronization.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This Solution Design Document provides a comprehensive architectural blueprint for the implementation of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI within Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). The primary purpose of this document is to guide both UMS stakeholders and the Enfrasys Solutions implementation team through the proposed data workflow, infrastructure, and integration strategies that will support UMS’s evolving business analytics requirements. The design is structured to ensure robust, scalable, and secure data management, enabling UMS to leverage advanced analytics and machine learning capabilities for informed decision-making.

The scope of the project encompasses the creation of a Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored to UMS’s operational context, the development of an end-to-end ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipeline, the orchestration of machine learning processes, and the seamless integration of Power BI for business-aligned analytics and visualization. This initiative is intended to modernize UMS’s data infrastructure, aligning the university’s cloud adoption strategy with the latest Microsoft Fabric services, including Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for big data analytics, and integrated Data Science tools for machine learning applications.

The engagement is structured around a formal design review, initiated on 6 November 2025, with clear milestones covering infrastructure design, workflow development, and actionable next steps. UMS is responsible for project sponsorship, governance, and final review of deliverables, ensuring alignment with institutional objectives and compliance requirements. Enfrasys Solutions is accountable for the authorship of the solution design, technical architecture, and implementation guidance, leveraging industry best practices and Microsoft’s latest platform capabilities.

This document is intended for UMS executive sponsors, IT leadership, business analytics teams, and the Enfrasys Solutions implementation specialists. It provides the foundation for subsequent phases of deployment, operational management, and continuous improvement, ensuring that UMS achieves measurable outcomes in data-driven decision support and digital transformation.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section presents a comprehensive overview of the core technologies forming the foundation of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data platform solution. Enfrasys Solutions has architected a modern, integrated environment leveraging Microsoft Fabric and its associated services to deliver robust data ingestion, transformation, analytics, and visualization capabilities. Each technology is defined below, with its specific role in the UMS solution. Responsibilities are distinctly assigned: Enfrasys Solutions is accountable for solution architecting, deployment, and technical enablement, while UMS retains ownership of data, business processes, and operational usage.

## 3.1 Core Technology Definitions and Roles

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform from Microsoft that consolidates data integration, engineering, science, and visualization into a single SaaS environment. Fabric enables organizations to streamline their data workflows, reduce operational complexity, and accelerate insights by integrating services such as Data Factory, Synapse, and Power BI under one umbrella. For UMS, Fabric provides a centralized workspace for managing end-to-end ETL pipelines, machine learning processes, and business-aligned analytics.

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence tool, designed for interactive data visualization and reporting. Power BI enables UMS to transform processed data into actionable insights, supporting informed decision-making across academic and administrative domains. Enfrasys Solutions ensures the secure integration of Power BI with Fabric and OneLake, while UMS is responsible for report design and business interpretation.

Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-native data integration service, offering orchestration and ETL capabilities. # 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the comprehensive network and security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in the context of deploying Microsoft Fabric and associated services. Enfrasys Solutions has designed a secure, cloud-integrated environment that leverages Azure networking best practices, conditional access controls, and a robust outbound-only connectivity model to ensure data confidentiality and operational integrity. The design addresses both cloud and on-premises integration requirements, assigning clear responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS for implementation and ongoing management.

## 4.1 Network Architecture Overview

The network architecture for UMS is centered around a hybrid model that seamlessly connects on-premises data sources to Microsoft Fabric in Azure. The core component facilitating this integration is the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), which is deployed within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) on the UMS infrastructure. This gateway acts as a secure bridge, enabling data transfer from the UMS SQL Server Data Warehouse to Microsoft Fabric without exposing any inbound ports, thus minimizing attack surfaces and adhering to strict security standards.

Outbound connectivity is strictly enforced; all communications from the OPDG VM to Microsoft Fabric and related Microsoft services occur over encrypted protocols (HTTPS/TCP 443). No inbound ports are opened on the VM, ensuring that external threats cannot directly access the gateway or underlying data sources. This approach is aligned with Azure’s Zero Trust principles and ensures that only authorized outbound traffic is permitted, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access or data exfiltration.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the design, implementation, and initial configuration of the network and security controls, including the setup of outbound security rules and conditional access policies. UMS is tasked with provisioning the VM, ensuring on-premises prerequisites are met, and maintaining the OPDG agent.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section details the end-to-end platform architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), encompassing data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. ## 6.1 Data Workflow Architecture

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, and business intelligence capabilities. It provides seamless connectivity between data sources, transformation layers, and visualization tools, all underpinned by OneLake—a centralized data lake for secure and scalable storage.

The data workflow for UMS is architected to optimize processing from raw ingestion through to actionable insights. Data originates from the UMS Staging Area, specifically a Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse. Azure Data Factory orchestrates the ingestion, ensuring reliable and auditable pipelines. Upon ingestion, data is stored in the Bronze Lakehouse, preserving its raw state for traceability. Subsequent layers—Silver and Gold Lakehouses—apply progressive cleansing, transformation, and enrichment, using Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query tools. This layered approach supports robust data governance, minimizes risk of data corruption, and facilitates advanced analytics.

OneLake acts as the backbone for data storage, enabling seamless integration across the workflow. Power BI connects directly to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake, allowing UMS stakeholders to visualize refined data and derive business insights. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and configuring the initial workflow, while UMS validates data quality and implements business logic.

## 6.2 AutoML Workflow Architecture

Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) within Microsoft Fabric accelerates model development by automating algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, and performance evaluation. Fabric Notebooks provide a flexible environment for both AutoML and manual machine learning, supporting custom feature engineering and model optimization.

For UMS, the AutoML workflow begins with cleansed data from the Silver Lakehouse. AutoML experiments and manual modeling are conducted in Fabric Notebooks, enabling tailored approaches for UMS’s unique datasets. Model outputs, including predictions and performance metrics, are stored in the Gold Lakehouse for downstream analysis and reporting. The Fabric Model Registry manages model lifecycle and versioning, supporting reuse and governance.

Power BI leverages the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake for visualization, ensuring that machine learning results are accessible to business users. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the AutoML workflow and configuring the necessary components, while UMS validates model outputs and aligns them with institutional objectives.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Solution Design

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This Solution Design Document provides a comprehensive overview of the proposed architecture and implementation plan for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Power BI and Microsoft Fabric deployment. The document is intended for UMS executive stakeholders, IT leadership, business analysts, and technical teams responsible for reviewing, approving, and supporting the project. The primary purpose is to articulate the solution design, technical decisions, and operational framework required to enable advanced data analytics, machine learning, and business intelligence capabilities within UMS.

The scope of the project encompasses the design and implementation of an end-to-end data workflow leveraging Microsoft Fabric, from data ingestion through transformation and visualization. The solution includes the establishment of a secure and scalable Fabric workspace, development of robust ETL pipelines, integration of machine learning processes, and deployment of Power BI for actionable business analytics. The design aligns with UMS’s cloud adoption strategy, ensuring the organization capitalizes on Microsoft Fabric’s integrated services—namely Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for big data processing and analytics, and Fabric Data Science for machine learning applications.

Key business drivers for this initiative include enhancing data-driven decision-making, improving operational efficiency, and enabling scalable analytics to support UMS’s academic and administrative objectives. By adopting Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, UMS aims to modernize its data infrastructure, streamline complex data workflows, and empower users with real-time insights and predictive analytics.

Project sponsorship and review responsibility is assigned to Universiti Malaysia Sabah, ensuring alignment with institutional goals and governance standards. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the solution design, technical implementation, and delivery of the project. This collaborative approach guarantees that the solution meets UMS’s requirements, adheres to best practices, and delivers measurable business value.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides authoritative definitions and contextual roles for each core technology that forms the foundation of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data workflow solution. The architecture leverages Microsoft’s modern data and analytics ecosystem to deliver secure, scalable, and business-aligned outcomes, from data ingestion through transformation, machine learning, and visualization.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single SaaS solution. Fabric consolidates multiple workloads—including Data Factory, Synapse, and Power BI—under one workspace, providing seamless data movement, advanced analytics, and governance. For UMS, Fabric serves as the central hub for orchestrating end-to-end data workflows, enabling efficient data ingestion, transformation, modeling, and visualization.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and analytics platform. It enables users to visualize data, build interactive dashboards, and generate actionable insights. Power BI integrates natively with Fabric and OneLake, allowing UMS to connect to curated datasets and semantic models, thereby empowering business users with real-time analytics and self-service reporting capabilities.

## 3.3 Fabric Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-native data integration and orchestration service within Microsoft Fabric. It provides ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, dataflows, and scheduling capabilities to automate data ingestion from various sources, including on-premises SQL Server and cloud repositories. For UMS, Data Factory orchestrates the movement of data from the staging area through bronze, silver, and gold lakehouse layers, ensuring data is cleansed, transformed, and business-ready.

## 3.4 Fabric Synapse

Fabric Synapse offers advanced analytics and big data processing within the Fabric ecosystem. It combines data warehousing, big data analytics, and real-time processing in a unified workspace. Synapse supports SQL, Spark, and Data Explorer workloads, enabling UMS to perform complex data transformations, run large-scale analytics, and build robust data models for downstream business intelligence and machine learning.

## 3.5 Data Science (AutoML, Notebooks)

The Data Science workload in Fabric encompasses automated machine learning (AutoML) and interactive notebooks. AutoML automates model selection, training, and hyperparameter tuning, while notebooks (using PySpark or Python) provide a flexible environment for manual feature engineering, algorithm customization, and model evaluation. UMS leverages these capabilities to build, train, and deploy machine learning models, storing results in the gold lakehouse for business consumption.

## 3.6 OneLake

OneLake is Fabric’s unified, cloud-native data lake storage solution. It provides a single logical repository for all data assets, supporting lakehouse, warehouse, and semantic models. OneLake ensures seamless integration across Fabric workloads, enabling UMS to store, manage, and access data efficiently, with direct connectivity to Power BI for real-time analytics.

## 3.7 On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure, lightweight agent installed on a virtual machine within UMS’s environment. It acts as a bridge between on-premises data sources (such as SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) and Fabric cloud services. OPDG securely transmits data outbound to Fabric and Power BI, without requiring inbound ports, thus minimizing security risks and ensuring compliance with Azure networking best practices.

## 3.8 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is the cloud-based identity and access management service used for authentication, authorization, and conditional access. Entra ID governs user access to Fabric, Power BI, and related services, enforcing security policies and enabling seamless integration with UMS’s existing identity infrastructure.

## 3.9 Azure SQL Server

Azure SQL Server is Microsoft’s managed relational database platform, offering high availability, security, and scalability. In UMS’s solution, Azure SQL Server serves as the primary staging area for data warehousing, supporting data ingestion into Fabric via Data Factory and OPDG.

### Technology Overview Table

The following table summarizes each technology, its description, and its specific role within the UMS solution:

| Technology                | Description                                                                                  | Role in Solution                                                                                     |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Fabric          | Unified analytics platform integrating data engineering, science, and BI in one SaaS suite   | Central hub for data workflows, orchestration, transformation, analytics, and visualization           |
| Power BI                  | Enterprise-grade BI platform for interactive dashboards and analytics                        | Visualizes business-ready data, connects to semantic models via OneLake                              |
| Fabric Data Factory       | Cloud-native ETL and orchestration service within Fabric                                     | Automates data ingestion, transformation, and movement across lakehouse layers                       |
| Fabric Synapse            | Advanced analytics and big data processing engine                                            | Enables complex data transformations, modeling, and large-scale analytics                            |
| Data Science (AutoML, Notebooks) | Machine learning tools for automated and manual modeling                              | Builds, trains, and deploys ML models; stores results in gold lakehouse for business consumption      |
| OneLake                   | Unified, cloud-native data lake storage solution                                             | Stores all data assets; enables seamless integration and direct connectivity to Power BI              |
| On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) | Secure agent bridging on-premises sources and cloud services                          | Facilitates secure, outbound data transfer from SQL Server to Fabric and Power BI                    |
| Microsoft Entra ID        | Cloud-based identity and access management                                                   | Governs authentication, authorization, and conditional access to Fabric and related services          |
| Azure SQL Server          | Managed relational database platform                                                         | Acts as staging area for data warehousing and ingestion into Fabric                                   |

This integrated technology stack ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data workflow is secure, scalable, and aligned with modern cloud analytics best practices. Each component is selected to optimize operational efficiency, data governance, and business value realization.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section details the network and security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), focusing on the integration of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), secure outbound connectivity, Azure outbound security rules, and access management through Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the configuration and implementation of these network and security controls, while UMS will provide the necessary on-premises access to facilitate deployment and ongoing operations.

## 4.1 On-Premises Data Gateway Architecture

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component in UMS’s hybrid cloud architecture. The OPDG is deployed within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) in the UMS on-premises environment. Its primary function is to securely bridge data sources, such as the Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse in the UMS Staging Area, with Microsoft Fabric and related Azure services. This architecture enables seamless data transfer and integration without exposing the internal network to external threats.

A key security design principle is the elimination of inbound ports on the OPDG VM. All communications initiated by the OPDG are outbound, leveraging HTTPS and HTTP protocols to connect with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure authentication endpoints. This approach significantly reduces the attack surface, as no external systems can directly initiate connections to the OPDG VM. Enfrasys Solutions will configure the OPDG VM to ensure compliance with Azure networking best practices, and UMS will facilitate access to the on-premises environment for installation and maintenance.

The following diagram illustrates the secure data flow from the UMS Staging Area to Microsoft Fabric via the OPDG, highlighting the outbound-only connectivity and the absence of inbound ports.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Secure data flow from UMS Staging Area to Microsoft Fabric via OPDG.

## 4.2 Azure Outbound Security Rules

To ensure the OPDG VM can securely communicate with Microsoft cloud services, Enfrasys Solutions will implement a set of Azure outbound security rules. These rules are designed to permit only essential outbound traffic, thereby maintaining a robust security posture. Outbound HTTPS traffic on TCP port 443 is allowed to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and core Azure domains, enabling secure data transfer and authentication. Additionally, outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 is permitted for connectivity verification.

Each rule is assigned a specific priority, source, destination, and protocol, ensuring granular control over network flows. Enfrasys Solutions will configure these rules within the Azure Network Security Group (NSG) associated with the OPDG VM, and UMS will provide the necessary information regarding internal IP addresses and network topology.

The table below summarizes the outbound security rules required for the OPDG VM:

| Name                       | Priority | Source                 | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|----------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services  | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication  | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                                                                             | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160     | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                                                                              | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules collectively ensure that the OPDG VM can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data securely while restricting unnecessary outbound traffic.

## 4.3 Access Management: Conditional Access and MFA

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) provides identity and access management capabilities for Azure and Microsoft Fabric environments. Conditional Access is a feature that allows organizations to enforce policies based on user, device, location, and risk signals before granting access to resources. However, based on the current assessment, UMS’s account does not meet the eligibility requirements for Conditional Access due to licensing constraints (Entra ID Free tier). Consequently, Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level to strengthen security and mitigate risks associated with unauthorized access.

MFA requires users to provide additional verification, such as a code from a mobile device, in addition to their password. This reduces the likelihood of compromised credentials leading to unauthorized access. Enfrasys Solutions will configure MFA for all UMS users accessing Microsoft Fabric and related services. Should UMS decide to upgrade to Entra ID P1 or P2 in the future, Conditional Access policies can be revisited and implemented for more granular control.

The following diagram demonstrates the authentication and access control flow, showing how Entra Conditional Access (or MFA enforcement) evaluates user signals, makes access decisions, and enforces policies before granting access to Microsoft Fabric.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 2: Authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric.

The table below summarizes the key access decisions and policies:

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                                      |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy                                                       |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts                   |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                     |

## 4.4 Security Responsibilities and Operational Workflow

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing, configuring, and maintaining the network and security architecture described above. This includes the deployment of the OPDG VM, implementation of Azure outbound security rules, and enforcement of MFA. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for providing timely access to on-premises infrastructure and supporting Enfrasys Solutions in gathering necessary network information and user details.

This collaborative approach ensures that security controls are properly implemented and maintained, reducing the risk of data breaches and unauthorized access. Future enhancements, such as the adoption of Conditional Access policies and Private Link, can be considered as UMS’s licensing and infrastructure evolve.

In summary, the network and security design for UMS leverages secure outbound connectivity, robust Azure NSG rules, and strong access management practices to protect sensitive data and maintain compliance with industry standards.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section defines the access model for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) within the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. It details the Conditional Access policy design, MFA enforcement strategy, and workspace role mapping, ensuring secure and appropriate access for both internal and external users. The design leverages Microsoft Entra ID capabilities and aligns with best practices for enterprise data and analytics platforms.

## 5.1 Conditional Access Policy Design

Microsoft Entra ID provides a robust framework for securing access to cloud resources through Conditional Access policies. Conditional Access is a security feature that allows organizations to define access requirements based on user identity, device state, location, and other signals. By enforcing these policies, UMS can ensure that only authenticated and authorized users are permitted to access sensitive workloads such as Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that UMS configure Conditional Access policies to cover all relevant services, including Power BI and Microsoft Fabric. However, based on the current assessment, UMS accounts are not eligible for advanced Conditional Access features (such as those requiring Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses). As a result, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) has been enforced at the tenant level, providing an additional layer of security for all users. This approach reduces the risk of unauthorized access and mitigates unexpected login prompts.

The Conditional Access model also considers future scalability. Should UMS decide to upgrade to Entra ID P1 or P2, additional Conditional Access features can be revisited and integrated. Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial configuration and policy design, while UMS will manage ongoing enforcement and user inclusion.

The diagram below illustrates the technical architecture for Conditional Access, including the relationship between Azure Resource Groups, UMS Fabric, external users, and policy enforcement.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 1: Conditional Access architecture for UMS Fabric and external users.

The following table summarizes the key Conditional Access decisions for UMS:

| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                                           |
|------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy                                                            |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts                        |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                          |

## 5.2 Multi-Factor Authentication Enforcement

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is a critical security measure that requires users to provide two or more verification methods before gaining access to resources. Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing MFA at the tenant level for UMS, compensating for the current limitations in Conditional Access eligibility. This approach ensures that all UMS users, regardless of their role or location, are subject to enhanced authentication protocols.

MFA enforcement reduces the likelihood of credential compromise and protects sensitive analytics workloads hosted within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. Enfrasys Solutions will assist UMS in configuring tenant-wide MFA settings, while UMS administrators will be responsible for monitoring compliance and addressing user issues.

The authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric, as governed by Entra Conditional Access policies and MFA, is depicted in the following diagram. The process begins with a user authentication attempt, which is evaluated against policy signals, decisions, and enforcement mechanisms before granting access to Microsoft Fabric components.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 2: Authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric using Entra Conditional Access and MFA.

## 5.3 Workspace Role Mapping and Permissions

Microsoft Fabric workspaces provide granular access control through role-based permissions. Each workspace role is mapped to specific responsibilities and UMS personnel, ensuring that access is limited to authorized individuals based on their operational needs. The workspace roles include Admin, Contributor, and Viewer, each with distinct capabilities.

Enfrasys Solutions will define the initial workspace role assignments and ensure that appropriate UMS personnel are mapped to each role. UMS will be responsible for maintaining role assignments, onboarding new users, and ensuring compliance with access policies. This clear delineation of responsibilities supports operational efficiency and reduces the risk of unauthorized data access.

The following tables present the workspace role mapping for UMS, including suggested roles and the designated UMS Person-In-Charge (PIC):

Aliuddin<br>Norhanieyati Binti Norhaizat<br>Zaidie @ Mohd Zaidie Bin Adilai<br>Professor Madya TS Dr Mohd Hanafi Bin Ahmad Hijazi |

## 5.4 Role Assignment and Policy Enforcement Responsibilities

The effective implementation of the access model requires clear assignment of responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah. Enfrasys Solutions will take ownership of the initial configuration, policy design, and technical enablement of Conditional Access and MFA. UMS will be responsible for ongoing management, including user onboarding, role assignment, and compliance monitoring.

The following table delineates the key activities and responsible parties:

| Item              | Activities                                                                                   | Action By           | Status         |
|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|---------------|
| Access Policy Design | Define Conditional Access and MFA enforcement policies                                    | Enfrasys Solutions  | Completed      |
| Workspace Role Assignment | Map UMS personnel to workspace roles (Admin, Contributor, Viewer)                    | Enfrasys Solutions  | Completed      |
| User Onboarding   | Add new users to workspace and enforce MFA                                                  | UMS                 | Ongoing        |
| Policy Enforcement | Monitor access policies and ensure compliance                                              | UMS                 | Ongoing        |
| License Review    | Assess need for Entra ID P1/P2 for advanced Conditional Access features                     | UMS                 | Pending        |

This structured access model ensures that UMS maintains a secure, scalable, and auditable environment for Microsoft Fabric and Power BI workloads, with clear lines of responsibility between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section outlines the platform architecture, workflow, and implementation responsibilities for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data analytics solution leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The design encompasses data ingestion, transformation, storage, machine learning, and visualization, ensuring a scalable and secure environment tailored to UMS's requirements.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Architecture

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence in a single environment. It leverages OneLake as a unified data storage layer, Azure Data Factory for orchestration, and Power BI for visualization. The proposed architecture for UMS ensures seamless data flow from source systems through transformation layers to advanced analytics and reporting.

Data is initially ingested from the UMS Staging Area, hosted on Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, using Azure Data Factory pipelines. The workflow follows a medallion architecture: raw data is stored in Bronze Lakehouse tables, cleansed and enriched data in Silver Lakehouse tables, and business-ready data in Gold Lakehouse tables. Data transformation is performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query within the SQL Analytics Endpoint. Machine learning processes, both automated (AutoML) and manual, are applied to Silver Lakehouse data, with results stored in the Gold Lakehouse. Power BI connects to the Semantic Model via OneLake for visualization, providing actionable insights to business users.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and configuring the overall workflow, including Azure Data Factory pipelines, lakehouse structures, and transformation processes. UMS is tasked with providing source data, validating transformation outcomes, and managing business requirements for reporting.

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data workflow within the UMS Fabric environment, highlighting the movement of data across ingestion, transformation, storage, analytics, and visualization components.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: Data workflow architecture from ingestion to visualization.

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Considerations

A robust data workflow is critical for ensuring data integrity, scalability, and operational efficiency. The medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) provides structured stages for data processing, allowing for incremental transformation and quality assurance. Azure Data Factory orchestrates data movement and transformation, while Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and SQL Analytics Endpoint enable flexible and powerful data engineering tasks.

Security and access control are managed through Identity_SM, ensuring only authorized users can interact with sensitive data. OneLake offers unified storage, simplifying data management and access across the platform. Power BI delivers business intelligence capabilities, connecting directly to the Semantic Model for real-time reporting.

Responsibility for implementing these design considerations is shared: Enfrasys Solutions configures the pipelines, lakehouses, and transformation tools, while UMS provides source data, reviews transformation logic, and manages reporting requirements.

| ID   | Description                                                                                                  | Workload Type     |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                         | Data Factory      |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                        | Data Engineering  |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                             | Data Engineering  |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                            | Data Engineering  |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering  |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).  | Data Factory      |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science      |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                 | Power BI          |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                      | Power BI          |

## 6.3 AutoML Workflow Design & Considerations

Microsoft Fabric provides integrated AutoML capabilities, enabling both automated and manual machine learning workflows. AutoML automates model selection, hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation, while manual ML using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) allows for custom feature engineering and algorithm optimization. Model outputs are stored in Gold Lakehouse tables, ensuring consistency and accessibility for downstream reporting.

UMS’s cleaned data from the Silver Lakehouse serves as the input for ML experiments. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring AutoML pipelines, notebook environments, and model registry integration. UMS is tasked with selecting relevant datasets, validating ML outcomes, and providing feedback for model refinement.

The following diagram depicts the AutoML workflow, illustrating data movement from Silver Lakehouse through ML experimentation to Gold Lakehouse and visualization.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: AutoML workflow from Silver Lakehouse to Power BI reporting.

| ID   | Description                                                                                                  | Workloads type    |
|------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering  |
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science      |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science      |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science      |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering  |
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering  |
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI          |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                      | Power BI          |

## 6.4 VM Sizing and Platform Specifications

The underlying platform must be provisioned with adequate resources to ensure optimal performance for data engineering, machine learning, and reporting workloads. The recommended VM specifications are based on best practices for Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployments.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for provisioning and configuring the VM infrastructure. UMS will utilize these resources for data processing, ML experimentation, and report generation.

| Component       | Specification                                  |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Operating System| Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework  | Version 4.8                                    |
| vCPU            | 8 cores                                        |
| RAM             | Minimum 8 GB                                   |

## 6.5 Naming Convention Design

Consistent and meaningful naming conventions are essential for resource management, operational clarity, and security within Microsoft Fabric. The naming schema incorporates identity, scenario/activity, and Fabric item name, ensuring traceability and ease of administration.

Enfrasys Solutions will establish and enforce naming conventions across all Fabric resources. UMS personnel are expected to adhere to these conventions when creating or modifying resources.

| No. | Item in Fabric   | Naming                                  |
|-----|------------------|------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity  | stagingareadevcapacity01                 |
| 2   | Workspace        | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                    |
| 3   | Lakehouse        | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK<br>StudentAffairs_Silver_LK<br>Etc… |
| 4   | Dataflow         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF<br>StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF<br>Etc.. |
| 5   | Semantic Model   | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_SM     |
| 6   | Pipeline         | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL<br>Etc..   |
| 7   | Report           | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_Report |

## 6.6 Implementation Responsibility Matrix

To ensure clarity and accountability, the following outlines the implementation responsibilities for each stage of the workflow:

- **Data Ingestion**: Enfrasys Solutions configures Azure Data Factory pipelines; UMS provides source data and validates ingestion.
- **Data Transformation**: Enfrasys Solutions sets up Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and transformation logic; UMS reviews and approves data quality.
- **Data Storage**: Enfrasys Solutions provisions and manages lakehouse layers; UMS maintains data governance and access policies.
- **Machine Learning**: Enfrasys Solutions configures AutoML and notebook environments; UMS selects datasets and validates models.
- **Visualization**: Enfrasys Solutions establishes Semantic Models and Power BI connections; UMS defines reporting requirements and consumes reports.

This collaborative approach ensures a robust, scalable, and secure analytics platform tailored to UMS’s needs.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section details the deployment and migration methodology for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), outlining the sequence of activities, ownership assignments, and prerequisites required for the successful rollout of the Microsoft Fabric solution. The approach leverages industry best practices to ensure a seamless transition from design approval through environment setup and integration with on-premises data sources.

## 7.1 Deployment Workflow Overview

The deployment and migration process for UMS is structured to minimize disruption and maximize operational readiness. Enfrasys Solutions will lead the technical implementation, while UMS will provide critical inputs and approvals at key stages. The workflow begins with formal design document delivery and sign-off, establishing a clear baseline for all subsequent activities. This is followed by confirmation of the new staging area database, which is essential for data ingestion and integration with Microsoft Fabric.

Once prerequisites are met, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the setup of the Fabric environment, ensuring that all configurations adhere to the approved design. The installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a collaborative effort, requiring both Enfrasys and UMS to coordinate on VM provisioning, network access, and gateway configuration. This phased approach allows for systematic validation at each step, reducing risks associated with data migration and integration.

## 7.2 Prerequisites and Dependencies

Successful deployment hinges on meeting several key prerequisites. First, the design document must be reviewed and formally signed off by UMS, confirming alignment between business requirements and technical architecture. Second, UMS must confirm the availability and readiness of the new server hosting the staging area database, which will serve as the primary data source for ingestion into Microsoft Fabric. These dependencies are critical to avoid delays and ensure that subsequent technical activities can proceed without impediment.

Additionally, network connectivity and VM provisioning for the On-Premises Data Gateway require advance preparation by UMS, with Enfrasys providing guidance and technical oversight. All tasks are sequenced to ensure that dependencies are resolved before initiating environment setup or gateway installation.

## 7.3 Deployment & Migration Activities

The following table summarizes the deployment and migration plan, assigning responsibilities to Enfrasys Solutions and UMS as indicated in the project schedule. Each activity is tracked for status and remarks to facilitate transparent project management.

| Item | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks |
|------|------------|--------------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1    | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 2    | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 3    | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started |  |
| 4    | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started |  |

## 7.4 Responsibility Assignment and Coordination

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for technical delivery, including the creation and configuration of the Microsoft Fabric environment and installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for reviewing and approving the design document, confirming the readiness of the new staging server, and supporting gateway installation by provisioning necessary infrastructure and access.

Effective coordination between Enfrasys and UMS is essential throughout the deployment. Regular status updates, milestone reviews, and collaborative troubleshooting will be employed to ensure timely completion of each activity. This structured approach provides UMS with clear visibility into project progress and ensures that all dependencies are addressed proactively.
