# SIRIM Analytics Deployment Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This document presents the comprehensive solution design for the SIRIM Analytics Deployment project, prepared by Enfrasys Solutions. The primary objective of this initiative is to architect a robust data workflow, encompassing data ingestion, transformation, and visualization, specifically tailored for SIRIM’s Human Resource use-case. The design aligns SIRIM’s cloud adoption strategy with the advanced capabilities of Microsoft Fabric, leveraging its Data Factory for integration and orchestration, and Synapse for big data analytics.

The scope of this document includes detailed infrastructure design, network security considerations, data gateway configuration, workspace permissions, and role-based access management. Each component is carefully selected to ensure operational efficiency, scalability, and security, addressing both current and future analytics requirements of SIRIM’s HR department. The design also incorporates best practices for cloud deployment, ensuring seamless integration with Microsoft Fabric services.

The intended audience for this document comprises SIRIM’s HR and IT stakeholders, as well as the Enfrasys Solutions project team. Enfrasys Solutions is assigned responsibility for overall project governance, including design validation, implementation oversight, and compliance with industry standards. SIRIM will serve as the key stakeholder, providing domain expertise and ensuring alignment with organizational objectives. This document serves as the authoritative reference for all technical, operational, and governance aspects of the analytics deployment, guiding both implementation and ongoing management.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides authoritative definitions and high-level descriptions of the core technologies selected for the SIRIM Human Resource data workflow solution. Enfrasys Solutions recommends these technologies based on their proven capabilities in modern cloud analytics, secure data integration, and scalable visualization. SIRIM shall review and confirm alignment with internal standards and operational requirements.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data science, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. It consolidates multiple workloads—such as Data Factory, Synapse, Lakehouse, Dataflow Gen2, and Semantic Model—under a unified governance and security model. This enables organizations to streamline data workflows from ingestion to visualization, reduce operational complexity, and accelerate time-to-insight.

Within SIRIM’s solution, Microsoft Fabric orchestrates the end-to-end data pipeline: Data Factory manages ingestion and integration, Synapse delivers advanced analytics and big data processing, Lakehouse provides scalable storage for raw, cleansed, and transformed data, Dataflow Gen2 automates data movement across layers, and Semantic Model underpins robust data modeling and row-level security for Power BI reporting.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and visualization platform. It empowers users to create interactive reports, dashboards, and analytics using data from diverse sources, including Microsoft Fabric’s Semantic Model and OneLake. Power BI supports advanced modeling, DAX calculations, and role-based access control, ensuring secure and relevant insights for HR stakeholders within SIRIM.

By connecting directly to Fabric’s Semantic Model, Power BI enables SIRIM to deliver tailored HR reports with row-level security, ensuring that sensitive workforce data is only visible to authorized personnel.

## 3.3 Azure Data Gateway

Azure Data Gateway acts as a secure bridge between on-premises data sources and cloud analytics services. Installed as an agent on a virtual machine, it enables seamless, encrypted connectivity from SIRIM’s PostgreSQL database (hosted on the TOPAZ VM) to Microsoft Fabric. This ensures data flows securely and reliably without exposing internal systems to the public internet.

Enfrasys recommends deploying the Data Gateway agent within a controlled VM environment, with SIRIM responsible for confirming whether to utilize an existing VM or provision a new one for production workloads.

## 3.4 Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD)

Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD) is a cloud-based desktop and application virtualization service on Azure. It provides secure, scalable access to Windows environments from any location, supporting remote administration and data gateway management. For SIRIM, WVD can be leveraged to host administrative tools and facilitate secure access to the Data Gateway VM, ensuring operational flexibility and compliance.

## 3.5 Azure Network Security Group (NSG)

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are foundational security constructs in Azure, enabling granular control over inbound and outbound traffic to resources. NSGs enforce rules based on source, destination, port, and protocol, thereby safeguarding the Data Gateway VM and other critical assets in SIRIM’s resource group. Enfrasys recommends configuring NSGs to restrict access to only trusted sources and necessary ports, minimizing the attack surface.

## 3.6 Private Endpoint

Private Endpoints in Azure enable secure, private connectivity to Azure services, bypassing public networks. By integrating Private Endpoints with Microsoft Fabric and Data Gateway, SIRIM ensures that sensitive HR data remains within the organization’s virtual network, reducing exposure and enhancing compliance with internal and regulatory standards.

## 3.7 Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a comprehensive identity and access management platform. It provides authentication, authorization, and governance for users and services across Azure and Microsoft 365. Entra ID underpins role-based access to Fabric workspaces, Power BI reports, and Data Gateway, ensuring that only authorized SIRIM personnel can access sensitive HR analytics.

## 3.8 Technology Summary Table

The following table summarizes each core technology, its purpose within the SIRIM solution, and key features. Enfrasys Solutions has provided these descriptions for SIRIM’s review and confirmation.

| Technology             | Purpose in Solution                                                               | Key Features                                                                                  |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Fabric       | Unified analytics platform for data ingestion, transformation, and visualization  | SaaS integration, multi-workload orchestration, governance, scalability                      |
| Data Factory           | Data integration and orchestration from PostgreSQL to Lakehouse                   | Pipeline automation, connectors, scheduling, monitoring                                      |
| Synapse                | Advanced analytics and big data processing                                        | SQL analytics, Spark processing, data engineering, scalable compute                          |
| Lakehouse              | Centralized storage for raw, cleansed, and transformed data                       | Delta tables, multi-layer architecture (bronze, silver, gold), ACID transactions             |
| Dataflow Gen2          | Automated movement of data between Lakehouse layers                               | Visual data transformation, incremental refresh, integration with pipelines                  |
| Semantic Model         | Data modeling and security for Power BI reporting                                 | Table relationships, DAX calculations, row-level security, reusable datasets                 |
| Power BI               | Visualization and business intelligence for HR analytics                          | Interactive dashboards, report sharing, role-based access, integration with OneLake          |
| Azure Data Gateway     | Secure bridge between on-premises PostgreSQL and Fabric                           | Encrypted connectivity, VM agent deployment, hybrid data access                              |
| Windows Virtual Desktop| Remote access to administrative tools and Data Gateway VM                         | Desktop virtualization, multi-session support, secure access                                 |
| Azure NSG              | Network security for Data Gateway and other Azure resources                       | Rule-based traffic control, granular access, audit logging                                   |
| Private Endpoint       | Secure, private connectivity to Azure services                                    | VNet integration, no public exposure, enhanced compliance                                    |
| Entra ID               | Identity and access management across the solution                                | Authentication, authorization, role assignment, conditional access                           |

SIRIM shall validate these technology selections against internal standards, ensuring alignment with organizational policies and security requirements. Enfrasys Solutions will provide further guidance on integration and operational best practices during subsequent phases of the project.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the comprehensive network and security architecture for SIRIM’s Azure deployment, focusing on robust segmentation, secure connectivity, and access control. Enfrasys Solutions has designed the network and security framework to ensure data protection, operational efficiency, and compliance with best practices. SIRIM is responsible for reviewing and approving the proposed architecture.

## 4.1 Azure Network Topology

A well-structured Azure network topology is essential for secure and efficient operations. The architecture leverages Azure Subscriptions, Resource Groups, Virtual Networks (VNETs), VNET Peering, Site-to-Site VPN, and Private Endpoints to ensure controlled connectivity between SIRIM’s on-premises environment, Azure services, and external users.

The Azure Subscription acts as the foundational layer for organizing resources and managing billing. Within this subscription, Resource Groups such as Fabric-RG and SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG are used to logically group related resources, supporting both operational management and access control. Multiple VNETs are provisioned, each with distinct IP address spaces and subnets, to isolate workloads and facilitate secure communication.

VNET Peering is implemented to enable seamless and high-speed communication between VNETs without traversing the public internet. Site-to-Site VPN connectivity is established via Azure Virtual Network Gateways, allowing secure, encrypted communication between SIRIM’s on-premises infrastructure and Azure resources. Private Endpoints are used to restrict access to sensitive services, ensuring that only internal network traffic can reach critical resources such as Fabric workspaces.

The diagram below illustrates the network architecture, depicting the flow of connectivity between SIRIM’s on-premises network, Azure VNETs, peering relationships, and the deployment of Private Endpoints for secure access.

![](images\slide_010_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Azure network topology with Site-to-Site VPN, VNET Peering, and Private Endpoints.

## 4.2 Segmentation and User Access Flows

Segmentation between internal SIRIM users and external users is a critical design consideration. Internal users are granted direct access to Fabric resources within Azure, managed by Conditional Access policies that enforce secure authentication, including Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), device compliance, and user risk assessments.

External users, on the other hand, are restricted from direct access to Fabric. Instead, they connect via Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD), which acts as a secure intermediary. The WVD is deployed within a dedicated subnet and VNET, with Network Security Groups (NSGs) applied to strictly control inbound and outbound traffic. This approach ensures that external users are isolated from the core Azure resources and only interact with Fabric through virtualized desktops, reducing the risk of unauthorized access.

The following diagram demonstrates the access flow, highlighting the separation between SIRIM and external users, the application of Conditional Access policies, and the role of WVD in mediating connections.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 2: User access flow with Conditional Access and WVD segmentation.

## 4.3 Security Controls: Conditional Access Policies

Conditional Access is a core security feature of Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory), enabling organizations to enforce policies that determine how and when users can access resources. Enfrasys Solutions recommends configuring Conditional Access to include critical services such as Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage.

Conditional Access policies for SIRIM users require secure login, MFA, device compliance, and user risk evaluation. These policies ensure that only authorized personnel with compliant devices can access sensitive resources. For external users, access is mediated through WVD, with NSG rules providing an additional layer of control.

The table below summarizes the access decisions for SIRIM and external users:

| No. | SIRIM user                                   | External user                                   |
|-----|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Direct Access to Fabric                      | Indirect access via Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD)|
| 2   | Managed using Conditional Access             | WVD access managed using Network Security Group (NSG)|
| 3   | User go through extra checks like secure login, MFA, etc.| User separated from the actual system using the virtual computer|
| 4   | Conditional Access policy includes Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage| NSG rule allows Fabric inbound and outbound|

## 4.4 Network Security Group (NSG) Rules

Network Security Groups are essential for enforcing granular traffic control at the subnet and VM level. Enfrasys Solutions has designed NSG rules to ensure only legitimate traffic can access Fabric resources, particularly for WVD deployments. The following tables detail the inbound and outbound NSG rules applied to the WVD subnet:

### Inbound NSG Rules

| Name                | Priority | Source      | Source ports | Destination           | Destination ports | Protocol | Access |
|---------------------|----------|-------------|--------------|-----------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_Fabric_Inbound| 110      | Service Tag | 443          | Vm Private IP Addresses| *                 | TCP      | Allow  |

### Outbound NSG Rules

| Name                | Priority | Source                | Source ports | Destination | Destination ports | Protocol | Access |
|---------------------|----------|----------------------|--------------|-------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_Fabric_Outbound| 110     | Vm Private IP Addresses| *           | Service Tag | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |

These NSG rules are tailored to permit secure communication between WVD and Fabric services, while blocking unauthorized access attempts.

## 4.5 Private Endpoint Design and Limitations

Private Endpoints in Azure provide secure, private connectivity to Azure services by mapping them into a VNET, thereby eliminating exposure to the public internet. Enfrasys Solutions recommends enabling Private Link for Fabric workspaces to restrict access exclusively to internal network traffic. This approach ensures that only users within the designated VNET can access Fabric resources, significantly reducing the attack surface.

However, there are critical limitations to the use of Private Endpoints for Fabric, which must be acknowledged:

- Visual query in Warehouse does not work when accessed via Private Endpoint.
- Copying data via Pipeline from and into a Data Warehouse is currently not possible through Private Endpoint.
- Power BI does not support Private Link for Fabric; access to datasets in Fabric must still use the public endpoint.
- Copilot features are not currently supported for Private Endpoint.

These limitations require careful consideration during deployment and user training, as certain workflows may necessitate public endpoint access or alternative integration strategies.

## 4.6 Security Design Considerations

The following table summarizes the key security design considerations for Conditional Access and Private Endpoint implementation:

| No. | Conditional Access                                                                 | Private Endpoint                 |
|-----|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| DC01| Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage | Enable Private Link in Fabric    |
| DC02| Configure NSG in existing SIRIM’s WVD for Fabric inbound and outbound              | Create Private Endpoint in Azure portal |
| DC03| Include SIRIM user inside Conditional Access policy                                | Disable Public Access from Fabric|

## 4.7 Responsibilities

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing, documenting, and implementing the network and security architecture, including the configuration of NSG rules, Conditional Access policies, Private Endpoints, and VNET peering. SIRIM is tasked with reviewing the design, approving configurations, and ensuring organizational policies align with the proposed security controls.

## 4.8 Summary

This network and security design establishes a robust foundation for SIRIM’s Azure deployment, ensuring secure connectivity, effective segmentation, and comprehensive access control. The architecture leverages Azure-native features to protect sensitive data, mitigate risks, and support scalable operations. Limitations of Private Endpoint for Fabric have been explicitly documented to inform operational planning and future enhancements.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section details the access model for SIRIM’s analytics deployment, covering Conditional Access policy design, workspace role mapping, and row-level security (RLS) within the Semantic Model. The design ensures secure, granular access to analytics resources, aligning with SIRIM’s operational and compliance requirements.

## 5.1 Conditional Access Policy Design

Conditional Access is a Microsoft Entra ID feature that enforces access controls based on user identity, device compliance, location, and application sensitivity. When properly configured, Conditional Access policies help protect sensitive analytics resources by requiring multi-factor authentication (MFA), device compliance, and restricting access to trusted networks.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that SIRIM implement Conditional Access policies covering all key analytics workloads, including Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage. Internal SIRIM users will have direct access to the Fabric analytics platform, with policies ensuring secure login and MFA. External users, meanwhile, will access resources indirectly via Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD), with additional isolation provided by Network Security Groups (NSGs).

This approach ensures that only authorized users can access analytics resources, with extra checks for internal users and network-level isolation for external users. The separation of access paths reduces the risk of unauthorized access and supports compliance with data privacy standards.

The following diagram illustrates the architecture and data flow for Conditional Access in SIRIM’s environment. Internal users are subject to Conditional Access policies, while external users access resources through a virtualized environment, further protected by NSG rules.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 1: Conditional Access and user flow in SIRIM’s analytics deployment.

## 5.2 Conditional Access vs. Private Endpoint Design Considerations

In designing secure access, Enfrasys Solutions evaluated both Conditional Access and Private Endpoint strategies. Conditional Access is ideal for enforcing user-level security, integrating seamlessly with Entra ID, and supporting MFA and device compliance. Private Endpoints, on the other hand, restrict network-level access by enabling Azure Private Link, ensuring resources are accessible only from approved virtual networks and disabling public access.

For SIRIM, the recommended approach is to combine Conditional Access for user authentication and authorization with Private Endpoints for network isolation. This dual-layer security ensures that only authenticated users from trusted locations can access analytics resources, while the resources themselves are shielded from public exposure.

The table below summarizes key design considerations for Conditional Access and Private Endpoint implementation:

| No. | Conditional Access | Private Endpoint |
|-----|-------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage | Enable Private Link in Fabric |
| DC02 | Configure NSG in existing SIRIM’s WVD for Fabric inbound and outbound | Create Private Endpoint in Azure portal |
| DC03 | Include SIRIM user inside Conditional Access policy | Disable Public Access from Fabric |

This layered approach enhances security, reduces attack surface, and aligns with SIRIM’s compliance requirements.

## 5.3 Workspace Role Mapping

Microsoft Fabric workspaces support role-based access control (RBAC), allowing assignment of granular permissions to users based on their responsibilities. Workspace roles include Admin, Contributor, Member, and Viewer, each with distinct capabilities. Proper mapping of these roles ensures that users have only the access necessary for their tasks, reducing risk and supporting operational efficiency.

Enfrasys Solutions proposes the following initial workspace role mappings for SIRIM personnel, based on organizational roles and responsibilities. SIRIM is responsible for confirming user assignments and group memberships, ensuring alignment with internal governance.

| No. | Workspace Role | Suggested Role | SIRIM PIC |
|-----|---------------|---------------|-----------|
| 1 | Workspace Admin: add/remove users, manage roles and permissions, publish/edit/delete content | Fabric Admin/Data Engineer | En Wazir, Puan Solehah |
| 2 | Workspace Contributor: create/edit/delete own content, cannot delete others’ content or change settings | Data Engineer / Business User Admin | Aina, Khairul, Puan Solehah |
| 3 | Workspace Viewer: view report/dashboard, cannot edit/publish content | Data Analyst | Aina, Khairul, Puan Solehah |
| 4 | Workspace Member: create/edit/delete reports, pipeline, etc., share content, cannot manage roles/permissions | Data Engineer | Aina, Khairul, Puan Solehah |

This mapping ensures clear separation of duties, supports auditability, and enables SIRIM to manage workspace access efficiently.

## 5.4 Row-Level Security (RLS) in the Semantic Model

Row-level security (RLS) is a critical feature in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI that restricts data visibility within reports based on user identity. By defining RLS roles in the Semantic Model, SIRIM can ensure that users see only the data relevant to their responsibilities, such as HR staff accessing only their own records.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends leveraging Microsoft 365 groups for RLS assignments, ensuring scalable and manageable access control. The Semantic Model should be designed to reflect SIRIM’s data relationships, with tables, measures, and calculated columns structured to support RLS policies. This approach protects sensitive data, supports compliance, and enables personalized reporting.

For example, HR reports can be configured so that only members of the designated Microsoft 365 group (e.g., sirimmgmt@sirim.my) can view specific rows, while other users are restricted to their own data. This granular control is essential for maintaining data privacy and supporting SIRIM’s operational needs.

## 5.5 Access Workflow and Responsibilities

The access model requires coordinated implementation and ongoing management. Enfrasys Solutions will propose initial role mappings and Conditional Access policies, while SIRIM will be responsible for confirming user assignments, maintaining group memberships, and monitoring access compliance.

The following table outlines key activities and responsibilities:

| Item | Activities | Action By | Status |
|------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Propose Conditional Access policies for analytics workloads | Enfrasys Solutions | In Progress |
| 2 | Implement workspace role mappings in Fabric | Enfrasys Solutions | In Progress |
| 3 | Confirm user assignments and group memberships | SIRIM | Pending |
| 4 | Configure Private Endpoints and NSG rules | Enfrasys Solutions | In Progress |
| 5 | Review and approve access model | SIRIM | Pending |

This workflow ensures that access controls are robust, auditable, and tailored to SIRIM’s requirements, with clear ownership and accountability throughout the deployment process.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section details the architectural design and technical decisions for SIRIM’s analytics platform, encompassing the end-to-end data workflow, Data Gateway VM deployment, and the standardized naming conventions for all Microsoft Fabric items. Enfrasys Solutions has documented the technical design, while SIRIM is responsible for validating data sources and naming standards to ensure alignment with organizational requirements.

## 6.1 End-to-End Data Workflow Architecture

Modern analytics platforms require a robust, scalable, and secure data workflow. Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics solution that combines data engineering, data science, and business intelligence capabilities. The proposed architecture for SIRIM leverages Azure Data Factory for data ingestion, Lakehouse layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold) for data refinement, Dataflow Gen2 for orchestration, and Power BI for visualization—all unified through OneLake for seamless data access.

Data ingestion begins with Azure Data Factory, which pulls data from SIRIM’s PostgreSQL instance hosted on the TOPAZ VM. The raw data is initially stored in the Bronze Lakehouse layer, preserving its original state for traceability and auditing. Data is then cleansed and transformed in the Silver Lakehouse, ensuring quality and consistency before further refinement in the Gold Lakehouse. The Gold layer contains highly curated datasets, optimized for analytics and reporting.

Dataflow Gen2 orchestrates movement and transformation between Lakehouse layers, automating processes such as cleansing, enrichment, and aggregation. The final, curated data is exposed through a Semantic Model, enabling row-level security and advanced data modeling. Power BI connects directly to the Semantic Model via OneLake, providing business users with real-time, secure access to analytics dashboards and reports.

This architecture ensures data lineage, governance, and scalability, supporting SIRIM’s evolving analytics needs while maintaining compliance and operational efficiency.

The following diagram illustrates the data workflow from ingestion to visualization:

![](images\slide_014_img_003.png)

Figure 1: End-to-end data workflow architecture for SIRIM Fabric.

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Considerations

A well-structured data pipeline is critical for reliability and maintainability. The design incorporates best practices for data engineering, security, and business intelligence. Data Factory is leveraged for ingestion, ensuring connectivity and automation with SIRIM’s PostgreSQL source. Lakehouse layers provide a clear separation of raw, cleansed, and transformed data, supporting traceability and iterative improvement. Dataflow Gen2 automates movement and transformation, reducing manual intervention and errors.

Semantic Models and row-level security are implemented to ensure that sensitive data is only accessible to authorized personnel, aligning with SIRIM’s compliance requirements. Power BI integration via OneLake guarantees a unified view, eliminating data silos and enabling cross-functional analytics.

The following table outlines the key design considerations and associated workloads:

| No.  | Description                                                                                  | Workloads type       |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from PostgreSQL.                                   | Data Factory         |
| DC02 | The bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from PostgreSQL.                   | Data Engineering     |
| DC03 | The silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.              | Data Engineering     |
| DC04 | The gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.             | Data Engineering     |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the bronze and silver Lakehouse will be performed using Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering     |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory         |
| DC07 | Data modeling and row-level security (RLS) configurations will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the gold Lakehouse. | Power BI             |
| DC08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.       | Power BI             |

## 6.3 Data Gateway VM Deployment

To facilitate secure and reliable connectivity between SIRIM’s on-premises PostgreSQL database and Microsoft Fabric, a Data Gateway agent is deployed on a dedicated Virtual Machine (VM). The Data Gateway VM acts as a bridge, ensuring encrypted, authenticated data transfer from the TOPAZ VM to the Fabric environment. This approach isolates sensitive data flows, enhances security, and enables centralized management of gateway credentials and configurations.

The Data Gateway agent has been installed on the GASPRA VM within the SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG resource group. This VM is managed by Enfrasys Solutions, who are responsible for its configuration, maintenance, and monitoring. SIRIM is tasked with validating the data source connectivity and ensuring that the gateway meets organizational security standards. This deployment supports scalability, allowing additional data sources to be integrated as SIRIM’s analytics requirements expand.

The following diagram illustrates the Data Gateway VM’s role in the data flow:

![](images\slide_016_img_004.png)

Figure 2: Data Gateway VM bridging PostgreSQL data source to SIRIM Fabric.

## 6.4 Naming Conventions for Fabric Items

Consistent and descriptive naming conventions are essential for resource management, operational clarity, and compliance. Enfrasys Solutions recommends adopting a standardized naming pattern for all Fabric items, combining identity, scenario/activity, and item type. This approach facilitates easier identification, auditing, and automation within the analytics environment.

SIRIM is responsible for validating these naming standards to ensure alignment with internal policies and data governance requirements. The following table summarizes the recommended naming conventions for Fabric items:

| 6   | Pipeline          | HR_Ingest_Data_PL<br>Etc..                                    |
| 7   | Report            | HR_HeadCountWorkForce_Report                                  |

Enfrasys Solutions will document the technical design and naming conventions, while SIRIM shall validate and approve the data sources and naming standards prior to production deployment. This collaborative approach ensures that all resources are managed efficiently and remain compliant with SIRIM’s operational and governance requirements.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration strategy for the SIRIM data integration initiative. The approach ensures a seamless transition from legacy data workflows to a modern, secure, and scalable architecture leveraging Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Enfrasys Solutions has designed the plan to minimize disruption, assign clear responsibilities, and optimize operational efficiency for SIRIM.

## 7.1 Data Gateway Agent Deployment

The deployment of the Data Gateway agent is a critical step in establishing secure and reliable connectivity between SIRIM's on-premises or virtualized data sources and the Microsoft Fabric platform. Microsoft Data Gateway acts as a bridge, enabling data transfer between local environments and cloud services such as Power BI, Power Automate, and Azure Data Factory. The agent must be installed on a dedicated virtual machine (VM) to ensure isolation, performance, and security.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends deploying the Data Gateway agent on a purpose-built Azure VM within the designated resource group (SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG). This VM, referred to as the Data Gateway VM, will facilitate data movement from the TOPAZ PostgreSQL database to SIRIM Fabric, as depicted in the architecture diagram below. By isolating the Data Gateway agent on its own VM, SIRIM benefits from enhanced control over access, simplified troubleshooting, and the ability to scale resources as data volumes grow. Furthermore, this approach aligns with best practices for data security and operational reliability.

![](images\slide_016_img_004.png)

Figure 7.1: Data flow architecture from TOPAZ PostgreSQL through Data Gateway VM to SIRIM Fabric.

## 7.2 Creation of Required Azure Resources

To support the migration and integration workflows, Enfrasys Solutions will provision the necessary Azure resources, including the Data Gateway VM and associated network, storage, and security components. The VM will reside within the SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG resource group, ensuring logical organization and adherence to SIRIM’s governance standards.

Resource creation will follow a structured process:
- Assessment of existing VM infrastructure to determine whether a new VM is required or an existing VM (such as GASPRA) can be repurposed.
- Configuration of VM specifications to meet performance and security requirements.
- Installation and configuration of the Data Gateway agent, including assignment of credentials and network access controls.
- Validation of connectivity between the TOPAZ PostgreSQL database, Data Gateway VM, and SIRIM Fabric.

This process ensures that all components are properly integrated, secure, and ready for production data flows. Enfrasys Solutions will coordinate with SIRIM to confirm technical requirements and operational readiness before proceeding to cutover.

## 7.3 Migration Timeline and Key Activities

A well-defined migration timeline is essential for ensuring clarity, accountability, and minimal disruption to business operations. The following table details the key activities, planned start and end dates, responsible parties, and current status. Enfrasys Solutions will lead technical tasks, while SIRIM will provide data stewardship and review.

### Deployment & Migration Activities

| No | Activities                                      | Planned Start     | Planned End       | Action By           | Status        |
|----|-------------------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------|
| 1  | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by SIRIM | Fri, 13-June-25   | Tues, 17-June-25  | Enfrasys, SIRIM     | Not-Started   |
| 2  | Confirm on the table to be ingested             | Wed, 11-June-25   | Fri, 13-June-25   | SIRIM               | Not-Started   |
| 3  | Create an Azure VM to establish Data Gateway    |                   |                   | Enfrasys            | Not-Started   |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for delivering the design documentation and provisioning the Azure VM for the Data Gateway agent. SIRIM is tasked with confirming the tables to be ingested, ensuring data readiness and alignment with business requirements. All activities are planned to commence in June 2025, with status updates and coordination sessions scheduled to ensure timely completion.

## 7.4 Responsibility Assignment and Operational Coordination

Clear assignment of responsibilities is crucial for the success of the deployment and migration initiative. Enfrasys Solutions will manage all technical aspects, including VM provisioning, Data Gateway installation, and integration testing. SIRIM will oversee data selection, review of deliverables, and provide access credentials as required.

Operational coordination will be maintained through regular project meetings, progress tracking, and escalation protocols. Enfrasys Solutions will provide post-migration support and troubleshooting to ensure a smooth transition to the new architecture.

By following this deployment and migration approach, SIRIM will achieve a robust, scalable, and secure data integration environment, enabling advanced analytics and business intelligence capabilities through Microsoft Fabric.

The diagram illustrates a technical architecture involving Azure components and user access flow. 

1. **Subscription**: Represents the Azure subscription under which resources are managed. It is the foundational layer for organizing and billing Azure services.

2. **WVD (Windows Virtual Desktop)**: This component is part of the subscription and provides virtualized Windows desktops and applications to users. External users connect to the WVD to access resources.

3. **Fabric-RG (Resource Group)**: A logical container within the Azure subscription that holds related resources for Azure solutions. It includes the SIRIM FABRIC component.

4. **SIRIM FABRIC**: A specific application or service hosted within the Fabric-RG. It is accessed by users through the WVD.

5. **Conditional Access**: A security feature that ensures only authorized users can access the SIRIM FABRIC. It applies policies to verify user identity and compliance before granting access.

6. **External User**: Represents users outside the organization who connect to the WVD to access the SIRIM FABRIC.

7. **SIRIM User**: Represents internal users who access the SIRIM FABRIC with conditional access policies applied.

**Data Flow**:
- External users connect to the WVD within the Azure subscription.
- The WVD facilitates access to the SIRIM FABRIC hosted in the Fabric-RG.
- Conditional Access policies are applied to ensure secure access for SIRIM users.
- The flow ensures secure and organized access to resources within the Azure environment.

The diagram illustrates a network architecture involving Azure Virtual Networks (VNETs), Virtual Network Gateways, and VNET Peering. 

1. **SIRIM**: Represents an on-premises network connecting to Azure via a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN. This connection is established through a Virtual Network Gateway within Azure.

2. **Subscription**: Indicates the Azure subscription under which the resources are deployed.

3. **VNET (x.x.x.x/xx)**: Two separate VNETs are shown, each with a specific IP address range. These VNETs are part of the Azure infrastructure.

4. **Virtual Network Gateway**: Located within a GatewaySubnet, it facilitates the S2S VPN connection from the on-premises network to Azure.

5. **VNET Peering**: Connects the two VNETs, allowing resources within them to communicate with each other. This peering is bidirectional.

6. **Fabric-RG and Fabric-VNET (x.x.x.x/xx)**: Represents a resource group and VNET dedicated to a specific service or application, possibly related to Microsoft Fabric.

7. **Fabric Private Endpoint**: Located within a Fabric-SUBNET, it provides secure access to Azure services over a private link.

8. **WVD (Windows Virtual Desktop)**: Deployed within one of the VNETs, accessible to external users, indicating remote desktop services.

9. **External User**: Represents users accessing the Windows Virtual Desktop from outside the Azure network.

The architecture ensures secure connectivity between on-premises and Azure resources, facilitates communication between different VNETs, and provides remote desktop services to external users.

The diagram represents a data workflow architecture within the SIRIM FABRIC environment. It illustrates the flow of data from ingestion to visualization using Azure services.

1. **Data Ingestion**:
   - The process begins with data ingestion from the `TOPAZ` system located in the `SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG` resource group. This data is ingested into Azure using `Data Factory`.

2. **Bronze Layer**:
   - Ingested data is stored in the `XX_Bronze_LK Tables`. This layer serves as the raw data storage, where data is kept in its original form.

3. **Silver Layer**:
   - Data from the Bronze layer is processed and transformed using `Data Factory` and `Synapse Engineering`. The transformed data is stored in the `XX_Silver_LK Tables`, which represents a more refined and cleansed version of the data.

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

## 2.1 Project Overview

The Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI and Microsoft Fabric initiative is strategically designed to modernize and optimize the university’s data analytics capabilities. The project encompasses the full data lifecycle, from data ingestion through transformation and visualization, leveraging the robust Microsoft Fabric platform. This initiative includes the establishment of a dedicated Fabric workspace, the development of comprehensive end-to-end ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, the enablement of advanced machine learning processes, and the seamless integration of Power BI to deliver actionable business intelligence. The overarching objective is to ensure that UMS’s cloud adoption strategy is fully aligned with Microsoft Fabric’s advanced service offerings, including Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for big data analytics, and Data Science for machine learning applications. These capabilities will empower UMS to derive deeper insights, support data-driven decision-making, and enhance operational efficiency across the institution.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

This Solution Design Document serves as the authoritative reference for the architecture, workflows, and implementation approach for the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric deployment at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. It details the technical and operational design decisions, providing comprehensive guidance for all stakeholders involved in the project. The document is intended to ensure a clear, consistent understanding of the solution scope, to facilitate informed decision-making, and to provide a baseline for implementation, governance, and future enhancements. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that all project participants reference this document throughout the project lifecycle to ensure alignment with the defined objectives and technical standards.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for a diverse audience comprising both technical and non-technical stakeholders within Universiti Malaysia Sabah and Enfrasys Solutions. The primary readers include UMS’s IT leadership, data engineering and analytics teams, business analysts, and project sponsors, as well as Enfrasys Solutions’ architects and implementation specialists. The content is structured to provide strategic context for executive stakeholders while delivering sufficient technical depth for solution architects, developers, and administrators responsible for the deployment and ongoing management of the Power BI and Microsoft Fabric solution.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides formal definitions and describes the roles of all core technologies utilized in the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data platform solution. Each technology is selected to ensure an integrated, secure, and scalable architecture, supporting the end-to-end data workflow from ingestion to analytics and machine learning.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence. It provides a single, SaaS-based environment that brings together multiple data workloads and services, streamlining the data lifecycle for organizations. Microsoft Fabric’s architecture enables seamless data ingestion, transformation, storage, and analysis, all governed under a unified security and compliance model.

For UMS, Microsoft Fabric serves as the central platform, orchestrating data flows from source systems to advanced analytics and visualization. Its modular design allows UMS to leverage specialized workloads such as Data Factory, Synapse, and Data Science, all within a consistent workspace and security boundary.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s business analytics service that enables users to visualize data, share insights, and drive business decisions through interactive reports and dashboards. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, allowing direct connectivity to data stored in OneLake and semantic models for real-time analytics.

In the UMS solution, Power BI is used to connect to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake, providing stakeholders with timely, accurate, and actionable insights. This integration ensures that data visualizations are always up to date and that users can self-serve their analytical needs within a governed environment.

## 3.3 Fabric Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-based data integration and orchestration service within Microsoft Fabric. It enables organizations to create, schedule, and manage data pipelines for ingesting, transforming, and moving data across various sources and destinations. Fabric Data Factory supports both code-free and code-based pipeline development, offering flexibility for different user personas.

UMS leverages Fabric Data Factory to automate the extraction of data from the on-premises SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse, orchestrate ETL processes, and move data through the Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers. This ensures data is efficiently ingested, cleansed, and prepared for downstream analytics and machine learning workloads.

## 3.4 Fabric Synapse

Fabric Synapse is a comprehensive analytics service within Microsoft Fabric, combining big data and data warehousing capabilities. It provides a unified experience for data exploration, transformation, and analysis using SQL, Spark, and Data Explorer engines. Fabric Synapse enables scalable processing of large datasets, advanced analytics, and integration with machine learning workflows.

For UMS, Fabric Synapse is used to perform advanced data engineering tasks, such as data cleansing, transformation, and enrichment within the Lakehouse architecture. Its support for Notebooks and Spark-based processing allows for flexible and powerful data manipulation, essential for preparing data for machine learning and reporting.

## 3.5 OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified data lake, designed to store structured and unstructured data at scale. It acts as a single logical repository for all data assets within Fabric, supporting direct access by multiple workloads and services. OneLake’s architecture ensures data consistency, security, and simplified management across the analytics platform.

In the UMS architecture, OneLake is the central storage layer for all ingested, processed, and analyzed data. Data flows from the Bronze (raw), Silver (cleansed), to Gold (transformed) Lakehouse tables, all residing in OneLake. This design enables seamless data access for Power BI, machine learning, and other analytics workloads.

## 3.6 Data Science (AutoML and Notebooks)

The Data Science workload in Microsoft Fabric provides tools for building, training, and operationalizing machine learning models. It includes AutoML (Automated Machine Learning), which automates the process of selecting algorithms and tuning models, and Notebooks, which support interactive development using languages such as Python and PySpark.

UMS utilizes both AutoML and Notebooks for machine learning experimentation. Cleaned data from the Silver Lakehouse is used as input for AutoML experiments and manual modeling in Notebooks. Trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, and scoring results are stored in the Gold Lakehouse. This approach enables UMS to derive predictive insights and operationalize machine learning within the same analytics platform.

## 3.7 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a comprehensive cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides authentication, authorization, and conditional access capabilities for users, groups, and applications across Microsoft cloud services.

In the UMS solution, Entra ID governs access to all Fabric resources, enforcing security policies such as Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and Conditional Access. This ensures that only authorized users—internal and external—can access sensitive data and analytics assets, in alignment with UMS’s security requirements.

## 3.8 On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway is a secure bridge that enables cloud services such as Microsoft Fabric and Power BI to access data stored in on-premises environments. It facilitates hybrid connectivity, allowing organizations to keep sensitive data on-premises while leveraging cloud analytics capabilities.

UMS deploys the On-Premises Data Gateway to connect Fabric Data Factory with the SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse. This ensures secure, reliable, and performant data ingestion from on-premises systems to the cloud, without exposing internal resources directly to the internet.

## 3.9 SQL Server 2017

Microsoft SQL Server 2017 is a relational database management system (RDBMS) that supports transactional and analytical workloads. It provides robust data storage, security, and querying capabilities for enterprise applications.

Within the UMS architecture, SQL Server 2017 serves as the primary staging area and source system for data ingestion. Data is extracted from this environment via the On-Premises Data Gateway and processed through the Fabric platform for analytics and reporting.

## 3.10 Additional Platforms and Components

- **Identity_SM**: Integrated as part of the data workflow to manage identities and access control, ensuring that only authorized users can interact with sensitive data at each processing stage.
- **Semantic Model**: Implemented in Power BI, this model provides a structured, business-friendly layer for data modeling, supporting efficient and consistent analytics across the organization.

## 3.11 End-to-End Data Flow and Security Architecture

The following diagram illustrates the secure, end-to-end data flow and access control mechanisms within the UMS solution. Data is ingested from the on-premises SQL Server 2017, processed through Fabric Data Factory and Synapse, and securely stored in OneLake. Machine learning and analytics workloads are executed within Fabric, with Power BI providing visualization. All access is governed by Entra ID and Conditional Access policies, ensuring compliance and security.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Secure Access and Data Flow Architecture with Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, and Entra Conditional Access

This architecture ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah benefits from a unified, secure, and scalable analytics platform, supporting its business intelligence and machine learning objectives while maintaining strict governance over data access and usage.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the comprehensive network and security architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), focusing on secure hybrid connectivity, virtual machine (VM) sizing for the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG), and the enforcement of outbound security rules. The design leverages Microsoft Azure best practices and Entra ID security controls to ensure robust protection of UMS’s cloud and on-premises assets.

## 4.1 Connectivity Architecture Overview

The network connectivity architecture for UMS is designed to facilitate secure, reliable, and scalable integration between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric services. The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) acts as a critical bridge, enabling seamless data transfer from the UMS Staging Area—powered by Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse—to the UMS Fabric environment in Azure. This approach eliminates the need for inbound ports, significantly reducing the attack surface and aligning with Azure’s security recommendations.

The OPDG is deployed within a dedicated Azure VM, which initiates outbound HTTPS connections to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and other Microsoft cloud services. This model ensures that sensitive data remains protected during transit, leveraging SSL/TLS encryption for all communications. The architecture also supports future scalability and integration with additional Microsoft services as UMS’s requirements evolve.

The diagram below illustrates the secure data flow between the UMS on-premises data warehouse, the OPDG, and the UMS Fabric environment. Data originates from the UMS Staging Area, traverses the OPDG via outbound connections, and is ingested into the UMS Fabric for analytics and processing.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Secure Data Flow from UMS Staging Area to UMS Fabric via OPDG

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the installation and configuration of the OPDG agent on the designated Azure VM. UMS will provide the necessary access credentials and network information for the on-premises data sources.

## 4.2 Virtual Machine Sizing for OPDG

The performance and reliability of the OPDG are directly influenced by the underlying VM specifications. Enfrasys recommends deploying the OPDG on a VM with sufficient resources to handle anticipated data loads and concurrent connections, ensuring minimal latency and high availability.

The VM must meet the following specifications to support the OPDG and associated workloads:

- Operating System: Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit)
- .NET Framework: Version 4.8
- vCPU: 8 cores
- RAM: Minimum 8 GB

These specifications are based on Microsoft’s guidelines for OPDG deployments, ensuring compatibility and optimal throughput for data transfer operations. Enfrasys Solutions will provision and configure the VM according to these requirements, while UMS will be responsible for ongoing monitoring and alerting of resource utilization.

## 4.3 Outbound Security Rules

Securing outbound traffic from the OPDG VM is essential to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration and to ensure that only sanctioned communication occurs with Microsoft services. The following Azure Network Security Group (NSG) outbound rules are defined to tightly control egress traffic, permitting only the necessary endpoints and ports required for OPDG operation.

Each rule is crafted to enable secure connectivity for data transfer, authentication, and network health verification, in alignment with Azure networking best practices. Enfrasys Solutions will implement and validate these rules within the Azure environment.

The table below details the outbound security rules for the OPDG VM:

| Name                        | Priority | Source                  | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                         | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|-------------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com     | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                      | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules ensure that the OPDG VM can securely communicate with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure core services, and authentication endpoints, while preventing unnecessary outbound traffic.

## 4.4 Conditional Access and MFA Enforcement

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a comprehensive cloud-based identity and access management solution that enables organizations to protect user identities and control access to resources. Conditional Access is a feature within Entra ID that evaluates user sign-in attempts based on signals such as user identity, location, and device compliance, enforcing policies to allow or block access accordingly.

For UMS, Conditional Access is not currently eligible due to licensing constraints; the institution is not equipped with Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses. As a result, Enfrasys Solutions recommends—and has enforced—Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level for all UMS users. This approach provides a robust baseline of security, ensuring that all users undergo additional identity verification during sign-in, thereby reducing the risk of unauthorized access.

The authentication and access control flow is depicted in the following diagram. User authentication attempts are evaluated by Entra ID, which enforces MFA at the tenant level. Upon successful verification, users are granted access to Microsoft Fabric resources.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 2: Authentication and Access Control Flow with Entra ID and MFA

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the configuration and enforcement of tenant-wide MFA policies. UMS is responsible for user onboarding, communication, and support related to MFA adoption.

## 4.5 Responsibility Assignment

- **Enfrasys Solutions**: 
  - Installation and configuration of the OPDG agent on the Azure VM.
  - Implementation and validation of Azure NSG outbound security rules.
  - Configuration of tenant-wide MFA enforcement in Entra ID.

- **Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS)**:
  - Provision of access credentials and network information for on-premises data sources.
  - Ongoing monitoring of VM resource utilization and user support for MFA.
  - User onboarding and communication regarding security policy changes.

This clear delineation of responsibilities ensures a smooth deployment, robust security posture, and effective operational management for UMS’s hybrid data integration with Microsoft Fabric.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section details the roles, access controls, and conditional access policy design for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) within the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. The following subsections outline the rationale, configuration, and responsibilities for secure access and workspace role assignment.

## 5.1 Conditional Access Policy Design

Conditional Access is a core capability of Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory), enabling organizations to enforce access controls on applications and resources based on specific conditions such as user identity, device state, location, and authentication strength. Conditional Access policies are essential for securing cloud resources, reducing the risk of unauthorized access, and ensuring compliance with organizational security standards.

For UMS, Enfrasys Solutions has designed a Conditional Access approach that aligns with the current licensing and operational constraints. Based on the assessment, UMS accounts are not presently eligible for advanced Conditional Access features due to licensing limitations (Entra ID P1/P2). As a result, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) has been enforced at the tenant level to provide a baseline of strong authentication across all users. This approach ensures that, even in the absence of granular Conditional Access policies, all users are subject to additional verification, significantly reducing the risk of credential compromise.

The design also considers future scalability. Should UMS acquire the necessary Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses, Enfrasys Solutions recommends revisiting the Conditional Access configuration to enable more granular policies, such as restricting access by network location, device compliance, or risk-based controls. For now, the enforced MFA serves as a robust fallback, ensuring that only authenticated users can access Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and associated Azure resources.

The following diagram illustrates the access flow, highlighting how user authentication requests are evaluated and enforced through Entra Conditional Access and MFA mechanisms.

The diagram below depicts the authentication and access control flow for Microsoft Fabric using Entra Conditional Access policies. When a user attempts to access Microsoft Fabric, the authentication request is evaluated against Entra Conditional Access policies, which consider signals such as user identity and network location. Based on these signals, a decision is made and enforced, granting or denying access. If access is granted, the user is allowed into Microsoft Fabric and its components, such as OneLake, ensuring secure and conditional access.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Microsoft Fabric Conditional Access Authentication Flow

The following table summarizes the key Conditional Access design decisions for UMS:

  
| No.  | Conditional Access                                                                                   |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy                                                   |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts                |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment                                                 |

  
Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration of Conditional Access policies and MFA enforcement within the Microsoft Entra tenant. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for user onboarding, ensuring that all designated users complete MFA registration and adhere to the authentication requirements.

## 5.2 MFA Fallback and Security Implications

Given the current licensing constraints, MFA has been enforced at the tenant level as the primary security control. Multi-Factor Authentication is a security mechanism that requires users to provide two or more verification factors to gain access to a resource, thereby adding an additional layer of protection against compromised credentials.

Enforcing MFA across the UMS tenant ensures that all users, regardless of their location or device, must authenticate using a combination of something they know (password) and something they have (such as a mobile device or authenticator app). This approach significantly mitigates the risk of unauthorized access, especially for privileged accounts and users with access to sensitive data within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI.

Should UMS decide to enhance its security posture in the future by acquiring Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses, Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing more granular Conditional Access policies, such as enforcing MFA only for high-risk scenarios, blocking legacy authentication protocols, or requiring device compliance. For the current phase, tenant-wide MFA provides a balance between security and operational simplicity.

## 5.3 Workspace Role Mapping and Assignment

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI utilize a workspace-based access model, where users are assigned roles that define their permissions within a workspace. The primary roles include Workspace Admin, Contributor, and Viewer. Proper role assignment is critical to maintaining data security, operational efficiency, and compliance with UMS governance policies.

Workspace Admins have full control over workspace settings, data, and user management. Contributors can add, modify, and publish content, while Viewers have read-only access to reports and datasets. Enfrasys Solutions has mapped these roles to suggested UMS responsibilities based on operational needs and stakeholder input.

Role assignment is a joint responsibility: Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial workspace roles and permissions, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing user management, ensuring that the correct personnel are assigned to each role and that access is regularly reviewed.

- **Enfrasys Solutions**: Responsible for the initial configuration of Conditional Access policies, MFA enforcement, and workspace role setup within the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment.
