# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section outlines the end-to-end platform architecture and workflow design for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric implementation. The design leverages Azure-native services and Microsoft Fabric to deliver a robust, scalable, and secure data platform supporting data engineering, machine learning, and business intelligence workloads.

## 6.1 End-to-End Data Workflow Architecture

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a layered data architecture that orchestrates data ingestion, transformation, storage, machine learning, and visualization through Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. This approach ensures data quality, governance, and seamless integration across analytical workloads.

The workflow begins with data ingestion from the UMS Staging Area, which is hosted on Microsoft SQL Server 2017. Azure Data Factory is utilized to orchestrate and automate the data ingestion process, ensuring reliable and scheduled movement of data into the Fabric environment. Once ingested, the data is systematically processed through three distinct Lakehouse layers—Bronze, Silver, and Gold—each serving a specific role in the data lifecycle:

- **Bronze Layer:** Stores raw, unprocessed data as ingested from the source.
- **Silver Layer:** Contains cleansed and enriched data, ready for analytical processing.
- **Gold Layer:** Holds highly refined and transformed data, optimized for reporting and advanced analytics.

Identity and access management are enforced using integrated identity services, ensuring that only authorized users and processes can interact with sensitive data at each stage. All data is centrally stored in OneLake, Microsoft Fabric’s unified data lake, providing a single source of truth and simplifying governance. The Gold Layer data is exposed to Power BI through OneLake, enabling interactive data visualization and self-service analytics for UMS stakeholders.

The diagram below illustrates the data flow and processing architecture:

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: End-to-End Data Workflow Architecture in Microsoft Fabric

## 6.2 Data Workflow Design Considerations

The design principles for the data workflow emphasize modularity, traceability, and operational efficiency. Each transformation stage is clearly delineated, ensuring that data lineage and quality can be monitored and audited. Data Factory pipelines automate the movement and transformation of data between Lakehouse layers, while Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query tools are leveraged for data cleansing and enrichment.

By adopting this structured approach, Universiti Malaysia Sabah benefits from:

- Improved data quality through staged cleansing and transformation.
- Enhanced security and governance via integrated identity management.
- Operational efficiency through automation and centralized storage.
- Scalable analytics and machine learning capabilities.

The following table details the key design considerations for the data workflow:

| ID   | Description                                                                 | Workload Type    |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.         | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server. | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse. | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse. | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse. | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization. | Power BI         |

## 6.3 AutoML Workflow Design

Microsoft Fabric’s AutoML capabilities enable Universiti Malaysia Sabah to accelerate machine learning experimentation and deployment. The platform supports both automated and manual machine learning workflows, allowing data scientists to select the approach best suited to their use case.

The AutoML workflow begins with cleansed data from the Silver Lakehouse, which serves as the input for machine learning experiments. Users can leverage Fabric Notebooks for manual model development—enabling advanced feature engineering, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter tuning—or utilize AutoML for rapid prototyping and baseline model generation. Model training, evaluation, and scoring are conducted within the notebook environment, with results and predictions stored in the Gold Lakehouse for downstream consumption.

All trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, supporting lifecycle management, versioning, and reuse. The Gold Lakehouse acts as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency and traceability. Power BI connects directly to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake, enabling real-time visualization of machine learning outcomes.

The following diagram depicts the AutoML workflow, highlighting the integration between data engineering, machine learning, and business intelligence components:

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: AutoML and Machine Learning Workflow in Microsoft Fabric

## 6.4 AutoML Workflow Design Considerations

The AutoML workflow is designed to maximize flexibility and transparency, supporting both automated and custom machine learning processes. By storing all results in the Gold Lakehouse and registering models in the Model Registry, Universiti Malaysia Sabah ensures robust governance and reproducibility.

Key benefits of this approach include:

- Accelerated experimentation through AutoML and notebook-based workflows.
- Centralized storage of model outputs for consistency and auditability.
- Seamless integration with Power BI for visualization and decision support.
- Enhanced model management via the Fabric Model Registry.

The table below summarizes the primary design considerations for the AutoML workflow:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                                        | Workloads type   |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering |
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science     |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science     |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science     |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering |
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering |
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI         |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                                            | Power BI         |

## 6.5 Naming Conventions

Consistent and descriptive naming conventions are critical for effective governance, discoverability, and operational management within Microsoft Fabric. Enfrasys Solutions has established a naming standard that encodes the identity, scenario/activity, and Fabric item type within each resource name. This approach facilitates clear lineage tracking, simplifies access management, and supports automation.

The naming convention format is: `<Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>`. For example, a Lakehouse for Student Affairs Bronze data would be named `StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK`.

The table below provides examples of the naming convention applied to key Fabric resources:

| No. | Item in Fabric   | Naming <Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>           |
|-----|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity  | stagingareadevcapacity01                                          |
| 2   | Workspace        | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                                             |
| 3   | Lakehouse        | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK<br>StudentAffairs_Silver_LK<br>Etc…      |
| 4   | Dataflow         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF<br>StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF<br>Etc.. |
| 5   | Semantic Model   | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_SM                              |
| 6   | Pipeline         | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL<br>Etc..                            |
| 7   | Report           | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_Report                          |

## 6.6 Responsibilities and Governance

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial setup of the data workflows, implementation of naming conventions, and configuration of governance controls within Microsoft Fabric. This includes the deployment of Data Factory pipelines, Lakehouse layers, and integration with OneLake and Power BI.

Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ongoing governance, including access management, data stewardship, and adherence to established naming conventions for all newly created resources. Enfrasys Solutions will provide knowledge transfer and documentation to ensure that UMS personnel are equipped to manage and extend the platform in alignment with best practices.

By clearly delineating responsibilities, Universiti Malaysia Sabah ensures operational continuity, compliance, and the ability to scale the platform as analytical needs evolve.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the structured deployment and migration strategy for the Microsoft Fabric solution, tailored for Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The approach is designed to ensure a seamless transition, clear assignment of responsibilities, and minimal disruption to ongoing operations.

## 7.1 Deployment Phases Overview

Enfrasys Solutions has developed a phased deployment and migration plan to address the requirements of Universiti Malaysia Sabah. This structured approach ensures that each critical milestone is achieved in a logical sequence, reducing risk and providing checkpoints for validation and sign-off. The deployment phases begin with the delivery and review of the design document, followed by infrastructure readiness, environment provisioning, and secure data gateway installation.

A phased approach benefits Universiti Malaysia Sabah by enabling clear communication, accountability, and the ability to address issues early in the process. Each phase is accompanied by defined responsibilities for both Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah, ensuring that all stakeholders are engaged and that handoffs occur smoothly. This methodology also allows for validation at each stage, ensuring alignment with the university’s operational and security requirements.

## 7.2 Migration Activities and Responsibilities

The migration activities are sequenced to ensure that prerequisites are satisfied before proceeding to subsequent steps. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the delivery of the design documentation, environment setup, and technical configuration, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for infrastructure readiness and key approvals. Joint activities, such as the installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway, require close collaboration to ensure secure connectivity and compliance with university policies.

The following table summarizes the key deployment and migration activities, their planned start dates, responsible parties, and current status.

  
| No | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks |
|----|------------|--------------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started |  |
| 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys, UMS | Not-Started |  |

  
## 7.3 Detailed Phase Descriptions

The deployment and migration plan for Universiti Malaysia Sabah consists of the following key phases:

- **Design Document Delivery and Sign-Off:** Enfrasys Solutions will deliver the finalized solution design document for review. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is required to review and provide formal sign-off. This ensures mutual understanding and agreement on the solution architecture before any technical implementation begins.
- **Infrastructure Confirmation:** Universiti Malaysia Sabah will confirm the availability and readiness of the new server intended to host the data warehouse copy (Staging Area DB). This step is critical to ensure that all data sources are prepared for integration into the Microsoft Fabric environment.
- **Fabric Environment Setup:** Enfrasys Solutions will provision and configure the Microsoft Fabric environment according to the approved design. This phase includes establishing workspaces, configuring security, and preparing the environment for data ingestion.
- **On-Premises Data Gateway Installation:** Both Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah will collaborate to install and configure the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) within the designated virtual machine. This gateway is essential for secure, reliable connectivity between on-premises data sources and the Microsoft Fabric cloud environment.

Each phase is designed to build upon the previous, ensuring that all technical and organizational prerequisites are met. This approach minimizes risk, facilitates troubleshooting, and ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah retains control and visibility throughout the migration process.

# SIRIM Analytics Deployment Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

## 2.1 Project Overview

The SIRIM Analytics Deployment project is focused on designing and implementing an end-to-end data workflow that supports the organization’s Human Resource use case. This initiative encompasses the entire data lifecycle, from ingestion and transformation to visualization. The project leverages Microsoft Fabric, integrating core services such as Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, and Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing. The solution is architected to align with SIRIM’s cloud adoption strategy, ensuring scalability, security, and operational efficiency while enabling actionable insights from HR data.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

This Solution Design Document provides a comprehensive blueprint for the deployment of SIRIM’s analytics platform. It details the technical architecture, design decisions, data workflows, security measures, and operational processes required for successful implementation. The document serves as an authoritative reference for all stakeholders, ensuring that the solution aligns with organizational objectives, adheres to best practices, and supports ongoing governance and compliance requirements.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for SIRIM’s executive leadership, IT management, data engineering teams, security officers, and project stakeholders involved in the analytics deployment. It is also relevant to Enfrasys Solutions’ consultants and technical specialists responsible for the design, implementation, and support of the platform. The content is structured to provide clear guidance and technical detail for decision-makers, implementers, and those responsible for operational management of the analytics solution.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides a formal overview of the core Microsoft technologies selected for the SIRIM Human Resource data workflow solution. Each technology is defined, and its designated role within the overall architecture is described. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the implementation and integration of all technologies outlined in this section.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that consolidates data integration, engineering, warehousing, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence under a single SaaS offering. Fabric provides a seamless experience for data professionals by integrating services such as Data Factory, Synapse, and Power BI into a cohesive environment. This integration enables organizations to build end-to-end data workflows with enhanced governance, security, and scalability.

Within the SIRIM solution, Microsoft Fabric serves as the foundational platform for the entire data pipeline. It orchestrates the ingestion, transformation, and visualization of human resource data, ensuring data consistency and operational efficiency. By leveraging Fabric, SIRIM benefits from streamlined data operations, reduced integration complexity, and accelerated time-to-insight.

## 3.2 Fabric Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-based data integration service that enables the creation, scheduling, and management of data pipelines. It supports the ingestion of data from diverse sources, transformation of raw data, and movement of processed data to designated storage or analytics layers. Data Factory is designed for scalability and reliability, supporting both batch and real-time data processing.

In the SIRIM architecture, Fabric Data Factory is responsible for ingesting data from the TOPAZ system and other sources, orchestrating the movement of data into the Bronze Lakehouse layer. This ensures that raw data is efficiently captured and made available for subsequent transformation and analytics processes. Enfrasys Solutions will configure and manage all Data Factory pipelines to guarantee secure, reliable, and auditable data flows.

## 3.3 Fabric Synapse

Fabric Synapse is an integrated analytics service that combines big data and data warehousing capabilities. It enables organizations to process, analyze, and visualize large volumes of data using familiar SQL-based and Spark-based tools. Synapse supports advanced analytics, data transformation, and machine learning workloads within the Fabric environment.

For SIRIM, Fabric Synapse is utilized to process and transform data as it moves from the Bronze to Silver and Gold Lakehouse layers. It provides the necessary compute and analytics capabilities to cleanse, aggregate, and optimize data for reporting and business intelligence. Enfrasys Solutions will implement Synapse workflows to ensure data quality, performance, and scalability.

## 3.4 Azure Data Gateway

Azure Data Gateway is a secure bridge that facilitates data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services. It enables hybrid data integration scenarios by providing encrypted connectivity, ensuring that sensitive data can be ingested into the cloud without exposing it to public networks.

In this solution, Azure Data Gateway will be configured to securely connect SIRIM’s on-premises PostgreSQL and other legacy systems to Microsoft Fabric Data Factory. This guarantees that data ingestion processes are compliant with organizational security policies and regulatory requirements. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for deploying and maintaining the Azure Data Gateway.

## 3.5 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise business intelligence and data visualization platform. It empowers users to create interactive reports and dashboards, connect to a wide range of data sources, and share insights across the organization. Power BI supports advanced analytics features, including semantic modeling and row-level security.

Within the SIRIM data workflow, Power BI is used to visualize and report on data processed in the Gold Lakehouse layer. It connects to the semantic model via OneLake, enabling secure and performant access to curated datasets. Enfrasys Solutions will design and publish Power BI reports, configure row-level security, and ensure seamless integration with the underlying data platform.

## 3.6 Azure Network Security Group (NSG)

Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs) are essential security components that control inbound and outbound network traffic to Azure resources. NSGs allow granular definition of security rules based on source, destination, port, and protocol, thereby enforcing network segmentation and minimizing attack surfaces.

For the SIRIM solution, NSGs will be implemented to protect all Azure resources involved in the data workflow, including Data Factory, Synapse, and supporting infrastructure. Enfrasys Solutions will define and manage NSG rules to ensure only authorized traffic is permitted, in accordance with SIRIM’s security requirements.

## 3.7 Azure Private Endpoint

Azure Private Endpoint is a network interface that connects Azure services privately and securely to a virtual network. By leveraging Private Endpoints, organizations can ensure that traffic between resources remains within the Azure backbone network, eliminating exposure to the public internet and reducing the risk of data breaches.

In the SIRIM architecture, Private Endpoints will be established for critical services such as Data Factory, Synapse, and OneLake, ensuring that all data transfers occur over private, isolated channels. Enfrasys Solutions will provision and manage all required Private Endpoints to maintain a robust security posture.

## 3.8 Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD)

Windows Virtual Desktop (now Azure Virtual Desktop) is a comprehensive desktop and app virtualization service running in the cloud. It enables secure remote access to Windows desktops and applications from any location, supporting flexible work arrangements and centralized management.

For SIRIM, Windows Virtual Desktop will be used to provide secure access for data engineers, analysts, and administrators who require connectivity to the Fabric environment and associated resources. Enfrasys Solutions will deploy and configure WVD environments, ensuring compliance with organizational security and operational policies.

## 3.9 OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified data lake storage solution. It offers a single, logical storage layer for all analytics workloads, supporting the Lakehouse paradigm for structured and unstructured data. OneLake integrates seamlessly with Data Factory, Synapse, and Power BI, ensuring consistent data access and governance.

In the SIRIM solution, OneLake serves as the backbone for the Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers. It provides high-performance, secure storage for raw, cleansed, and transformed data, and acts as the integration point for Power BI semantic models. Enfrasys Solutions will architect and manage OneLake storage to optimize performance, security, and cost-efficiency.

## 3.10 Data Workflow Architecture Diagram

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data workflow as implemented in the SIRIM Fabric environment. It depicts the flow of data from ingestion through transformation to visualization, highlighting the integration of Microsoft Fabric, Data Factory, Synapse, OneLake, and Power BI, as well as the supporting security and connectivity components.

![](images\slide_014_img_003.png)

Figure 1: SIRIM Data Workflow Architecture

This architecture ensures that data is securely ingested from source systems, processed through structured Lakehouse layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold), and made available for advanced analytics and visualization. Integration with OneLake and Power BI enables SIRIM to deliver timely, actionable insights to business stakeholders while maintaining strict governance and security controls.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the comprehensive network and security architecture for the SIRIM Fabric deployment, focusing on secure connectivity, gateway configuration, network segmentation, and the use of private endpoints. The design ensures robust protection for both internal and external access, while maintaining operational flexibility and compliance with industry best practices.

## 4.1 Connectivity: VPN and VNET Peering

Secure connectivity forms the backbone of the SIRIM Fabric deployment. Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN connection between SIRIM’s on-premises environment and Azure. This connection is facilitated by the Azure Virtual Network Gateway, which resides in a dedicated GatewaySubnet and establishes encrypted tunnels for data in transit. The VPN ensures that sensitive data traverses a secure channel, mitigating risks associated with exposure to the public internet.

To enable seamless communication between different Azure workloads, Virtual Network (VNET) peering is established between the primary VNET hosting the SIRIM Fabric resources and other relevant VNETs, such as those containing Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD) instances. VNET peering allows resources in separate VNETs to communicate using Azure’s backbone network, ensuring low latency and high throughput without the need for additional gateways or public IP addresses. This design not only optimizes performance but also simplifies network management and enhances security by keeping traffic internal to Azure.

The following diagram illustrates the network connectivity, highlighting the S2S VPN, VNET peering, and the placement of key resources:

![](images\slide_010_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Network connectivity architecture with S2S VPN, VNET peering, and private endpoint integration.

## 4.2 Gateways: Virtual Network Gateway and Data Gateway VM

The Azure Virtual Network Gateway is a critical component that enables hybrid connectivity between SIRIM’s on-premises infrastructure and Azure resources. Enfrasys Solutions will provision and configure the Virtual Network Gateway, ensuring that all necessary parameters—such as IP address allocation, routing, and shared keys—are securely established. This gateway is responsible for maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of data as it moves between environments.

For scenarios requiring data integration or hybrid analytics, a Data Gateway VM may be deployed within the Azure environment. This VM acts as a bridge for secure data movement between on-premises sources and Azure services, such as Power BI or Azure Data Factory. By isolating the Data Gateway within a controlled subnet and applying strict network security group (NSG) rules, Enfrasys ensures that only authorized traffic is permitted, reducing the attack surface and aligning with SIRIM’s compliance requirements.

Ongoing management of the Virtual Network Gateway and Data Gateway VM—including monitoring, patching, and scaling—shall be the responsibility of SIRIM’s IT operations team, following the initial configuration and handover by Enfrasys Solutions.

## 4.3 Network Security Groups (NSGs)

Network Security Groups (NSGs) are fundamental to enforcing granular access control within the Azure environment. NSGs allow or deny network traffic to Azure resources based on source, destination, port, and protocol. For the SIRIM Fabric deployment, dedicated NSGs are applied to the subnets hosting the WVD and Fabric resources.

Inbound and outbound rules are meticulously crafted to permit only essential traffic. For example, inbound access to Fabric resources is restricted to secure protocols (e.g., TCP 443) and authorized sources, while outbound rules ensure that traffic flows only to approved service tags. This approach minimizes exposure to potential threats and aligns with the principle of least privilege.

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial creation and validation of all NSG rules. SIRIM’s IT team will maintain, review, and update these rules as part of ongoing operational governance.

The following tables detail the specific NSG rules applied to the environment:

### Inbound NSG Rules

Name | Priority | Source | Source ports | Destination | Destination ports | Protocol | Access

Allow_Fabric_Inbound | 110 | Service Tag | 443 | Vm Private IP Addresses | * | TCP | Allow

### Outbound NSG Rules

Name | Priority | Source | Source ports | Destination | Destination ports | Protocol | Access

Allow_Fabric_Outbound | 110 | Vm Private IP Addresses | * | Service Tag | 443 | TCP | Allow

## 4.4 Private Endpoint: Design and Limitations

Private Endpoints in Azure provide a secure, private connection to platform services by mapping a private IP address from the VNET to the service. This eliminates exposure to the public internet, ensuring that only resources within the trusted network can access sensitive services such as the SIRIM Fabric workspace.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends enabling Private Link for all supported Fabric resources. This ensures that access to data and services is restricted to internal networks, significantly reducing the risk of data leakage or unauthorized access. However, it is important to recognize the current limitations associated with Private Endpoints in Azure Fabric:

- Visual query capabilities in the Data Warehouse are not supported when accessed via Private Endpoint.
- Data pipeline operations for copying data into or out of the Data Warehouse are currently not possible through Private Endpoint.
- Power BI does not support Private Link for Fabric datasets; access to these datasets will still occur over the public endpoint.
- Copilot features are not available when using Private Endpoint.

Given these constraints, SIRIM must carefully assess which workloads and user groups require private access and which may need to rely on public endpoints for full functionality. Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial Private Endpoints and document all limitations, while SIRIM’s IT team will manage ongoing access policies and monitor for feature updates.

## 4.5 Design Considerations

A secure and robust network architecture requires careful consideration of both conditional access and private endpoint implementation. Enfrasys Solutions will lead the initial configuration of conditional access policies, NSG rules, and private endpoint creation. SIRIM is responsible for the ongoing maintenance, monitoring, and review of these controls to ensure continued alignment with organizational policies and regulatory requirements.

The following table summarizes the key design considerations for conditional access and private endpoint deployment:

No. | Conditional Access | Private Endpoint

DC01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage | Enable Private Link in Fabric

DC02 | Configure NSG in existing SIRIM’s WVD for Fabric inbound and outbound | Create Private Endpoint in Azure portal

DC03 | Include SIRIM user inside Conditional Access policy | Disable Public Access from Fabric

## 4.6 Conditional Access: User Segmentation and Policy Enforcement

Conditional Access is a cornerstone of SIRIM’s security posture. This Azure AD feature enables the enforcement of contextual policies based on user identity, device compliance, location, and risk signals. For SIRIM, internal users are granted direct access to Fabric resources, subject to conditional access policies that mandate secure login, multi-factor authentication (MFA), and device compliance checks. This ensures that only authorized and verified users can interact with sensitive data.

External users, by contrast, are granted access via Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD), which acts as a secure intermediary. This separation ensures that external traffic does not reach the core Fabric environment directly, and all access is mediated through hardened virtual desktops protected by NSG rules and additional security controls.

The following diagram illustrates the access flow for both internal and external users, highlighting the enforcement of conditional access and network segmentation:

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 2: User access flow with Conditional Access and network segmentation for SIRIM Fabric.

By combining conditional access, NSG enforcement, and private endpoints, the SIRIM Fabric deployment achieves a layered security model that protects data, ensures compliance, and supports secure collaboration for both internal and external stakeholders.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section outlines the roles, access controls, and security mechanisms for SIRIM’s analytics deployment. It details the assignment of workspace roles, implementation of Conditional Access, user access flows, workspace mapping, and the enforcement of Row-Level Security (RLS) within the semantic model.

## 5.1 Admin Roles (Workspace Permission)

Microsoft Fabric workspaces are collaborative environments where users can develop, publish, and manage analytics content. Workspace roles determine the level of access and permissions each user or group has within a workspace. The main roles include Admin, Contributor, Member, and Viewer, each with distinct capabilities ranging from full administrative control to read-only access.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a clear segregation of duties within SIRIM’s analytics environment to ensure operational efficiency and security. Assigning roles based on job responsibilities minimizes the risk of unauthorized changes and enhances accountability. For example, Data Engineers and Fabric Admins should have elevated permissions to manage content and workspace settings, while Data Analysts and Business Users should have limited access tailored to their reporting needs.

Enfrasys Solutions will perform the initial setup of workspace roles and permissions. SIRIM is responsible for the ongoing assignment and management of users and groups, ensuring that only authorized personnel are granted access according to their roles.

The following table summarizes the recommended workspace role assignments for SIRIM:

  
No. | Workspace Role | Suggested Role | SIRIM PIC
--- | -------------- | -------------- | ---------
1 | Workspace Admin: add/remove users, manage roles and permissions, publish/edit/delete content | Fabric Admin/Data Engineer | En Wazir, Puan Solehah
2 | Workspace Contributor: create/edit/delete own content, cannot delete others’ content or change settings | Data Engineer / Business User Admin | Aina, Khairul, Puan Solehah
3 | Workspace Viewer: view report/dashboard, cannot edit/publish content | Data Analyst | Aina, Khairul, Puan Solehah
4 | Workspace Member: create/edit/delete reports, pipeline, etc., share content, cannot manage roles/permissions | Data Engineer | Aina, Khairul, Puan Solehah
  

## 5.2 Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a key security feature in Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) that enforces access policies based on user identity, device compliance, location, and risk signals. It provides an adaptive layer of security that only allows trusted users and devices to access sensitive resources, such as Microsoft Fabric, Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage.

For SIRIM, Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing Conditional Access policies to differentiate between internal (SIRIM) users and external users. Internal users will access Fabric resources directly and undergo additional security checks such as Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). External users, on the other hand, will access resources indirectly via Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD), which acts as a secure gateway and isolates them from the core analytics environment.

This approach ensures that only compliant and authenticated users can access critical data, while external access is tightly controlled through network security and virtualization boundaries. Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial Conditional Access policies, including integration with SIRIM’s existing user groups. SIRIM is responsible for maintaining user and group membership to ensure ongoing compliance.

The following diagram illustrates the access flow for SIRIM and external users. The flow demonstrates how Conditional Access and WVD are used to secure the environment and segregate user access.

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 1: User Access Flow for SIRIM and External Users

The following table compares access mechanisms for SIRIM users and external users:

  
No. | SIRIM user | External user
--- | ----------- | -------------
1 | Direct Access to Fabric | Indirect access via Windows Virtual Desktop (WVD)
2 | Managed using Conditional Access | WVD access managed using Network Security Group (NSG)
3 | User goes through extra checks like secure login, MFA, etc. | User separated from the actual system using the virtual computer
4 | Conditional Access policy that includes Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage | NSG rule that allows Fabric inbound and outbound
  

## 5.3 Workspace Mapping (Role Assignment)

A structured mapping of users and groups to workspace roles is essential for maintaining security and operational clarity. By aligning users with specific roles, SIRIM can ensure that permissions are granted on a need-to-know and need-to-do basis, reducing the risk of privilege escalation and data leaks.

Enfrasys Solutions will establish the initial role-to-user/group mapping within the Fabric workspaces. SIRIM will manage ongoing assignments, leveraging Microsoft 365 groups for scalable and auditable access control. This approach allows for seamless onboarding and offboarding of users while ensuring that access rights remain current and appropriate.

The table in section 5.1 serves as the authoritative mapping for workspace role assignments. SIRIM should periodically review and update these assignments to reflect organizational changes.

## 5.4 Row-Level Security (RLS) in the Semantic Model

Row-Level Security (RLS) is a critical feature in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI that restricts data access at the row level, ensuring that users only see data relevant to their role or department. RLS is implemented within the semantic model, which defines the structure, relationships, and business logic of the underlying data.

For SIRIM, RLS will be used to ensure, for example, that HR staff only view data relevant to their responsibilities, preventing unauthorized access to sensitive information across the organization. This is achieved by defining RLS roles and associating them with specific Microsoft 365 groups or users. The semantic model will include table relationships, measures, and calculated columns that enforce these data boundaries.

Enfrasys Solutions will design and implement the initial RLS policies within the semantic model. SIRIM is responsible for managing group membership and ensuring that users are assigned to the correct roles for ongoing compliance.

**Key benefits of RLS for SIRIM:**
- Ensures data privacy and compliance with internal policies and regulations.
- Simplifies report development by using a single model with dynamic data filtering.
- Enhances operational security by minimizing the risk of data exposure.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide documentation and training to SIRIM’s administrators to support ongoing management of RLS assignments.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section outlines the platform architecture, resource organization, and governance decisions for the SIRIM analytics deployment. The design leverages Microsoft Azure and Fabric components to ensure a secure, scalable, and governed analytics environment.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Architecture

A robust and well-structured data workflow is essential for efficient data processing, transformation, and visualization in the SIRIM analytics platform. Enfrasys Solutions has architected a layered data workflow leveraging Azure Data Factory, Synapse, Lakehouse storage, and Power BI. This architecture ensures data integrity, traceability, and scalability, supporting SIRIM’s analytics and reporting requirements.

The workflow begins with data ingestion from the TOPAZ system, orchestrated by Azure Data Factory. Raw data lands in the Bronze Lakehouse layer, preserving its original state for audit and traceability. Subsequent cleansing and transformation processes move data through the Silver and Gold Lakehouse layers, each representing increasing levels of data quality and readiness for analytics. Azure Synapse Engineering is utilized for advanced data processing, while Dataflow Gen2 automates movement between layers. Identity and access management is enforced throughout the workflow, ensuring only authorized users access sensitive data. Finally, Power BI connects via OneLake to the Gold layer, enabling rich data visualization and business intelligence.

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data flow, highlighting the integration between Azure services and the secure movement of data from source to visualization.

![](images\slide_014_img_003.png)

Figure 1: SIRIM Data Workflow Architecture

The diagram demonstrates the sequential flow from data ingestion (TOPAZ) through Azure Data Factory, the Lakehouse layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold), advanced processing with Synapse, and secure access management, culminating in data visualization via Power BI. OneLake serves as the integration layer, ensuring seamless connectivity between storage and analytics.

### 6.1.1 Data Workflow Design Considerations

A well-defined data workflow ensures that each stage of the data lifecycle is governed, auditable, and optimized for performance. Enfrasys Solutions recommends the following design considerations for SIRIM’s analytics platform. These considerations address ingestion, storage, transformation, security, and visualization, ensuring that each workload is mapped to the appropriate Azure and Fabric service. This approach maximizes operational efficiency, supports compliance, and enables rapid insights generation.

Key considerations include the use of Data Factory pipelines for ingestion, Lakehouse layers for data staging and transformation, Dataflow Gen2 for automated data movement, and Power BI for analytics. Security is enforced through row-level security in the Semantic Model, and all data movement is orchestrated for traceability and auditability.

The table below summarizes the main workflow considerations and their associated workloads.

| No.  | Description                                                                 | Workloads type   |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from PostgreSQL.                   | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from PostgreSQL.  | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse. | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse. | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the bronze and silver Lakehouse will be performed using Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | Data modeling and row-level security (RLS) configurations will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the gold Lakehouse. | Power BI         |
| DC08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization. | Power BI         |

## 6.2 Resource Organization and Naming Convention

A consistent and logical resource organization is critical for the manageability, scalability, and security of the SIRIM analytics platform. Enfrasys Solutions recommends adopting a standardized naming convention for all Fabric resources. This approach simplifies resource identification, supports automation, and ensures compliance with SIRIM’s governance policies.

The naming convention is structured as `<Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>`, where each component provides context about the resource’s purpose and ownership. For example, “HR_dev_WS” clearly identifies a workspace dedicated to HR development activities. This structure supports clear segregation of environments (e.g., development, production), simplifies access management, and aligns with Azure best practices.

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial setup and implementation of the naming convention. SIRIM shall ensure ongoing compliance and governance, maintaining consistency as new resources are provisioned.

The following table details the recommended naming convention for key Fabric items:

| No. | Item in Fabric    | Naming <Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>                      |
|-----|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity   | hrdevcapacity01                                                               |
| 2   | Workspace         | HR_dev_WS                                                                     |
| 3   | Lakehouse         | HR_Bronze_LK<br>HR_Silver_LK<br>Etc..                                         |
| 4   | Dataflow          | HR_Bronze_to_Silver_DF<br>HR_Silver_to_Gold_DF<br>Etc..                       |
| 5   | Semantic Model    | HR_HeadcountWorkforce_SM<br>HR_EmployTurnAttrit_SM<br>HR_AttendLeave_SM<br>HR_RecruitHire_SM<br>HR_EmployPerformDev_SM<br>HR_EmployEngage_SM<br>HR_DEI_SM<br>HR_WorkforcePlan_SM |
| 6   | Pipeline          | HR_Ingest_Data_PL<br>Etc..                                                    |
| 7   | Report            | HR_HeadCountWorkForce_Report                                                  |

## 6.3 Data Governance Workflow Considerations

Effective data governance is essential for ensuring data quality, security, and regulatory compliance within the SIRIM analytics platform. Enfrasys Solutions will establish the initial governance framework, including access controls, data lifecycle management, and audit logging. SIRIM shall be responsible for the ongoing enforcement of data governance policies, including the review and approval of data access requests, monitoring of data usage, and adherence to the established naming conventions.

The governance workflow is designed to ensure that all data assets are cataloged, access is role-based and auditable, and data movement is fully traceable. This approach minimizes risk, supports compliance with internal and external regulations, and enables SIRIM to maintain high standards of data stewardship.

Key governance considerations include:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) for all Fabric resources.
- Implementation of row-level security (RLS) in Power BI Semantic Models.
- Regular audits of resource naming and data access logs.
- Ongoing training for SIRIM data stewards on governance policies and tooling.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide initial training and documentation to SIRIM’s data governance team, ensuring a smooth transition to operational ownership. SIRIM shall maintain governance processes and ensure compliance as the platform evolves.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration approach for the SIRIM data platform initiative. The strategy is designed to ensure a structured, transparent, and auditable migration process, with clearly defined responsibilities for both Enfrasys Solutions and SIRIM.

## 7.1 Deployment Sequencing and Rationale

A phased deployment approach is adopted to minimize operational risk and ensure all stakeholders are aligned at each critical stage. Enfrasys Solutions recommends beginning with formal documentation delivery, followed by data confirmation activities, and culminating in the technical provisioning of the Azure Virtual Machine (VM) required for the Data Gateway. This sequence ensures that SIRIM’s business and technical requirements are validated before infrastructure is provisioned, thereby reducing the likelihood of rework or misconfiguration.

The initial phase focuses on delivering the finalized design document to SIRIM for review. This document serves as the baseline reference for all subsequent activities. Once SIRIM confirms the list of tables and queries to be ingested, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the provisioning of the Azure VM. This VM will host the Data Gateway, a critical component for secure and reliable data transfer between on-premises sources and the cloud environment.

## 7.2 Azure VM Provisioning for Data Gateway

The Azure Data Gateway acts as a secure bridge, enabling seamless data movement from SIRIM’s on-premises systems to the cloud. Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the end-to-end setup of the Azure VM, including operating system configuration, network integration, and installation of the Data Gateway component. This ensures that the gateway is hardened, compliant with best practices, and ready for immediate use once SIRIM confirms the ingestion tables.

Provisioning the VM at this stage allows for any network or security adjustments to be made in parallel with SIRIM’s data confirmation efforts. This parallelization reduces overall project timelines and provides SIRIM with early visibility into the operational environment.

## 7.3 Data Ingestion Confirmation Process

Data ingestion is a critical step in the migration process, as it validates that the correct datasets are available and accessible for downstream analytics and reporting. SIRIM is responsible for confirming the list of tables and queries to be ingested, ensuring alignment with business objectives and regulatory requirements. This confirmation must be completed before the Data Gateway is activated, as it directly influences the configuration and access policies applied to the gateway.

Enfrasys Solutions will coordinate closely with SIRIM’s designated data owners to ensure that all necessary queries and data relationships are well-understood. This collaborative approach mitigates the risk of data quality issues and ensures a smooth transition to operational use.

## 7.4 Migration Timeline and Key Activities

The following table details the migration timeline, key activities, responsible parties, and current status. This structured schedule provides transparency and accountability throughout the deployment process.

  
| No | Activities                                         | Planned Start      | Planned End        | Action By         | Status       |
|----|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| 1  | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by SIRIM    | Fri, 13-June-25    | Tues, 17-June-25   | Enfrasys, SIRIM   | Not-Started |
| 2  | Confirm on the table to be ingested                | Wed, 11-June-25    | Fri, 13-June-25    | SIRIM             | Not-Started |
| 3  | Create an Azure VM to establish Data Gateway        |                    |                    | Enfrasys          | Not-Started |


## 7.5 Responsibility Assignment

- **Enfrasys Solutions** is responsible for delivering the design documentation, provisioning the Azure VM, and configuring the Data Gateway.
- **SIRIM** is responsible for confirming the list of tables and queries to be ingested, in coordination with internal stakeholders.

This division of responsibilities ensures clear ownership and facilitates efficient project execution. Regular status updates and checkpoints will be conducted to track progress and address any emerging issues promptly.

The diagram illustrates a technical architecture involving Azure components and user access flow. 

1. **Subscription**: Represents the Azure subscription under which resources are managed. It is the foundational layer for resource organization and billing.

2. **WVD (Windows Virtual Desktop)**: This component is part of the subscription and provides virtual desktop infrastructure. External users connect to the WVD, which acts as a gateway for accessing resources.

3. **Fabric-RG (Resource Group)**: A logical container within the Azure subscription that holds related resources. It includes the SIRIM FABRIC component.

4. **SIRIM FABRIC**: This is a specific application or service hosted within the Fabric-RG. It is accessed by users through the WVD.

5. **Conditional Access**: This security layer ensures that only authorized SIRIM users can access the SIRIM FABRIC. It likely involves policies that evaluate user identity and compliance before granting access.

6. **External User**: Represents users outside the organization who connect to the WVD to access resources.

7. **SIRIM User**: Represents internal users who access the SIRIM FABRIC through conditional access policies.

The data flow begins with external users connecting to the WVD, which provides access to the SIRIM FABRIC within the Fabric-RG. Conditional Access policies are applied to ensure secure access for SIRIM users.

The diagram illustrates a network architecture involving Azure Virtual Networks (VNETs), Virtual Network Gateways, and VNET Peering. 

1. **SIRIM**: Represents an on-premises network connecting to Azure via a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN. This connection is established through a Virtual Network Gateway within Azure.

2. **Subscription**: Indicates the Azure subscription under which the resources are deployed.

3. **VNET (x.x.x.x/xx)**: Two separate VNETs are shown, each with a specific IP address range. These VNETs are part of the Azure infrastructure.

4. **Virtual Network Gateway**: Located within a GatewaySubnet, it facilitates the S2S VPN connection from the on-premises network to Azure.

5. **VNET Peering**: Connects the two VNETs, allowing resources within them to communicate with each other. This peering is bidirectional, enabling seamless data flow.

6. **Fabric-RG and Fabric-VNET**: Represents a resource group and VNET dedicated to a specific service or application, possibly related to Azure Fabric.

7. **Fabric Private Endpoint**: Located within a specific subnet, it provides secure access to Azure services without exposing them to the public internet.

8. **WVD (Windows Virtual Desktop)**: Deployed within one of the VNETs, allowing external users to access virtual desktops hosted in Azure.

9. **External User**: Connects to the WVD, indicating remote access capabilities for users outside the Azure environment.

The architecture ensures secure connectivity between on-premises and Azure resources, leveraging VPN and private endpoints for enhanced security and performance.

The diagram represents a data workflow architecture within the SIRIM FABRIC environment. It illustrates the flow of data from ingestion to visualization using Azure services.

1. **Data Ingestion**:
   - **TOPAZ**: Data is ingested from the TOPAZ system within the `SIRIM-BIGDATA-EDWH-RG` resource group.
   - **Data Factory**: Azure Data Factory is used to orchestrate the data ingestion process, moving data from TOPAZ to the Bronze layer.

2. **Data Lake Structure**:
   - **XX_Bronze_LK Tables**: The initial landing zone for raw data. Data is stored in its original format for further processing.
   - **XX_Silver_LK Tables**: Data is transformed and cleaned, moving to the Silver layer for more structured storage.
   - **XX_Gold_LK Tables**: The final layer where data is aggregated and optimized for analytics and reporting.

3. **Data Processing**:
   - **Synapse Engineering**: Azure Synapse is used for advanced data processing and analytics, transforming data between the Silver and Gold layers.

4. **Identity Management**:
   - **identity_SM**: Represents identity and security management, ensuring data access is controlled and secure.

5. **Data Visualization**:
   - **Power BI**: Data from the Gold layer is connected via OneLake to Power BI for visualization and reporting.

6. **Integration**:
   - **OneLake**: Facilitates seamless data integration and connectivity between the Gold layer and Power BI.

This architecture leverages Azure services to create a robust data pipeline, ensuring efficient data processing, management, and visualization.

# KPJ Healthcare Microsoft 365 Migration Project Design Workshop

# 2.0 Executive Summary

## 2.1 Project Overview

KPJ Healthcare is undertaking a comprehensive migration to the Microsoft 365 platform to modernize its collaboration, communication, and productivity capabilities. This initiative encompasses the assessment of the current environment, the migration of users, policies, and configurations, and the introduction of new governance and security policies. The migration scope includes pre-migration planning, pilot migration phases, full production rollout, and post-migration support, with special attention to cross-tenant synchronization, administrative unit structuring, and Single Sign-On (SSO) application integration.

The primary objectives of this migration are to enhance operational efficiency, improve security posture, and ensure seamless user experience across the organization. Enfrasys Solutions will provide expert guidance and execution throughout the migration lifecycle, ensuring that KPJ Healthcare’s transition to Microsoft 365 is secure, compliant, and aligned with industry best practices.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

This Solution Design Document serves as the authoritative reference for the Microsoft 365 migration project. It details the architectural decisions, migration strategies, risk mitigation measures, and operational workflows that will govern the execution of the migration. The document provides a structured approach to migrating existing workloads, implementing new policies, and managing change across KPJ Healthcare’s digital landscape.

By consolidating design considerations and procedural guidelines, this document ensures that all stakeholders have a clear understanding of the migration’s technical scope, the rationale behind key decisions, and the expected outcomes. It establishes a foundation for effective collaboration between KPJ Healthcare and Enfrasys Solutions, supporting informed decision-making and consistent project delivery.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for KPJ Healthcare’s IT leadership, technical teams, business process owners, and project sponsors. It is also relevant to Enfrasys Solutions’ project managers, architects, and migration engineers who are responsible for planning, executing, and supporting the migration. The content is structured to provide both high-level context for executive stakeholders and detailed technical guidance for implementation teams, ensuring alignment and clarity throughout the project lifecycle.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides formal definitions and architectural context for the core Microsoft technologies and migration utilities that form the foundation of the KPJ Healthcare Microsoft 365 environment. Each technology is described in terms of its purpose, integration points, and operational responsibilities as they relate to KPJ Healthcare’s hybrid cloud and modern workplace strategy.

## 3.1 Microsoft 365

Microsoft 365 is a comprehensive, cloud-based productivity suite that integrates Office applications, collaboration tools, security solutions, and device management into a unified platform. It enables organizations to enhance communication, streamline workflows, and enforce security across users, devices, and data. Microsoft 365 is the central platform for KPJ Healthcare’s digital transformation, providing a consistent user experience and robust administrative controls.

Ongoing management and user support for Microsoft 365 shall be the responsibility of KPJ Healthcare’s IT teams. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration, tenant setup, and migration activities to ensure a secure and optimized deployment.

## 3.2 Exchange Online

Exchange Online is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade, cloud-hosted email and calendaring service. It offers secure email hosting, advanced threat protection, and seamless integration with Outlook and other Microsoft 365 applications. Exchange Online supports compliance requirements such as eDiscovery, retention policies, and data loss prevention.

For KPJ Healthcare, Exchange Online replaces legacy on-premises email systems, centralizing mailbox management and improving reliability. Enfrasys Solutions will perform the migration of mailboxes and configure Exchange Online to align with KPJ Healthcare’s operational requirements. Post-migration, KPJ Healthcare will manage user accounts, distribution lists, and day-to-day email administration.

## 3.3 SharePoint Online

SharePoint Online is a cloud-based collaboration and document management platform. It enables secure sharing, content management, workflow automation, and intranet portal capabilities. SharePoint Online integrates with Microsoft Teams, OneDrive for Business, and Power Platform to support advanced business processes.

KPJ Healthcare will leverage SharePoint Online for hospital-wide document repositories, team sites, and policy distribution. Enfrasys Solutions will configure site collections, migrate existing data, and establish governance policies. Ongoing site management and content lifecycle responsibilities will transition to KPJ Healthcare’s IT and business units.

## 3.4 OneDrive for Business

OneDrive for Business is Microsoft’s enterprise cloud storage solution for individual users. It provides secure file storage, synchronization across devices, and sharing capabilities, all under the control of organizational security policies. OneDrive for Business ensures that KPJ Healthcare staff can access their files from any location, supporting flexible and remote work scenarios.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure OneDrive for Business, set up security and compliance policies, and migrate user data. KPJ Healthcare will be responsible for ongoing support and user training.

## 3.5 Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams is a unified communication and collaboration platform that brings together chat, video meetings, file sharing, and application integration. Teams enhances productivity by centralizing conversations, meetings, and content in a single workspace, with deep integration across Microsoft 365.

KPJ Healthcare will utilize Microsoft Teams for both internal and cross-entity collaboration, including secure communication with JCORP users via cross-tenant synchronization. Enfrasys Solutions will configure Teams policies, enable cross-tenant access, and migrate existing Teams data. KPJ Healthcare will manage Teams lifecycle and governance post-migration.

## 3.6 Microsoft Intune

Microsoft Intune is a cloud-based endpoint management solution that enables organizations to manage devices, enforce security policies, and ensure compliance across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android platforms. Intune supports device enrollment, application deployment, and conditional access, integrating with Microsoft Defender for comprehensive endpoint protection.

Enfrasys Solutions will deploy Intune, configure device compliance policies, and onboard KPJ Healthcare’s endpoints and mobile devices. KPJ Healthcare will maintain device management, compliance monitoring, and support.

## 3.7 Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is an enterprise endpoint security platform designed to prevent, detect, investigate, and respond to advanced threats. # 5.0 Roles and Access

This section defines the administrative roles, access scopes, and responsibilities for KPJ Healthcare’s Microsoft 365 environment. ## 5.1 Microsoft 365 Group Creation Governance

Microsoft 365 Groups are a foundational element in Microsoft’s collaboration ecosystem, underpinning resources such as Teams, SharePoint sites, and Planner. Unrestricted group creation can lead to sprawl, security risks, and governance challenges. To address this, Enfrasys Solutions recommends implementing strict controls to restrict Microsoft 365 Group creation rights to a defined set of authorized users.

By limiting group creation, KPJ Healthcare ensures that only vetted personnel can initiate new Teams or SharePoint sites, reducing the risk of data leakage and ensuring compliance with internal policies. This governance model also enables a standardized request and approval process, providing clear audit trails and enhancing visibility across the organization’s collaboration landscape.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure these controls within Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory), ensuring that only members of a designated security group can create Microsoft 365 Groups. KPJ Healthcare is responsible for validating the authorized users and maintaining the membership of this group in accordance with organizational requirements.

## 5.2 Administrative Units and Delegated Administration

Administrative Units (AUs) in Entra ID are containers that allow organizations to delegate administrative permissions over subsets of users, groups, and devices. This approach supports the principle of least privilege, ensuring that branch-level administrators (HOS IT Admins) can manage only the resources relevant to their hospital, while KPJ HQ Admins retain global oversight.

Enfrasys Solutions will establish a two-tiered administrative model:

- **KPJ HQ Admins** are assigned global administrative rights, enabling them to manage tenant-wide settings, enforce policies, and oversee all users, groups, and devices across KPJ Healthcare.
- **HOS IT Admins** are assigned administrative rights scoped to their respective hospital’s Administrative Unit, allowing them to manage users, groups, and devices within their own hospital, but without access to tenant-wide resources or policy management.

This structure ensures operational autonomy for hospital IT teams while maintaining centralized governance and compliance. It also supports scalability and simplifies onboarding of new hospitals or units.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the comprehensive deployment and migration approach for KPJ Healthcare’s Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migration. The strategy encompasses migration limitations, detailed phase breakdowns, wave scheduling, activity timelines, and explicit role responsibilities to ensure a seamless transition with minimal business disruption.

## 7.1 Migration Limitations

A successful migration requires a clear understanding of inherent limitations and their mitigations. KPJ Healthcare’s migration involves multiple Microsoft 365 workloads, each with specific constraints. Enfrasys Solutions has identified these limitations to proactively address user experience issues and operational risks. For example, certain workloads such as Microsoft Forms, SharePoint shared links, and Power Automate flows are not natively transferable between tenants, necessitating manual intervention or user action post-migration.

These limitations have direct implications for end-user readiness, IT support, and business continuity. Enfrasys Solutions will provide targeted communication and technical workarounds to minimize impact. KPJ Healthcare must ensure that users are informed about required post-migration actions, such as recreating sharing links or reattaching PST files. This collaborative approach is essential to maintain productivity and data integrity throughout the migration process.

**Key limitations and mitigations include:**

- Microsoft Forms: Forms themselves cannot be migrated; only results are transferable. Users will need to recreate forms in the target tenant.
- Microsoft Teams: Meeting links may break and require temporary policy changes to facilitate access.
- Endpoint Devices: Cached credentials may prevent re-sign-in; a script will be deployed to clear cache.
- SharePoint/OneDrive: Shared links and external permissions will not persist; users must recreate these after migration.
- Exchange Online: Client-side mail rules and PST file associations are not migrated and require user action.
- Power Automate/Power Apps: Flows and apps must be rebuilt in the new tenant.

**Detailed Limitation Matrix:**

  
| Workload                | Description                                                                 | Mitigation                                                        |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Microsoft Form          | Forms not migrated; only results are transferred                            | Users must recreate forms in the new tenant                       |
| Microsoft Teams         | Meeting links may be inaccessible post-migration                            | Temporary policy: “Who can bypass the lobby” set to “Everyone”    |
| Endpoint                | Device sign-in issues due to cached credentials                             | Script deployment to clear endpoint cache                         |
| SharePoint/OneDrive     | Shared links and external permissions not migrated                          | Users must recreate links and permissions                         |
| Power Automate/PowerApps| Flows/apps connected to old tenant resources                                | Identify and rebuild in new tenant                                |
| Exchange Online         | Mail rules and PST file associations not migrated                           | Users must recreate rules and reattach PST files                  |
| SharePoint              | Custom sites not migrated (e.g., KPJ Buzz)                                  | Manual reconfiguration required                                   |
| Microsoft Teams         | Stream/OneDrive meeting recordings access issues                            | Users must re-share recordings                                    |

# 8.0 Appendix

## 8.1 Introduction/Prerequisites

Quest On-Demand Migration is a leading SaaS-based migration solution widely utilized for Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations. It supports Exchange Online, OneDrive, Teams, and SharePoint migrations, but like all migration tools, it has specific limitations and boundaries that must be considered during planning and execution. Understanding these constraints is critical to ensuring a smooth migration for KPJ Healthcare and to avoid unexpected issues or unsupported scenarios.

Migration boundaries are often dictated by Microsoft APIs, platform capabilities, and third-party tool limitations. Enfrasys Solutions recommends that KPJ Healthcare reviews all relevant limitations, unsupported features, and boundaries prior to migration cutover. This section provides a comprehensive listing of Quest On-Demand’s current limitations, extracted from the latest product documentation and Microsoft sources, and includes direct links to official references for further detail.

## 8.2 Limits and Boundaries

### Quest On-Demand Limitation (Exchange)

Quest On-Demand Migration for Exchange supports most mailbox types and content, but there are notable exclusions and caveats. For example, migration of messages inside the mailbox root folder (TIS / Top of Information Store) is not supported, calendar processing settings for resource mailboxes are not migrated, and PST personal archives require a separate migration solution. Additionally, client-specific settings such as Outlook customizations or user-defined fields are not migrated. It is essential for KPJ Healthcare to understand these boundaries to set proper expectations for end-users and IT staff.

The following table summarizes the supported and unsupported Exchange objects and features:

| User mailbox             | ✔       |          |
| Shared mailbox           | ✔       |          |
| Distribution Group       | ✔       |          |
| Microsoft 365 Groups     | ✔       |          |
| Resource mailbox         | ✔       | e.g. conference rooms, equipment |
| Inbox                    | ✔       |          |
| Folders                  | ✔       |          |
| Email                    | ✔       | Migration of messages inside the mailbox root folder (TIS / Top of Information Store) is not supported. |
| Calendars                | ✔       |          |

| Notes                    | ✔       |          |

| Folder Permissions       | ✔       |          |
| Public folders           | ✔       |          |
| Calendar acceptance status emails | ✔ |      |
| Resource calendar permissions     | ✔ |      |
| Calendar processing settings (for resource mailboxes like rooms and equipment mailboxes) | ✖ | |
| Personal distribution lists       | ✔ |      |
| Personal contacts                | ✔ |      |

| Delivery Status Notifications (DSN) | ✔   |  |

### Quest On-Demand Limitation (OneDrive)

Quest On-Demand Migration for OneDrive provides robust support for documents, permissions, and version history, but does not support legal holds, retention labels, Microsoft Information Protection policies, or Microsoft public preview features. Power Platform integrations and SharePoint lists or subsites added to a user's OneDrive are also not migrated. If you rename a tab in the source team and then re-migrate, the renamed tab will be migrated. The target will then have two tabs, one with the old name and one with the new name. Whiteboard tabs are migrated if the Whiteboard files, in the OneDrive of the Whiteboard creator, is pre-migrated to the target tenant.
