Aliuddin, Norhanieyati Binti Norhaizat, Zaidie @ Mohd Zaidie Bin Adilai, Professor Madya TS Dr Mohd Hanafi Bin Ahmad Hijazi |

This mapping ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah maintains a secure and well-governed environment for analytics and reporting, with clear accountability for each workspace and role.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section outlines the platform architecture, workflow designs, and naming conventions that will underpin Universiti Malaysia Sabah's (UMS) implementation of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI for advanced analytics and machine learning. The following subsections detail the end-to-end data workflow, machine learning integration, and the standards for resource organization.

## 6.1 Data Workflow (ETL, Lakehouse Staging)

A robust data workflow is essential for ensuring the integrity, scalability, and efficiency of analytics platforms. Microsoft Fabric’s Lakehouse architecture, combined with Azure Data Factory, provides a modern approach to Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) processes. This workflow is designed to ingest, cleanse, transform, and model data, enabling UMS to unlock actionable insights efficiently.

The data journey begins with ingestion from the UMS Staging Area, specifically a Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse. Azure Data Factory orchestrates the data extraction, moving it into the Bronze Lakehouse tables, which serve as the raw data landing zone. The data then undergoes cleansing and transformation in the Silver Lakehouse, leveraging Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. This ensures that only high-quality, structured data advances to the Gold Lakehouse, where it is further refined and enriched for analytics and machine learning use cases.

The final stage involves connecting the Gold Lakehouse to Power BI via OneLake, enabling seamless data visualization and reporting. This architecture ensures data lineage, governance, and scalability, supporting both current and future analytical needs at UMS. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for documenting the detailed workflow design, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall validate its alignment with business requirements and regulatory standards.

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data workflow, highlighting each stage and data movement within the UMS Fabric environment.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: UMS Data Workflow Architecture – from SQL Server ingestion to Power BI via Fabric Lakehouse layers.

The table below summarizes the key design considerations and workload types for each stage of the data workflow.

| ID   | Description                                                                                          | Workload Type    |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                 | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                     | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                    | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold). | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.          | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.               | Power BI         |

## 6.2 Machine Learning Workflow (AutoML, Manual ML)

Microsoft Fabric integrates advanced machine learning capabilities, allowing organizations to operationalize artificial intelligence within their analytics platform. Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) and manual machine learning workflows are both supported, catering to varying levels of data science expertise and project requirements. AutoML simplifies the process by automatically selecting, training, and tuning models, while manual ML provides flexibility for custom feature engineering and algorithm optimization using Fabric Notebooks.

In the UMS context, the machine learning workflow begins with cleansed data from the Silver Lakehouse. AutoML experiments are conducted to automatically identify the best classification models, particularly useful for scenarios such as predicting student risk profiles (e.g., at risk vs. not at risk). The results are scored and evaluated using Notebooks, with outputs stored in the Gold Lakehouse for consistency and traceability. Manual ML workflows complement this by allowing data scientists to build, tune, and optimize models directly, ensuring that unique UMS requirements are addressed.

All trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, supporting lifecycle management and versioning. Scored results, predictions, and performance metrics are stored centrally, and Power BI connects to these results for advanced visualization and reporting. This integrated workflow accelerates AI adoption, enhances transparency, and ensures that machine learning outcomes are both explainable and actionable for UMS stakeholders. Enfrasys Solutions is tasked with documenting the workflow design, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for validating alignment with institutional objectives.

The following diagram depicts the machine learning workflow, illustrating the flow from data preparation to model deployment and reporting.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: UMS Machine Learning Workflow – integrating AutoML, manual ML, and Power BI reporting.

The table below details the design considerations and workload types for the AutoML and manual machine learning processes.

| ID   | Description                                                                                                          | Workloads type    |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering  |
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science      |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science      |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science      |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering  |
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering  |
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI          |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                               | Power BI          |

## 6.3 Resource Organization (Naming Convention)

A consistent and descriptive naming convention is critical for managing resources within Microsoft Fabric, ensuring clarity, traceability, and ease of administration. Enfrasys recommends adopting a standardized pattern for all Fabric items, following the structure: `<Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>`. This approach allows for immediate recognition of the resource’s purpose, environment, and associated business unit, reducing operational risk and supporting effective governance.

For example, Fabric Capacity resources are named to reflect their environment and purpose (e.g., `stagingareadevcapacity01`), while Workspaces and Lakehouses are named to indicate their business domain and stage (e.g., `StudentAffairs_dev_WS`, `StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK`). Pipelines, Dataflows, Semantic Models, and Reports follow similar conventions, ensuring that all stakeholders can quickly identify and manage assets across development, testing, and production environments.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for documenting and implementing the naming standards within the Fabric environment. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall review and validate these conventions to ensure they align with institutional nomenclature and operational practices.

The table below outlines the recommended naming conventions for key Fabric resources.

| No. | Item in Fabric    | Naming <Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>           |
|-----|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity   | stagingareadevcapacity01                                         |
| 2   | Workspace         | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                                            |
| 3   | Lakehouse         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK StudentAffairs_Silver_LK Etc…           |
| 4   | Dataflow          | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF Etc.. |
| 5   | Semantic Model    | StudentAffairs_ StudentPerformance_SM                            |
| 6   | Pipeline          | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL Etc..                              |
| 7   | Report            | StudentAffairs_ StudentPerformance_Report                        |

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the recommended approach for deploying and migrating the new data platform solution for Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The deployment and migration strategy is designed to ensure a controlled, auditable, and low-risk transition to the new Microsoft Fabric-based architecture.

## 7.1 Deployment Timeline

A well-structured deployment timeline is essential for minimizing disruption to business operations and ensuring all stakeholders are aligned throughout the process. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a phased implementation, beginning with foundational environment setup and progressing through to migration of critical data components. Each phase is sequenced to allow for validation and sign-off before proceeding to subsequent steps, reducing the risk of unforeseen issues.

The deployment will commence upon formal approval of the Solution Design Document. Key milestones include the provisioning of new infrastructure by Universiti Malaysia Sabah, setup of the Microsoft Fabric environment by Enfrasys Solutions, and the installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) to facilitate secure hybrid data connectivity. This structured approach ensures that all technical prerequisites are met, and that Universiti Malaysia Sabah retains full visibility and control over the migration process.

Enfrasys Solutions will lead all deployment activities, leveraging its expertise in Microsoft cloud and data platforms. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for providing timely access to infrastructure and data sources, as well as confirming readiness of any on-premises resources required for migration.

## 7.2 Migration Activities

Migration activities are carefully orchestrated to ensure data integrity, security, and operational continuity. The migration process begins with the delivery and review of the Solution Design Document, followed by the confirmation of the new staging area database that will serve as the data warehouse copy. Once the staging environment is validated, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the setup of the Microsoft Fabric environment, ensuring all necessary configurations and security controls are in place.

The installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway is a critical step, as it enables secure, reliable data transfer between Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s on-premises systems and the Microsoft Fabric environment. Enfrasys Solutions will coordinate closely with Universiti Malaysia Sabah IT personnel to ensure the gateway is deployed according to best practices and organizational security standards. All activities will be tracked, with clear ownership and status reporting, to provide full transparency and accountability throughout the migration.

The following table summarizes the key deployment and migration activities, responsible parties, and current status:

| No. | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks |
|-----|------------|--------------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started | |
| 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started | |
| 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started | |
| 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started | |

This structured approach ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s migration to the new platform is executed efficiently, with clear accountability and minimal risk to ongoing operations.

slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides an executive overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI and Microsoft Fabric solution design, outlining the project’s scope, objectives, and intended outcomes. It also clarifies the purpose and audience of this Solution Design Document.

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has embarked on a strategic initiative to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence capabilities. The primary scope of this project is to design and implement a comprehensive data workflow that spans from raw data ingestion through transformation, advanced analytics, and visualization, leveraging the Microsoft Fabric platform. Key objectives include:

- Establishing a robust Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored for UMS’s organizational requirements.
- Developing an end-to-end ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipeline to automate and streamline data integration processes.
- Implementing machine learning processes to support advanced data science and predictive analytics use cases.
- Integrating Power BI for interactive, business-aligned analytics and reporting, enabling data-driven decision-making across the university.

The solution incorporates Microsoft Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and embedded Data Science capabilities for machine learning applications. This approach ensures that UMS’s cloud adoption strategy is fully aligned with the latest Microsoft Fabric services, providing a scalable, secure, and future-ready analytics environment.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The purpose of this Solution Design Document is to formally capture the architecture, design decisions, workflows, and technology components that underpin the UMS Power BI and Microsoft Fabric implementation. This document serves as the authoritative reference for all stakeholders, detailing the technical and operational blueprint required to achieve the project’s objectives. It ensures alignment between business requirements, technology strategy, and implementation actions, and provides a foundation for governance, risk management, and future enhancements.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for a diverse audience involved in the planning, implementation, and ongoing management of the UMS Power BI and Microsoft Fabric solution. The primary readers include:

- UMS IT management and technical teams responsible for solution adoption, integration, and support.
- UMS business stakeholders and analytics users who will leverage the platform for reporting and decision-making.
- The Enfrasys Solutions implementation team, accountable for delivering the architecture, configuration, and migration activities as described herein.

By addressing the needs of both technical and business stakeholders, this document facilitates clear communication, shared understanding, and coordinated execution throughout the project lifecycle.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides an authoritative overview of the core Microsoft technologies forming the foundation of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data platform solution. Each technology is defined, its role in the overall architecture is detailed, and responsibilities are clearly delineated between Enfrasys Solutions (as solution architect and implementer) and UMS (as the consumer and operator).

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform that unifies data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Fabric brings together capabilities from Power BI, Azure Synapse, and Azure Data Factory, providing a seamless experience for data professionals and business users. It is designed to simplify data workflows, enhance collaboration, and accelerate time-to-insight for organizations.

Within the UMS solution, Microsoft Fabric serves as the central platform orchestrating the entire data lifecycle—from ingestion and transformation to machine learning and visualization. Fabric workspaces are provisioned to encapsulate datasets, pipelines, notebooks, and models, ensuring logical separation and secure management of resources. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for architecting, configuring, and deploying the Fabric environment, including best practice workspace governance and security. UMS will operate, maintain, and extend the solution, leveraging Fabric’s self-service capabilities for ongoing analytics and reporting.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s industry-leading business intelligence and data visualization service. It enables users to connect to a wide range of data sources, build interactive reports and dashboards, and share insights across the organization. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric, supporting direct access to curated data in OneLake and semantic models for real-time analytics.

In the UMS architecture, Power BI is the primary tool for business-aligned analytics and data visualization. It connects directly to the semantic model hosted within Fabric, allowing UMS stakeholders to explore, analyze, and present data insights securely. Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial Power BI integration, establish workspace access controls, and provide enablement for UMS users. Ongoing report creation, data modeling, and dashboard management will be the responsibility of UMS’s analytics and business teams.

## 3.3 Fabric Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory is the data integration and orchestration service within Microsoft Fabric, built on the proven capabilities of Azure Data Factory. It enables organizations to ingest, prepare, transform, and orchestrate data flows across hybrid and cloud environments. Data Factory supports a wide range of connectors, robust ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, and advanced data movement scenarios.

For UMS, Fabric Data Factory is used to automate the ingestion of data from the on-premises Microsoft SQL Server data warehouse into the Fabric platform. It manages the flow of data through the bronze, silver, and gold lakehouse layers, ensuring data quality and lineage. Enfrasys Solutions will design and implement the ETL pipelines, set up data movement schedules, and validate data integrity. UMS will monitor pipeline executions and manage ongoing data integration requirements.

## 3.4 Fabric Synapse

Fabric Synapse provides advanced data analytics and big data processing capabilities within the Fabric ecosystem. It combines the power of Apache Spark, data engineering, and data exploration tools, enabling large-scale data processing, transformation, and analysis. Synapse supports both code-first and low-code experiences, empowering data engineers and scientists to work efficiently.

In the UMS solution, Fabric Synapse is leveraged for complex data transformations, data cleansing, and preparation of datasets for downstream analytics and machine learning. It is also used for notebook-based development and interactive data exploration. Enfrasys Solutions will architect the data engineering workflows and implement the necessary Synapse components, while UMS data professionals will use these tools for ongoing data preparation and advanced analytics.

## 3.5 OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified, enterprise-grade data lake storage solution. It provides a single, secure location for all organizational data, supporting both structured and unstructured datasets. OneLake is deeply integrated with all Fabric workloads, enabling seamless data access, governance, and sharing across analytics, data science, and business intelligence use cases.

For UMS, OneLake acts as the central repository for all ingested, processed, and curated data. It stores raw (bronze), cleansed (silver), and business-ready (gold) lakehouse tables, ensuring data consistency and accessibility. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for configuring OneLake storage, implementing data security policies, and optimizing storage tiers. UMS will manage data lifecycle, access controls, and data sharing within the organization.

## 3.6 Data Science and AutoML

Data Science and AutoML (Automated Machine Learning) capabilities in Microsoft Fabric empower organizations to build, train, and operationalize machine learning models at scale. Fabric provides integrated notebooks, AutoML experiments, and model management tools, supporting both code-first and automated approaches for predictive analytics.

In the UMS solution, Data Science and AutoML are used to conduct machine learning experiments on cleansed data from the silver lakehouse. Both manual (notebook-based) and automated (AutoML) modeling approaches are supported, with results registered in the Fabric Model Registry and scored outputs stored in the gold lakehouse. Enfrasys Solutions will enable the data science environment, establish model lifecycle management processes, and provide initial training. UMS data scientists and analysts will develop, deploy, and maintain machine learning models to address business challenges.

## 3.7 On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure bridge that facilitates connectivity between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Fabric and Power BI. It allows cloud-based workloads to access and refresh data from on-premises databases without exposing the internal network to inbound connections, ensuring secure data transfer via outbound HTTPS.

For UMS, the OPDG is installed on a dedicated virtual machine within the campus network. It enables Fabric Data Factory to securely ingest data from the on-premises Microsoft SQL Server data warehouse. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the installation, configuration, and validation of the OPDG, including network security group (NSG) rule implementation. UMS will monitor gateway health, manage credentials, and ensure high availability for ongoing data integration.

## 3.8 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, conditional access, and identity governance for users, applications, and resources. Entra ID is a foundational security component for all Microsoft cloud services, including Fabric and Power BI.

In the UMS solution, Entra ID enforces authentication and conditional access policies for all users accessing Fabric resources. It integrates with the organization’s user directory, supports multi-factor authentication, and enables granular access controls to protect sensitive data. Enfrasys Solutions will design and implement the Entra ID integration, configure conditional access policies, and document best practices. UMS will administer user identities, manage access assignments, and monitor security events.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the comprehensive network and security architecture designed for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), focusing on robust access control, secure data bridging, and strict outbound security enforcement. The design leverages Microsoft’s best practices and aligns with UMS’s operational requirements to ensure data protection, regulatory compliance, and seamless user experience.

## 4.1 Conditional Access & MFA

Conditional Access is a critical capability within Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory). It enables organizations to automate access control decisions based on user, location, device, and application risk, thereby reducing the attack surface and enforcing security policies dynamically. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an essential layer of security by requiring users to provide multiple forms of verification before accessing sensitive resources.

For UMS, Enfrasys Solutions has designed an access control framework that leverages tenant-wide MFA enforcement due to current licensing constraints. While Conditional Access policies provide granular control over cloud resource access, UMS’s current Entra ID licensing (Free tier) does not support advanced Conditional Access features. Therefore, MFA is enforced at the tenant level to ensure all users undergo additional verification, mitigating risks associated with credential compromise and unauthorized access.

The architecture ensures that every authentication attempt to Microsoft Fabric and related services is evaluated for MFA requirements. Users are prompted for secondary authentication, reducing the likelihood of unauthorized access even if primary credentials are compromised. This approach, while lacking some advanced Conditional Access capabilities (such as location or device-based policies), provides a strong baseline security posture for UMS. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration and enforcement of MFA, while UMS will maintain and monitor the policy for ongoing compliance.

The following diagram illustrates how user authentication attempts are evaluated and enforced through Entra ID’s security controls, ensuring that only authorized users gain access to Microsoft Fabric resources.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Conditional Access and MFA Enforcement Workflow

The design decisions for Conditional Access and MFA enforcement are summarized below:

| No. | Conditional Access |
|-----|-------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment |

Limitations:
- Advanced Conditional Access policies (e.g., device or location-based controls) are unavailable due to licensing.
- Private Link integration is deferred for future consideration.
- Additional licensing (Entra ID P1/P2) is required to unlock more granular Conditional Access capabilities.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial MFA enforcement and Conditional Access policies. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing monitoring, user management, and future licensing upgrades as required.

## 4.2 Data Gateway & VM Design

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft component that acts as a secure bridge between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, and Azure Data Explorer. It enables secure data transfer without exposing internal resources to the public internet, leveraging outbound-only connections and strong encryption.

For UMS, the OPDG will be deployed on a dedicated virtual machine (VM) within the on-premises environment. This VM will facilitate secure, outbound data flows from the UMS staging area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) to Microsoft Fabric, ensuring that sensitive data is never exposed via inbound firewall rules. The gateway agent authenticates with Microsoft cloud services using outbound HTTPS connections, eliminating the need for complex perimeter firewall changes.

This architecture provides several operational and security benefits:
- Data remains protected within the UMS network, with no inbound ports required.
- All data transfers are encrypted using SSL/TLS, ensuring confidentiality and integrity.
- The gateway VM can be centrally managed, monitored, and updated by UMS IT administrators.
- The design is scalable and can be extended to support additional data sources in the future.

Enfrasys Solutions will perform the initial deployment and configuration of the OPDG and its underlying VM. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing operation, maintenance, and monitoring of the gateway infrastructure.

The following diagram depicts the secure data flow between the on-premises data warehouse, the OPDG, and Microsoft Fabric:

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 2: OPDG Data Flow Architecture

The recommended VM specifications for hosting the OPDG are as follows:

| Component | Specification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework | Version 4.8 |
| vCPU | 8 cores |
| RAM | Minimum 8 GB |

These specifications ensure optimal performance, reliability, and compatibility with the latest Microsoft gateway software.

## 4.3 Outbound Security Rules

Strict outbound security rules are essential to ensure that the OPDG VM can communicate only with approved Microsoft cloud endpoints while minimizing the risk of data exfiltration or unauthorized access. Enfrasys Solutions has designed a set of Azure Network Security Group (NSG) rules that explicitly allow outbound traffic required for gateway operation, authentication, and connectivity verification.

Each rule is crafted to fulfill a specific operational need:
- **Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services**: Permits outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) traffic to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core service domains. This is necessary for secure data transfer and service interaction.
- **Allow_OPDG_Authentication**: Enables outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) traffic to Microsoft Entra ID and authentication endpoints. This allows the gateway to perform identity verification, token retrieval, and secure session establishment.
- **Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test**: Allows outbound HTTP (TCP 80) traffic to Microsoft’s network connectivity status endpoint, supporting troubleshooting and service availability checks.

These rules ensure that the gateway VM is restricted to only the minimum required network access, significantly reducing the attack surface and aligning with Azure security best practices.

Enfrasys Solutions will implement the initial NSG configuration. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing review, monitoring, and adjustment of these rules as operational needs evolve.

The outbound security rules are detailed below:

| Name | Priority | Source | Source Ports | Destination | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services | 130 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443 | TCP | Allow |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication | 140 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443 | TCP | Allow |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160 | VM Private IP Addresses | * | *.msftncsi.com | 80 | TCP | Allow |

This layered security approach ensures that UMS’s data integration with Microsoft Fabric is both secure and operationally resilient.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section defines the roles, responsibilities, and access control model for Microsoft Fabric workspaces within Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). It details the mapping of workspace roles to UMS personnel, clarifies the division of responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS, and establishes the foundation for secure and effective workspace administration.

## 5.1 Access Control Model Overview

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Its security and governance are enforced through a robust role-based access control (RBAC) model, ensuring that only authorized users can access, manage, or interact with data assets. 

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a clear segregation of duties within Fabric workspaces to minimize risks, enforce the principle of least privilege, and streamline operational workflows. During the initial deployment and configuration phase, Enfrasys Solutions will provision and assign critical administrative roles to ensure a secure baseline. Upon successful handover, Universiti Malaysia Sabah will assume responsibility for ongoing administration, including the assignment and management of workspace roles.

The RBAC model in Fabric workspaces provides granular permissions, allowing UMS to designate specific personnel for administrative, contributor, and viewer responsibilities. This model not only supports compliance with internal governance policies but also enhances auditability and operational efficiency.

## 5.2 Role Definitions and Assignment Rationale

Workspace roles in Microsoft Fabric are designed to align with typical data and analytics team functions:

- **Workspace Admin:** This role possesses full control over workspace configuration, dataset management, and access provisioning. Assigning this role to senior data engineers and analytics leaders ensures that only qualified personnel can perform critical administrative tasks.
- **Workspace Contributor:** Contributors are empowered to create, edit, and manage content within the workspace but do not have permissions to alter workspace-level settings or assign roles. This role is suitable for operational data engineers and business user administrators who are responsible for developing and maintaining data products.
- **Workspace Viewer:** Viewers have read-only access, enabling stakeholders, analysts, and project directors to consume reports and dashboards without the risk of unintentional changes to data or configurations.

Enfrasys Solutions will assign initial Workspace Admin and Contributor roles to designated UMS personnel during deployment. These assignments will be validated in collaboration with UMS to ensure alignment with organizational structure and project requirements. After deployment, UMS will manage role assignments, ensuring ongoing compliance with internal policies.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section details the technical platform architecture, naming standards, and machine learning workflow that underpin Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric implementation. Each design decision is made to ensure scalability, maintainability, and operational clarity for UMS’s data-driven initiatives.

## 6.1 Data Workflow Design

A robust data workflow is essential for transforming raw data into actionable insights. Microsoft Fabric provides an integrated analytics platform that unifies data movement, transformation, and visualization. At UMS, the data workflow is structured around a modern lakehouse architecture, leveraging Azure Data Factory for orchestration and Power BI for business intelligence.

The workflow begins with data ingestion from the UMS Staging Area, which is hosted on Microsoft SQL Server 2017. Azure Data Factory orchestrates the extraction, loading, and transformation (ETL/ELT) processes, ensuring reliable and repeatable data movement into the Fabric environment. Data is first landed in the Bronze Lakehouse layer, which serves as the immutable raw data repository. This approach preserves data fidelity and supports auditability.

Subsequent processing stages refine the data through Silver and Gold Lakehouse layers. The Silver layer focuses on cleansing and structuring, using Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. This ensures the data is accurate, consistent, and analytics-ready. The Gold layer contains business-curated, highly transformed data, optimized for reporting and advanced analytics. Integration with OneLake provides centralized, scalable storage, while identity management components enforce secure access.

Power BI connects directly to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake, enabling seamless data visualization and self-service analytics for UMS stakeholders. This structured workflow ensures data integrity, operational efficiency, and supports advanced analytics and machine learning use cases.

The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end data workflow, highlighting the movement from data ingestion to business intelligence reporting:

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: UMS Data Workflow Architecture – Ingestion, Lakehouse Layers, and Power BI Integration

The table below summarizes key workflow considerations and the associated technology components:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                     | Workload Type   |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                            | Data Factory    |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                           | Data Engineering|
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                                | Data Engineering|
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                               | Data Engineering|
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering|
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).     | Data Factory    |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science    |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                    | Power BI        |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                         | Power BI        |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the overall data workflow architecture, configuring Azure Data Factory pipelines, and establishing the initial lakehouse structure. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for data ownership, ongoing data quality monitoring, and operational management of data pipelines.

## 6.2 Naming Convention

Consistent and descriptive naming conventions are critical for managing and scaling resources within the Microsoft Fabric environment. Proper naming ensures clarity, reduces operational errors, and facilitates governance, especially as UMS’s data platform grows in complexity.

Enfrasys recommends adopting a structured naming pattern for all Fabric resources, following the format: `<Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>`. This approach embeds context, ownership, and function directly into resource names, making them easily identifiable by both technical and business users. For example, a Lakehouse storing bronze-level student affairs data would be named `StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK`, while a data pipeline for ingestion might be `StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL`.

Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall ensure strict adherence to these conventions for all new resources. Enfrasys Solutions will provide initial configuration and validation of naming standards during the rollout phase. Ongoing compliance and governance of resource naming will be the responsibility of UMS’s IT and data management teams.

The following table outlines the recommended naming conventions for key Fabric items:

| No. | Item in Fabric    | Naming <Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>              |
|-----|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity   | stagingareadevcapacity01                                            |
| 2   | Workspace         | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                                               |
| 3   | Lakehouse         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK, StudentAffairs_Silver_LK, etc.            |
| 4   | Dataflow          | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF, StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF, etc. |
| 5   | Semantic Model    | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_SM                                |
| 6   | Pipeline          | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL, etc.                                 |
| 7   | Report            | StudentAffairs_StudentPerformance_Report                            |

UMS must ensure that all Fabric resource names are unique, descriptive, and consistently follow the agreed structure. This will support automation, monitoring, and future platform expansion.

## 6.3 AutoML & Data Science Workflow

Advanced analytics and machine learning are integral to extracting maximum value from UMS’s data assets. Microsoft Fabric provides both AutoML and manual machine learning capabilities, enabling a flexible approach to model development and deployment. AutoML simplifies the process of building predictive models, while manual workflows using Fabric Notebooks allow for custom feature engineering, algorithm selection, and model optimization.

The data science workflow begins with cleansed data from the Silver Lakehouse, which serves as the input for both AutoML experiments and manual modeling. AutoML experiments automate model selection and tuning, while manual approaches leverage PySpark or Python notebooks for greater control and explainability. All trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, supporting lifecycle management, versioning, and reuse.

Scoring notebooks are used to apply trained models to new or unseen data, with results—such as predictions and performance metrics—stored in the Gold Lakehouse. This ensures a standardized repository for all modeled outputs, maintaining consistency across AutoML and manual ML processes. The Gold Lakehouse then feeds the Semantic Model, which is exposed to Power BI via OneLake for visualization and reporting.

The following diagram depicts the AutoML and data science workflow, illustrating the integration of data engineering, model training, and business intelligence:

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: UMS AutoML and Data Science Workflow – Model Training, Scoring, and Integration with Power BI

The table below summarizes key considerations for the AutoML and data science workflow:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                     | Workloads type  |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering|
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science    |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science    |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science    |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering|
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering|
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI        |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                         | Power BI        |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing the machine learning workflow, configuring the Fabric Model Registry, and developing initial notebook templates for model training and scoring. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for data selection, model development, validation, and ongoing management of the data science lifecycle.

This comprehensive platform design ensures UMS can efficiently manage data, enforce governance, and drive advanced analytics in a secure and scalable Microsoft Fabric environment.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the structured deployment and migration approach for Universiti Malaysia Sabah, detailing the coordinated activities required to operationalize the Microsoft Fabric solution. The approach is designed to ensure a seamless transition from design to implementation, with clear assignment of responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah.

## 7.1 Overview of Deployment and Migration Phases

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a phased deployment and migration strategy to minimize operational risks and ensure all stakeholders are aligned at each stage. The process begins with the formal delivery and review of the Solution Design Document, ensuring Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s requirements are fully captured and agreed upon before any technical implementation. This sign-off is critical to establish a shared understanding of the solution’s scope and architecture.

Following design approval, Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for confirming the availability and readiness of the new server environment, specifically the data warehouse copy designated as the Staging Area Database. This step is essential to guarantee that all required data sources are prepared for integration into the Fabric environment, preventing downstream delays and ensuring data integrity throughout the migration process.

## 7.2 Execution of Technical Deployment Steps

Once prerequisites are confirmed, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the setup of the Microsoft Fabric environment. This involves provisioning the necessary Fabric workspaces, configuring security and access controls, and establishing connectivity to required data sources. The Fabric environment setup is a critical foundation, as it enables subsequent data ingestion, transformation, and analytics workflows.

A key component of the deployment is the installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) within a designated virtual machine. This gateway acts as a secure conduit for data transfer between on-premises systems and Microsoft Fabric, ensuring compliance with Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s security and governance requirements. The installation and configuration of the OPDG will be a joint effort, with Enfrasys Solutions leading the technical execution and Universiti Malaysia Sabah providing necessary access and validation.

## 7.3 Activity Timeline and Responsibilities

The following table summarizes the planned activities, responsible parties, and current status for each deployment and migration task. Each activity has been clearly assigned to either Enfrasys Solutions, Universiti Malaysia Sabah, or both, to ensure accountability and transparency throughout the process.

| 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started |  |
| 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started |  |

This structured approach ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah and Enfrasys Solutions maintain clear communication and alignment at every stage of the deployment and migration process. By following this plan, the organization will achieve a secure, scalable, and well-governed Microsoft Fabric environment, ready to support advanced analytics and data-driven initiatives.

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. # UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI & Microsoft Fabric solution design, its purpose, and the intended readership for this document.

## 2.1 Project Overview

The Power BI & Microsoft Fabric project for Universiti Malaysia Sabah is designed to modernize and optimize the university’s data workflow, enabling a seamless transition from data ingestion through transformation to advanced analytics and visualization. The project scope encompasses the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored for UMS, the development of robust end-to-end Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipelines, and the integration of comprehensive machine learning processes. These components are strategically aligned to support UMS’s business objectives by enabling data-driven decision-making and enhancing analytical capabilities across the institution.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends leveraging the full suite of Microsoft Fabric services to realize these objectives. Fabric Data Factory will facilitate secure and scalable data integration and orchestration from multiple sources. Fabric Synapse will provide advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, ensuring that UMS can analyze large and complex datasets efficiently. The Data Science component will enable the application of machine learning models, supporting predictive analytics and business innovation. Power BI will serve as the visualization layer, delivering actionable insights to stakeholders through interactive dashboards and reports. This integrated approach ensures that UMS’s cloud adoption strategy is fully aligned with the latest Microsoft technologies, maximizing operational efficiency, scalability, and future readiness.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this Solution Design Document is to formally capture the architecture, design decisions, and implementation roadmap for the Power BI & Microsoft Fabric solution at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. It provides a detailed blueprint that outlines the technical approach, technology components, data workflows, and integration strategies recommended by Enfrasys Solutions. This document serves as a foundational reference for all project stakeholders, ensuring alignment on objectives, responsibilities, and expected outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This Solution Design Document is intended for the following audiences:

- Universiti Malaysia Sabah IT leadership and technical teams responsible for data infrastructure and analytics.
- UMS data engineering and analytics teams who will be involved in the development, management, and utilization of the Fabric and Power BI environment.
- Enfrasys Solutions consultants and implementation specialists overseeing the design, deployment, and support of the solution.
- Any other UMS stakeholders involved in governance, compliance, or strategic decision-making related to data and analytics modernization.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of the core technologies forming the foundation of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data analytics solution. Each technology is defined in the context of its role within the overall architecture, ensuring all stakeholders have a clear understanding of the solution’s components and their integration. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the following technology definitions and the rationale for their selection.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform designed to unify data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS environment. Fabric consolidates disparate data services into a cohesive ecosystem, streamlining data workflows and governance. For UMS, Microsoft Fabric serves as the central platform orchestrating data ingestion, transformation, machine learning, and visualization, thereby reducing operational complexity and accelerating time-to-insight.

### 3.1.1 Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-based data integration service within Microsoft Fabric that enables the creation, scheduling, and orchestration of data pipelines. It facilitates the movement and transformation of data from various sources, both on-premises and in the cloud. In the UMS solution, Data Factory is responsible for ingesting data from Microsoft SQL Server and orchestrating ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) workflows across the Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers. This ensures that UMS can automate data flows, enforce data quality, and maintain consistency across the analytics lifecycle.

### 3.1.2 Synapse

Fabric Synapse provides advanced analytics and big data processing capabilities, combining enterprise-grade data warehousing with Spark-based data engineering and data science. Synapse empowers UMS to perform large-scale data transformations, advanced analytics, and machine learning within the Fabric environment. By leveraging Synapse, UMS benefits from scalable compute resources, seamless integration with Lakehouse storage, and support for collaborative analytics across teams.

### 3.1.3 Lakehouse

The Lakehouse architecture within Microsoft Fabric merges the benefits of data lakes and data warehouses. It provides a unified, scalable repository for structured and unstructured data, supporting both analytical and operational workloads. For UMS, the Lakehouse is implemented in three logical layers: Bronze (raw data), Silver (cleansed data), and Gold (transformed and modeled data). This layered approach enables efficient data management, traceability, and supports advanced analytics and machine learning scenarios.

### 3.1.4 OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified data lake storage solution, designed to centralize and standardize data storage across the organization. OneLake provides a single, secure location for all data assets, enabling direct access from Fabric services and external analytics tools. UMS leverages OneLake to ensure data consistency, simplify data governance, and facilitate seamless integration with Power BI and other analytics components.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization platform. It enables users to connect to diverse data sources, build interactive reports, and share insights across the organization. Within the UMS solution, Power BI is tightly integrated with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, allowing business users and analysts to visualize data from the Gold Lakehouse layer. This integration supports real-time analytics, self-service reporting, and data-driven decision-making, ensuring that UMS stakeholders have timely access to actionable insights.

## 3.3 Dataflow Gen2

Dataflow Gen2 is an enhanced data preparation and transformation service within Microsoft Fabric. It allows users to design, automate, and manage data transformation workflows using a low-code/no-code interface. Dataflow Gen2 supports scalable data movement between Lakehouse layers (such as Bronze to Silver and Silver to Gold) and enables advanced cleansing, enrichment, and transformation tasks. For UMS, Dataflow Gen2 streamlines ETL processes, reduces manual intervention, and ensures data quality across the analytics pipeline.

## 3.4 Notebooks

Notebooks in Microsoft Fabric provide an interactive environment for data exploration, transformation, and advanced analytics using languages such as Python, PySpark, and SQL. Notebooks facilitate collaborative development, enabling data engineers and data scientists at UMS to perform custom data preparation, feature engineering, and model development. The use of notebooks ensures transparency, reproducibility, and flexibility in the machine learning lifecycle.

## 3.5 AutoML

AutoML (Automated Machine Learning) is a feature within Microsoft Fabric that automates the process of selecting, training, and tuning machine learning models. AutoML accelerates the development of predictive models by handling algorithm selection, hyperparameter optimization, and model evaluation. In the UMS context, AutoML is used to implement binary classification models for student risk prediction, supporting both automated and manual machine learning workflows. This approach empowers UMS to derive predictive insights from their data with minimal manual intervention while maintaining the option for custom modeling via notebooks.

## 3.6 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides authentication, authorization, and identity governance for users accessing Microsoft cloud resources. In the UMS solution, Entra ID secures access to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related services, enforcing organizational security policies and enabling seamless single sign-on experiences. Entra ID is also the enforcement point for Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), ensuring only authorized users can access sensitive data and analytics assets.

## 3.7 On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure bridge that facilitates data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services. The gateway is installed on a dedicated virtual machine within the UMS environment, enabling Fabric Data Factory and Power BI to access data stored in the Microsoft SQL Server data warehouse without exposing internal systems to the public internet. OPDG ensures secure, encrypted data movement, supports compliance requirements, and maintains data sovereignty for UMS.

## 3.8 Microsoft SQL Server

Microsoft SQL Server is a relational database management system widely used for transactional and analytical workloads. In the UMS architecture, SQL Server serves as the primary data warehouse and staging area for source data. Data is extracted from SQL Server using the On-Premises Data Gateway and ingested into Microsoft Fabric for further processing, transformation, and analytics. This approach leverages the robustness and reliability of SQL Server while enabling advanced analytics in the cloud.

## 3.9 Conditional Access and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Conditional Access is a security feature in Microsoft Entra ID that provides automated access control decisions based on user, device, location, and risk signals. It allows organizations to enforce policies such as requiring MFA, blocking access from untrusted locations, or granting access only to compliant devices. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an additional layer of security by requiring users to provide a second form of verification during sign-in. For UMS, Conditional Access and MFA are critical for protecting sensitive data and ensuring that only authorized users can access Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related services.

The following diagram illustrates the high-level authentication and access control workflow for Microsoft Fabric, demonstrating how Entra ID, Conditional Access, and MFA secure user access to analytics resources.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Authentication and Conditional Access Workflow for Microsoft Fabric

In this workflow, user authentication attempts are evaluated against Entra conditional access policies. Signals such as user identity, group membership, and network location are collected and assessed. Based on these signals, access is either granted or denied, and MFA may be enforced as an additional security measure. This process ensures that only users meeting UMS’s security requirements can interact with Microsoft Fabric and its integrated services.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the network and security architecture for the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric implementation. The design ensures secure, reliable connectivity between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric, while enforcing robust access controls and compliance with best practices.

## 4.1 Data Gateway & Connectivity

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a critical component in the UMS architecture. Microsoft’s On-Premises Data Gateway enables secure data transfer between on-premises data sources, such as Microsoft SQL Server, and cloud-based services like Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure Data Explorer. The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, eliminating the need for inbound firewall rules by establishing outbound connections to Microsoft endpoints over HTTPS.

For UMS, Enfrasys Solutions recommends deploying the OPDG agent within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) hosted in the on-premises environment. This VM is specifically sized to handle the anticipated data throughput and concurrency requirements, ensuring high availability and optimal performance for data refreshes and query operations. The gateway VM will connect to the UMS staging area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) and securely transmit data to Microsoft Fabric for analytics and reporting workloads.

The selection of VM specifications is informed by Microsoft’s best practices and Enfrasys’s experience with similar higher education deployments. The recommended configuration provides sufficient compute and memory resources to support multiple concurrent data operations, while maintaining compatibility with the OPDG software stack.

The following table summarizes the recommended VM specifications for the OPDG deployment:

| Component      | Specification                                      |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework | Version 4.8                                        |
| vCPU           | 8 cores                                            |
| RAM            | Minimum 8 GB                                       |

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial deployment and configuration of the OPDG VM, including installation of the gateway agent and integration with UMS’s on-premises SQL Server. Ongoing management and operational monitoring of the VM and gateway service will be transitioned to Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s IT team upon project completion.

The following diagram illustrates the data flow from the UMS on-premises data warehouse, through the OPDG, and into Microsoft Fabric. This architecture ensures that sensitive data remains protected within the UMS network, with only outbound, encrypted connections permitted.

Figure 1: Secure Data Flow from On-Premises SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via OPDG

## 4.2 Outbound Security Rules

Securing the OPDG VM’s network connectivity is paramount to prevent unauthorized access while enabling required communication with Microsoft cloud services. The OPDG operates exclusively over outbound connections, leveraging HTTPS (TCP port 443) for all data transfers and authentication processes. This approach aligns with modern security best practices, as it avoids exposing any inbound ports on the UMS network perimeter.

Enfrasys Solutions has defined a set of outbound network security group (NSG) rules to be applied to the OPDG VM. These rules are designed to:

- Permit only the minimum necessary outbound traffic to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services.
- Enable secure authentication with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory).
- Allow connectivity checks for troubleshooting and service availability.

The following table details the required outbound security rules for the OPDG VM:

| Name                       | Priority | Source                | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                           | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|----------------------------|----------|-----------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services  | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication  | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                      | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test | 160    | VM Private IP Addresses | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                        | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

Enfrasys Solutions will implement these NSG rules during the initial setup of the OPDG VM. Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s IT team will be responsible for ongoing review and maintenance of these security rules to ensure continued compliance and to accommodate any future changes in Microsoft service endpoints.

## 4.3 Conditional Access & MFA

Conditional Access is a core capability of Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) that enables organizations to enforce automated access control decisions based on user, location, device, and risk context. For UMS, Conditional Access policies are recommended to secure access to Microsoft Fabric and its integrated services.

However, due to current licensing constraints, Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s tenant is not eligible for advanced Conditional Access features (such as those requiring Entra ID P1 or P2). As a result, Enfrasys Solutions has enforced Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at the tenant level to provide an essential layer of identity protection for all users accessing Microsoft Fabric resources.

This approach ensures that every authentication attempt is subject to an additional verification step, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access due to credential compromise. While this configuration does not provide the full granularity of Conditional Access policies, it aligns with Microsoft security recommendations for tenants without premium Entra ID licenses.

The following diagram illustrates the access control workflow, where user authentication attempts are evaluated and MFA enforcement is applied before granting access to Microsoft Fabric:

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 2: Authentication and Access Control Workflow with MFA Enforcement

Enfrasys Solutions recommends that Universiti Malaysia Sabah periodically reviews its licensing posture and considers upgrading to Entra ID P1 or P2 to unlock advanced Conditional Access capabilities, such as location-based access, session controls, and risk-based policies.

The following table summarizes the recommended Conditional Access and MFA enforcement decisions:

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration of tenant-wide MFA and any Conditional Access policies that can be enabled within the current licensing constraints. Ongoing management, user support, and policy review will be the responsibility of Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s IT administrators.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section outlines the roles, permissions, and access control mechanisms for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) in the context of Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment. It details workspace role assignments, conditional access, and multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforcement to ensure secure and well-governed access to data and analytics resources.

## 5.1 Workspace Roles & Permissions

Microsoft Fabric workspaces are collaborative environments where users can develop, share, and manage data assets and analytics solutions. Each workspace supports role-based access control (RBAC), enabling granular assignment of permissions according to user responsibilities. Enfrasys Solutions recommends a structured mapping of workspace roles to UMS personnel, ensuring clear accountability and operational efficiency.

The assignment of roles such as Workspace Admin, Contributor, and Viewer is critical for maintaining proper segregation of duties and minimizing the risk of unauthorized access or unintentional changes. Workspace Admins are entrusted with full control over the workspace, including managing access and configurations. Contributors are empowered to create and modify content, supporting ongoing analytics development. Viewers, typically stakeholders and project leads, are granted read-only access to ensure data visibility without the risk of modification.

Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the initial configuration of workspace roles and permissions. Universiti Malaysia Sabah shall assume responsibility for ongoing user management, including periodic review and updates to role assignments as personnel or project requirements change. ## 5.2 Conditional Access & MFA

Conditional Access is a core capability of Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) that provides automated, policy-based access controls for cloud applications. It evaluates user sign-in attempts against a set of configurable conditions—such as user identity, group membership, device state, and network location—to enforce access requirements and reduce security risks. For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, access to Microsoft Fabric and related services is governed by tenant-level MFA enforcement. However, Enfrasys Solutions has designed the access workflow to leverage available controls, ensuring robust authentication and minimizing unauthorized access risks.

The user access flow begins with an authentication attempt to Microsoft Fabric. The request is evaluated against tenant-wide MFA policies, requiring users to complete additional verification steps. Upon successful authentication, users are granted access to Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, and other integrated services. This approach balances security with user experience, reducing the likelihood of unexpected login prompts while maintaining strong protection for sensitive data.
