# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section outlines the technical platform architecture, data and machine learning workflows, and naming conventions to be adopted for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric implementation. The design ensures robust, scalable, and secure data management, enabling advanced analytics and machine learning capabilities.

## 6.1 Data Workflow & ETL

A well-structured data workflow is critical for enabling UMS to transform raw operational data into actionable insights. Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, and business intelligence capabilities. In this architecture, data flows from the UMS staging area (Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) through various transformation stages within Fabric, leveraging Azure Data Factory for orchestration and OneLake for scalable storage.

The end-to-end data pipeline begins with the ingestion of raw data from SQL Server into the Bronze Lakehouse layer, which acts as the immutable source of truth. Data is then cleansed and transformed in the Silver Lakehouse, where advanced processing and data preparation occur. The Gold Lakehouse holds the final, analytics-ready data optimized for reporting and machine learning. Data movement between these layers is facilitated by Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint, ensuring traceability and governance.

Identity management is integrated throughout the workflow to ensure secure access and compliance. The final Gold layer is exposed to Power BI through OneLake, enabling seamless data visualization and business intelligence reporting. This layered approach enhances data quality, supports advanced analytics, and ensures operational efficiency for UMS.

The following diagram illustrates the data workflow architecture, highlighting each stage and the flow of data from ingestion to visualization.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: End-to-End Data Workflow from SQL Server to Power BI in Microsoft Fabric

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial setup and configuration of the data workflows, including pipeline orchestration, lakehouse structuring, and integration with OneLake and Power BI. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing data operations, monitoring, and maintenance.

Below are the key considerations for the data workflow:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                         | Workload Type    |
|------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                                | Data Factory     |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                               | Data Engineering |
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                                    | Data Engineering |
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                                   | Data Engineering |
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering |
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).         | Data Factory     |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science     |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                        | Power BI         |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                             | Power BI         |

## 6.2 Machine Learning Workflow

Microsoft Fabric provides an integrated environment for both automated and manual machine learning, enabling UMS to leverage advanced analytics for student performance prediction and other use cases. AutoML (Automated Machine Learning) streamlines the process of model selection and hyperparameter tuning, while manual ML via Fabric Notebooks enables data scientists to apply custom algorithms and feature engineering for greater control and accuracy.

The workflow begins with cleansed data from the Silver Lakehouse, which serves as the input for machine learning experiments. UMS can utilize AutoML to rapidly prototype models or employ manual ML approaches using Python or PySpark in Fabric Notebooks for more tailored solutions. Model training, evaluation, and optimization are performed within this environment, with results registered in the Fabric Model Registry for lifecycle management and versioning.

Scored outputs, predictions, and performance metrics are stored in the Gold Lakehouse, ensuring a standardized and auditable repository for all machine learning results. The Gold Lakehouse is then connected to the Semantic Model and visualized in Power BI, delivering actionable insights to stakeholders. This design supports both rapid experimentation and robust production deployment, aligning with UMS’s goal to predict student risk using binary classification algorithms.

The following diagram depicts the machine learning workflow, illustrating both AutoML and manual ML paths, and the integration with downstream analytics.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: AutoML and Manual Machine Learning Workflow in Microsoft Fabric

Enfrasys Solutions will implement the initial machine learning workflow, including the setup of AutoML experiments, Fabric Notebooks, and model registration processes. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will manage ongoing model training, evaluation, and operationalization.

Key considerations for the AutoML and manual ML workflow are summarized below:

| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science     |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science     |

| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering |
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI         |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                             | Power BI         |

## 6.3 Resource Organization & Naming Conventions

A consistent and logical naming convention is essential for managing resources efficiently, enabling automation, and ensuring compliance with best practices in large-scale analytics environments. Microsoft Fabric resources—including capacities, workspaces, lakehouses, dataflows, semantic models, pipelines, and reports—must be named in a way that reflects their purpose, ownership, and environment.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends adopting a structured naming pattern: `<Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>`. This approach improves discoverability, supports governance, and simplifies troubleshooting. For example, a workspace dedicated to student affairs development would be named `StudentAffairs_dev_WS`, while a dataflow moving data from the bronze to silver lakehouse would be named `StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF`.

Enfrasys Solutions will establish the initial naming standards, configure the resource hierarchy, and document the conventions. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for maintaining and adhering to these standards for all new resources and ongoing operations.

The following table details the recommended naming conventions for key Fabric items:

| No. | Item in Fabric    | Naming <Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>         |
|-----|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity   | stagingareadevcapacity01                                      |
| 2   | Workspace         | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                                         |
| 3   | Lakehouse         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK StudentAffairs_Silver_LK Etc…        |
| 4   | Dataflow          | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF Etc.. |
| 5   | Semantic Model    | StudentAffairs_ StudentPerformance_SM                         |
| 6   | Pipeline          | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL Etc..                           |
| 7   | Report            | StudentAffairs_ StudentPerformance_Report                     |

This structured approach ensures that Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s analytics environment remains organized, scalable, and aligned with industry best practices as the platform grows.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the structured deployment and migration approach recommended for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) as part of the Microsoft Fabric implementation. The approach ensures clarity of responsibilities, minimizes risk, and provides a clear timeline for each critical activity.

## 7.1 Overview of Deployment and Migration Phases

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a phased deployment and migration strategy to ensure that all components of the Microsoft Fabric environment are established in a controlled and auditable manner. This approach enables UMS to validate each stage, address issues proactively, and maintain business continuity throughout the process.

The deployment begins with the delivery and review of the Solution Design Document, followed by confirmation of the new staging area database server. Once these prerequisites are met, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the setup of the Fabric environment and the installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG). Each phase is designed to build upon the previous, ensuring that technical dependencies are respected and that UMS stakeholders are engaged at every critical decision point.

## 7.2 Roles and Responsibilities

Clear delineation of responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS is essential for a successful migration. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for all technical deployments, configuration of the Fabric environment, and guidance on best practices. UMS is responsible for internal approvals, resource provisioning (such as the staging area database server), and sign-off at key milestones. Collaborative activities, such as the installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway, require joint participation to ensure both technical and operational requirements are met.

## 7.3 Migration Activities and Timeline

The following table summarizes the key deployment and migration activities, the planned start dates, responsible parties, current status, and any relevant remarks. This structured timeline provides UMS with a transparent view of the project’s progression and highlights where active participation or sign-off is required.

| No | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks |
|----|------------|---------------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started |  |
| 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started |  |

## 7.4 Benefits of the Structured Approach

By following this structured deployment and migration approach, Universiti Malaysia Sabah will benefit from:

- Reduced risk of misconfiguration or oversight, as each phase includes validation and sign-off steps.
- Clear accountability, ensuring that both Enfrasys Solutions and UMS are aware of their responsibilities and deliverables.
- Improved communication and project transparency, with all stakeholders informed of progress and upcoming activities.
- A foundation for scalable and secure Microsoft Fabric operations, as technical dependencies are addressed in sequence.

This approach positions UMS for a smooth transition to the new environment, maximizing the value of the Microsoft Fabric platform while maintaining operational stability throughout the migration.

defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

## 2.1 Project Overview

Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) has embarked on a strategic initiative to modernize its data analytics and business intelligence capabilities by adopting Microsoft Fabric. The primary objective of this project is to design and implement a robust data workflow that encompasses data ingestion, transformation, and visualization, tailored to UMS’s diverse business requirements. This initiative will establish a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace, enabling UMS to leverage an end-to-end Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipeline, support advanced machine learning processes, and integrate Power BI for actionable business analytics.

The design is aligned with UMS’s cloud adoption strategy, ensuring that the solution fully utilizes the latest Microsoft Fabric services. This includes Fabric Data Factory for seamless data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and large-scale data processing, and Data Science capabilities to support machine learning applications. The implementation of this architecture will empower UMS to derive timely insights, enhance decision-making, and maintain a competitive edge through data-driven strategies.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

This Solution Design Document serves as the authoritative reference for the architecture, design decisions, and implementation approach for the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI deployment at Universiti Malaysia Sabah. It provides a comprehensive blueprint for the proposed data workflow, detailing the rationale behind each design choice and the anticipated benefits for UMS. The document outlines the technical and operational considerations necessary to ensure a secure, scalable, and maintainable analytics platform, and serves as the foundation for subsequent implementation, migration, and operational support activities.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This document is intended for the following audience groups:
- Universiti Malaysia Sabah IT leadership and technical teams responsible for data management, analytics, and cloud adoption.
- Enfrasys Solutions architects, consultants, and project delivery teams tasked with the design, implementation, and support of the Microsoft Fabric and Power BI solution.
- Project sponsors, decision-makers, and stakeholders overseeing the digital transformation and strategic analytics initiatives at Universiti Malaysia Sabah.

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of the core Microsoft technologies selected for the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) data platform solution. Each technology is defined, and its specific role within the proposed architecture is detailed. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the selection, configuration, and integration of these technologies to ensure optimal alignment with UMS’s business and analytics objectives.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated, end-to-end analytics platform designed to unify data movement, data engineering, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence within a single SaaS solution. Fabric consolidates multiple data services under one umbrella, providing a seamless experience for data ingestion, transformation, storage, machine learning, and visualization. Its unified workspace and governance model enable organizations to manage data assets efficiently and securely.

Within the UMS solution, Microsoft Fabric forms the foundational platform, orchestrating the entire data workflow from ingestion to analytics. It enables the creation of robust ETL pipelines, supports advanced analytics, and ensures secure data access and collaboration. By leveraging Fabric, UMS benefits from a scalable, cloud-native environment that accelerates time-to-insight and reduces operational complexity.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is a business analytics service by Microsoft that enables users to visualize data, share insights, and drive informed decision-making through interactive reports and dashboards. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, providing seamless access to curated datasets and semantic models.

In the UMS architecture, Power BI is the primary tool for data visualization and business intelligence. It connects directly to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake, allowing users to explore, model, and present data in an intuitive manner. This approach empowers UMS stakeholders with self-service analytics capabilities, fostering a data-driven culture across the institution.

## 3.3 Data Factory

Microsoft Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-based data integration and orchestration service that enables the creation, scheduling, and management of data pipelines. It supports the ingestion of data from diverse sources, transformation through dataflows and notebooks, and movement across different storage layers.

For UMS, Data Factory is responsible for orchestrating the end-to-end ETL process. It ingests data from the on-premises SQL Server staging area, loads it into the Bronze Lakehouse, and manages the transformation and movement of data through Silver and Gold layers. This ensures data is efficiently processed, cleansed, and made analytics-ready.

## 3.4 Synapse

Microsoft Fabric Synapse is an integrated analytics service that brings together big data and data warehousing capabilities. It enables large-scale data processing, advanced analytics, and real-time data exploration using familiar tools such as SQL and Spark.

In the UMS solution, Synapse is leveraged for advanced data engineering and analytics tasks, including data cleansing, transformation, and enrichment. It provides the computational power needed to process large datasets and supports the creation of refined analytical models, which are crucial for downstream machine learning and reporting activities.

## 3.5 OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified, enterprise-grade data lake storage solution. It provides a single, logical storage layer for all data assets, supporting both structured and unstructured data, with robust security and governance controls.

UMS utilizes OneLake to store all ingested, processed, and curated data. Data is organized into Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouses, representing raw, cleansed, and transformed datasets, respectively. This centralized approach simplifies data management, enhances discoverability, and ensures consistent access controls across the data lifecycle.

## 3.6 Data Gateway

The Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure bridge that facilitates data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Fabric and Power BI. The gateway ensures encrypted, reliable connectivity, enabling cloud-based analytics without compromising data security.

For UMS, the Data Gateway enables secure ingestion of data from the on-premises SQL Server into Microsoft Fabric. It is configured to comply with Azure networking best practices, ensuring only authorized and encrypted traffic flows between UMS’s environment and the cloud.

## 3.7 Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is a comprehensive identity and access management service that provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and conditional access policies for users and applications. Entra ID is integral to enforcing governance, compliance, and security across Microsoft cloud services.

In the UMS solution, Entra ID governs user access to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related services. Conditional Access policies are implemented to ensure that only authenticated and authorized users can access sensitive data and analytics resources, including support for external collaborators where necessary.

## 3.8 AutoML

AutoML (Automated Machine Learning) in Microsoft Fabric enables users to automatically build, train, and deploy machine learning models with minimal manual intervention. It leverages advanced algorithms to select features, optimize models, and evaluate performance, accelerating the development of predictive analytics solutions.

UMS leverages AutoML to demonstrate machine learning processes on cleansed datasets from the Silver Lakehouse. The results are stored in the Gold Lakehouse for further analysis and visualization, supporting advanced analytics use cases such as forecasting and classification.

## 3.9 Notebooks

Notebooks in Microsoft Fabric provide an interactive, code-first environment for data exploration, transformation, and machine learning. Supporting languages such as Python and PySpark, notebooks enable data scientists and engineers to perform custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model evaluation.

Within the UMS architecture, notebooks are used for manual machine learning workflows, allowing deeper customization and control over the modeling process. Outputs from these notebooks are registered in the Fabric Model Registry and stored in the Gold Lakehouse, ensuring consistency and traceability of analytical results.

---

The following diagram illustrates the high-level data workflow and technology integration within the UMS solution. Data flows from the on-premises SQL Server through the Data Gateway into Microsoft Fabric, is processed and transformed across multiple layers in OneLake, and is ultimately visualized in Power BI. Security and access are governed by Entra ID and Conditional Access policies, while advanced analytics and machine learning are enabled through Synapse, AutoML, and Notebooks.

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: End-to-end Data Workflow Architecture for UMS

---

Enfrasys Solutions will lead the selection, configuration, and ongoing optimization of all above-mentioned technologies to ensure that Universiti Malaysia Sabah achieves a secure, scalable, and future-ready analytics platform.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the network and security architecture designed for Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to ensure secure, reliable, and high-performing connectivity between on-premises resources and Microsoft Fabric. The design leverages best practices for hybrid connectivity, secure data transfer, and robust access control.

## 4.1 Connectivity

A critical component of the network architecture for UMS is the establishment of a secure, resilient connection between the on-premises data warehouse and Microsoft Fabric in the cloud. Enfrasys Solutions recommends the deployment of the Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) hosted in the UMS data center. The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, enabling seamless data movement between the on-premises SQL Server environment and Microsoft Fabric without exposing internal resources to inbound internet connections.

The sizing of the virtual machine hosting the OPDG is a key design decision to ensure optimal performance and reliability. Based on Microsoft’s latest recommendations and Enfrasys Solutions’ experience with enterprise workloads, the VM should be provisioned with a minimum of 8 vCPUs and 8 GB RAM, running either Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit). The .NET Framework version 4.8 is required to ensure compatibility and support for the gateway agent. This configuration provides sufficient resources for concurrent data transfers, high availability, and future scalability.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial design, sizing recommendation, and deployment guidance for the OPDG VM. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for the procurement, provisioning, and ongoing management of the virtual machine within their environment. This clear delineation of responsibilities ensures operational clarity and sustained support for the solution.

The following table summarizes the recommended VM specifications for the On-Premises Data Gateway:

| Component        | Specification                           |
|------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Operating System | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework   | Version 4.8                             |
| vCPU             | 8 cores                                 |
| RAM              | Minimum 8 GB                            |

## 4.2 Data Gateway

The Microsoft On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure, lightweight agent that facilitates encrypted data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Fabric, Power BI, and Azure Data Explorer. The gateway eliminates the need for inbound firewall exceptions by establishing outbound-only connections, thereby reducing the organization’s attack surface and adhering to modern security best practices.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, the OPDG will be installed on the dedicated VM described in the previous section. The gateway acts as a trusted intermediary, securely relaying queries and data between the on-premises SQL Server 2017 data warehouse and Microsoft Fabric. All communication is encrypted using industry-standard SSL/TLS protocols, ensuring data confidentiality and integrity throughout the transfer process.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide installation guidance, configuration best practices, and operational handover documentation for the OPDG. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for the installation, day-to-day operation, and monitoring of the gateway. This approach empowers UMS to maintain direct control over data flows while benefiting from Enfrasys Solutions’ implementation expertise.

The following diagram illustrates the data flow between the UMS on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric via the On-Premises Data Gateway. The data originates from the SQL Server data warehouse, traverses the OPDG, and is securely transmitted to the Fabric environment for processing and analytics.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Secure data flow from UMS SQL Server to Microsoft Fabric via On-Premises Data Gateway

## 4.3 Outbound Security Rules

To safeguard the OPDG VM and ensure only necessary communications are permitted, Enfrasys Solutions has defined a set of outbound network security rules. These rules restrict the gateway’s outbound traffic to approved Microsoft service endpoints, minimizing the risk of unauthorized data exfiltration and aligning with Azure networking best practices.

The outbound rules are as follows:

- **Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services**: Permits outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) traffic from the VM to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and core Azure service domains. This enables secure data transfers and service interactions.
- **Allow_OPDG_Authentication**: Allows outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) traffic to Microsoft identity and authentication endpoints, supporting secure sign-in and token validation.
- **Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test**: Enables outbound HTTP (TCP 80) traffic to Microsoft’s network connectivity status endpoint for troubleshooting and connectivity verification.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for defining and documenting these security rules. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for implementing and maintaining these rules within their network security group (NSG) or equivalent firewall solution.

The table below details the required outbound security rules:

| Name                       | Priority | Source                 | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                                             | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|----------------------------|----------|------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services  | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication  | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com                         | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160     | VM Private IP Addresses| *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                                                          | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

By implementing these outbound rules, Universiti Malaysia Sabah ensures that the OPDG VM can securely communicate with Microsoft cloud services while maintaining a strong security posture and compliance with organizational policies.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section details the roles and access architecture for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. The design ensures robust security controls and clear assignment of responsibilities, leveraging Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access, and workspace-level permissions to safeguard sensitive data and streamline operational efficiency.

## 5.1 Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a core security feature within Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) that enables organizations to automate access control decisions based on user, location, device, and risk signals. It is designed to enforce policies such as Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), restrict access to critical resources, and provide granular control over cloud application access.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Enfrasys Solutions has assessed the current licensing and technical environment. The UMS tenant currently does not possess Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses, which are prerequisites for advanced Conditional Access policies. As a result, Conditional Access cannot be fully implemented at this stage. However, to maintain a strong security posture, Enfrasys Solutions has enforced tenant-wide Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all UMS users. This approach ensures that all users undergo an additional verification step, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized access due to compromised credentials.

The design acknowledges that certain advanced controls—such as restricting access via private endpoints or implementing location-based policies—are not feasible under the current licensing. These enhancements are recommended for future consideration, contingent upon the procurement of appropriate Microsoft Entra ID licenses. The initial configuration focuses on securing access to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage, with all UMS users subject to MFA.

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration of tenant-wide MFA and providing guidance on Conditional Access best practices. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for user enrollment in MFA and for managing user compliance. Should UMS acquire advanced Entra ID licenses in the future, Enfrasys Solutions will support the design and implementation of more granular Conditional Access policies.

The following table summarizes the Conditional Access design decisions:

| No. | Conditional Access |
|-----|-------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment |

The following diagram illustrates the secure access workflow for Microsoft Fabric, highlighting how user authentication requests are evaluated by Entra Conditional Access policies and enforced with MFA:

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Authentication and Conditional Access Workflow for Microsoft Fabric

This workflow ensures that only authenticated and verified users are granted access to Microsoft Fabric resources, thereby protecting sensitive analytics and operational data.

## 5.2 Workspace Permissions

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI employ a role-based access control model at the workspace level, allowing organizations to assign granular permissions to users based on their responsibilities. The primary workspace roles include Admin, Contributor, and Viewer, each with distinct capabilities:

- **Workspace Admin**: Full control over workspace settings, content, and user assignments.
- **Workspace Contributor**: Ability to create, edit, and publish content but without administrative privileges.
- **Workspace Viewer**: Read-only access to reports and dashboards.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends mapping these roles to UMS’s organizational structure to ensure that responsibilities are clearly defined, and data governance is maintained. The assignment of roles is based on job function and the principle of least privilege, ensuring that users have only the access necessary for their duties.

Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial workspace structure and role definitions within Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for nominating the appropriate personnel (Persons In Charge, or PICs) for each role and for ongoing user management, including onboarding, offboarding, and periodic access reviews.

The following table presents the recommended workspace role assignments and the designated UMS personnel:

| No. | Workspace Role | Suggested Role | UMS PIC |
|-----|---------------|---------------|---------|
| 1 | Workspace Admin | Fabric Admin / Data Engineer | Dr Suraya Binti Alias, Sektor Analitik Data DARTIC, PPDM Official, Mohd. Zamrie Bin Musa, Noor Afiza Binti Momen, Ts AG Azihar @ AG KU Azihar Bin AG Tangah |
| 2 | Workspace Contributor | Data Engineer / Business User Admin | Mohd Khairul Nizam Bin Senu (DB), Assie Zaee Petrus (DB), Muhaimin Bin Mad Noor (Infra), Nuraliah Binti Alias (Infra), Chong Tze Chien (Server Security), Abdul Latif Matali (Server Security) |
| 3 | Workspace Viewer | Data Analyst / Stakeholder / Project Director | Director, Dr Farashazillah Binti Yahya, Stakeholders: Roslee Bin Talip, Dayangku Rozlina BTE PG. Aliuddin, Norhanieyati Binti Norhaizat, Zaidie @ Mohd Zaidie Bin Adilai, Professor Madya TS Dr Mohd Hanafi Bin Ahmad Hijazi |

This mapping ensures that data engineering and administrative responsibilities are centralized with qualified personnel, while business users and stakeholders maintain appropriate access to analytics and reports.

Enfrasys Solutions will provide training and documentation to facilitate effective role management. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ensuring that all role assignments are kept up to date and that access is periodically reviewed to comply with internal governance and audit requirements.

The following diagram illustrates the high-level access management architecture, showing the interaction between UMS users, Conditional Access enforcement, and the Microsoft Fabric environment:

![](images\slide_006_img_001.png)

Figure 2: High-Level Access Management Architecture for Microsoft Fabric

This architecture ensures that all access to the UMS Fabric environment is mediated by security controls, with clear role segregation and accountability.

# 6.0 Platform Design & Decisions

This section outlines the platform architecture and critical design decisions for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric implementation. The design ensures robust, scalable, and secure data workflows from ingestion to analytics, with clear responsibilities assigned between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS.

## 6.1 Data Workflow

Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform that integrates data engineering, data science, and business intelligence workloads. It leverages OneLake as a central data lake, supporting seamless data movement and analytics across the organization. The proposed data workflow for UMS is designed to ensure data integrity, traceability, and optimal performance for analytics and reporting.

The end-to-end data flow begins with data ingestion from the UMS Staging Area, specifically Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse. Azure Data Factory orchestrates the extraction, loading, and initial transformation of data into the Fabric environment. Data is then processed through a structured multi-layered approach:

- **Bronze Layer**: Stores raw or minimally processed data for auditing and recovery purposes.
- **Silver Layer**: Contains cleansed and standardized data, ready for further transformation.
- **Gold Layer**: Hosts fully transformed, analytics-ready data optimized for reporting and machine learning outputs.

Throughout these stages, Dataflow Gen2, Notebooks, and Visual Query tools are used for data transformation and cleansing. Data movement between layers is managed by Data Factory pipelines, ensuring automation and repeatability. Security and access are enforced through the Identity_SM component, which integrates with Microsoft Entra ID for robust identity management.

Once data reaches the Gold Lakehouse, it is exposed to Power BI via OneLake, enabling advanced analytics and visualization for business stakeholders. This architecture supports operational efficiency, data governance, and rapid insights delivery for UMS.

The following diagram illustrates the data workflow, highlighting the flow of data from ingestion to final visualization:

![](images\slide_009_img_003.png)

Figure 1: End-to-end Data Workflow Architecture for UMS – from SQL Server ingestion, through multi-layered Lakehouses, to Power BI visualization.

The table below summarizes the key design considerations for each stage of the workflow:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                    | Workload Type   |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| DC01 | Data Pipeline will be used to ingest data from Microsoft SQL Server.                                            | Data Factory    |
| DC02 | The Bronze Lakehouse will store raw/original data ingested from Microsoft SQL Server.                          | Data Engineering|
| DC03 | The Silver Lakehouse will store cleansed data sourced from the bronze Lakehouse.                               | Data Engineering|
| DC04 | The Gold Lakehouse will store transformed data sourced from the silver Lakehouse.                              | Data Engineering|
| DC05 | Data cleansing and transformation for the Silver Lakehouse will be performed using Dataflow Gen2, Notebook and Visual Query in the SQL Analytics Endpoint. | Data Engineering|
| DC06 | Dataflow Gen2 will be used to move data between Lakehouses (e.g., from bronze to silver or silver to gold).    | Data Factory    |
| DC07 | AutoML from Data Science will be used to demonstrate the Machine Learning Process, and the results will be stored in Gold Lakehouse | Data Science    |
| DC08 | Data modeling will be implemented in the Semantic Model, using data from the Gold Lakehouse.                   | Power BI        |
| DC09 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                        | Power BI        |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial design and deployment of the data workflow, including pipeline configuration, Lakehouse setup, and integration with Power BI. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for ongoing data management, monitoring, and operational governance of the data and models.

## 6.2 AutoML & Machine Learning

Microsoft Fabric provides integrated capabilities for both Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) and custom, manual machine learning workflows. AutoML automates the process of feature selection, model training, and evaluation, allowing users to rapidly prototype and deploy predictive models. Manual machine learning, on the other hand, leverages Fabric Notebooks (using PySpark or Python) for advanced users to perform custom feature engineering, algorithm selection, and model optimization.

For UMS, the design enables both approaches. Cleaned data from the Silver Lakehouse serves as the input for machine learning experiments. Users can initiate AutoML experiments directly within the Fabric environment, or opt for manual modeling using Notebooks for greater control and customization. All trained models are registered in the Fabric Model Registry, supporting versioning and lifecycle management.

Once models are trained and evaluated, scoring notebooks are used to apply the models to new or unseen data. The outputs, including predictions and performance metrics, are stored in the Gold Lakehouse, ensuring a standardized repository for all analytical results. The Gold Lakehouse is then connected to the Semantic Model, which Power BI accesses via OneLake for visualization and business reporting.

The diagram below depicts the AutoML and manual machine learning workflow, illustrating the integration between data layers, machine learning processes, and visualization:

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: AutoML and Manual Machine Learning Workflow – from Silver Lakehouse input, through model training and scoring, to Gold Lakehouse and Power BI.

The following table outlines the key design considerations for the AutoML and machine learning workflow:

| ID   | Description                                                                                                    | Workloads type  |
|------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| DE01 | The cleaned data stored in Silver Lakehouse will serve as the input for all machine learning experimentation. The chosen data will be one of the programs selected from the overall Staging DB. | Data Engineering|
| DE02 | The Project will primarily adopt the Manual Machine Learning approach using Fabric Notebooks (PySpark or Python) to enable custom feature engineering, algorithm tuning, and model optimization. | Data Science    |
| DE03 | Users will perform model training, evaluation, and fine-tuning directly in the Notebook environment to achieve more accurate and explainable results tailored to UMS’s datasets. | Data Science    |
| DE04 | Trained models will be registered in the Fabric Model Registry to support model lifecycle management, versioning, and potential reuse across further adoption. | Data Science    |
| DE05 | Scoring Notebooks will be used to apply trained models to new or unseen data. The scored outputs, predictions, probabilities, and performance metrics will be stored in the Gold Lakehouse. | Data Engineering|
| DE06 | The Gold Lakehouse will serve as the standardized repository for all modeled or scored results, ensuring consistency between AutoML and manual ML outputs. | Data Engineering|
| DE07 | The Semantic Model will connect to the Gold Lakehouse via Direct Lake (OneLake) and Data Modelling will be implemented | Power BI        |
| DE08 | Power BI Desktop will connect to the Semantic Model via OneLake for data visualization.                         | Power BI        |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for designing and implementing the initial machine learning infrastructure, including AutoML configuration, Notebook setup, and Model Registry integration. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will manage ongoing model training, evaluation, and operationalization of machine learning assets.

## 6.3 Naming Convention

A consistent and descriptive naming convention is critical for maintainability, clarity, and governance within the Microsoft Fabric environment. Enfrasys recommends a structured pattern: `<Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>`. This approach enables clear identification of resources by purpose, ownership, and environment, which is essential for large-scale deployments.

The naming convention applies to all core Fabric components, including capacities, workspaces, Lakehouses, dataflows, semantic models, pipelines, and reports. For example, a Lakehouse for student affairs in the bronze stage would be named `StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK`, while a dataflow moving data from bronze to silver would be `StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF`.

The following table outlines the recommended naming convention for each Fabric item:

| No. | Item in Fabric   | Naming <Identity>-<Scenario/Activity>-<FabricItemName>          |
|-----|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1   | Fabric Capacity  | stagingareadevcapacity01                                      |
| 2   | Workspace        | StudentAffairs_dev_WS                                         |
| 3   | Lakehouse        | StudentAffairs_Bronze_LK StudentAffairs_Silver_LK Etc…        |
| 4   | Dataflow         | StudentAffairs_Bronze_to_Silver_DF StudentAffairs_Silver_to_Gold_DF Etc.. |
| 5   | Semantic Model   | StudentAffairs_ StudentPerformance_SM                         |
| 6   | Pipeline         | StudentAffairs_Ingest_Data_PL Etc..                           |
| 7   | Report           | StudentAffairs_ StudentPerformance_Report                     |

Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for establishing and documenting the initial naming convention standard. Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ensuring ongoing compliance and applying the convention to all future assets created within the Fabric environment. This governance practice will facilitate efficient management, auditing, and scaling of the platform.

# 7.0 Deployment & Migration Approach

This section outlines the structured deployment and migration methodology for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) data platform modernization initiative. The approach is designed to ensure a seamless transition to the new architecture, minimize operational disruptions, and clearly delineate responsibilities between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS throughout each phase.

## 7.1 Deployment Methodology Overview

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a phased deployment and migration approach to ensure that all critical dependencies are addressed and stakeholders remain engaged at each stage. This methodology reduces risk by validating each milestone before proceeding to the next, ensuring that UMS’s requirements are met and that the technical environment is prepared for production workloads.

The deployment commences with the formal sign-off of the solution design, establishing a mutual understanding between Enfrasys Solutions and UMS. Following this, UMS is responsible for confirming the readiness of the new server environment, specifically the staging area database that will serve as the data warehouse copy. This confirmation is essential to ensure that all data sources are available for subsequent integration and ingestion activities.

Once the server environment is confirmed, Enfrasys Solutions will proceed with the setup of the Microsoft Fabric environment. This step involves configuring core components, security controls, and foundational services necessary for data operations. The installation of the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is then jointly executed by Enfrasys Solutions and UMS, establishing secure connectivity between on-premises data sources and the cloud-based Fabric environment. This gateway is critical for hybrid data scenarios, enabling seamless, secure data movement and integration.

## 7.2 Roles and Responsibilities

A successful deployment depends on clear assignment of tasks and accountability. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for all technical configuration, deployment, and integration activities, while UMS is accountable for providing timely approvals, infrastructure readiness, and operational support. This delineation ensures that technical expertise is leveraged efficiently, and that organizational requirements and compliance standards are maintained.

Enfrasys Solutions will lead the delivery of the design document, setup of the Fabric environment, and installation of the OPDG. UMS will review and sign off on the design documentation, confirm the readiness of their new server infrastructure, and provide access and support for the OPDG installation. Collaborative activities, such as document sign-off and gateway installation, require close coordination to ensure alignment and knowledge transfer.

## 7.3 Migration Timeline and Next Actions

The following table summarizes the key deployment and migration activities, along with planned start dates, responsible parties, and current status. This structured timeline ensures transparency and accountability, facilitating effective project tracking and prompt issue resolution.

| No | Activities | Planned Start | Action By | Status | Remarks |
|----|------------|---------------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | Deliver Design Document to be reviewed by UMS & Sign Off | Fri, 7-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 2 | Confirmation on the new server (data warehouse copy – Staging Area DB) to be ingested | Mon, 10-Nov-25 | UMS | Not-Started |  |
| 3 | Fabric Environment Setup | Wed, 12-Nov-25 | Enfrasys | Not-Started |  |
| 4 | Install On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) in VM to establish Data Gateway | Mon, 17-Nov-25 | Enfrasys UMS | Not-Started |  |

This schedule provides a clear roadmap for the deployment and migration process. Enfrasys Solutions will maintain regular communication with UMS to monitor progress, address challenges, and ensure that all prerequisites are satisfied before advancing to subsequent phases. This collaborative approach is essential for a successful, timely, and secure migration to the new data platform environment.

slides.title: Azure Outbound Security Rules Consideration
slides.notes:
defines the outbound network rules required to allow the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) virtual machine (VM) to securely connect to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related Microsoft cloud services. These rules ensure that the gateway can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data through HTTPS in compliance with Azure networking best practices.

Rule Name : Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services
Purpose: Enables HTTPS communication from the gateway VM to Microsoft Fabric and Power BI endpoints.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound TCP traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) from VM Private IP Addresses to essential Microsoft domains, including Fabric, Power BI, and Azure core services (e.g., *.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com). It ensures that the gateway can send and receive data securely using SSL/TLS encryption.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Authentication
Purpose: Enables authentication and identity verification with Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTPS traffic (TCP port 443) to identity and login domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msftauth.net, and login.windows.net. It enables user sign-ins, token validation, and secure connection establishment with Microsoft cloud services.

Rule Name: Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test
Purpose: Supports network connectivity verification for the OPDG service.
Explanation: This rule allows outbound HTTP traffic on port 80 (TCP) to *.msftncsi.com, a Microsoft endpoint used for network connectivity status indication and troubleshooting. It ensures the VM can verify external internet access and service availability.

# UMS Power BI & Fabric Design Review

# 2.0 Executive Summary

This section provides a concise overview of the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Power BI & Microsoft Fabric solution design, articulating the project’s scope, the purpose of this document, and its intended readership.

## 2.1 Project Overview

The Power BI & Microsoft Fabric initiative for Universiti Malaysia Sabah is strategically designed to modernize and streamline the university’s data management, analytics, and reporting capabilities. The project encompasses the end-to-end design of a comprehensive data workflow, beginning with data ingestion, progressing through transformation and advanced analytics, and culminating in business-aligned visualization using Microsoft Power BI. 

Key objectives include the establishment of a dedicated Microsoft Fabric workspace tailored to UMS requirements, the development of robust ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines, and the enablement of machine learning processes to support data-driven decision-making. The solution leverages the integrated capabilities of Microsoft Fabric Data Factory for data integration and orchestration, Fabric Synapse for advanced analytics and big data processing, and built-in data science tools for machine learning applications. This approach ensures that UMS aligns its cloud adoption strategy with industry-leading Microsoft technologies, delivering scalable, secure, and efficient analytics services to support academic and administrative objectives.

## 2.2 Document Purpose

The intent of this Solution Design Document is to provide a detailed, authoritative blueprint for the implementation of Power BI and Microsoft Fabric within Universiti Malaysia Sabah. It outlines the architectural decisions, technology components, workflow designs, and security considerations that underpin the proposed solution. This document serves as the definitive reference for all stakeholders involved in the project, ensuring clarity, alignment, and traceability from initial design through to deployment and ongoing operations.

## 2.3 Document Audience

This Solution Design Document is intended for the following audiences:
- Universiti Malaysia Sabah IT management and technical teams responsible for implementation and ongoing support
- Enfrasys Solutions consultants, architects, and project delivery personnel
- Project sponsors and executive stakeholders at Universiti Malaysia Sabah who require oversight of the solution’s alignment with institutional goals and compliance requirements

# 3.0 Technology Overview

This section provides a comprehensive overview of the core technologies that form the foundation of the data workflow solution for Universiti Malaysia Sabah. Each technology is defined, its role within the architecture is described, and responsibilities for configuration and management are clearly assigned to Enfrasys Solutions and Universiti Malaysia Sabah.

## 3.1 Microsoft Fabric

Microsoft Fabric is an integrated analytics platform that unifies data engineering, data integration, data science, real-time analytics, and business intelligence into a single SaaS offering. It provides a seamless experience for ingesting, transforming, storing, and visualizing data, leveraging the scalability and security of the Microsoft cloud. Microsoft Fabric enables organizations to break down data silos, accelerate time-to-insight, and simplify data governance through a unified workspace and service model.

In the Universiti Malaysia Sabah solution, Microsoft Fabric serves as the central platform orchestrating the end-to-end data lifecycle. It hosts the data ingestion pipelines, transformation logic, machine learning processes, and business intelligence reporting. Enfrasys Solutions is responsible for the initial configuration of the Fabric environment, including workspace setup, security policies, and integration with other Microsoft services. Universiti Malaysia Sabah will manage day-to-day operations, data curation, and user access within the established framework.

## 3.2 Power BI

Power BI is Microsoft’s enterprise-grade business intelligence and data visualization tool. It empowers users to transform raw data into interactive dashboards and reports, supporting informed decision-making across the organization. Power BI integrates natively with Microsoft Fabric and OneLake, allowing seamless access to curated and transformed data for analytics and reporting.

Within this solution, Power BI is used to connect to the Gold Lakehouse via OneLake, enabling Universiti Malaysia Sabah to visualize and analyze data outputs from the ETL and machine learning pipelines. Enfrasys Solutions will configure the initial connectivity, semantic models, and access controls, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will be responsible for developing and maintaining business-specific reports and dashboards.

## 3.3 Fabric Data Factory

Fabric Data Factory is a cloud-based data integration service within Microsoft Fabric that enables the creation, scheduling, and orchestration of data pipelines. It supports the ingestion of data from diverse sources, transformation using dataflows and notebooks, and movement of data across different layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold) within the data lakehouse architecture.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Fabric Data Factory orchestrates the ETL processes, automating the movement of data from the on-premises SQL Server data warehouse through the Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers. This ensures data is consistently cleansed, transformed, and made available for downstream analytics. Enfrasys Solutions will design and implement the core pipelines, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will monitor and maintain operational dataflows post-deployment.

## 3.4 Fabric Synapse

Fabric Synapse is an advanced analytics service within Microsoft Fabric that combines big data and data warehousing capabilities. It enables large-scale data processing, complex transformations, and advanced analytics using SQL, Spark, and data engineering tools. Fabric Synapse is optimized for high-performance workloads and supports seamless integration with other Fabric components.

In this architecture, Fabric Synapse is utilized for advanced data engineering tasks, including data cleansing, transformation, and aggregation within the Silver and Gold Lakehouse layers. It also supports the execution of notebooks for both manual and automated machine learning workflows. Enfrasys Solutions will provision and configure the Synapse environment, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will leverage the platform for ongoing data engineering and analytics tasks.

## 3.5 OneLake

OneLake is Microsoft Fabric’s unified data lake storage layer, providing a single, secure, and scalable repository for all data assets across the analytics platform. It supports multi-format data storage, fine-grained access control, and high-performance data access for both structured and unstructured data.

OneLake is central to the Universiti Malaysia Sabah solution, storing raw, cleansed, and transformed data in the Bronze, Silver, and Gold Lakehouse layers. It also serves as the data source for Power BI and machine learning models. Enfrasys Solutions will establish the OneLake storage hierarchy and configure access policies, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will manage data lifecycle and retention within the lake.

## 3.6 Data Gateway / On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG)

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a secure bridge that enables cloud services such as Microsoft Fabric and Power BI to access data stored in on-premises environments. The gateway facilitates secure, outbound-only connectivity, ensuring that sensitive data can be ingested into the cloud without exposing internal networks.

For Universiti Malaysia Sabah, OPDG is installed on a dedicated virtual machine within the university’s network. It enables the ingestion of data from the on-premises SQL Server data warehouse into Microsoft Fabric, supporting both scheduled and on-demand data transfers. Enfrasys Solutions will be responsible for the installation, configuration, and initial testing of the OPDG, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will oversee ongoing gateway operations and maintenance.

## 3.7 Microsoft Entra ID

Microsoft Entra ID, formerly known as Azure Active Directory, is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. It provides secure authentication, single sign-on, and conditional access policies for users and applications across the Microsoft ecosystem. Entra ID is essential for enforcing security, compliance, and governance in cloud environments.

In this solution, Entra ID governs user authentication and access to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, and related services. Conditional access policies are applied to ensure only authorized users, both internal and external, can access sensitive data and analytics resources. Enfrasys Solutions will design and implement the initial identity and access policies, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will manage user lifecycle and access reviews.

The following diagram illustrates the conditional access workflow, where user authentication attempts are evaluated against Entra ID policies, and access to Microsoft Fabric is granted or denied based on policy enforcement.

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Entra ID Conditional Access Workflow for Microsoft Fabric

## 3.8 Data Science / AutoML

Data Science capabilities within Microsoft Fabric empower organizations to build, train, and operationalize machine learning models using both automated (AutoML) and manual approaches. AutoML automates feature engineering, algorithm selection, and hyperparameter tuning, accelerating the development of predictive models without extensive data science expertise. Fabric Notebooks provide a collaborative environment for custom model development using Python or PySpark.

In the Universiti Malaysia Sabah solution, cleaned data from the Silver Lakehouse is used as input for machine learning experimentation. Both AutoML and manual notebook-based approaches are supported, with trained models registered in the Fabric Model Registry and scored results stored in the Gold Lakehouse. Enfrasys Solutions will establish the data science environment and initial workflows, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s data science team will conduct ongoing experimentation, model training, and evaluation.

The following diagram demonstrates the integration of AutoML and manual machine learning workflows, highlighting data movement from OneLake’s Silver layer through model training and scoring, with results made available for business analytics.

![](images\slide_021_img_005.png)

Figure 2: Data Science and AutoML Workflow within Microsoft Fabric and OneLake

---

In summary, the integration of these core Microsoft technologies within the Universiti Malaysia Sabah solution ensures a secure, scalable, and future-proof data analytics environment. Enfrasys Solutions will lead the initial deployment, configuration, and enablement of all technologies, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah will assume responsibility for ongoing operations, data stewardship, and business value realization.

# 4.0 Network & Security Design

This section outlines the network and security architecture for the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Microsoft Fabric deployment, focusing on connectivity, data gateway configuration, and outbound security controls. The design ensures secure, reliable integration between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services, while maintaining compliance with best practices and minimizing risk.

## 4.1 Connectivity

A secure and robust connectivity model is essential to enable seamless data movement between UMS’s on-premises environment and Microsoft Fabric. Enfrasys Solutions recommends deploying the On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) within a dedicated virtual machine (VM) hosted in UMS’s infrastructure. The OPDG acts as a secure bridge, forwarding data from on-premises sources such as Microsoft SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse to Microsoft Fabric in the cloud. This architecture eliminates the need for inbound firewall exceptions, as all communication is outbound-initiated, reducing the attack surface and simplifying network security management.

The selection of the VM size for the OPDG is critical to ensure optimal performance and reliability. Enfrasys Solutions has defined the VM specifications based on Microsoft’s latest recommendations and the expected workload. The VM must run either Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit), with a minimum of 8 vCPUs and 8 GB RAM, and have .NET Framework version 4.8 installed. These specifications ensure the gateway can handle concurrent data transfers and maintain high availability for mission-critical reporting and analytics workloads.

The following architecture diagram illustrates the data flow between UMS’s on-premises data warehouse, the OPDG VM, and Microsoft Fabric. The diagram emphasizes the secure outbound connection model, with no inbound ports required, thereby enhancing the overall security posture.

![](images\slide_011_img_004.png)

Figure 1: Data flow architecture between UMS Data Warehouse, On-Premises Data Gateway, and Microsoft Fabric

The responsibilities for the connectivity setup are as follows:
- Enfrasys Solutions will provide guidance on VM provisioning and OPDG installation.
- UMS is responsible for provisioning the VM according to the specifications, ensuring network connectivity to the internet, and maintaining the VM’s operating system and security patches.

The VM sizing requirements are summarized below:

| Component         | Specification                        |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Operating System  | Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows Server 2019 (64-bit) |
| .NET Framework    | Version 4.8                          |
| vCPU              | 8 cores                              |
| RAM               | Minimum 8 GB                         |

## 4.2 Data Gateway

The On-Premises Data Gateway (OPDG) is a Microsoft-provided agent that facilitates secure data transfer between on-premises data sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Fabric and Power BI. The OPDG operates by establishing outbound HTTPS connections to Microsoft endpoints, ensuring that sensitive data never traverses unsecured channels or requires exposure of internal services to the public internet.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends installing the OPDG on a dedicated VM within UMS’s trusted network segment. This approach isolates the gateway from other workloads, reducing the risk of resource contention and potential lateral movement in the event of a security incident. The gateway agent must be configured to connect to the necessary on-premises data sources (e.g., SQL Server 2017 Data Warehouse) and registered with the UMS Microsoft Fabric tenant.

The installation and configuration workflow is as follows:
- UMS provisions the VM and ensures internet connectivity.
- Enfrasys Solutions will provide detailed installation and configuration steps for the OPDG agent, including registration with Microsoft Fabric and validation of connectivity.
- UMS is responsible for maintaining operational health of the VM and the OPDG agent, including monitoring, patching, and troubleshooting as required.

This architecture enables UMS to leverage Microsoft Fabric’s advanced analytics and reporting features without compromising data security or violating network segmentation policies.

## 4.3 Outbound Security Rules

To ensure secure and reliable operation of the OPDG, outbound security rules must be defined and enforced at the network perimeter. These rules restrict the OPDG VM’s outbound traffic to only the necessary Microsoft endpoints, minimizing the risk of unauthorized data exfiltration and ensuring compliance with UMS’s security policies.

Enfrasys Solutions has defined the following outbound security rules, which must be implemented on the network security group (NSG) or equivalent firewall protecting the OPDG VM. These rules allow outbound HTTPS (TCP port 443) traffic to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure core services, and identity endpoints, as well as outbound HTTP (TCP port 80) for connectivity testing. No inbound rules are required, as all connections are initiated by the gateway.

UMS is responsible for implementing and maintaining these outbound security rules according to the specifications provided by Enfrasys Solutions.

The required outbound security rules are detailed below:

| Name                        | Priority | Source                   | Source Ports | Destination                                                                                                                   | Destination Ports | Protocol | Access |
|-----------------------------|----------|--------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Allow_OPDG_HTTPS_Services   | 130      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.servicebus.windows.net, *.download.microsoft.com, *.core.windows.net, *.frontend.clouddatahub.net, *.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com, *.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com, *.powerbi.com, *.analysis.windows.net | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Authentication   | 140      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, aadcdn.msauth.net, aadcdn.msftauth.net, *.microsoftonline-p.com, login.live.com | 443               | TCP      | Allow  |
| Allow_OPDG_Connectivity_Test| 160      | VM Private IP Addresses  | *            | *.msftncsi.com                                                                                                               | 80                | TCP      | Allow  |

These rules ensure that the OPDG VM can authenticate, communicate, and transfer data securely with Microsoft cloud services, while maintaining a minimal and controlled network exposure in line with Azure networking best practices.

# 5.0 Roles and Access

This section outlines the roles, access controls, and permissions model for Universiti Malaysia Sabah’s (UMS) Microsoft Fabric and Power BI environment. The design leverages Microsoft’s security best practices to ensure that only authorized users can access sensitive data and resources, while maintaining operational flexibility and compliance.

## 5.1 Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a core security feature within Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) that enables organizations to enforce automated access control decisions for accessing cloud applications. Policies are evaluated in real time based on user identity, device health, location, and risk signals, allowing organizations to require multi-factor authentication (MFA), restrict access, or block connections as needed.

For UMS, Enfrasys Solutions has assessed the feasibility of Conditional Access policies. Due to licensing constraints—UMS currently does not hold Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licenses—full Conditional Access policy enforcement is not available. As a result, Enfrasys Solutions recommends enforcing MFA at the tenant level to provide an additional security layer for all users accessing Microsoft Fabric and Power BI services. This approach ensures that all authentication attempts, including those from external users, are subject to robust verification, reducing the risk of unauthorized access while maintaining user productivity.

The Conditional Access design also considers current platform limitations, such as the inability to implement Private Link for Fabric at this stage. Enfrasys Solutions advises that as UMS’s security requirements evolve or as additional licensing becomes available, the organization should revisit Conditional Access for more granular controls. In the interim, the enforced MFA policy provides a strong baseline for identity security.

The following diagram illustrates the Conditional Access workflow for Microsoft Fabric, showing how authentication attempts are evaluated and enforced based on defined policies and MFA requirements:

![](images\slide_006_img_002.png)

Figure 1: Conditional Access Workflow for Microsoft Fabric

In this workflow, users attempting to access Microsoft Fabric are evaluated against Entra Conditional Access policies. Signals such as user identity, group membership, and network location are collected to inform the access decision. If the policy requirements are met, including MFA enforcement, access is granted to the environment.

The following table summarizes the Conditional Access design decisions for UMS:

| No. | Conditional Access |
|-----|-------------------|
| DD01 | Configure Policy in Conditional Access to include Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, and Azure Storage |
| DD02 | Include UMS user inside Conditional Access policy |
| DD03 | UMS users go through additional verification, MFA, to reduce unexpected login prompts |
| DD04 | Users able to access Microsoft Fabric’s environment |

**Limitations and Recommendations:**
- Conditional Access policies requiring Entra ID P1/P2 features are not currently enforceable due to licensing.
- MFA is enforced tenant-wide as a compensating control.
- Private Link integration is deferred for future consideration.
- Enfrasys Solutions will assist with policy configuration and provide guidance for future enhancements as UMS’s licensing posture changes.

## 5.2 Workspace Permissions

Microsoft Fabric and Power BI utilize a role-based access control (RBAC) model within workspaces to manage permissions for users and groups. Each workspace role provides a specific set of capabilities, ensuring that users have only the access necessary for their responsibilities. This granular model supports security, operational efficiency, and compliance with organizational policies.

Enfrasys Solutions recommends a structured assignment of workspace roles to ensure clear accountability and separation of duties. The following roles are defined:

- **Workspace Admin:** Full administrative rights over the workspace, including user management, content publishing, and configuration.
- **Workspace Contributor:** Permissions to create, edit, and manage content, but without full administrative privileges.
- **Workspace Viewer:** Read-only access to reports, dashboards, and datasets for stakeholders and decision-makers.

Role assignments must be carefully managed to prevent privilege escalation and ensure compliance with UMS’s governance requirements. Enfrasys Solutions will assign initial administrative roles during the deployment phase. Thereafter, Universiti Malaysia Sabah is responsible for ongoing role management, including the assignment and revocation of Contributor and Viewer roles as organizational needs evolve.

The following tables map the recommended workspace roles to specific UMS personnel, ensuring that each role is assigned to the appropriate point of contact (PIC) within the university:

**Role Assignment Responsibilities:**
